meta.source: 新世纪走遍美国（Connect with English）
meta.note: 全 45 单元（U09 含第 10–12 集内容，原表以 N010–N012 标记并入）

topics.question: Describe a dream or long-term goal you are working towards. Why is it important to you, and what are you doing to achieve it?
topics.questionZh: 描述你正在努力追求的一个梦想或长期目标。它为什么对你重要？你正在做什么去实现它？
hints: 是什么梦想、从什么时候开始
a long-term goal / I've wanted to do this ever since...
为什么重要：它对你的意义
it's not just a hobby, it's part of who I am / it keeps me going
正在做什么：日常努力、学习计划
I practise every single day / I'm saving up / I'm applying to...
现实困难与态度
success takes time / I know it won't happen overnight
vocab: apply to a school / for a job
sample: Well, the dream I'm working towards is to become truly fluent in English and use it in my job, instead of just passing exams.
呃，我正在努力的梦想，是让英语达到真正流利并在工作中使用，而不只是通过考试。
I know it might sound like a small goal compared with becoming a pop star or something, but for me it really matters.
我知道跟当明星之类的大目标相比，这听起来很小，但对我而言真的很重要。
I started taking it seriously about two years ago, when I realised that reading documentation was slowing down my work.
大约两年前我开始认真对待这件事，那时我意识到读英文文档拖慢了我的工作。
So I made a plan: I listen to podcasts on my commute every day, I keep a notebook of useful expressions, and I've been trying to speak with real people online once a week.
于是我定了个计划：每天通勤听播客，用本子记有用的表达，还坚持每周在线上和真人开口说一次。
It's not always easy to keep up — some weeks I'm too tired and I skip a session — but I always come back to it the next day.
坚持并不总那么容易——有些星期太累会漏掉一次——但第二天我总会捡起来。
The reason this goal is so important to me is that English is like a door.
这个目标对我如此重要，是因为英语就像一扇门。
Behind that door there are better career opportunities, and also things I simply enjoy, like films and music.
门后有更好的职业机会，也有我纯粹喜欢的东西，比如电影和音乐。
When I understand a joke in English without subtitles, honestly, it feels brilliant.
当我不用字幕就能看懂英语笑点时，说实话，感觉棒极了。
Of course, people around me sometimes say it's too difficult, or that I'm too old to learn a language properly.
当然，身边的人有时会说这太难，或者说我年纪大了学不好一门语言。
But I believe success takes time, and I'm not in a hurry.
但我相信成功需要时间，我并不着急。
As long as I keep improving little by little, I'm getting closer to my dream.
只要我一点点持续进步，我就在离梦想越来越近。
That's why I keep going.
这就是我一直坚持的原因。

topics.question: Describe a time when someone close to you doubted your plan or decision. How did you feel and how did you respond?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你身边的人怀疑你的计划或决定的经历。你当时是什么感受，又是如何回应的？
hints: 背景：什么计划、谁质疑
when I told my friend / family about my plan to...
他们质疑的理由
they said it was too tough / too risky / not practical
你的感受
honestly, I felt hurt / frustrated at first
你怎么回应：坚持并证明
instead of arguing, I decided to prove it with actions
sample: I remember clearly when I decided to change my career direction and focus on software development.
我清楚地记得决定转行专注软件开发的那一次。
When I told one of my closest friends, he just laughed and said, 'You're banging your head against the wall. That field is far too competitive.'
当我告诉一个最要好的朋友时，他笑着说：'你这是拿头撞墙，那个行业竞争太激烈了。'
At first, honestly, I felt hurt.
说实话，一开始我很受伤。
When someone you trust is negative about your dream, it hits you harder than when a stranger says it.
当你信任的人对你的梦想泼冷水时，比陌生人说同样的话杀伤力大得多。
For a couple of days I even doubted myself — maybe he was just being realistic and I was the one being naive.
有几天我甚至怀疑自己——也许他只是现实，天真的人是我。
But then I calmed down and thought about why he said that.
但后来我冷静下来，想他为什么这么说。
He wasn't trying to hurt me; he was worried about me wasting time.
他不是想伤害我，而是担心我浪费时间。
So instead of arguing, I told him, 'I understand your concern, but let me try. If I fail, at least I won't regret not trying.'
所以我没有争论，而是告诉他：'我理解你的担心，但让我试试。就算失败，至少不会后悔没试过。'
And after that, I just worked quietly — I took courses, built small projects, and little by little I got better.
那之后我只是安静地努力——上课、做小项目，一点一点变强。
About a year later, when I showed him what I had built, he was actually impressed and said, 'OK, I was wrong about this.'
大约一年后，当我把做出来的东西给他看时，他真的被打动了，说：'好吧，这点我看走眼了。'
That moment felt great, not because I won the argument, but because I proved it with actions.
那一刻感觉很好，不是因为吵赢了，而是用行动证明了自己。
So now, when people doubt my plans, I don't get angry.
所以现在有人怀疑我的计划时，我不会生气。
I listen to their reasons, take the useful part, and then let my results speak.
我会听他们的理由，吸收有用的部分，然后让结果说话。
Actions are always louder than words.
行动永远比言语更有力。

topics.question: Do you think it is possible to balance a busy work or study life with a personal relationship? Use your own experience to explain.
topics.questionZh: 你认为繁忙的工作/学习与感情可以兼顾吗？请结合自身经历说明。
hints: 观点先行：可以，但需要用心
yes, but only if both people make an effort
你或身边人的经历
we both had two jobs / there was no time left for each other
问题出在哪
a real relationship takes time / it's hard to find time
解决办法：小事与仪式感
small gestures matter / we fixed a date night every week
vocab: have no time for each other
真正的感情需要时间经营
sample: That's a good question, because I've lived through exactly this situation.
这个问题问得好，因为我恰好亲身经历过。
My answer is: yes, it's possible, but only if both people treat the relationship as a priority, not as something left over after work.
我的答案是：可以，但前提是两人都把感情当作优先事项，而不是工作之余剩下的东西。
A while ago, my partner and I were both extremely busy.
前阵子，我和我对象都忙得不可开交。
I was working overtime almost every day, and she was preparing for an important exam.
我几乎天天加班，她在准备一场重要考试。
We lived in the same city, but sometimes a whole week went by and we barely had a real conversation.
我们住在同一座城市，可有时整整一周都没能好好说上一句话。
We were tired, a bit impatient with each other, and I started to worry that we were becoming just roommates.
我们都很累、对彼此有点不耐烦，我开始担心我们正在变成'合租室友'。
Then one day we sat down and talked honestly about it.
后来有一天，我们坐下来坦诚地聊了这件事。
We realised the problem wasn't love — it was time.
我们意识到问题不在感情，而在时间。
So we made two simple rules.
于是我们定了两条简单的规矩。
First, no matter how busy we are, we have dinner together at least twice a week, phones away.
第一，不管多忙，每周至少一起吃两顿晚饭，手机放到一边。
Second, we keep one fixed evening for a date, even if it's just a walk.
第二，固定留一个晚上约会，哪怕只是散散步。
It sounds small, but those small promises changed everything.
听起来很小，但这些小小的承诺改变了一切。
I think a real relationship takes time, as simple as that.
我认为真正的感情需要时间投入，就这么简单。
You can't water a plant once a month and expect flowers.
你不能一个月浇一次花还指望它开花。
Busy periods will always come and go, but if two people make time for each other on purpose, the relationship survives.
忙碌期总会来来去去，但如果两人有心为彼此挤时间，感情就能存活。
If nobody makes an effort, even free time won't help — you'll just sit in the same room staring at your phones.
如果谁都不努力，有空也没用——你们只会坐在同一个房间里各自刷手机。

topics.question: Describe a time when a friend, classmate or colleague decided to leave a team or project you were both part of. How did you feel and what did you do?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次朋友/同学/同事离开你们共同团队或项目的经历。你的感受如何？你做了什么？
hints: 背景：什么团队/项目、这个人是谁
we'd been working together for two years
他为什么离开
family reasons / the pay wasn't good / it was just peanuts
你的感受：失望但理解
I was disappointed, but I understood
你接下来做了什么
I had to find someone new / I carried on alone
sample: I'd like to talk about my former colleague, Chen.
我想讲讲我以前的同事陈。
We joined the same project team around the same time, and for almost two years we worked side by side — debugging together, complaining about deadlines together, celebrating small wins together.
我们差不多同一时间进的项目组，并肩干了将近两年——一起改 bug，一起吐槽截止日期，一起庆祝小小的胜利。
He was more than a teammate; he was my partner in that project.
他不只是队友，更是我在那个项目里的搭档。
Then one day he told me he was leaving.
后来有一天，他告诉我他要走了。
Honestly, I saw it coming.
说实话，我早有预感。
The salary wasn't great — to be frank, compared with the hours we put in, it was peanuts — and his wife had just had a baby, so the bills were piling up.
薪水不算高——坦白讲，跟我们投入的时间相比就是杯水车薪——而他妻子刚生了孩子，账单越堆越多。
A company offered him a much better position.
有家公司给了他一个好得多的职位。
How could I blame him for that?
这我怎么能怪他呢？
Still, when he said goodbye, I felt a mixture of sadness and worry.
尽管如此，他道别时我心里还是又难过又担忧。
Sad, because good partners are hard to find.
难过，因为好搭档难找。
Worried, because I had to take over his work and find someone new.
担忧，因为我得接手他的活儿，还得找新人。
For a couple of months it was really tough; I was doing the job of two people.
有几个月真的很艰难，我干着两个人的活。
But looking back, I learned something important.
但回头看，我学到了重要的一课。
When a teammate leaves, don't take it personally.
队友离开时，不要觉得是针对你。
People have their own families, their own pressures.
每个人都有自己的家庭、自己的压力。
What you can do is stay on good terms — we still have dinner now and then — and make sure the team keeps moving.
你能做的是保持好关系——我们现在还时不时聚个饭——并确保团队继续前进。
Since then, whenever I work with someone good, I try to learn as much as possible from them while they're still around.
从那以后，每当和优秀的人共事，我都会趁他还在时尽可能多学。

topics.question: Describe two people in your family who have very different personalities. How are they different, and how do they get along?
topics.questionZh: 描述你家两位性格差异很大的家庭成员。他们有哪些不同？相处得如何？
hints: 两位家人是谁、什么关系
my younger brother and I are like chalk and cheese
生活习惯差异：饮食、学习
he lives on junk food / I'm the one making plans and lists
各自的性格亮点
he's easygoing — math is a breeze for him / I'm the careful one
虽有摩擦但感情好
we drive each other insane, but we still look out for each other
vocab: put what you want on the list
想要什么就写在单子上
sample: The two people I'd like to talk about are my younger brother and me, because although we grew up in the same house, we are completely different.
我想说的是我弟弟和我，因为虽然我们在同一个屋檐下长大，俩人却完全不同。
He's eighteen and easygoing about almost everything, while I'm the serious older sister who worries about deadlines and money.
他十八岁，对什么事都大大咧咧；而我呢，是那个操心截止日期和钱的严肃姐姐。
The funniest difference is our eating habits.
最逗的是我们在吃的上的差别。
He drinks milk straight from the carton and lives on cookies and peanut butter.
他喝牛奶直接对着盒子吹，日常就靠饼干和花生酱活着。
Every week I ask him, 'When are you going to give up junk food and eat something healthy?' and every week he gives me the same answer — he'll start when healthy food tastes as good as cookies.
我每周都问他：'你到底什么时候才能戒掉垃圾食品，吃点健康的？'他每周都给我同一个答案——等健康食品吃起来跟饼干一样香的时候。
I do the grocery shopping now, so I've learned to just say, 'Put what you want on the list.'
现在买菜的是我，所以我学会了只说一句：'想要什么就写在单子上。'
When it comes to school, we're opposites too.
说到上学，我们俩也是两个极端。
I prepare for exams weeks in advance; he opens his book the night before.
我提前好几周就开始复习，他头天晚上才翻书。
Last June, before his math final, I was a nervous wreck, but he just laughed and said, 'Relax, math is a breeze,' and then he actually got one of the top grades.
去年六月他数学期末考前，我紧张得不行，他却笑着说：'放宽心，数学小菜一碟。'结果他真考了年级前几名。
Honestly, he drives me insane sometimes, with the loud music, the mess, and the empty cereal boxes he never replaces.
说实话，他有时候真把我逼疯——音乐开得震天响、屋里乱糟糟，麦片吃完了也从来不补。
But at the end of the day we get along really well.
但到头来我们相处得非常好。
He makes me laugh when I'm stressed, and in return I help him fill out his college application forms, which want to know everything — interests, hobbies, awards, on and on.
我压力大的时候他能把我逗笑，作为回报，我帮他填大学申请表——那表格什么都想知道，兴趣、爱好、获奖，没完没了。
I think our differences balance each other out, and home would be boring without him.
我觉得我们的不同正好互补，家里没有他可就太无聊了。

topics.question: Do you think it is important for young people to save money? How do you or people around you manage to save?
topics.questionZh: 你认为年轻人攒钱重要吗？你或身边的人是怎么攒下来的？
hints: 观点：攒钱给人选择权
saving gives you options and a safety net
身边人的攒钱习惯
deposit the paycheck into a savings account / take out a fixed amount in cash
借钱给朋友要谨慎
if you lend money to a friend, you might kiss that money goodbye
攒钱不等于亏待自己
use coupons / treat yourself now and then
vocab: 跟那笔钱说拜拜（要不回来了）
two for the price of one
sample: Yes, I think saving is really important for young people, and I learned this from my older cousin.
是的，我觉得攒钱对年轻人真的很重要，这一点是我表姐教我的。
She had a clear goal — paying for college by herself — so her motto was simple: save, save, save.
她有个明确的目标——自己挣出上学的钱——所以她的座右铭特简单：攒钱、攒钱、攒钱。
Every payday, she deposited almost her whole paycheck into her savings account.
每次发工资，她都把几乎整张工资单存进储蓄账户。
When she needed cash, she took out a small fixed amount from the cash machine, maybe forty dollars at a time, and made it last for the week.
需要现金时，她就去取款机取一小笔固定的钱，一次大概四十块，撑一个星期。
The rest of us joked that she was too strict with herself, but she just said, 'How else am I going to pay for college?'
我们其他人常笑话她对自己太狠，她只回一句：'不然我拿什么交学费？'
She also taught me to be careful about lending money.
她还教会我借钱给人要小心。
Once she lent some money to a workmate, and when I asked about it later, she sighed and said, 'You can kiss that money goodbye.'
有一次她借了点钱给同事，后来我问起，她叹口气说：'那笔钱你就当告别了吧。'
She was right — he never paid it back, and it wasn't even enough to cover her bills that month.
她说对了——那人再没还钱，而那点工资连她当月的账单都不够付。
Since then, if a friend asks to borrow money, I only lend what I can afford to lose.
从那以后，朋友找我借钱，我只借我输得起的那部分。
Of course, saving doesn't mean never spending.
当然，攒钱不等于一分不花。
My cousin still loved coupons — those two-for-the-price-of-one offers made her day — and she'd treat herself now and then.
我表姐照样爱用优惠券——买一赠一能让她高兴一整天——偶尔也会犒劳一下自己。
To me, the point of saving is freedom: with money in the bank, you can say no to a bad job, or say yes to a chance that really matters.
对我来说，攒钱的意义是自由：卡里有积蓄，你才敢对烂工作说不，也才敢抓住真正要紧的机会。
That's the habit I'm trying to build now, little by little.
这也是我现在正一点点培养的习惯。

topics.question: Do you find it difficult to persuade your family members to eat and live more healthily? Why?
topics.questionZh: 你觉得劝家人吃得更健康、活得更健康难吗？为什么？
hints: 谁需要改变、坏习惯是什么
my dad's diet is full of junk food
你做过哪些尝试
keep the fridge stocked with fruit / cook at home twice a week
为什么难：习惯连着感情
old habits die hard / food is how some people show love
小目标更有效
aim for small wins instead of a total ban
vocab: tastes as good as cookies and peanut butter
吃起来跟饼干花生酱一样香
sample: In my family, yes, it's honestly quite difficult, and the person I keep trying to change is my dad.
在我家，说实话挺难的，我一直想改变的那个人是我爸。
He's worked hard all his life, but his diet is terrible — he skips breakfast, eats instant noodles at midnight, and thinks vegetables are a waste of money.
他辛苦了一辈子，可吃得太差——不吃早饭，半夜啃泡面，还觉得买蔬菜纯属浪费钱。
Over the years I've tried everything.
这些年我什么招都试过。
I cook dinner twice a week, I hide the snacks, and I keep writing healthy things on the grocery list before he can complain that we're out of cereal again.
我每周做两次晚饭，把零食藏起来，还抢在他抱怨麦片又吃光之前，把健康食品写进购物单。
When I ask him, 'When are you going to give up junk food and eat something healthy?' he just smiles and says he'll think about it when healthy food tastes as good as fried chicken.
我问他：'你什么时候才能戒掉垃圾食品，吃点健康的？'他就笑笑说，等健康食品跟炸鸡一样好吃他就考虑。
Then he goes to the shop and comes back with three jars of peanut butter — after I just bought that jar last week.
然后他去趟超市，拎回来三罐花生酱——上周我才刚买过一罐。
I think the reason it's so hard is that eating habits are tied to feelings.
我觉得难就难在，饮食习惯是和情感绑在一起的。
For my dad, those late-night snacks were his reward after long shifts, so my healthy list sounds like criticism to him.
对我爸来说，深夜加餐是他上了长班之后给自己的犒赏，所以我那张健康清单在他听来像是在数落他。
In his generation, feeding someone is also how parents show love, so when I turn down his treats, he feels turned down.
在他们那代人里，给你塞吃的也是父母表达爱的方式，所以我拒绝他买的零食，他会觉得是被我拒绝了。
So now I aim for small wins instead of total change.
所以现在我追求小胜，不求彻底改造。
We agreed on one rule — fruit after dinner instead of dessert, six days a week.
我们定了一条规矩：一周六天，晚饭后用水果代替甜点。
It's not perfect, but his last check-up was better, and honestly, that's enough for me.
这不完美，但他上次体检指标好了些，说真的，对我来说这就够了。

topics.question: Some people chase big, exciting dreams while others prefer a simple, stable life. Which do you prefer, and why?
topics.questionZh: 有人追逐宏大又刺激的梦想，有人偏爱简单安稳的小日子。你更喜欢哪一种？为什么？
hints: 两种活法各自的魅力
big dreams keep life exciting / a simple life gives you peace of mind
身边两类人的例子
she's applying to music schools far away / I chose a stable job near home
你的选择与理由
I'd rather aim high and fail than never try — or the opposite
尊重不同选择
there's no right answer / happiness looks different for everyone
vocab: dreaming of this for a long time
get anywhere in the music world
sample: I've thought about this a lot, because my best friend and I are living proof of both types.
这个问题我想过很多次，因为我最好的朋友和我正好是这两种人的活例子。
She has big, exciting dreams, while I've always preferred a simple, stable life — a decent job, get married and have a family, stuff like that.
她有着宏大又刺激的梦想，而我一直偏爱简单安稳的日子——一份体面的工作，结婚组建家庭，诸如此类。
My friend is applying to music schools on the other side of the country.
我朋友申请的都是国家另一头的音乐学院。
It costs a lot of money just to apply, but she says she's been dreaming of this for a long time, and it's the only way she'll ever get anywhere in the music world.
光申请就要花一大笔钱，但她说这是她梦想已久的事，也是她在音乐界闯出名堂的唯一路子。
She has even prepared backup schools in case she's rejected everywhere.
她甚至连备选学校都准备好了，就怕全部被拒。
When she talks about getting her degree and making something of herself, her eyes are shining.
每当说起拿到学位、干出名堂，她眼睛都在发光。
Meanwhile, I chose the safe route: a stable job near home and weekends with my family.
与此同时，我选了保险的路：家门口的稳定工作，周末陪家人。
Sometimes, when she says, 'Your dreams are so big and exciting — mine are so simple,' I actually feel a bit small.
有时她说：'你的梦想那么大、那么带劲，我的也太朴素了。'我反倒会有点自惭形秽。
But then I look at my life — a job I don't hate, people I love nearby — and honestly, I have nothing to complain about.
可再看看我的生活——一份不算讨厌的工作，爱的人都在身边——说真的，我没什么可抱怨的。
In the end, I respect both choices.
说到底，两种选择我都尊重。
I'd rather be content than anxious, but I know she'd rather fail big than spend her life wondering what might have been.
我宁愿心安也不想焦虑，但我知道她宁愿轰轰烈烈地输，也不愿一辈子想'当初要是试了会怎样'。
When she gets her first hit song, I'll be the first one cheering, and she promised to send me a free copy.
等她出了第一首走红歌曲，我肯定是第一个欢呼的，她都答应送我一张免费的。

topics.question: Describe a time you went with a family member to see a doctor. What happened and how did you feel?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你陪家人去看病的经历。发生了什么？你当时感觉如何？
hints: 陪同谁、因为什么病
I went with my grandfather to his check-up / he had a ten o'clock appointment
在医院的过程
check in at the front desk / spell your name / wait for your turn
医生说了什么、给了什么建议
start an exercise program / a strict diet / get the prescription filled
你的感受
hospitals make me nervous too, but company matters
sample: Last spring I went with my grandfather to the hospital for his annual check-up, and it's an experience I won't forget.
去年春天，我陪爷爷去医院做年度体检，那次经历我忘不了。
He had a ten o'clock appointment, so we arrived early, checked in at the front desk, and waited on the hard chairs.
他约的是十点钟的号，所以我们到得早，在前台报到后坐在硬椅子上等。
I could tell he was tense, because hospitals make him nervous and doctors put him on edge.
我看得出他挺紧张，因为医院让他发怵，医生也让他心里不踏实。
His left leg has been stiff for years — he hurt it in an accident at work when he was young, and he's been on disability pay ever since.
他左腿僵了好多年了——年轻时在工伤事故中伤的，从那以后就一直领伤残补助。
He kept saying that doctors never tell him anything useful, and I kept replying that if he didn't take care of that leg, it would only get worse.
他一个劲儿说医生从来讲不出什么有用的，我就一遍遍回他：这腿再不好好治，只会越来越糟。
When his name was finally called, the doctor was thorough.
终于叫到他时，医生查得很仔细。
She said his cholesterol was very high, the EKG showed a slight heart problem, and the circulation in his leg was getting worse.
她说他胆固醇很高，心电图显示心脏有点小毛病，腿部的血液循环也在变差。
She warned him, quite seriously, that without changes he could end up having a stroke, so she put him on a strict diet and an exercise programme, plus a prescription.
她相当严肃地警告说，再不改变就可能中风，所以给他上了严格节食加锻炼方案，还开了药方。
In the taxi home, I asked him what the doctor had said, and he just shrugged: 'Not much. Everything's OK. No real problems.'
回家的出租车上，我问医生说了什么，他只是耸耸肩：'没什么，一切还好，没什么大问题。'
I knew he was playing it down, partly to protect me.
我知道他是在轻描淡写，一部分是为了不让我担心。
That day I realised that going along with older relatives isn't just about company — it's about making sure the truth doesn't get lost on the way home.
那天我明白了，陪家里老人看病不只是作伴——还要确保真话不会在回家路上弄丢。

topics.question: Do you think it is right to hide bad news, such as a health problem, from the people you love? Use an example to explain.
topics.questionZh: 你认为向亲人隐瞒坏消息（比如健康问题）是对的吗？请举例说明。
hints: 观点：瞒不如好好说
I'd tell them, but gently and at the right time
家人为什么选择隐瞒
they don't want us to worry / they're protecting themselves too
隐瞒的代价
the truth comes out anyway / things only get worse
更好的沟通方式
sit down together / face it as a family
vocab: it's only going to get worse
sample: My view is that in most cases you shouldn't hide bad news completely, but you can choose the right moment and the gentlest words.
我的看法是：多数时候不该把坏消息彻底瞒住，但可以挑对时机、用最温和的方式说。
I learned this when my grandfather got his check-up results and decided to keep them from us.
这一点是爷爷拿到体检结果、决定瞒着我们的时候，我才体会到的。
The doctor had found several problems — high cholesterol and a heart condition — and said that if we didn't do something right away, it would only get worse.
医生查出了好几个问题——高胆固醇加心脏毛病——还说如果不马上处理，只会越来越糟。
But on the way home, my grandfather told everyone, 'Everything's OK, no real problems. Let's go straight home.'
可回家路上，爷爷跟所有人说：'一切还好，没什么大问题，咱们直接回家吧。'
He was doing the best he could to protect us; the trouble is, he was also protecting himself from the scary words.
他是在尽最大努力护着我们；麻烦的是，他同时也想躲开那些吓人的字眼。
The hiding almost backfired.
这一瞒差点坏了事。
He skipped his pills, kept eating fried food, and got annoyed whenever we mentioned the diet, because officially there was nothing wrong with him.
他药也不好好吃，油炸照吃，我们一提忌口他就烦——因为按他的说法，自己根本没病。
My mother found the unfilled prescription in his coat pocket and cried in the kitchen.
我妈在他大衣兜里发现那张没取的药方，在厨房里哭了。
If we had talked about it openly at the start, he might have taken it seriously much sooner.
要是我们一开始就摊开说，他也许会早得多当回事。
So eventually we sat him down and said, look, we're worried about you, and we'd rather face this together than pretend it isn't there.
于是最后我们拉他坐下来说：听着，我们担心你，我们宁愿一起面对，也不愿假装没事。
He finally admitted he was scared — he said he was always worried about my mum and us kids, and he couldn't stand the idea of being a burden.
他终于承认自己害怕——他说他总是担心我妈和我们几个孩子，受不了自己成为拖累。
Now I believe bad news is like a stone in your shoe: shaking it out hurts for a second, but ignoring it makes every step worse.
现在我相信，坏消息就像鞋里的石子：倒出来疼一下，硬忍着却步步都疼。

topics.question: What would you do if your parents disagreed with your study or career plans?
topics.questionZh: 如果父母不认同你的学业或职业规划，你会怎么做？
hints: 分歧从哪来
they want something practical for me / I have my own dream
先听懂反对背后的爱
behind the criticism there's usually love and fear
怎么表明立场但不吵架
it's not me / I won't change my mind, but I won't shout either
用计划代替争吵
show them costs, backup plans and job prospects
vocab: 你和另外一百万人都一样
sample: This actually happened to me when I told my parents I wanted to study music production instead of accounting.
这事儿真在我身上发生过：我告诉父母我想学音乐制作，不学会计。
My father's first reaction was to ask why I didn't study nursing or something safe, and then came the famous line: 'You and a million others want the same thing.'
我爸第一反应是问我为什么不去学个护理之类稳妥的，然后甩出那句名言：'想干这个的，你和另外一百万人都一样。'
He listed the jobs he considered proper, and I kept repeating, 'It's not me. It's not what I want.'
他把心目中正经的工作数了个遍，我翻来覆去就是一句：'那不适合我，不是我想要的。'
At one point he said, 'If you ask me, you're making a big mistake,' and I shouted back, 'Not if it's what I want to do!'
到后来他说：'要我说，你这是在犯一个大错。'我吼回去：'只要这是我想做的，就不算错！'
The funny thing is, we're too alike — I take after my father, and neither of us backs down easily.
好笑的是，我们太像了——我随我爸，谁都不肯轻易让步。
What changed things wasn't winning the argument.
真正扭转局面的，不是吵赢。
I calmed down and did my homework: I showed him the course list, the costs, the job numbers for graduates, and a backup plan in case the first path failed.
我冷静下来做足了功课：给他看课程设置、费用、毕业生就业数据，还有一条失败后退而求其次的备选路线。
I also admitted that his worries about money and competition were reasonable, which surprised him.
我还承认他对钱和竞争的担心有道理，这倒让他吃了一惊。
He still doesn't love the idea, but he stopped fighting it.
他谈不上喜欢这个主意，但不再拦着了。
My advice to anyone in this situation: don't turn it into a war.
给同处境的人一个建议：别把这变成一场战争。
Listen for the love behind the criticism, answer with a plan instead of tears, and give your parents time — mine needed about two months.
听懂批评背后的爱，用一份计划而不是眼泪去回应，再给父母一点时间——我爸妈大概用了两个月。

topics.question: Describe a friend of yours whose romantic relationship makes you worried. What have you said to them about it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一位其恋爱状况让你担心的朋友。关于这件事，你对他们说过什么？
hints: 朋友和伴侣的情况
her boyfriend can be charming, but he has a temper
让你担心的具体表现
he lost his temper again / he'd had too many beers
你劝过什么、她怎么回应
she says he's really a good guy / she gets defensive
朋友之间的边界
say it once, then just be there for her
vocab: have a little girl like that some day
将来也有个这样的小女儿
sample: I have a close friend whose relationship has worried me for about two years.
我有个要好的朋友，她的感情状况让我担心了差不多两年。
Her boyfriend can be charming — he introduces her to everyone as the love of his life — but he also has a temper.
她男朋友嘴甜的时候很迷人——逢人就介绍她是自己的此生挚爱——可他脾气也真大。
Things came to a head at a friend's barbecue last summer.
去年夏天，在朋友的烧烤聚会上，事情彻底爆发了。
He'd had too many beers, and when my friend wasn't ready to leave, he announced, 'I'm leaving. If you want to stay, you can stay,' and marched off.
他啤酒喝多了，见我朋友还没准备走，就撂下一句'我走了，你想留就留着吧'，然后扬长而去。
Later we learned he had lost his job that very week — and of course he lost it right after he lost his temper with his manager. Again.
后来我们才知道，就在那一周他丢了工作——而且不用说，是又跟经理发了火之后丢的。
I've tried to talk to her, gently.
我试过委婉地跟她聊。
She once said she wants to have a little girl like our neighbour's daughter some day, so I asked her, don't you want the right man for that — someone who will be a good father?
她说过将来也想有个邻居小女儿那样的孩子，我就问她：那你是不是该找对的人——一个能当好爸爸的人？
She gets defensive and answers, 'He's really a good guy, he just gets so crazy sometimes.'
她一听就护短：'他其实是个好人，只是有时候太不靠谱。'
And then I know it's time to change the subject.
每到这时我就知道，该换个话题了。
In the end I've learned where my line is.
最后我摸清了自己的分寸。
I say what I see, once, without drama — 'I just want you to be happy, that's all' — and then I stop repeating it, because lectures only push her towards him.
我会不带情绪地说一次我看到的——'我只是希望你幸福，仅此而已'——然后不再重复，因为说教只会把她往他那边推。
She knows my door is open at three in the morning, and until she's ready, that's honestly the best I can do.
她知道我家的门凌晨三点也开着；在她自己想通之前，说真的，我能做的就到这儿了。

topics.question: Describe a graduation ceremony or a celebration of achievement that you attended and enjoyed.
topics.questionZh: 描述一场你参加过并且很享受的毕业典礼或成就庆祝活动。
hints: 什么场合、为谁庆祝
my cousin's high school graduation last summer
仪式上有什么
caps and gowns / students come forward to receive their diplomas
拍照与家人感言
look this way and say cheese / I'm proud of you
为什么难忘
it felt like the family's hard years had finally paid off
vocab: I want to get a picture
sample: The celebration I remember best is my cousin's high school graduation two years ago.
我记得最牢的一场庆祝，是两年前我表弟的高中毕业典礼。
It was held in the school hall, and the whole family drove over that morning — aunts, uncles, grandparents, everyone.
典礼在学校礼堂举行，那天早上全家都开车赶了过去——姨妈、舅舅、外公外婆，一个不落。
When the head teacher called the graduating class forward to receive their diplomas, the hall went quiet for a second and then exploded.
当校长念到毕业班上前领取毕业证书时，礼堂安静了一瞬，随后掌声轰然响起。
All the students wore their caps and gowns; my cousin complained that his smelled funny from storage, but he looked proud and suddenly grown-up in it.
学生们都穿着学位帽和毕业礼服；表弟抱怨他那身放了太久有股怪味，可穿在身上，他看着又自豪、又一下子长大了。
Afterwards, out on the lawn, we must have taken a hundred photos.
之后在草坪上，我们少说拍了一百张照片。
My aunt kept shouting, 'Stand over there, all together — I want to get a picture! Look this way and say cheese!'
我姨妈一直在喊：'都站那边，一起拍一张！看镜头，说 cheese！'
Then my uncle gave a little speech and said he was proud of every single graduate that day.
接着我舅舅来了段小发言，说那天他为每一位毕业生骄傲。
Somewhere in the second row, a grandmother was quietly wiping her eyes.
第二排某个座位上，有位奶奶正悄悄抹眼睛。
There were hugs, silly poses, and far too much cake.
拥抱、搞怪姿势，还有多得吃不完的蛋糕。
What made the day unforgettable wasn't the ceremony itself.
真正让那天难忘的，其实不是典礼本身。
My cousin had nearly dropped out the year before to help at home, so that diploma meant two years of the whole family pushing together.
前一年他差点辍学回家帮忙，所以那张毕业证书背后，是全家一起扛的两年。
When I see the photo of us holding his diploma, I remember that some celebrations are really about survival.
每次看到我们举着他毕业证书的合影，我都会想起：有些庆祝，庆祝的其实是挺过来。

topics.question: Describe an experience of being rejected several times before finally getting what you wanted. How did you handle it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一段屡遭拒绝、最终得偿所愿的经历。你是怎么撑过来的？
hints: 目标是什么、申请了几个
I applied to four schools
接连被拒的感受
each rejection letter stings / I couldn't believe it
怎么撑过来的
focus on the one chance left / make a backup plan
结果与感悟
keep your fingers crossed / one yes makes up for three noes
sample: Last year I applied to four universities, and for a while it felt like the universe was saying no to me personally.
去年我申请了四所大学，有一阵子感觉整个宇宙都在专门对我说'不'。
The first rejection letter arrived in March, the second came a week later, and by the third I actually laughed when I opened it, because three rejections in one month felt absurd.
第一封拒绝信三月到，第二封一周后到，拆第三封时我反而笑了——一个月连吃三个闭门羹，荒诞到好笑。
Each letter started the same way: 'We are sorry to inform you...'
每封信的开头都一模一样：'我们很遗憾地通知您……'
Even though I told myself not to take it personally, I couldn't believe it — I had worked on those applications for months.
尽管我告诉自己别往心里去，还是难以置信——那些申请材料我磨了好几个月。
My mother watched me open the third one and quietly asked what I was going to do, and for a moment I had no answer at all.
我妈看着我拆开第三封，轻声问我打算怎么办，那一刻我完全答不上来。
What kept me going was that one school hadn't answered yet.
撑住我的是：还有一所学校没回音。
They had put me on their waiting list, so every morning I checked the mailbox like a fool and told my friends, 'Keep your fingers crossed for me.'
他们把我放进了候选名单，于是每天早上我都像个傻子一样去查信箱，还跟朋友说：'替我祈个好运吧。'
At the same time I made a backup plan — retake one exam in autumn, apply again, find a job in between.
与此同时我也定了备用方案——秋天重考一门，来年再申，中间先找份工作。
Having a plan B didn't mean giving up on plan A; it just stopped me from falling apart.
有 B 计划不等于放弃 A 计划，它只是让我不至于垮掉。
In April the last letter came, and this time it began, 'We are pleased to inform you...'
四月，最后一封信到了，这次开头是'我们很高兴地通知您……'
I was accepted, with financial aid — my one last hope had come through.
我被录取了，还带着奖学金——最后一线希望成了真。
Now I actually think rejections are useful, because they test whether you want something badly enough to keep going after being turned down.
现在回头想，被拒其实有用：它试出你到底有多想要，被拒之后还想不想继续。
One yes really can make up for three noes.
一个'行'，真能抵过三个'不行'。

topics.question: Describe someone you know who had to take on adult responsibilities while still young.
topics.questionZh: 描述一个你认识的、年纪轻轻就扛起大人责任的人。
hints: 是谁、家里发生了什么
when her mother passed away, she stepped right in
她承担了什么
cooking, school forms, taking care of her father and brother
她自己的态度
she never complained / there was no one else, she says
你的评价
she grew up fast / capable and calm beyond her age
sample: The person who comes to mind is my cousin Lisa.
我脑子里立刻冒出来的人是我表姐 Lisa。
When her mother passed away, Lisa was fifteen, and she basically stepped right in and became the mother of the family.
她母亲去世那年，Lisa 十五岁，她几乎是立刻顶了上去，成了家里的'妈妈'。
There was no one else — her father worked night shifts, and her brother was only eleven.
也确实没有别人——爸爸上夜班，弟弟才十一岁。
So she learned to cook, signed the school forms, packed lunches, and took good care of both her father and her brother.
于是她学会了做饭、签学校的通知单、装午饭，把爸爸和弟弟都照顾得很好。
While her classmates were worrying about pop stars, she was comparing vegetable prices at the market.
同学还在追星的时候，她已经在菜市场比菜价了。
What I admire most is that she never made a drama of it.
我最佩服的是，她从没把这事渲染成苦情戏。
At her brother's graduation party, an aunt praised her: 'Don't be so modest — you basically raised this boy.'
弟弟毕业聚会上，一位姨妈夸她：'别谦虚了，这孩子等于是你拉扯大的。'
Lisa just shrugged and said, 'Well, there was no one else,' as if running a household at fifteen were the most normal thing in the world.
Lisa 只是耸耸肩：'呃，又没有别人。'仿佛十五岁撑起一个家是天底下最平常的事。
She grew up fast, and maybe she missed some careless teenage years.
她长得太快，也许错过了本该没心没肺的少年时光。
But today she is the most capable, calm person I know — nothing panics her, because she has already handled real problems.
但如今她是我认识的最能干、最沉得住气的人——没有什么能让她慌，因为真正的问题她早就处理过了。
I think people like her deserve more than praise; they deserve rest, and a chance to be taken care of in return.
我觉得这样的人配得上不止一句夸奖，她们配得上休息，配得上被人反过来照顾一次。

topics.question: Would you give up a stable job to follow a dream that might not pay off? Why?
topics.questionZh: 你会为一个未必有回报的梦想放弃稳定的工作吗？为什么？
hints: 观点：会，但要算好账
I would — as long as the plan survives honest maths
别人怎么质疑
would you give up your job in this economy? No way
你怎么降低风险
savings for eighteen months / a partial scholarship / part-time work
梦想需要计划
it's good to have dreams, but attach numbers to them
vocab: give up your job in this economy
这种经济环境下你还辞职
sample: I honestly think I would, and I say that as someone who has already done it once, on a small scale.
说实话，我觉得我会——而且这话是出自一个已经小规模干过一次的人。
Two years ago I quit a stable job to prepare for graduate school full-time, and almost everyone thought I had lost my mind.
两年前我辞掉稳定的工作，全职备考研究生，当时几乎所有人都觉得我疯了。
My colleagues were blunt.
同事们话说得很直。
One asked me, 'Would you give up your job in this economy? No way.'
一个问我：'这种经济环境下你还辞职？想什么呢。'
Another told me that a dream doesn't pay the rent, and they weren't wrong to worry — the risk was real.
另一个说梦想付不起房租。他们的担心没有错，风险是真的。
Still, their doubts made me check my plan twice, which was probably healthy.
不过，他们的质疑让我把计划又核了两遍，这说不定反而是好事。
But I was dead serious about the change, and being serious meant planning, not just dreaming.
可我对这次转身是绝对认真的，而认真意味着做计划，不是光做梦。
My reasoning was simple: I did the maths.
我的逻辑很简单：先把账算清。
Savings for eighteen months, plus financial aid if I got in, plus part-time teaching on the side.
攒下的钱够撑十八个月，若考上了还有经济资助，再加上兼职教课的收入。
So it wasn't a blind jump; it was a plan with a safety net.
所以这不是闭眼跳崖，而是一张带安全网的计划。
And deep down I knew that if I didn't try, I'd spend my forties wondering what if.
而且我心里清楚：这回不试，四十岁时我就会一直在想'当初要是试了会怎样'。
I'd tell anyone considering the same move: it's good to have dreams, but attach numbers to them.
我会对每个有同样念头的人说：有梦想是好事，但要给梦想配上数字。
Dreams without a budget are just wishes.
没有预算的梦想只是许愿。
If the plan survives honest maths, then quitting isn't reckless — sometimes staying might be the bigger risk.
只要这份计划经得起老实的算术，辞职就不算莽撞——有时候不走才是更大的冒险。

topics.question: Is it brave or risky to move far away from your hometown? And why do some people never want to leave?
topics.questionZh: 远离家乡去生活，是勇敢还是冒险？为什么有些人永远不想离开？
hints: 远走的好处与代价
new opportunities / you don't know a soul out there
有人离不开家的原因
family, old friends / it's still home
邀请朋友同行的经历
I asked my best friend to come with me / she said no thanks
如何看待两种选择
courage isn't only about leaving / home means different things
vocab: you don't know a soul out there
你在那儿一个熟人都没有
nice of you to ask, but no thanks
谢谢你邀请，还是算了吧
sample: I moved to a city eight hundred kilometres from my hometown for work, so I've lived both sides of this question.
我因为工作搬到了离老家八百公里的城市，所以这个问题的两面我都尝过。
And when I left, I actually tried to take my best friend with me.
而且走的时候，我还真试过把我最好的朋友一起带走。
I found her a job lead, offered to share my flat at first, and asked her, 'Think about it — what's keeping you here?'
我帮她物色了工作线索，提出可以先和我合住，还问她：'想想看，到底是什么把你拴在这儿？'
She laughed and listed her reasons: her mother, the familiar streets, weekends with her old classmates.
她笑着数了一堆理由：她妈、闭着眼都认得的街道、和老同学的周末。
In the end she said, 'It's nice of you to ask, but no thanks. This is still home — it's my town.'
最后她说：'谢谢你想到我，还是算了吧。这里毕竟是家，这才是我的城市。'
At first I thought she was simply scared.
一开始我以为她只是胆小。
Now I understand her much better.
现在我理解她多了。
I'm the one who didn't know a soul in the new city and had to build a life from zero; she's the one with a warm network that took twenty years to grow.
我是在新城市一个熟人都没有、从零搭起生活的那个人；而她拥有的是花了二十年长出来的温暖人际网。
When I go back, I can see her power: she knows every shopkeeper, and her mother's dumplings are ten minutes away.
每次回去，我都能看到她的'底气'：每家店主她都认识，她妈包的饺子十分钟就能到嘴。
Her hometown is her strength, not her cage.
家乡是她的力量，不是她的牢笼。
So is moving far away brave or risky?
那么远走他乡到底是勇敢还是冒险？
I'd say it's brave and risky, and staying can be just as valid a choice.
我想说：既勇敢又冒险，而留下来也同样可以是正确的选择。
Courage isn't only about leaving; sometimes it's about knowing what home means to you and choosing it with open eyes.
勇气不只体现在离开；有时候，勇气是想清楚'家'对你意味着什么，然后睁着眼睛选它。

topics.question: Describe an important decision you made that your parents disagreed with at first. How did you win them over?
topics.questionZh: 描述一个你做出、起初遭到父母反对的重要决定。你是怎么说服他们的？
hints: 什么决定、父母为何反对
they thought it was too far away / too risky
第一次谈话如何崩掉
I just want your approval — no way, end of conversation
你换了什么方法
show facts and numbers / promise to call every week
最终结果
go for it — their support meant everything
vocab: you don't always get what you want
这世上你不会总能如愿
sample: When I decided to take a job in another city, my father's answer was short: no way.
当我决定去另一座城市工作時，我爸的回答只有两个字：不行。
I remember saying, 'Dad, I'm not asking for money. I just want your approval.'
我记得我说：'爸，我不是要钱，我只想要你的点头。'
He replied, 'You want my approval? N-O,' stood up, and announced that it was the end of conversation.
他回我：'想要我同意？N-O。'然后站起来，宣布谈话到此为止。
His reasons weren't silly: the city was far, I'd be on my own, and rents were high.
他的理由并不糊涂：城市远、我一个人、房租贵。
He told me, 'You don't always get what you want in this world,' and in his generation that was practically a law of nature.
他教导我：'在这个世界上，你不会总能如愿。'在他们那代人眼里，这几乎就是自然法则。
Every talk ended the same way, until I stopped arguing and changed my method.
每次谈话都是同一个结局，直到我不再争辩，换了方法。
Instead of debating, I showed him facts.
我不跟他辩了，改为给他摆事实。
I made one page: salary, rent, and the exact distance — six hours by train, not the other side of the earth, as he kept claiming.
我做了一页纸：工资、房租、精确距离——坐火车六个小时，不像他一口咬定的'在地球另一端'。
I introduced him to my future flatmate on a video call, and I promised to phone home every Sunday.
我还让他跟我未来的合租室友视频见了面，并保证每周日给家里打电话。
Most importantly, I asked him about his own youth, and it turned out he had once wanted to work in another province but gave it up for the family.
最关键的是，我问起了他年轻时候的事——原来他也曾想去外省闯，为了家里才放弃。
Something softened after that conversation.
那次谈话之后，有什么东西软了下来。
One evening he simply said, 'Go for it. Call me when you arrive.'
某天晚上他只说了一句：'去吧。到了来个电话。'
Winning parents over, I've learned, isn't about defeating their arguments — it's about showing them a plan instead of a dream, and giving them time to let go.
我学到，说服父母不在于驳倒他们，而在于让他们看到一份计划而不只是一个梦，再给他们一点放手的时间。

topics.question: Describe a time you disagreed with a friend's decision about their relationship. What did you do?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你不认同朋友在感情上做的某个决定。你当时是怎么做的？
hints: 朋友做了什么决定
she told me she was moving in with her boyfriend
你担心的理由
the two of them are always fighting
你怎么说、她怎么回
I just want you to be happy / let's just change the subject
学会守边界
say it once, then stay close and keep clapping
vocab: the two of you are always fighting
I just want you to be happy
I think I can make it work
sample: This happened to me last spring, and it still makes me a little uncomfortable to remember it.
这事发生在去年春天，现在想起来我还是有点不自在。
A close friend announced, of all places in a shop's changing room, that she was moving in with her boyfriend — a secret not even her mother knew.
一位好朋友在商场的试衣间里——偏偏是那种地方——宣布她要搬去和男朋友同居，这事儿连她妈都还不知道。
I didn't react well at first.
起初我的反应不太好。
I blurted out, 'The two of you are always fighting!' because it was true — half our dinners ended with stories of some fresh argument.
我脱口而出：'你们俩总是吵架！'因为这是实话——我们一半的聚餐都以她新吵架的剧情收尾。
She just shrugged and said, 'Things change.' And I shot back, 'Yeah, but people don't.'
她只是耸耸肩：'情况会变的。'我立刻顶回去：'会变的是事，不变的是人。'
I could see she was getting angry, so I took a breath and said the only true thing I had: 'Look, I just want you to be happy, that's all.'
眼看她要动气，我深吸一口气，说了我仅有的实话：'听着，我只是希望你幸福，仅此而已。'
She cut me off with, 'I know you don't think it's a good idea, so let's just change the subject.'
她打断我：'我知道你觉得这不是好主意，那咱们换个话题吧。'
So we did — we paid for our dresses and went for noodles.
于是我们换了话题——付了裙子的钱，去吃了碗面。
Later I asked myself whether I should have pushed harder, and I still don't know.
后来我反复想，当时是不是该再多劝一句，至今没有答案。
But I've settled on two rules: I say my worry once, clearly and without drama, and then I keep quiet and stay close.
但我给自己定了两条规矩：担心的话只清楚地说一次、不渲染，然后就闭嘴，人留在她身边。
She told me later, 'I think I can make it work,' and maybe she can — friendship doesn't come with a veto, it comes with a front-row seat.
她后来跟我说：'我想我能把日子过好。'也许她真能——友谊没有否决权，只有第一排的座位。
You keep clapping even when you can see the cracks.
哪怕看得出裂缝，你也要继续鼓掌。

topics.question: What should people pay attention to when buying a second-hand item like a car? Do you have any experience of bargaining?
topics.questionZh: 买二手车这类二手物品时应该注意什么？你有讲价的经验吗？
hints: 先定预算
set a budget first — fifteen hundred, max
检查车况
look at the engine and tires / bring a friend who knows cars
讲价技巧
can you come down a little in the price? / silence is a weapon
防坑心态
be ready to walk away / we're just looking, thanks
vocab: come down a little in the price
how much do you want to spend
sample: Last year I bought my first second-hand car, and it taught me more about bargaining than any textbook.
去年我买了人生第一辆二手车，它给我上的讲价课比任何教科书都多。
My budget was fixed, and I told every salesman the same thing: fifteen hundred, max.
预算是定死的，我跟每个销售说的都一样：最多一千五。
At the first lot, the dealer showed me a shiny car and promised it was in A-1 condition — new tires, excellent engine.
第一家车行里，销售指给我看一辆锃亮的车，拍胸脯说车况一流——新轮胎、好引擎。
But it was far over budget, and the moment I said my limit, he suddenly had nothing for me — except a friend of his, four blocks away, who 'might have something'.
可价格远超预算，我一报上限，他那儿立刻就'没货'了——只剩他一个朋友，在四个街区外，'也许有合适的车'。
That's a classic trick: pass you to the next seller until you're too tired to negotiate.
这是经典套路：把你往下一家推，推到你累得不想谈为止。
By the fourth lot, I had a system.
逛到第四家，我已经有了一套流程。
Walk in calm and say, 'We're just looking, thanks,' so nobody pressures you.
进门先稳住，说一句'我们只是随便看看'，别人就没法逼你。
Never answer 'How much do you want to spend?' with your real ceiling — give a number below it.
对方问'您打算花多少钱'，绝不说真实上限——报一个更低数。
Then ask directly, 'Can you come down a little in the price?' and stay quiet; silence is a weapon.
然后直截了当问：'价格能再让一点吗？'问完就闭嘴——沉默是武器。
And bring a friend who knows engines, because you want something you can count on, not a pretty disaster.
再带上懂车的朋友，因为你要的是靠得住的伙计，不是一台漂亮的灾难。
In the end I paid thirteen hundred for an old but honest little car.
最后我花一千三买下了一辆老旧但实在的小车。
A good bargain isn't about winning the argument; it's about being ready to walk away.
会讲价不是靠吵赢，而是随时敢转身走人。
The moment you stop looking desperate, the price starts moving.
你一不露'非买不可'的相，价格自己就开始松动了。

topics.question: Describe a difficult conversation you had with a family member before a big change in your life.
topics.questionZh: 描述在人生大变动之前，你与家人进行的一次艰难谈话。
hints: 什么大变化、心结是什么
I was leaving for a city far away / we weren't speaking
怎么开启对话
would you please talk to me? / say the thing you're afraid to say
对方真实的心情
I don't have to like it, do I?
和解的意义
everyone has to leave home sometime / untie the knot before you go
vocab: everyone has to leave home sometime
I don't want to leave with you angry at me
我不想带着你的气离开
try to be happy for me
I don't have to like it, do I
我不见得非得喜欢它，不是吗
would you please talk to me
sample: Yes — the night before I left for university, my father and I had the hardest talk we've ever had.
有——去上大学的前一夜，我和我爸进行了我们之间最艰难的一次谈话。
We had been giving each other the silent treatment for days, because he disagreed with my choice of city.
我们已经冷战了好几天，起因是他不认同我选的城市。
Finally I sat down next to him and said, 'This is silly. Would you please talk to me?'
最后我挨着他坐下说：'这样多傻啊，能跟我说说话吗？'
He said, 'I'm not angry,' which clearly wasn't true, so I said the thing I'd been afraid to say: 'Dad, I'm leaving tomorrow, and I don't want to leave with you angry at me.'
他说'我没生气'——这显然是假的，于是我说出了那句我一直不敢说的话：'爸，我明天就走了，我不想带着你的气离开。'
He was quiet for a while, and then he admitted, 'I just don't see why you have to go so far away.'
他沉默了一会儿，然后承认：'我就是不明白，你非得去那么远。'
I said, 'Try to be happy for me.'
我说：'试着为我高兴点吧。'
And he answered with a sentence I'll never forget: 'I know, I know. But I don't have to like it, do I?'
他回了一句我终生难忘的话：'我知道，我知道。可我不见得非得喜欢它，不是吗？'
That was as close to a blessing as he could get, and strangely, it was enough.
这已经是他能给出的最接近祝福的话了，说来奇怪，这就够了。
We talked until midnight about small, wonderful things — bus timetables, winter clothes, my grandmother's soup.
我们一直聊到半夜，聊的都是细碎又美好的事——班车时刻表、冬衣、奶奶的汤。
Now I understand what he couldn't say: everyone has to leave home sometime, but nobody warns the parents.
如今我懂了他没能说出口的话：人总有离家的一天，可没人提前提醒过父母。
Big changes go better when you untie the knot before you go — otherwise you carry it with you for years.
大变动之前先把心结解开，路才走得顺——不然你会背着它走很多年。

topics.question: Describe a time you had to say goodbye to a child you taught or took care of. How did you explain it to them?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你不得不与教过或照顾过的小孩道别。你是怎么向孩子解释的？
hints: 孩子是谁、你们的关系
I tutored a nine-year-old girl on the piano
怎么告诉孩子这个消息
tell her early, simply and honestly
孩子的反应
where is that? / I won't be able to see you?
你能做的安排
one more lesson / find her a good teacher / keep in touch
vocab: sorry I'm late for my lesson
I'll try to find you a good teacher
我会尽力给你找个好老师
sample: For two years I tutored a nine-year-old girl in piano, one lesson every Saturday morning, so saying goodbye to her was strangely harder than saying it to adults.
有两年时间，我每週六上午给一个九岁的小姑娘上钢琴课，所以跟她道别，竟出奇地比跟大人道别还难。
Children feel the loss just as much, but they can't really understand the reasons.
孩子同样能感到失落，只是他们没法真正理解缘由。
I told her at the start of my last month, because I didn't want her to hear the news from her parents.
我在最后一个月的开始就告诉了她，因为我不想让她从父母那儿听到消息。
That day she ran in a little late and said, 'Sorry I'm late for my lesson,' and then, before we began, I said I had to tell her something: I was going back to school, far away.
那天她跑进来时迟到了一会儿，说'对不起老师我迟到了'，随后在开课前，我说有件事要告诉她：我要回学校念书了，在很远的地方。
Her first question wasn't about me at all — it was, 'Where is that?' So we found the city on a map, and she stared at the distance and asked, 'I won't be able to see you?'
她的第一个问题压根与我无关——'那在哪儿呀？'于是我们在地图上找到那座城，她盯着那段距离问：'那我就见不到你了？'
I kept my promise about our remaining lessons, and for the last one I let her choose everything.
剩下的课我一节没爽约，最后一节，全由她说了算。
She always loved to play the blues, so we played her favourite piece one final time — badly and joyfully.
她一直爱弹蓝调，于是我们把她的保留曲目最后弹了一遍——弹得不怎么样，但特别开心。
I also told her, 'I'll try to find you a good teacher, OK?' and she answered, 'But you're the best music teacher.' I nearly cried right there on the piano stool.
我还对她说：'我会尽力给你找个好老师，好不好？'她回答：'可你是最好的音乐老师呀。'我差点当场在琴凳上哭出来。
What I learned is that with children you don't need clever words — you need honesty and a slow goodbye.
我学到的是：对孩子不需要漂亮话——需要的是诚实，和一场慢慢来的告别。
We still exchange short videos: she plays, I clap, she laughs at my clapping.
我们至今还互发小视频：她弹琴，我鼓掌，她笑我拍得难听。
Goodbyes for children should be like our lessons — regular, gentle, and never suddenly cancelled.
给孩子的告别就该像上课一样——有规律、温和，绝不突然取消。

topics.question: Do you think long-distance relationships can work? Why or why not?
topics.questionZh: 你认为异地恋能长久吗？为什么？
hints: 观点先行
they can work — with a shared finish line
异地恋的现实困难
expensive visits / different schedules / growing apart
一个失败或成功的例子
I'm not a long-distance kind of guy / we have different dreams
关键是什么
distance isn't the killer / a deadline is a must
vocab: I'm not a long-distance kind of guy
我不是能熬异地恋的人
我以为下一个就该轮到我们了
sample: I believe long-distance relationships can work, but only for a while, and only when both people are running towards the same finish line.
我相信异地恋能成，但只能撑一段时间，而且前提是两个人朝着同一个终点跑。
I've watched one fail up close, and it taught me more than any article about love.
我近距离看过一段异地恋的失败，它给我上的课比任何情感文章都多。
My friend went abroad to study, and her boyfriend of five years stayed in our hometown.
我朋友出国读书，相恋五年的男朋友留在了老家。
He wasn't a bad man, but he told her honestly, 'I'm not a long-distance kind of guy.'
他不是坏人，但他坦白地告诉她：'我不是那种能熬异地恋的人。'
At first they managed — video calls, monthly visits, shared calendars.
起初他们撑住了——视频、每月见面、共享日历。
But their timetables drifted apart, and so did their lives.
可两人的生活节奏渐渐错开，人生也跟着错开了。
The real problem was never the kilometres.
真正的问题从来不是那几千公里。
When she talked about her future, it was full of new things; his future was exactly where he had left it.
她谈起未来，满眼都是新鲜事；他的未来，还停在原地一动没动。
In the end he said, 'You and I, we have different dreams. I think it's better to call quits.'
最后他说：'你和我，我们的梦想不一样。我看还是到此为止吧。'
The most painful line was this one: 'All our friends are getting married and having kids. I thought we were next.'
最扎心的是那句：'朋友们都结婚生孩子了，我以为下一个就该轮到我们了。'
Distance didn't kill it; distance just made the difference impossible to ignore.
杀死这段感情的不是距离；距离只是让两个人的不同再也没法视而不见。
So my answer is: yes, it can work — if both people want the same future and can name the date when the distance ends.
所以我的答案是：能——前提是两人想要同一个未来，并且能说清异地哪天结束。
A long-distance relationship without a deadline is just a slow goodbye.
没有截止日期的异地恋，只是一场慢动作的分手。
If someone refuses to name that date, they have already answered your question.
如果对方死活不肯给出那个日期，其实他早已回答了你的问题。

topics.question: Describe a surprise farewell party or an unexpected gift from a group of friends or teammates.
topics.questionZh: 描述一场惊喜送别会，或一群朋友、队友送你的意外礼物。
hints: 什么场合、为什么意外
after my last game / I didn't see it coming
惊喜时刻与礼物
you didn't have to do this! / a team jacket with my name
你的告别感言
we had more fun than any other team / don't replace me too soon
为什么感动
teams measure results / people remember warmth
vocab: you didn't have to do this
你们不必这么破费费心
sample: The most touching farewell I've ever had came from my university softball team, and I honestly didn't see it coming.
我经历过最感人的送别，来自我的大学垒球队，而且说实话，我完全没料到。
It was the last game of my final year, we lost badly, so I was in about the worst mood possible.
那是我毕业年级的最后一场比赛，我们输得很惨，我的心情跌到了谷底。
Afterwards, in the clubhouse, my teammates suddenly gathered round with a big parcel.
赛后在俱乐部里，队友们忽然围过来，抱着一个大包裹。
I kept saying, 'You guys didn't have to do this — this is too much!' and they just laughed and told me to hurry up and open it.
我直说：'你们不必这么破费的，太隆重了！'她们只是笑，催我快拆。
Inside was a team jacket with our logo and my name on it.
里面是一件队服外套，绣着我们的队标和我的名字。
It sounds like a small thing, but standing there in my muddy uniform, I actually got a bit emotional.
听起来是件小东西，可穿着一身泥的队服站在那儿，我真的有点绷不住。
Then everyone wanted a speech, and I'm afraid mine wasn't very elegant.
接着大家起哄要我讲话，恐怕我讲得一点儿不体面。
I told them we hadn't won many games, but we'd had more fun than any other team in the league.
我说，我们赢的比赛不多，但我们比联赛里任何一支队都玩得开心。
I said I'm gonna miss them more than they know, and then, half-joking, half-not: 'Don't replace me too soon, OK?'
我说我会超乎他们想象地想念大家，然后半开玩笑半认真地补了一句：'别太快找人顶替我，行吗？'
One of the girls shouted, 'You'll be a hit out there!' and everybody raised their drinks.
一个姑娘喊：'你出去肯定大放异彩！'所有人都举起了杯子。
That jacket still hangs by my door.
那件外套至今挂在我门边。
What I keep from that day is simple: teams measure themselves in results, but people remember each other in warmth.
那天留下的道理很简单：球队用成绩衡量自己，而人记住彼此，靠的是温度。
Losing my last game, and still feeling like the luckiest one there — that's friendship.
最后一场输了球，却仍觉得自己是全场最走运的人——这就是友谊。

topics.question: Do you agree that taking part matters more than winning? Use your own experience of sport or games to explain.
topics.questionZh: 你同意“参与比获胜更重要”吗？请结合你自己的运动或比赛经历说明。
hints: 一场惨败的经历
we lost twenty-two to two
当场情绪与争执
I argued with the umpire / end of discussion
朋友怎么安慰或取笑
how about a little sympathy? / you're supposed to be cheering me on
你怎么想通的
what the heck, it's only a game / memories beat medals
vocab: I lost my last softball game
我输掉了最后一场垒球赛
what the heck, it's only a game
you're supposed to be cheering me on
sample: I agree completely, though I admit I didn't always think this way.
我完全同意，虽然我承认自己并非一直这么想。
My conversion happened at my last softball match, the worst defeat of my life.
让我转变的，是我最后一场垒球赛——我此生最惨的一次失利。
We lost twenty-two to two.
我们二比二十二输了。
Twenty-two to two — it wasn't a game, it was a public education.
二十二比二——那不叫比赛，那叫当众上课。
On top of that, I argued bitterly with the umpire about one call at home base.
更糟的是，本垒的一次判罚让我和裁判吵得不可开交。
I insisted my teammate was safe; the umpire looked at me, said one word — 'Safe' — and then added, 'End of discussion.'
我坚持我方队友上垒了；裁判看了我一眼，吐出一个词'出局'，然后补了一句：'不许再争了。'
I sulked for a good hour afterwards.
之后我足足赌气了一个钟头。
My best friend, who had come to watch, first made everything worse.
来看球的我最好的朋友，先是在伤口上撒盐。
When I complained, she said, 'Well, how about a little sympathy? I lost my last softball game!'
我一抱怨，她就说：'那……给点同情心行不行？我可是输掉了最后一场垒球赛的人！'
I told her, 'You're supposed to be cheering me on, not enjoying my misery!' — and then, somehow, we both started laughing.
我对她说：'你本该给我加油才对，不是看我笑话！'——不知怎么，我们俩都笑出了声。
On the bus home, someone finally said the magic words: 'What the heck, it's only a game.'
回家的车上，有人说出了那句咒语：'算了，不过是一场比赛。'
Eating cold fries and replaying the disaster, I realised those two embarrassing hours had given me a story, an inside joke, and a closer team.
啃着凉薯条复盘那场灾难时，我忽然明白：那丢人的两小时，给了我一箩筐故事、一个只有我们懂的梗，和一支更亲的队伍。
Nobody remembers the scoreboard of an amateur match; everybody remembers who they played it with.
业余比赛的比分没人记得；一起打球的人，谁都记得。
We lost the game that day, but we won the ride home.
那天的比赛我们输了，可回家的那趟车，我们赢了。

topics.question: Describe a surprise gift that someone gave you and that you will never forget.
topics.questionZh: 描述一件别人送你的、让你终生难忘的惊喜礼物。
hints: 什么场合收到礼物
the night before I left home
礼物是什么、你的反应
it's your new car / I was speechless
礼物背后的心意
you need it and you deserve it / I got a good deal
这件礼物后来的意义
it carried me for years / every time I press the horn
sample: The gift I'll never forget arrived the night before I left home for university.
那件让我终生难忘的礼物，出现在我离家上大学的前一夜。
I was upstairs, busy packing and fighting with my suitcase, when my little brother shouted that Dad wanted to show me something downstairs.
我正在楼上忙着收拾行李、跟箱子较劲，我弟弟突然喊：爸在楼下要给你看样东西。
In front of the house stood a small second-hand car, freshly washed.
房前停着一辆洗得锃亮的二手小车。
My father said, 'It's your new car,' and I actually laughed and told him, 'Dad, you're joking.'
我爸说：'这是你的新车。'我当场笑了，跟他说：'爸，你开玩笑呢。'
When I understood he wasn't joking, I was — I'm not exaggerating — speechless, and my family enjoyed that enormously, because I never stop talking.
等我明白他不是玩笑时，我毫不夸张地——说不出话了。全家人为此乐坏了，因为我这张嘴从来不停。
Then he handed me the keys and said, 'Try the horn.'
然后他把钥匙递给我说：'试试喇叭。'
He had prepared everything: the papers, and the insurance already paid for the first year.
他把一切都备好了：手续，还有付掉的第一年保险。
I said, 'You must have spent a fortune on it,' and he just waved his hand: 'Not really. I got a good deal.'
我说：'你肯定为它花了一大笔钱。'他只是摆摆手：'没有，我捡了个好价钱。'
Then came the two sentences that really stayed with me: 'You need a car. And you deserve it.'
接着是那句真正刻进我心里的话：'你需要一辆车。而且，这是你应得的。'
That little car carried me through four years and thousands of kilometres.
那辆小车驮着我跑过了四年和几万公里。
It never once broke down on an exam morning.
它从没在考试日的早晨抛过锚。
My father isn't a man who says 'I love you' easily; that car was the sentence he couldn't pronounce.
我爸不是轻易说得出'我爱你'的人；那辆车就是他发不出音的那句话。
Every time I press the horn, I hear him.
每次按响喇叭，我都听得见他。

topics.question: Describe an object that has been passed down in your family. Why is it so special to you?
topics.questionZh: 描述一件在你们家代代相传的物品。它为什么对你如此特别？
hints: 传家物是什么
a thin gold necklace from my grandmother
谁把它交给你、当时场景
my mother put it in my hand and said, I want you to have this
背后的故事与意义
bought with her first salary / a chain that stays unbroken
你会不会继续传下去
one day I'll pass it to my own daughter
vocab: I want you to have this
keep an eye on Kevin and Dad
替我照看好凯文和爸爸
sample: The most precious object in my family is a thin gold necklace that belonged to my grandmother, and now it belongs to me.
我们家最珍贵的东西，是一条外婆留下的细细的金项链，如今它到了我手里。
It isn't worth much money, but in our family it carries the most weight.
它值不了几个钱，可在我们家的分量最重。
My grandmother passed away when I was in high school, and for years the necklace sat quietly in my mother's jewellery box.
外婆在我高中时去世，此后很多年，那条项链一直安安静静躺在我妈的首饰盒里。
Then, the week I moved abroad, my mother took it out and said simply, 'I want you to have this.'
后来在我出国那一周，我妈把它取出来，只说了一句：'我想让你收下这个。'
I asked twice whether she was sure — it felt far too valuable to accept.
我问了两遍她是否想好了——它贵重得让我不敢接。
She said it was never about money; it was about keeping the chain unbroken.
她说这从来不是钱的事，而是要让这条链子不断。
My grandmother bought it with her first salary, in a year when the family could barely afford meat.
这条项链是外婆用人生第一笔工资买的，那一年家里连肉都难得吃上。
She wore it at every important moment of her life, so to me it holds forty years of ordinary courage.
她人生每个重要时刻都戴着它，所以对我来说，它装着四十年平凡的勇气。
When my mother handed it over, she said something I still repeat to myself: 'This is your home. If you ever need help, or change your mind, remember — we're here.'
我妈递给我时说的一句话，我至今常常默念：'这里永远是你的家。什么时候需要帮忙，或者改了主意，记住——我们都在。'
I don't wear it every day — I'm too clumsy — but it flies with me on every trip, like a portable piece of home.
我不敢天天戴——我太毛手毛脚——但每次出远门我都带着它，像随身带的一小块家。
And I've already promised my mother: one day I'll put it in my own daughter's hand and tell her the whole story.
而且我已经答应了我妈：将来有一天，我会把它放进我自己女儿的手心，把整个故事讲给她听。
That way the chain stays unbroken for one more generation.
这样，这条链子就再多传一代。

topics.question: How did you feel before leaving home to live in a new city? Describe your preparations and emotions.
topics.questionZh: 离家去新城市生活之前，你的心情如何？请描述你的准备和感受。
hints: 收拾行李的纠结
should I take all this stuff? what if I need it?
出发前夜的心情
I get butterflies in my stomach
家人各自的表达
a typed list of chores / it's gonna be kind of strange without you
不舍与新开始并存
I'm gonna miss this place / it's also a fresh start
vocab: you've got a big day tomorrow
it's gonna be kind of strange without you
sample: The week before I left home to study in another city, I was a complete mess — excited, terrified and sentimental all at once.
离家去外地读书的前一周，我整个人乱成一团——兴奋、害怕、伤春悲秋，全搅在一起。
People say you get butterflies in your stomach before big moments; I had the whole zoo.
人们说大事临头心里会七上八下；我这儿简直是开了个动物园。
Packing nearly broke my heart.
收拾行李差点把我弄哭。
I kept thinking, maybe I shouldn't take all this stuff — and five minutes later, but what if I need it?
我一会儿想：这么多东西或许不该带——五分钟后又反悔：可万一我用得着呢？
In the end I packed three suitcases, and my brother had to sit on the biggest one so it would close; he found this extremely funny.
最后我塞了三个箱子，最大的那个得让我弟弟坐上去才扣得上，他觉得这画面好笑极了。
On my last evening, my mother handed me a typed list — I'm not joking, typed — of things to be done on a regular basis: take out the garbage, recycle the cans and newspapers, buy the groceries.
最后一个晚上，我妈递给我一张打印的清单——没开玩笑，打印的——上面是平时要做的家务：倒垃圾、回收瓶罐和报纸、买日用品。
The list was really for my father and brother, but giving it to me was her way of saying, you were the one holding this family together.
清单其实是给我爸和我弟的，但把它交到我手上，是她在说：一直以来撑着这个家的人是你。
My brother went quiet that night and finally admitted, 'It's gonna be kind of strange without you.' From him, that was practically a poem.
那晚我弟难得安静，最后憋出一句：'没有你会有点不习惯。'从他嘴里出来，这几乎算一首诗了。
The next morning, my father only said, 'You'd better get some sleep — you've got a big day tomorrow,' as if anyone could sleep.
第二天早上，我爸只说了一句：'你最好再睡会儿——明天可是你的大日子。'好像那晚真睡得着似的。
I'm gonna miss that place every single day, and I still do.
我会天天想念那个家，事实上现在也想。
But leaving it was how I learned to love it properly.
而离开它，恰恰教会了我怎样真正地爱它。

topics.question: Do you think keeping a diary is a good habit? What would you write down, and would you let anyone read it?
topics.questionZh: 你认为写日记是个好习惯吗？你会写下什么？会允许别人看吗？
hints: 写日记的价值
memory fades / writing things down helps you see clearly
都写些什么
write down all the good stuff / I want it all in writing
隐私与分享
a diary is for your eyes only
朋友送日记的趣事
since I gave you the diary, I get to read it — over my dead body!
vocab: write down all the good stuff
I want it all in writing
a little something for good luck
sample: Yes, I think keeping a diary is one of the most underrated habits, and I can say this with confidence because I've kept one, on and off, for ten years.
是的，我觉得写日记是最被低估的习惯之一，这话我说得有底气——因为断断续续地，我已经写了十年。
When a friend gave me a new notebook as a farewell present, her card said: write it all down.
有位朋友送我一本新笔记本当践行礼物，卡片上写着：都写下来吧。
My memory is terrible; without the diary, whole years would simply evaporate.
我记性很差；没有这本日记，整年整年的时光都会直接蒸发。
My friend said, 'I want you to write down all the good stuff.' I asked, 'What about the bad stuff?' and she answered, 'Absolutely — I want it all in writing.'
朋友说：'我要你把美好的事都记下来。'我问：'那糟心的事呢？'她答：'当然也要——我要你把一切都写下来。'
That's exactly what a diary is for: the small triumphs and the embarrassing failures, both of which fade slower on paper than in the head.
日记的用处正在于此：小小的得意和丢脸的糗事，落在纸上的，都比记在脑子里的褪色慢。
Of course, a diary only works if it stays private.
当然，日记只有在私密时才有用。
My friend joked, 'Since I gave you the diary, I get to read it,' and I shot back, 'Over my dead body!' — and we both knew I meant it.
朋友开玩笑：'既然日记是我送的，我可是要读的。'我立刻回她：'想都别想，除非我死了！'——我们俩都知道我是认真的。
Privacy is what lets you be honest on the page; the moment you imagine an audience, you start performing.
隐私正是让你在纸上说真话的东西；一旦想象出一位读者，你就开始表演了。
So yes, I'd recommend the habit to anyone, especially students.
所以，我会向任何人推荐这个习惯，尤其是学生。
You don't need talent — you need ten minutes and a little stubbornness.
不需要天赋——只需要十分钟和一点固执。
Years later, rereading your own handwriting is like getting a letter from a younger, sillier self, and honestly, it's the cheapest therapy there is.
多年后重读自己写的字，就像收到一封来自更年轻、更傻的自己的信——说真的，这是世上最便宜的心理治疗。

topics.question: Describe a long journey you have made by car. Where did you go, and what did you enjoy about it?
topics.questionZh: 描述你的一次长途自驾旅行。你去了哪里？旅途中有哪些你喜欢的部分？
hints: 去哪、和谁、为什么出发
I set off from... / I was heading for... / new sights, new adventures
路上的见闻与风景
the land was flat and empty, but beautiful in a strange way / the music on the radio was so different
途中的实际小事：加油、检查、找住处
I had to fill it up every few hours / can you check the oil?
感受与收获
it gave me a real sense of freedom / I'd do it again in a second
vocab: That's a heck of a drive
在前不着村后不着店的地方
sample: A couple of summers ago, I drove across half the country with two friends, from our hometown all the way to the west.
前年夏天，我和两个朋友开车横穿了半个国家，从老家一路开到西部。
We just wanted new sights and new adventures, so we planned the route ourselves, filled the tank and hit the road.
我们就是想看新风景、找点新体验，于是自己规划了路线，加满油就上路了。
The best part was watching the country change through the window.
最棒的是隔着车窗看大地一点点变换模样。
In the east there were cities and forests, but after two days of driving the land became flat and almost empty.
东部还是城市和森林，可开了两天之后，大地变得平坦而空旷。
Honestly, it was beautiful in a strange way, and the local music on the radio was nothing like the stations back home.
说实话，那是一种奇特的美，收音机里的地方音乐也和家乡的电台完全不同。
Of course, a road trip has its practical side.
当然，自驾游也有很现实的一面。
Our car was a real gas guzzler, so we had to stop and fill it up every few hours, and we learned to check the oil regularly as well.
我们的车是个十足的'油老虎'，每隔几小时就得停下来加油，我们还学会了定期检查机油。
Once we nearly ran out of fuel in the middle of nowhere, which taught us to plan our stops carefully.
有一次我们差点在前不着村后不着店的地方没油了，这让我们学会了仔细规划停靠点。
In the end, the small troubles became the best stories, and the trip gave me a huge sense of freedom.
最后，那些小麻烦反而成了旅途中最有趣的故事，这趟旅行也给了我巨大的自由感。
Travelling by car means you can stop whenever something catches your eye, and that freedom is addictive.
开车旅行意味着随时可以为一处风景停下，这种自由会让人上瘾。
If I get the chance, I'd do it again in a second.
如果有机会，我会毫不犹豫地再来一次。

topics.question: Describe a time when a stranger helped you when you were in trouble. What happened, and how did you feel?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你遇到麻烦时陌生人帮助你的经历。发生了什么？你当时感受如何？
hints: 什么事、什么麻烦
my car broke down in the middle of nowhere / I was stuck with no phone signal
陌生人怎么帮的
he offered to check it out / he went out of his way to help
你最初的犹豫与之后的信任
with all the stories you hear, you have to be careful
结果与感受
I was really touched / I didn't know how to thank him
sample: This happened last autumn, when my car suddenly died on a quiet country road late at night.
这是去年秋天的事，一天深夜我的车在一条僻静的乡间公路上突然熄火了。
I was driving home from a trip when the engine just stopped, and I found myself stuck in the middle of nowhere with no phone signal.
我旅行返程的路上发动机就这么停了，我被困在前不着村后不着店的地方，手机还没有信号。
After about twenty minutes, a car pulled over and a man in his thirties got out.
大约二十分钟后，一辆车停了下来，一个三十多岁的男人下了车。
He could see I had car trouble, so he simply said, 'Don't worry about me. Why don't you pop open the hood, and I'll check it out?'
他看出我的车出了毛病，就很干脆地说：'别担心我。要不你把引擎盖打开，我来帮你检查？'
He spent almost an hour trying to start it up again, and he never asked for anything in return.
他花了将近一个小时试着把车重新发动起来，而且从头到尾没要求任何回报。
To be honest, I was cautious at first.
说实话，我一开始是有戒心的。
With all the stories you hear, you have to be careful, so I kept my distance and stayed close to my car.
毕竟外面听来的那些事儿那么多，你不得不多留个心眼，所以我保持着距离，一直站在自己车旁。
But he was so calm and practical that my worry slowly went away.
但他是那么沉着、实在，我的担心也就慢慢消散了。
When he couldn't fix it, he even drove me to the nearest town so I could find a mechanic.
见他修不好，他还干脆把我送到最近的镇上，好让我找到修车师傅。
In the end, my car was repaired the next morning, and I honestly don't know what I would have done without him.
第二天早上我的车修好了，说真的，没有他我真不知道该怎么办。
That experience changed how I see strangers.
那次经历改变了我看待陌生人的方式。
Most people genuinely want to help when someone's in trouble, and now I always stop for others when I can.
看到别人陷入麻烦时，大多数人是真心想帮的，所以现在只要力所能及，我也会为别人停下来。

topics.question: Describe a time when your travel plans did not work out as expected. What did you do about it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次旅行计划没能按预期进行的经历。你是怎么应对的？
hints: 原计划是什么
I had planned to drive straight through / I expected to find a cheap motel
出了什么岔子
the motel was out of business / everything closes at sundown
你当时的情绪
I felt stuck / now what am I going to do?
怎么应对、学到什么
take it one step at a time / always have a plan B
vocab: Things pretty much close at sundown
太阳一落山店铺基本都关门
You may have to wait until morning
你可能只能等到第二天早上
I guess I don't have much choice
我估计我也没别的选择了
Now what am I gonna do?
sample: This spring I took a driving trip to a national park with a friend, and we had everything planned: leave early, arrive by evening, and spend the night in a cheap motel by the park gate.
今年春天我和朋友自驾去一个国家公园，一切都计划好了：早点出发，傍晚到达，在公园门口一家便宜的汽车旅馆过夜。
It sounded simple, and in the end it was completely wrong.
听起来很简单，结果证明完全不是那么回事。
Reality had other ideas.
现实自有安排。
Heavy rain slowed us down for hours, and when we finally reached the motel, there was a sign on the door: it had gone out of business.
一场大雨拖了我们好几个小时，等终于赶到旅馆时，门上贴着告示：这家店已经停业了。
We drove around the little town looking for another place, but out there things pretty much close at sundown, so there was nothing open and nobody to ask.
我们开着车在小镇上到处找，可在那种地方太阳一落山店铺基本都关了，哪儿都不开门，也找不到人问。
For a moment I just stood in the rain thinking, 'Now what am I gonna do?'
有一会儿我就站在雨里想：'这下我该怎么办？'
My friend stayed calm and said we should take it one step at a time: first petrol, then food, then a bed.
我朋友倒很镇定，说我们一步一步来：先解决油，再解决吃的，最后找住处。
In the end we found a room above a restaurant two towns away, and we laughed about the whole thing over a late dinner.
最后我们在隔了两个镇的镇子上找到一家餐馆楼上的房间，深夜吃晚饭时把这一路狼狈当笑话讲。
That trip taught me that plans are useful, but flexibility matters more.
那趟旅行让我明白，计划有用，但随机应变更重要。
Now, whenever I travel, I book the first night in advance and always have a plan B.
现在只要出门旅行，我都会提前订好第一晚的住处，并且永远准备一个备选方案。
When things go wrong on the road, staying calm is honestly half the solution.
在路上出了岔子时，说实话，保持镇定就已经解决了一半。

topics.question: Do you think it is wise to accept help from strangers? Why or why not?
topics.questionZh: 你认为接受陌生人的帮助是明智的吗？为什么？
hints: 观点：多数情况下可以，但要留心
in most cases yes, but keep your guard up
为什么需要谨慎
with all the stories you hear, you have to be careful
如何判断与自保
trust your gut / stay in public places / keep your valuables with you
善意也真实存在
most people are decent / the kindness of strangers
vocab: with all the stories you hear
外面听来的那些事儿那么多
sample: Generally speaking, yes, I think accepting help from strangers is wise, as long as you keep a clear head at the same time.
总体上说是的，我认为接受陌生人的帮助是明智的，前提是你同时保持清醒的头脑。
Refusing all help would make life, especially travel, almost impossible.
拒绝一切帮助会让生活——尤其是旅行——变得几乎寸步难行。
My reason is simple: most people are decent.
我的理由很简单：大多数人是正派的。
When my car broke down on a trip, a complete stranger spent an hour helping me, and he even said sorry for scaring me when he first walked over.
有一次旅途中我的车抛锚，一个素不相识的人花了一个小时帮我，第一次走近时还为自己的突然出现吓到我而道歉。
Stories like that happen everywhere, every single day.
这样的故事每天都在世界各地上演。
Turning down every kind hand, in my opinion, would be a sad and lonely way to live.
在我看来，拒绝每一只善意的手，会是一种悲哀又孤单的活法。
That said, you can't be naive.
话虽如此，人不能天真。
With all the stories you hear, you have to be careful, especially at night or in isolated places.
外面听来的那些事儿那么多，你不得不多加小心，尤其在深夜或偏僻的地方。
My rule is to use common sense: prefer busy, well-lit spots, keep your valuables with you, and if an offer feels wrong, politely say no.
我的原则是凭常识判断：尽量待在热闹明亮的地方，贵重物品随身带，如果对方的提议感觉不对，就礼貌拒绝。
When a stranger suggested I wait alone by the road while he drove off, that was not a good idea, and I said so.
曾有个陌生人建议我独自留在路边等他开车走开，这可不是好主意，我就照直说了。
So my attitude is balance: trust, but with boundaries.
所以我的态度是平衡：信任，但有分寸。
Say thank you, accept reasonable help, and stay alert at the same time.
该道谢就道谢，该接受的帮助就接受，同时保持警觉。
In my experience, being too suspicious costs you far more than being carefully open.
依我的经验，过度多疑的代价比谨慎地敞开要大得多。

topics.question: Describe a time when you had difficulty finding a place to stay while travelling. What did you do in the end?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次旅行中你很难找到住处的经历。最后你是怎么解决的？
hints: 什么场合、为什么难找
it was late at night / everywhere was fully booked
具体困难
there was only one room left / the next motel was hours away
谁帮了你、怎么解决
a friend gave up his room / someone slept in the car
事后感想
always book the first night ahead / I'll never forget that night
vocab: Do you have any rooms available?
It's not the Ritz, but it'll be fine
虽算不上高级酒店，但也够住了
Do you mind keeping it down?
sample: This happened on a trip a few years ago, when my bus was delayed for hours and I arrived in a small town with a friend well after midnight.
这是几年前旅行时的事，长途车晚点了好几个小时，我和朋友后半夜才抵达一个小镇。
I hadn't booked anything, because my clever plan was to find a cheap guesthouse on arrival.
我什么都没预订，因为我的'聪明'计划就是到了再找家便宜旅馆。
That was a big mistake.
这是个巨大的错误。
The first two places we tried were completely full, and at the third one the owner said there was just one room left.
头两家都客满了，第三家的老板说只剩一个房间。
He assumed we were together, so we had to explain, 'No, we're not a couple, that's why we need two rooms.' But there was only one, and the next town was a ninety-minute drive away.
他以为我们是一对儿，我们只好解释：'不，我们不是情侣，所以才要两个房间。'可只剩一间了，而下一个镇子开车要一个半小时。
What my friend did next really moved me.
朋友接下来的举动让我特别感动。
He simply said, 'You take the room. I've slept in my car before, and I'll sleep in it again.' No matter how I protested, he wouldn't change his mind.
他只说：'你住这间。我以前睡过车里，再睡一次也没什么。'不管我怎么反对，他都不改主意。
In the middle of the night a truck parked next to him with its engine roaring, and he actually had to ask the driver, 'Do you mind keeping it down?'
半夜一辆卡车停在他旁边，发动机轰隆作响，他甚至不得不去问司机：'能不能麻烦小点声？'
The room itself was tiny and basic, but honestly it was fine, and I slept like a log.
房间本身又小又简陋，但说实话够用了，我睡得特别沉。
Since that night I always book my first night in advance, especially in small towns.
从那晚起，我总是提前订好第一晚的住处，尤其是在小镇。
And I learned something about friendship too: real friends don't just share the good times, they take the uncomfortable seat so you can rest.
我也懂得了友情的一课：真朋友不只同享好时光，还会把不舒服的位置留给自己，让你能好好休息。

topics.question: Describe a time when you bargained over the price of something. Did you get a good deal in the end?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你为某样东西讨价还价的经历。最后你谈到好价钱了吗？
hints: 买卖背景
I was selling my old... / I needed the money urgently
对方如何出价、你如何应对
he made a low offer / it's worth much more than that
谈判过程
we went back and forth / that's as high as I can go
结果与心得
we settled on a fair price / know the value before you talk
vocab: It's worth a thousand at least
Five is as high as I can go
五百是我能出的最高价
my good deed for the day
sample: The last time I bargained seriously was when I sold my old laptop to a second-hand shop.
我最近一次认真讨价还价，是把旧笔记本电脑卖给二手店的时候。
I was leaving the city and needed cash quickly, so I didn't have much power in the negotiation, but I still wanted a fair price.
我马上要离开这座城市，急着用钱，谈判里其实没什么底气，但我还是想要个公道价。
The shopkeeper looked it over and made a really low offer, about three hundred.
店主检查了一下，开了一个特别低的价，大概三百。
I knew it was worth a thousand at least, so I refused politely and gave my reasons: it worked perfectly, and even the parts alone were valuable.
我知道它至少值一千，所以我客气地拒绝并摆出理由：机器运转完好，光零件都不止这个价。
He raised it to four hundred, and we went back and forth for a while like two old friends playing cards.
他加到四百，我们又来回拉锯了一会儿，像两个打牌的老朋友。
At one point he shook his head and said, 'Five is as high as I can go,' and I could tell from his face that he meant it.
后来他摇摇头说：'五百是我能出的最高价了。'我看得出来他是认真的。
So I pushed just once more, and we finally settled on five hundred and fifty.
于是我只再争取了一下，最终以五百五成交。
When he agreed, he laughed and said it was his good deed for the day, and I laughed too and said, 'Sold.'
他答应时笑着说，这算他今天做的好事，我也笑了，说了声：'成交。'
Looking back, I learned two things about bargaining.
回头想想，讲价这事我学到两点。
First, know the real value of your things before you start, because the numbers give you confidence.
第一，开口之前先弄清东西的真实价值，数字会给你底气。
Second, stay friendly, because a smile usually gets you a better price than anger.
第二，保持友善，因为一个笑脸往往比发火更能换来好价钱。

topics.question: Describe a person you met by chance who later became a friend. How did you meet?
topics.questionZh: 描述一位你偶然认识、后来成为朋友的人。你们是怎么认识的？
hints: 怎么偶遇
we met on a trip / he helped me out of a difficult situation
第一印象
he seemed easygoing / I liked him immediately
怎么熟起来
we got talking / what a coincidence, we're from the same city
这段友谊的意义
small world / some of the best friends start as strangers
vocab: Thanks for being such a good sport
sample: The person who comes to mind is a guy I met completely by chance on a long-distance bus a few years ago.
我想到的是一个几年前在长途汽车上偶然认识的人。
I was travelling to a new city to start school, feeling nervous and alone, and he happened to have the seat next to mine.
我去一座新城市求学，又紧张又孤单，他恰好坐在我旁边。
We didn't talk at first, but when I mentioned where I was heading, he sat up and said, 'What a coincidence, that's where I live!'
一开始我们都没说话，但当我说起自己的目的地时，他一下子坐直了：'太巧了，我就住那儿！'
We started chatting, and it turned out we liked the same kind of folk music.
我们聊了起来，发现彼此喜欢同一类民谣。
It really is a small world sometimes.
有时候世界真是小。
What made him special was how easygoing he was.
他特别的地方在于为人特别随和。
When my suitcase was heavy, he carried it without being asked, and when my plans got messed up, he just laughed and helped me think of a plan B, never complaining once.
我的箱子沉，他二话不说就帮忙拎；我的计划出了乱子，他也只是笑笑，帮我想备选方案，一句怨言都没有。
Before we said goodbye, he suggested we get together once I settled in, and he actually called a week later to show me around.
分别前他提议等我安顿下来聚一聚，一周后他真的打来电话，带我逛了那座城市。
We've been good friends ever since, and that chance meeting taught me something important.
从那以后我们一直是好朋友，那次偶遇也教会我一件事。
Keep your heart open to strangers, because some of the best people in your life start out as strangers on a bus.
对陌生人敞开心扉，因为你生命里最好的一些人，最初不过是车上偶遇的陌生人。
Years later, he is still the first friend I call when things go wrong.
这么多年过去，遇到麻烦时他仍是我第一个打给的朋友。

topics.question: Talk about your family background. Where does your family come from, and how does that history influence you?
topics.questionZh: 谈谈你的家族背景。你的家族来自哪里？这段历史对你有什么影响？
hints: 家族来自哪里
my grandparents are from... / a small village in the countryside
当年为什么迁移
to have a better life / to get an education / to make a living
家里流传的故事或传统
my grandpa always tells stories about the old days
对你的影响
it reminds me to work hard / I'm proud of my roots
vocab: 我的祖父母来自爱尔兰
sample: My family roots are in the countryside.
我家的根在农村。
My grandparents grew up in a small farming village, and like many families of their generation, they moved to the city when they were young to have a better life.
祖父母在一个小农村长大，和那一代的许多家庭一样，他们年纪轻轻就进城闯荡，只为过上更好的日子。
My grandfather used to say there was no money and no work in the village, so he left with almost nothing and took hard jobs in the city to make a living.
爷爷常说，村里没钱也没活儿干，所以他几乎身无分文地离开，在城里靠干重活谋生。
My grandmother followed him, and they saved for years so their children could get an education.
奶奶随后也跟了过去，两人省吃俭用好多年，就为了让孩子们能读书。
In my family that story is told again and again, almost like a legend.
在我们家，这个故事被反复讲起，几乎成了家族传说。
Because of their sacrifice, each generation has moved one step forward.
因为他们的付出，每代人都往前走了一步。
My parents were the first in the family to go to university, and now I'm studying music, which would have been unimaginable back in the village.
我父母是家里第一代大学生，而我如今在学音乐，这在当年的村子里根本无法想象。
When I chose this major, my mother laughed and said, 'You'll be the first in the whole family,' and everyone laughed with her, but it was proud laughter.
我选这个专业时，妈妈笑着说：'你会是全家第一个。'大家都跟着笑，那是自豪的笑。
This background influences me deeply.
这样的家底深深影响着我。
I never take my opportunities for granted, and I still visit the village every spring festival.
我从不把机会视作理所当然，每年春节还会回村里看看。
Knowing where I come from gives me a kind of anchor, and it pushes me to keep working hard so the family keeps moving forward.
知道自己从哪里来，就像有了锚，推着我不断努力，让这个家继续往前走。

topics.question: Describe a difficult decision your family has made about caring for an elderly relative. How did it turn out?
topics.questionZh: 描述一个你的家庭在照顾年迈亲人方面做出的艰难决定。结果如何？
hints: 面临什么难题
grandpa couldn't live on his own any more / he fell down once at home
有哪些选择、各自难处
a retirement home vs. taking care of him at home
如何决定、家人感受
it was a very difficult decision for all of us / somebody felt guilty
决定之后的生活
he comes home once a week / we visit him regularly
vocab: a retirement home for the elderly
costs a fortune to keep up
Renting out rooms seemed like a good solution
把房间租出去似乎是个好办法
He was always such a strong man
他曾经是那么强壮的一个人
sample: A few years ago, my family faced a really hard decision about my grandpa.
几年前，我们家在爷爷的照料问题上面临一个特别艰难的决定。
Grandma passed away early, and grandpa had managed alone for years, but then his health got worse, and one afternoon he fell down at home and couldn't get up by himself.
奶奶走得早，爷爷独自生活了好些年，可后来身体每况愈下，有一天下午他在家摔倒了，自己根本爬不起来。
My aunt was the one taking care of him, but it became too much: bathing him, dressing him, cooking, plus her own job.
主要是我姑姑在照顾他，但实在撑不住了：给他洗澡、穿衣服、做饭，还有她自己的工作。
We discussed it for months: should he move in with one of us, or should we find him a retirement home?
我们商量了好几个月：是搬到子女家里，还是送他去养老院？
Keeping him at home felt safer emotionally, but nobody could watch him around the clock.
留在家里情感上更踏实，但谁也没法二十四小时守着他。
In the end we chose a good care home near my aunt's house, and it was a very difficult decision for everyone.
最后我们选了姑姑家附近一家不错的养老院，对所有人来说这都是个艰难的决定。
My aunt felt guilty, and honestly the fees were high, so high that she even rented out a spare room at home to help cover them.
姑姑心里很内疚，而且老实说费用不菲，她甚至把家里一间空房租了出去来贴补。
I offered to pay my share from my part-time savings, because I didn't want her to carry everything alone.
我提出用兼职攒的钱分担自己的一份，因为我不想让她一个人扛下所有。
Now grandpa lives there, and every weekend one of us brings him home for dinner.
现在爷爷住在那里，每个周末都有人接他回家吃顿饭。
He was always such a strong man, so it hurts to see him frail, but he's safe, well fed and never lonely.
他曾是那么强壮的一个人，看到他虚弱难免心酸，但他是安全的、吃得好，也不孤单。
That experience taught me that caring for the elderly is about love, but also about honest, practical choices.
那段经历让我明白：照顾老人靠的是爱，但也需要坦诚而务实的抉择。

topics.question: Describe a time when something you were counting on fell through at the last minute. How did you cope?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你满心指望的事情在最后一刻落空的经历。你是怎么应对的？
hints: 你指望什么、用在哪
I was counting on that job / that money to pay for tuition and rent
落空的经过
because of budget cuts / I got the news a few days after arriving
你的第一反应
I couldn't believe it / how am I going to pay for this?
如何应对
look at the alternatives / keep my resume on file / find the next door
vocab: I was counting on that money
You still have your partial scholarship
sample: This happened in my first year of university.
这是我大一时的事。
I had a work-study arrangement, a part-time job on campus, and I was counting on that money to help pay for books, food and rent.
我有一份勤工俭学的安排，也就是校内的兼职，我就指望着那笔钱来付书本费、伙食费和房租。
Everything was settled before the summer, so I thought the money side of college was taken care of.
暑假前一切都敲定了，所以我觉得上大学钱的事已经不用愁了。
