Then, a few days after I arrived, I went to the office to arrange my schedule, and the staff member told me the programme had been cancelled because of budget cuts.
可报到没几天，我去办公室安排日程，工作人员告诉我，因为预算削减，这个项目被取消了。
She was kind about it, but my first reaction was disbelief: what do you mean, there's no job for me?
她态度很好，但我的第一反应是不敢相信：什么叫没有工作给我了？
I even asked her to check my name again, just in case there had been a mistake.
我甚至请她再查一遍我的名字，生怕是搞错了。
After the shock, I forced myself to look at alternatives.
缓过神之后，我逼自己去看还有哪些别的路子。
The office suggested I check the bulletin board in the hallway and keep my resume on file, so I wrote one that same week and printed copies at the computer lab.
办公室建议我去看看走廊里的告示栏，并把简历存档备查，所以当周我就写好了简历，在机房打印了几份。
I also reminded myself that the situation wasn't hopeless, because I still had my partial scholarship, so tuition itself was partly covered.
我也提醒自己情况还没到绝境，因为我还有部分奖学金，学费本身已经覆盖了一部分。
Within two weeks I found a job tutoring a middle-school student, which actually paid better than the campus one.
两周之内我找到了一份给初中生做家教的工作，报酬其实比校内那份还高。
Looking back, I'm almost grateful, because I learned that plans fall through all the time, and the only thing you really control is how fast you find the next door.
回头看，我甚至有点感激，因为我明白了计划随时会泡汤，而真正能掌控的，只有你多快找到下一扇门。

topics.question: Describe your experience of moving to a new city. What was the most difficult part, and how did you adapt?
topics.questionZh: 描述你搬到一座新城市的经历。最难的是什么？你是如何适应的？
hints: 为什么搬、第一印象
I moved for school / the city felt huge and strange
文化冲击与不适应
a certain amount of culture shock / everything was different
谁帮了你
a family friend took me in / my housemates helped me
如何适应过来
give it time / take whatever comes my way
vocab: Here's to the beginning of a new life
Variety is the spice of life
多样化是生活的调味品
sample: I moved to a big city two thousand kilometres from home when I started university, and my first week was a strange mix of excitement and panic.
上大学时，我搬到了一座离家两千公里的大城市，第一周的心情是兴奋与慌乱交织。
The buses, the food, even the way people talked felt completely new to me.
公交、食物，甚至人们说话的方式，对我来说都完全是新的。
There was definitely a certain amount of culture shock.
文化冲击肯定是有的。
Back home, shops closed early and neighbours knew each other; in the city, everything ran late and nobody on the street cared who I was.
在老家，店铺关得早，邻里都认识；在大城市，一切都营业到很晚，街上也没人在乎我是谁。
Simple things became small adventures, like learning which bus to take and asking the driver to tell me where to get off.
连小事都成了小冒险，比如搞清楚坐哪路车，还要请司机到站时提醒我一声。
What saved me was the people.
真正救了我的是人。
A friend of my mother's took me in, and on my first night she cooked dinner and raised her glass: 'Here's to the beginning of a new life.'
妈妈的一位朋友收留了我，第一晚她做了晚饭，举杯说：'为新生活的开始干杯。'
My housemates came from completely different backgrounds, and one of them cooked food so spicy it made me cry.
室友们背景各不相同，其中一位做的菜辣得我直掉眼泪。
Thanks to them I slowly understood that variety really is the spice of life.
多亏了他们，我慢慢懂得：多样化真的是生活的调味品。
It took about one term before the city felt like mine.
大概过了一个学期，这座城市才有了'我的城市'的感觉。
I joined a student club, found my favourite noodle shop, and stopped getting lost.
我加入了社团，找到了最喜欢的面馆，也不再迷路了。
Now when something unexpected happens, I just tell myself to take whatever comes my way, because that move taught me I can adapt to almost anything.
现在遇到意外，我只会告诉自己迎接扑面而来的一切，因为那次搬家让我知道，我几乎能适应任何环境。

topics.question: Do you think sharing a house with other people is a good way to live? What are the challenges?
topics.questionZh: 你认为和别人合租房子是一种好的生活方式吗？有哪些挑战？
hints: 观点与自身经历
I've shared a house for two years / the advantages outweigh the troubles
好处
we each pay our share of the rent / you're never lonely
挑战与磨合
the rent's due on the same day / noise and shared space
相处之道
simple house rules / small gestures matter
vocab: I'll give it to you tonight
sample: Yes, overall I think sharing a house works really well, and I say that after two years of living with housemates from very different backgrounds.
总的来说，我认为合租是很不错的生活方式，这是我跟背景各异的室友同住两年后的结论。
One is a nursing student, one is a business student from abroad, and somehow we make it work.
一个是护理专业的学生，一个是留学的外国学生，我们居然处得很好。
The biggest advantage is practical: when the rent's due, we each pay our share, so everyone saves a lot compared with living alone.
最大的好处很实际：房租到期时各付各的，比一个人住省下不少钱。
But it's more than money.
但不只是钱的事。
In our house, we wait for the bathroom in the mornings with our coffee, shout 'It's all yours!' when we finish, and complain about deadlines together.
在我们家，大家早上端着咖啡等卫生间，用完就喊一声'归你了'，还会一起吐槽赶不完的作业。
It feels like a small, slightly messy family.
感觉就像一个小小的、有点乱糟糟的家庭。
Of course there are challenges.
当然也有挑战。
Money is the sensitive one: someone always pays late, and the person collecting has to remind them without sounding like a debt collector.
钱是最敏感的：总有人晚交，收钱的人得提醒又不能显得像讨债的。
Shared space is the other: dishes pile up, and one person's mess quickly becomes everyone's argument.
公共区域是另一大难题：碗越堆越多，一个人的邋遢很快就变成所有人的争吵。
Early on, we had a few uncomfortable weeks until we set some simple rules.
一开始我们过了几周别扭日子，直到定下几条简单的规矩。
What really made it work was small gestures.
真正让合租变好的是些小细节。
One housemate handed me a big mug and said, 'Consider it yours,' and somehow that little thing made me feel at home.
有位室友递给我一个大杯子说：'就当是你自己的。'不知怎的，这个小举动让我有了家的感觉。
So my advice is: talk about money early, respect the shared space, and be generous with the small stuff.
所以我的建议是：钱的事早说清，公共区域多尊重，小事上大方一点。

topics.question: When you are far away from home, how do you keep in touch with your family? Describe a phone call that was special to you.
topics.questionZh: 当你远离家乡时，你是如何与家人保持联系的？描述一通对你特别的电话。
hints: 平时怎么联系
we video-call once a week / short messages and photos every day
为什么重要
they worry about me / hearing a voice still matters
一次特别的电话
I called after a hard day / I said everything's fine
报喜不报忧的矛盾
you hide your troubles so they won't worry / but you need them too
vocab: I'll talk to you real soon
sample: I study far from home, so my family and I keep in touch mostly through video calls: a long one every Sunday, plus short messages and photos in between.
我在离家很远的地方上学，和家人主要靠视频通话联系：每周日一次长聊，平时发发消息和照片。
The photos are mostly of food and my cat, which sounds silly, but they keep us close.
照片多半是吃的和我的猫，听着傻，却让我们觉得亲近。
One call I'll never forget happened on a terrible day.
有一通电话我永远不会忘记，那天我倒霉透顶。
My job arrangement at school had just fallen through and everything seemed to be going wrong, but when my little brother called that night, I put on a bright voice.
学校那份工作的安排刚落空，什么事都不顺，可那晚弟弟打来电话时，我还是装出轻快的声音。
He asked what had happened, and I just said, 'Don't ask.'
他问我怎么了，我只说：'别提了。'
Then, because my dad was already asleep, I quickly added, 'Don't wake him, just tell him everything's OK.'
接着因为爸爸已经睡了，我赶紧补了句：'别吵醒他，就告诉他一切都好。'
We talked about silly things instead, and before hanging up my brother said, 'I'll talk to you real soon.'
我们转而聊了些有的没的，挂电话前弟弟说：'我很快再打给你。'
Somehow that ordinary sentence comforted me more than any advice could.
不知怎么的，这句平常话比任何建议都更能安慰我。
I realised these calls aren't really about exchanging information; they're how we hold each other together across the distance.
我意识到这些电话其实不是为了交换信息，而是我们隔着距离彼此支撑的方式。
People say my generation only sends messages, but I believe hearing a voice still matters.
人们说我们这代人只发消息，但我认为听见声音依然重要。
When I tell my parents, 'It'll be just fine,' I'm not only calming them down, I'm calming myself down too.
当我对父母说'一切都会好起来的'，我不只是在安抚他们，也是在安抚我自己。
That hour on the phone every Sunday is honestly the highlight of my week.
每周日那一小时的通话，说真话是我一周里最期待的时刻。

topics.question: Describe a day when everything seemed to go wrong. What happened in the end?
topics.questionZh: 描述一天里诸事不顺的经历。最后怎么样了？
hints: 一天如何开始
it started badly and only got worse
接二连三的倒霉事
I was late / no luck with the interviews / the phone call got cut off
情绪与低谷
Don't ask / I can't believe this
转机与结尾
a friend cheered me up / an unexpected phone call
sample: I remember one day last term when I honestly wanted to climb back into bed and start over.
我记得上学期有一天，我真想钻回被窝里重新开始。
It began with my alarm failing, so I ran to class with wet hair and arrived in the middle of a quiz.
一早就闹钟没响，我顶着一头湿发狂奔去教室，到的时候正赶上随堂小测。
At noon I rushed to a job interview across the city, but the bus got stuck in traffic and I arrived fifteen minutes late.
中午我赶去城另一头参加面试，结果公交堵在路上，迟到了十五分钟。
The manager was polite but clearly unimpressed.
经理很客气，但显然没被打动。
After that I used a payphone to ask about another job advertisement, but the call ate all my coins and cut off mid-sentence.
之后我用投币电话询问另一个招聘广告，结果电话吞光了我的硬币，话说到一半就断了。
When I finally got through, the position was already gone, and I just stood there thinking, I can't believe this.
等我终于打通，职位已经招满了，我站在那儿心想：真是难以置信。
By evening I was in a terrible mood, and when my housemate asked, 'How was your day?', I only said, 'Don't ask.'
到了晚上我心情糟透了，室友问我'今天怎么样'，我只回了句：'别提了。'
She looked at me and said, 'Was it that bad?' and somehow that simple question made me laugh and tell her everything.
她看着我问道：'有那么糟吗？'不知怎的，这个简单的问题让我笑出了声，把一切都倒给了她。
Her only advice was, 'OK, so today was a disaster. What are you gonna do about it tomorrow?'
她唯一的建议是：'行，今天是灾难。那明天你打算怎么办？'
What saved the day was something small: she made me noodles and we watched a silly film together.
拯救这一天的是件小事：她给我煮了面，我们一起看了部傻乎乎的电影。
Nothing had actually been fixed, but I felt human again.
其实什么问题都没解决，但我找回了自己。
The next morning I sent out three more applications, and one of them turned into an offer, so now, when a day collapses, I just tell myself: survive today, fix tomorrow.
第二天早上我又投了三份申请，其中一份拿到了机会。所以现在每当一天崩掉，我就告诉自己：先熬过今天，明天再修。

topics.question: Describe a job interview you have had. How did it go, and what did you learn from it?
topics.questionZh: 描述你经历过的一次求职面试。进行得如何？你从中学到了什么？
hints: 面试背景
I applied for a part-time job as a receptionist / I saw the ad in the paper
被问到什么
tell me about yourself / your responsibilities in your last job
表现如何、哪里失手
I could learn very fast / my skills didn't match what they needed
学到什么
read the job description carefully / match your strengths to their needs
vocab: I'm calling about the ad in the paper
我打电话是想问问报纸上的招聘
Thank you anyway for coming in
不管怎样，谢谢你跑一趟
sample: Last summer I applied for a part-time receptionist job that I had seen in an advertisement, and I still remember the interview clearly, because it was a complete lesson in what not to do.
去年夏天，我应聘了一份在招聘广告上看到的兼职前台工作，那场面试我至今记得清清楚楚，因为它完整地教会了我什么不该做。
The start actually went well.
开场其实很顺利。
I described my previous experience: I had supervised a small team, looked after the day-to-day operations and handled quality control.
我介绍了自己的过往经历：带过一个小团队，负责日常运作和质量控制。
The manager nodded along, and I started to feel confident, maybe too confident.
经理不停点头，我开始觉得有把握了，也许是太有把握了。
Then she asked about data entry and office software, and my heart sank.
接着她问到数据录入和办公软件，我的心一下子沉了下去。
My experience was with machines, not documents, and to be honest I didn't type that well.
我的经验在机器上，不在文书上，而且说实话我打字并不利索。
I said, 'I could learn very fast,' and I meant it, but she had already decided.
我说：'我学东西很快。'我是认真的，可她已经做出决定了。
A minute later came the polite ending: 'We're interviewing a lot of people... thank you anyway for coming in.'
一分钟后就是那句客气的收场：'我们还在面试不少人……不管怎样，谢谢你跑一趟。'
On the bus home I wrote down exactly what went wrong: I hadn't read the job description carefully, so I had presented the wrong skills.
回家的公交上，我逐条写下问题所在：我没有仔细读职位描述，展示的技能根本不对口。
The next application I sent was for a teaching-assistant job that matched me perfectly, and I got it.
我投的下一份申请是一份完全对口的助教工作，而且拿到了。
That failed interview taught me more than any successful one: first find out what they actually need, then show them exactly that.
那次失败的面试比任何成功面试都让我受益：先弄清对方要什么，再精准地展示那一点。

topics.question: Describe a time when you were treated disrespectfully and spoke up for yourself. What did you do?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你受到不尊重对待并为自己发声的经历。你是怎么做的？
hints: 什么场合
at a job interview / in the workplace
对方做了什么、你的感受
it crossed the line / I felt angry and uncomfortable
你如何回应
I said forget it / I walked out
事后与反思
tell someone you trust / don't stay silent
vocab: don't you feel like just slapping them
你难道不想扇他们一巴掌吗
and then I lost my job
sample: This isn't a happy story, but it's an important one.
这不是个愉快的故事，但很重要。

A few years ago, at a job interview, the manager kept asking personal questions that had nothing to do with the position, and then he said plainly that he wanted 'an attractive woman' to work with him.
几年前的一场面试上，经理不停问与职位毫无关系的私人问题，后来更是直说想要'一位有魅力的女性'和他共事。
For a second I froze.
有那么一秒我整个人僵住了。
Then he touched my arm, and that crossed every line.
接着他碰了我的手臂，这彻底越过了所有界限。
I stood up, said 'I say forget it,' took my resume off his desk and walked out.
我站起身，说'我的回答是：算了吧'，从他桌上拿回简历，走了出去。
My hands were shaking in the elevator, but I also felt strangely proud of myself.
在电梯里我的手一直在抖，但心里却有种说不出的自豪。
That evening I told my housemate everything, and I'll never forget her reaction.
当晚我把一切都告诉了室友，她的反应我一辈子都忘不了。
Instead of questioning me, she said, 'That's harassment, and it happened to me too.'
她没有质疑我，而是说：'这就是骚扰，这种事我也遇到过。'
She had slapped her manager after he touched her, and then she lost her job, and hearing that made me both angry and sad.
她被上司动手动脚后扇了对方一巴掌，然后丢了工作。听到这些，我又愤怒又难过。
We talked until midnight about how common this is and how silent everyone stays.
我们聊到半夜，聊这种事有多普遍，而大家又有多沉默。
The next day I reported the interview to my school's careers office so they could warn other students.
第二天我把这次面试反映给学校就业办，让他们提醒其他同学。
If I've learned anything, it's this: your dignity is worth more than any job, and speaking up, even just to one friend, is the first step.
如果说这次教会了我什么，那就是：你的尊严比任何工作都值钱，而开口——哪怕只是告诉一个朋友——就是第一步。

topics.question: Describe a time when a friend insisted on inviting you out when you didn't feel like going. How did it turn out?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次朋友在你本不想出门时执意邀请你的经历。结果如何？
hints: 背景：你那天的状态
I'd had a difficult day / I wasn't in the mood at all
朋友如何坚持
I won't take no for an answer
你如何犹豫、最终答应
I still had so much to do / finally I gave in
结果如何
it completely changed my mood / I'm glad I went
vocab: I won't take no for an answer
Let me show you the city
sample: This happened in my first month in a new city, on a day when my plan for a part-time job had just collapsed and I was sitting in my room feeling sorry for myself.
这是我到新城市的第一个月，那天兼职的安排刚落空，我一个人坐在屋里自怜自艾。
In the evening, out of nowhere, an old classmate who lived in the same city phoned me.
傍晚，一位住在同城的老同学突然打来电话。
He asked what I was doing that night, and I said, 'Nothing special.'
他问我今晚有什么安排，我说：'没什么特别的。'
He announced he was coming to pick me up in an hour to show me the city, and when I started making excuses, he just laughed and said, 'I won't take no for an answer.'
他宣布一小时后来接我，带我看看这座城市。我开始找借口推脱，他只是笑着说：'我不接受拒绝。'
Honestly, I nearly stayed home.
说真的，我差点就没去。
But at eight he was standing at the door, and my housemate grinned at me and said, 'Ooh, I see you have a date!'
可八点时他已经站在门口，室友冲我坏笑：'哟，你这是有约会啊！'
That made us both laugh, and somehow my bad mood started to dissolve.
这话把我们俩都逗笑了，不知怎的，坏心情开始消散。
He drove me along the river, showed me the lit-up bridges, and bought me a late dinner.
他开车带我看江边亮灯的大桥，还请我吃了顿夜宵。
He didn't lecture me about being positive; he simply refused to leave me alone with my worries.
他没有跟我大讲要乐观，只是不肯把我一个人丢在坏情绪里。
By the end of the night I was planning my next steps with new energy, and I understood something: sometimes the kindest thing a friend can do is not to ask, just to insist.
那晚结束时我已经满血复活地盘算下一步了。我由此明白：有时朋友最贴心的举动，不是询问，而是坚持。

topics.question: If a friend visited your city for the first time, where would you take them and why?
topics.questionZh: 如果朋友第一次来你的城市，你会带他们去哪里？为什么？
hints: 你的推荐路线
I'd start with the old town by the river
一个对你有个人意义的地方
this is one of my favorite places / I go there as often as I can
特色体验：食物、夜景
the best food in the city / a night view of the bridges
为什么喜欢当向导
to see your city through new eyes / sharing is half the fun
vocab: show you a bit of San Francisco
This is one of my favorite places
这是我最喜欢的地方之一
I've never seen anything like this before
我从来没见过这样的地方
给你的下一份旧金山惊喜
sample: If a friend visited my city for the first time, I'd start in the old town by the river, because that's where the whole story of the city began.
如果朋友第一次来我的城市，我会先带他们去河边的老城，因为这座城市的故事就是从那里开始的。
We'd walk slowly, and I'd point out the small details that tourists usually miss.
我们会慢慢走，我负责指出那些游客通常会错过的小细节。
Everyone needs a plan for that first day, and mine has never failed.
谁都需要一份'第一天'的方案，而我这套从没失手过。
In the afternoon I'd take them to my favourite place, a hilltop park above the harbour.
下午我会带他们去我最喜欢的地方：港口上方的山顶公园。
I go there as often as I can, especially at sunset, when the light hits the water and the towers turn gold.
我一有空就去，尤其是日落时分，光线洒在水面上，高楼被染成金色。
Every guest I've brought there has said the same thing: 'I've never seen anything like this before.'
每个被我带去的朋友都会说同一句话：'我从来没见过这样的地方。'
Then, of course, food.
接下来自然是吃的。
I'd pick a small family restaurant serving local dishes, the kind of place with plastic stools and a queue outside, because the queue tells the truth.
我会选一家做本地菜的家庭小馆，就是那种摆着塑料凳、门口排长队的店，因为队是不会骗人的。
My city is famous for its noodles and grilled fish, and I'd order a little of everything so my friend could try it all.
我们这座城市以面条和烤鱼闻名，我会每样点一点，让朋友都尝到。
Finally, a night boat trip to see the bridges lit up.
最后，坐一趟夜游船看亮灯的大桥。
Showing someone my city is a bit selfish too: through their eyes, the streets I walk every day become fresh and exciting again.
带人逛我的城市也有一点私心：透过他们的眼睛，我每天走过的街道又变得新鲜而动人。
That, honestly, is the real pleasure of being a tour guide.
说实话，这才是当向导真正的乐趣。

topics.question: Describe a song that has special meaning to you. Why is it important?
topics.questionZh: 描述一首对你有特殊意义的歌。它为什么重要？
hints: 什么歌、谁唱给你听
a lullaby my mother used to sing / a slow, simple melody
与什么记忆相连
I used to sing it to my little brother / hard nights at home
什么时候会想起它
when I feel homesick / at quiet moments
它对你的意义
it connects three generations / more than music
vocab: I used to sing it to my brother
我以前常唱给我弟弟听
What a great place to record a song
sample: The song that means the most to me isn't a pop hit; it's an old lullaby my mother used to sing when I was small, a slow, simple melody about stars and moonlight.
对我最有意义的歌不是什么流行金曲，而是小时候母亲常唱的一首摇篮曲，一段关于星星和月亮的缓慢简单的旋律。
Here's the special part: my mother didn't learn it from a record.
特别之处在于：这首歌不是母亲从唱片里学来的。
My grandmother sang it to her, and later my mother sang it to my little brother, and I learned it just by listening.
外婆唱给母亲听，后来母亲唱给弟弟听，而我只是听着听着就会了。
When I sing it now, I'm carrying three generations in one melody.
如今我唱起它，一段旋律里装着三代人。
Friends sometimes ask, 'Did you write that song?' and I smile and explain that it belongs to my family.
朋友有时问：'这歌是你写的吗？'我笑着解释，它属于我们全家。
The song connects to hard memories too.
这首歌也连着一段艰难的记忆。
My mother passed away when we were young, so I helped take care of my brother, and on nights when he couldn't sleep, I used to sing it to him in the dark.
母亲在我们年幼时就去世了，我帮着照顾弟弟，在他睡不着的夜晚，我就在黑暗中唱这首歌给他听。
It calmed him down, and honestly, it calmed me even more.
歌声能让他安静下来，说实话，更能让我自己平静。
These days I sing it when I feel homesick.
如今想家的时候我就会哼起它。
Once I sang it in an empty hall with wonderful acoustics, and the echo floated everywhere.
有一次我在一座空旷、音响效果极好的大厅里唱了它，回声四处飘荡。
I remember thinking, what a great place to record a song, and maybe someday I will.
我记得当时想：真是个录歌的好地方，也许有一天我真的会录。
A song like this isn't just music; it's a person, a place and a promise you can carry in your pocket.
这样的歌不只是音乐，它是一个人、一段时光，是一个能装进口袋的约定。

topics.question: Describe a family business you know. What makes it special?
topics.questionZh: 描述一家你了解的家族生意。它的特别之处在哪里？
hints: 是什么生意、开多久了
a small family restaurant / it's been on that corner for twenty years
谁在经营、家人分工
the parents built a good reputation / the eldest son runs it now
面临的挑战
the parents are retiring / the hours are brutally long
它特别在哪
regulars are like friends / it holds the whole family together
vocab: My wife and I are retiring
sample: The family business I know best is a small restaurant near my aunt's flat.
我最熟悉的一家家族生意，是我姑姑住处附近的一家小餐馆。
The couple who own it came from the south of the country, and they've served their regional food on that same corner for over twenty years.
老板夫妇来自南方，二十多年来一直在那个街角做他们的家乡菜。
My aunt has eaten there nearly every Sunday for as long as I can remember.
从我记事起，姑姑几乎每个周日都在那儿吃饭。
It's a real family operation.
那是一场真正的全家总动员。
The father cooks, the mother chats with every table and recites what the specials are tonight like poetry, and their eldest son now runs the business alongside them.
父亲掌勺，母亲挨桌寒暄，把今晚特色菜念得像诗一样，大儿子如今也在旁边打理生意。
Neighbours call him the dutiful son, because he gave up his own plans to keep the family kitchen alive.
邻居们都叫他'孝顺的儿子'，因为他放弃了自己的打算，就为守住这家家庭厨房。
They worked extremely hard to build a good reputation: fresh food, fair prices, and they remember every regular's favourite dish.
他们极其努力才树立起好口碑：食材新鲜、价格公道，还记得每位老顾客爱点的菜。
But the business has its weight.
但这门生意也有它的分量。
The hours are brutally long, the son rarely sees his own kids before bedtime, and now that the parents are retiring, the whole family is quietly discussing who will carry it on.
工时长得吓人，儿子很少能在孩子睡前到家；如今父母要退休了，全家人正悄悄商量谁来接棒。
What makes it special to me is that it's more than commerce.
它之于我的特别，在于它不只是生意。
That restaurant paid for two children's education, and it's where the whole neighbourhood gathers.
那家店供出了两个孩子的学业，也是整条街坊聚脚的地方。
When I eat there, I'm not just a customer; I'm part of a small, warm story that's still being written.
在那里吃饭时，我不只是顾客，还是一个仍在续写的小小暖心故事的一部分。

topics.question: Do you think it is stressful to live in a place where natural disasters, such as earthquakes, can happen? How do people cope?
topics.questionZh: 你认为生活在可能发生地震等自然灾害的地方压力大吗？人们是如何应对的？
hints: 观点：压力确实存在
it must be a little nerve-racking
大多数时间无感、偶有紧张
most of the time you don't even think about it / the next little tremor comes along
人们如何应对
buildings are designed to withstand earthquakes / regular safety drills
你的态度
preparedness beats panic / life has to go on
vocab: It must be a little nerve-racking
the next little tremor comes along
you think it's the big one
sample: I lived for three years in a coastal city famous for its earthquakes, so I can answer this from experience: yes, there is stress, but it's quieter than people imagine.
我在一座以地震闻名的海滨城市住过三年，所以可以凭亲身经历回答：压力确实有，但比人们想象的安静。
My friends back home used to ask me the same question, worried that I was living on top of a time bomb.
家乡的朋友也总这样问我，担心我是住在一颗定时炸弹上。
Most of the time, you don't even think about it.
大多数时候，你根本想不起来这回事。
You know the new towers are engineered to withstand earthquakes, schools run regular drills, and almost everyone keeps a small emergency kit at home.
你知道新高楼都做了抗震设计，学校定期演习，几乎家家都备着急救包。
The danger becomes background noise, a bit like rain.
危险成了背景噪音，有点像下雨。
But then the next little tremor comes along: a lamp sways, a window hums, and for two seconds your heart stops, because you think it's the big one.
可下一次小震动一来：灯一晃，窗一响，有那么两秒你的心脏会停跳，因为你会以为大地震来了。
I remember a friend joking at exactly such a moment, 'Relax, I promise no earthquakes tonight,' and we all laughed, half nervous, half relieved.
我记得朋友正是在那样的一刻开玩笑：'放松，我保证今晚没有地震。'我们都笑了，一半紧张，一半释然。
People cope through preparation and humour, honestly.
说真的，人们靠准备和幽默感来应对。
Fear shrinks when you know exactly what to do: stay away from windows, keep shoes by the bed, agree on a family meeting point.
当你清楚该做什么时，恐惧就会缩小：远离窗户，床边放双鞋，和家人约好集合点。
Living with risk is the price of that beautiful city, and most people there decide it's worth paying.
与风险共存是住在那座美丽城市的代价，而那里的大多数人都觉得这代价值得。
Preparation, not panic, is the answer, and once you're prepared, the fear slowly turns into respect.
答案是有备无患而不是恐慌，而一旦准备妥当，恐惧会慢慢变成敬畏。

topics.question: Describe a course or subject you have studied that you found very difficult. How did you deal with it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一门你觉得非常难的课程或科目。你是怎么应付的？
hints: 什么课、为什么难
the hardest course I've ever taken / totally new concepts
第一反应
it's a killer / I'll have to do a lot of reading first
你的应对方法
form a study group / go over the assignment together
结果与收获
I got through it / difficult courses teach you how to learn
vocab: the hardest course I've ever taken
我这辈子上过最难的一门课
Maybe we can help each other
也许我们可以互相帮忙
sample: The most difficult course I've ever taken was a theory class in my first term.
我上过最难的课是第一学期的一门理论课。
The teacher was brilliant, but he spoke like an encyclopedia, and after the first lecture the student next to me whispered, 'This is the hardest course I've ever taken.'
老师水平很高，但讲起课来像一本百科全书。第一堂课结束后，旁边的同学小声说：'这是我这辈子上过最难的一门课。'
I could only nod.
我只能点头。
For the first two weeks I panicked.
头两周我是慌的。
It's a killer, everybody said so; the reading list alone looked like a phone book.
这课真要命，人人都这么说，光阅读书目就厚得像电话簿。
I understood maybe half of each lecture and copied the rest down blindly.
每堂课我大概只听懂一半，剩下的照抄不误。
What saved me was other people.
救我的是身边的人。
A classmate suggested, 'How about we go over the assignment together? Maybe we can help each other.'
一位同学提议：'我们要不要把作业一起过一遍？也许可以互相帮忙。'
So four of us met in the student lounge twice a week: one person explained the concepts, another checked the details, and slowly the fog lifted.
于是我们四个人每周在学生活动室碰头两次：一个人讲概念，一个人抠细节，迷雾渐渐散了。
When you say a difficult idea out loud, you suddenly discover which parts you don't really understand.
把难懂的内容大声讲出来，你会立刻发现自己哪里其实没懂。
I ended that course with a much better grade than I expected, but the real gain was the method.
结课成绩比我预期好得多，但真正的收获是方法。
Now, whenever a subject feels impossible, I find two things early: a study group, and time to do the reading before the assignment, not after.
现在无论哪门课感觉啃不动，我都会尽早做两件事：找到学习小组，以及在写作业之前、而不是之后完成阅读。
Difficulty, it turns out, is often just loneliness in disguise.
原来，'难'常常只是'孤军奋战'的伪装。

topics.question: Describe a part-time job you have done that involved working with children. What was it like?
topics.questionZh: 描述一份你做过的、需要和孩子打交道的兼职。那是什么感受？
hints: 什么工作、怎么得到
an after-school program / someone recommended me for the job
实际做了什么
sports, music, arts and crafts / I took over softball practice
挑战与乐趣
kids ask endless questions / every day is different
收获
patience and quick thinking / it doesn't pay much but it's rewarding
vocab: This job doesn't pay a lot
keep your eye on the ball
sample: For about a year I worked at an after-school programme near my campus, looking after children in the afternoons with games, music and a bit of homework help.
大概有一年时间，我在学校附近的一个课后班兼职，下午带孩子做游戏、玩音乐，辅导一点作业。
A friend whose son attended there recommended me for the job, so I skipped the usual application queue.
是一位孩子在那儿上课的朋友推荐了我，所以我没走正常排队的申请流程。
The interview was refreshingly direct.
那场面试直接得让人耳目一新。
The director looked at my resume for ten seconds and asked, 'Why should I hire you?'
主管看了十秒简历就问：'我为什么要录用你？'
I said I love working with children, I had taught guitar to kids before, and I used to play on a softball team.
我说我喜欢和孩子相处，以前教过孩子弹吉他，还打过垒球。
She said, 'Great, you can take over softball practice today,' so I was hired and tested in the same hour.
她说：'太好了，你今天就能接手垒球训练。'于是录用和试用发生在同一个小时里。
The work itself was chaotic and wonderful.
这份工作本身既混乱又美好。
I taught ten-year-olds to keep their eye on the ball, dried tears over lost games, and answered the question 'Why is the sky blue?' about forty times.
我教十岁的孩子眼睛盯住球，为输球的孩子擦眼泪，还要回答大约四十遍'天为什么是蓝的'。
The job doesn't pay a lot, and part-timers got no benefits, not even paid holidays, but no office job ever made me laugh that much.
薪水不高，兼职没有任何福利，连带薪假期都没有，可没有任何坐办公室的工作让我笑得那么开心。
That year taught me patience and quick thinking, because children sense immediately when you're only pretending to listen.
那一年教会我耐心和随机应变，因为孩子能瞬间察觉你是不是在假装听。
It also confirmed something about me: I'm genuinely good with people, small ones included.
它也让我确认了一件事：我确实擅长和人打交道，包括最小号的人。
I'd recommend that every student tries one term of it.
我推荐每个大学生都去尝试一学期。

topics.question: Do you think money should be the most important consideration when making career decisions? Why or why not?
topics.questionZh: 你认为在做职业选择时，钱应该是最重要的考量吗？为什么？
hints: 观点：重要但不该是唯一标准
money matters, but it's not everything
身边的例子
he refused a big offer / there's more to life than money
什么更值得权衡
family, meaning, health, time
现实的平衡
we all have bills to pay / it's about enough, not more
vocab: There's more to life than money
sample: My answer is no: money should be one consideration, but never the most important one, and I've watched this question play out in my own family.
我的回答是否定的：钱是要考虑的一项，但永远不该是最重要的一项，而且我亲眼见过这个问题在我家上演。
My uncle runs a small restaurant that my grandparents opened almost thirty years ago.
我叔叔经营着一家小餐馆，那是我祖父母将近三十年前开的。
Last year investors offered him serious money to buy the place, and everyone expected him to sell.
去年有投资人开出货真价实的一大笔钱想收购这家店，所有人都以为他会卖。
He simply refused: 'It's not for sale. It would break Papa's heart.'
他只是拒绝：'这里不卖。那会伤透爸爸的心。'
His brother argued with him, saying, think of the money, and he answered, 'There's more to life than money.'
他哥哥跟他争执，说想想那些钱吧，他回答：'生活里不只有钱。'
Of course the practical side is real.
当然，现实的一面是真实存在的。
My uncle works long hours, and with the business and his young son, he often can't do both, and both would suffer if he tried.
叔叔工时很长，在店和孩子之间，他常常没法两头都顾上，硬要兼顾只会两头受损。
That's the honest cost of his choice, and I don't want to pretend it doesn't exist.
这是他选择的真实代价，我不想假装它不存在。
But when I see him teaching his son to cook in that kitchen, I understand what he is protecting, something a bank balance can't measure.
可当我看到他在那间厨房教儿子做菜时，我明白他在守护什么——那是银行余额衡量不了的东西。
So my view is balance with a bottom line.
所以我的观点是：有底线的平衡。
Earn enough to live with dignity, and after that, choose work for meaning, for people and for time.
赚到足以体面生活的钱，之后就要为了意义、为了人、为了时间来选择工作。
Money can buy the table, but it can't buy the family sitting around it.
钱买得起那张餐桌，却买不来围坐桌旁的一家人。

topics.question: When you were a child, what job did you dream of doing? Do you think children today have different dreams?
topics.questionZh: 你小时候梦想做什么工作？你认为现在的孩子梦想不一样了吗？
hints: 你儿时的梦想
I wanted to be a singer / I could never decide between two things
为什么着迷
it looked exciting / I admired someone in my family
梦想如何变化
as I grew up, reality taught me... / I found a middle path
今天孩子的梦想与你的看法
kids today want to be vloggers or rock stars / never laugh at a child's dream
vocab: We want to be rock stars
sample: When I was about ten, my best friend and I were practically glued together, and we had a running argument about the future: he wanted to be a professional baseball player, and I wanted to be a singer.
我十岁左右时，和最好的朋友几乎形影不离，我们总为一个问题争个不停：他想当职业棒球运动员，我想当歌手。
We can't decide, we used to say to adults, maybe we'll do both.
我们常对大人说：我们拿不定主意，也许两个都干。
I was obsessed with music because of my cousin, who played guitar at every family gathering.
我迷上音乐是受表哥影响，每次家庭聚会他都弹吉他。
To me, standing on even a small stage looked like the most magical thing in the world, and I practised songs with a hairbrush as a microphone.
在我看来，哪怕是站上小舞台也是世上最神奇的事，我常拿着发刷当麦克风练歌。
Of course the dream changed shape as I grew up.
当然，长大后梦想变了形状。
I learned that very few people make a living on stage, and I discovered that I also loved teaching.
我明白靠舞台吃饭的人凤毛麟角，也发现自己同样热爱教学。
In the end I found a middle path: I study music and teach children part-time, so the ten-year-old me isn't entirely disappointed.
最终我找到了一条中间路线：学音乐，同时兼职教孩子，所以十岁的我也没有完全失望。
Children today dream differently.
如今孩子的梦想不一样了。
When I ask my students what they want to be, half of them say vloggers or rock stars, and they laugh, 'That's a tough choice.'
我问学生想做什么，一半人说想当视频博主或摇滚明星，还笑着说：'这个选择真难。'
I never tell them their dreams are unrealistic, because the dream itself isn't the point.
我从不告诉他们梦想不现实，因为梦想本身并不是重点。
It's the practising, the trying and the growing that slowly turn a child into someone.
真正让孩子慢慢成人的，是练习、尝试和成长的过程。

topics.question: Describe your first job or a part-time job you have done. What did you do, and what did you learn from it?
topics.questionZh: 描述你的第一份工作或做过的一份兼职。你做了什么？从中学到了什么？
hints: 什么工作、怎么得到的
a friend told me about the opening / I went for the interview that same week
入职细节：表格、证件、录用瞬间
fill out a pile of forms / bring in identification / 'You're hired!'
工作日常与辛苦之处
the children arrived at three o'clock sharp / there wasn't a single quiet minute
收获与感悟
keep up the good work / a first job isn't just about the pay
sample: Well, my first proper job was working at an after-school program for kids here in the city.
呃，我第一份正式的工作，是在本市的一个课后活动中心带小孩。
A friend of mine told me about the opening, and honestly I needed the money, so I went for the interview that same week.
一个朋友告诉我那儿有空缺，说实话我也缺钱，所以同一周我就去面试了。
The interview was quite informal, but before I could start, I had to fill out a pile of forms and bring in identification, to prove I could work legally.
面试挺随意的，但要上岗之前，我得填一沓表格，还要带证件去，证明我可以合法打工。
When the manager finally looked at me and said, 'You're hired. Welcome aboard', I nearly jumped out of my chair.
当经理最后看着我说'你被录用了，欢迎加入'的时候，我差点从椅子上跳起来。
The job itself was busier than I expected.
这份工作本身比我预想的要忙得多。
The children arrived at three o'clock sharp, and between homework, games and sports, there wasn't a single quiet minute.
孩子们三点整准时到，写作业、做游戏、打球轮着来，一分钟安静的时候都没有。
Some days I got home and fell asleep within ten minutes, but my manager kept telling me to keep up the good work, and that really kept me going.
有几天我到家十分钟内就睡着了，但经理总让我继续保持，这话真的让我干劲十足。
Once I turned a spelling game into a race so even the quietest boy wanted to join in, and he still talks about it.
有一次我把拼词游戏改成了比赛，连最腼腆的男孩都抢着参加，他到现在还念叨这事。
Looking back, that job taught me three things: being punctual, staying patient, and planning ahead.
现在回头看，那份工作教会了我三件事：守时、耐心、提前做计划。
A first job isn't just about the pay — it's about learning how to show up and be reliable.
第一份工作不只是为了挣钱，而是学会怎么到位、怎么让人放心。
That confidence has stayed with me ever since.
这份自信一直留在我身上到现在。

topics.question: Describe a time when you helped someone with their studies. Who did you help, and how did it go?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你帮别人复习功课的经历。你帮了谁？过程如何？
hints: 背景：谁、什么考试
he had a big test the next day / his parents were both working late
怎么帮：一个个过单词
I offered to help him study / we went through the word list one by one
小细节与小波折
he got it wrong at first, then corrected himself / 'Nice going!'
结果与感悟
he got a perfect score / it's about showing them they can do it
vocab: You just need a little practice
sample: Last term I helped my neighbour's son with his spelling.
上学期我帮邻居家的小男孩复习拼写。
He's eight, and he had a big test the next morning, but his parents were both stuck at work, so he was waiting alone near our building.
他八岁，第二天早上有场大考，可他爸妈都被工作拖住了，他只能一个人在我们楼附近等着。
I had a pile of my own homework that night, but half an hour wouldn't kill me, so I offered to help him study while he waited for his dad.
那晚我自己也有一堆作业，但半小时而已，死不了人，所以我就提出在他等爸爸的时候帮他复习。
We went through his word list one by one: I said the word, he spelled it out.
我们把单词表一个一个过：我念单词，他拼出来。
'Island' was easy, he said. But he started 'medicine' wrong — 'M-E-D-E' — then stopped, corrected himself, and got it right.
他说'island'简单，但'medicine'一开头拼错了，念到M-E-D-E停住，自己改了过来，拼对了。
I told him, 'Nice going!', and he grinned like he'd won a prize.
我跟他说'干得漂亮'，他咧嘴一笑，像拿了大奖似的。
The sweet part came after. He asked me why I was carrying books, and I explained that adults go to school too and have tests.
更暖的是后面。他问我怎么也抱着书，我解释说大人也要上学、也要考试。
He found it hilarious that a grown-up also complained about homework, and somehow that made us a team.
他觉得很搞笑，大人居然也抱怨作业，就这么着，我们成了一队的。
A few days later he rang our doorbell just to announce that he'd got everything right.
几天后他来按我家门铃，就为了宣布他全拼对了。
Honestly, it cost me thirty minutes, but I felt proud for a whole week.
说真的，我只花了三十分钟，却骄傲了整整一个星期。
Helping someone study isn't mainly about explaining knowledge; it's about sitting next to a nervous person and showing them, word by word, that they can do it.
帮人复习其实主要不是讲解知识，而是坐在一个紧张的人身边，一个词一个词地让他看到：你能行。

topics.question: Describe a sport you are good at, or used to be good at. How did you learn it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一项你擅长或曾经擅长的运动。你是怎么学会的？
hints: 什么运动、水平如何
I can catch, throw and hit better than most people
谁教的、怎么练
he'd coach me in the park for hours / keep your eye on the ball
高光时刻
I made a catch that won the game / the kids gave me a nickname
这项运动对你的意义
it travels from one generation to the next
vocab: keep your eye on the ball
sample: The sport I'm best at is softball.
我最拿手的运动是垒球。
I'm nowhere near professional, but I can catch, throw and hit better than most people I know, and I genuinely love the game.
离专业水平差得远，但接球、传球、击球都比身边大多数人强，而且我是真心喜欢这项运动。
I learned it from my father.
这是我爸教我的。
When I was small, he'd coach me in the park for hours: batting, catching, throwing.
我小时候，他会在公园里一练就是几个小时：挥棒、接球、传球。
His one rule was simple — keep your eye on the ball — and he repeated it maybe fifty times a session.
他只有一条规矩，特简单——眼睛盯住球——一次训练能念叨五十遍。
If I missed a catch, he'd just say, 'You just need a little practice. Wanna try again?' He never once shouted at me.
我要是接丢了球，他只会说'你只是需要多练练，再试一次？'他从来没冲我喊过。
He also taught me to get my body behind the glove, so the ball wouldn't get past me.
他还教我把身体移到手套后面去，这样球就不会从我身边漏过去。
All that practice paid off at school.
这些苦练在学校里见了成效。
In one match I made a catch in the last minute that won us the game, and after that the other kids gave me a nickname from a famous baseball poem.
有一场比赛最后一分钟我接杀对方，帮全队赢了球，之后伙伴们就用一首著名棒球诗里的名字给我起了外号。
It was silly, but I was proud for a whole year.
挺傻的，可我骄傲了整整一年。
These days I sometimes help coach younger children, and funny enough, my father's words come out of my own mouth.
现在我偶尔帮着带带小孩子，好笑的是，我爸那些话从我嘴里原样冒了出来。
That's what I love about sport: it travels from one person to the next, like a language spoken with the hands.
这就是我爱体育运动的地方：它会从一个人传给下一个人，就像一门用手说的语言。

topics.question: Describe a special invitation you have received. What was it for, and how did you feel about it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你收到的特别邀请。是去做什么？你当时感觉如何？
hints: 邀请是什么、怎么收到
flowers arrived with a card: 'Save Saturday for me!'
活动内容与你的担心
a gallery opening / I didn't have anything dressy
现场体验
stand around, look at the art, schmooze a little / good people-watching
为什么难忘
seeing my friend's work on the wall / it was worth it
sample: A few months ago, I received an invitation I still remember clearly.
几个月前，我收到一份至今记得清清楚楚的邀请。
A friend of mine who's serious about photography had flowers sent to my workplace, with a card that said, 'Save Saturday for me! Something big is happening.'
一个玩摄影玩得很认真的朋友，把花送到了我单位，卡片上写着：'把周六留给我！有件大事要发生。'
It turned out he wanted to take me to a gallery opening where some of his photos were exhibited.
原来他想带我去一个画廊开幕式，他的一些照片在那里展出。
I'd never been to anything like that, so I had no idea what to expect.
我从没参加过这种场合，完全不知道会是什么样。
I even worried about what to wear, because I didn't have anything dressy, but he laughed and said I'd be pleasantly surprised.
我连穿什么都发愁，因为我没有一件像样的正装，他笑了，说我会又惊又喜的。
The evening itself was wonderful.
那天晚上本身就很棒。
People stood around looking at the art, drinking wine, eating tiny sandwiches, and schmoozing.
大家站着看画、喝点酒、吃小块三明治、互相寒暄。
There was even good people-watching — honestly, observing the elegant and the strange guests is half the fun of such evenings.
看人也很有意思——说真的，观察那些又优雅又古怪的来客，是这种夜晚一半的乐趣。
What made it truly special was seeing my friend's work on the wall with a small crowd gathering in front of it.
真正特别的是看到我朋友的作品挂在墙上，还有一小群人聚在前面看。
I felt genuinely proud of him.
我打心底为他骄傲。
He picked me up at four and had me home by eight, because I was swamped with homework.
他四点来接我，八点前送我到家，因为我功课多得应付不过来。
I still had to stay up late that night, but honestly, it was worth it.
那晚我还是熬了夜，但说真的，值了。
It's still the nicest invitation anyone has ever sent me.
那至今都是别人发给我的最好的一次邀请。

topics.question: Describe an exhibition or a work of art that impressed you. Why did it impress you?
topics.questionZh: 描述一个给你留下深刻印象的展览或艺术作品。它为什么让你印象深刻？
hints: 什么展览、和谁去的
a friend invited me to the opening night / photographs by local artists
总体印象
some of the photographs were quite striking
最打动你的一件作品
one portrait was drawing quite a crowd / the title was 'Dream Catcher'
感受与后续
I had to pull an all-nighter, but it was worth it
vocab: You were the star of the evening
sample: The exhibition that impressed me most was a small photography show by local artists.
给我印象最深的展览，是一场本地艺术家的小型摄影展。
A friend invited me to the opening night, and to be honest, I didn't expect much — I'm not really an art person.
一个朋友邀请我去看开幕夜，说实话我没抱什么期待——我不算懂艺术的人。
But the moment I walked in, I had to admit some of the photographs were quite striking.
可一走进去我就得承认，有些照片真的相当震撼。
They were black-and-white pictures of ordinary people: a fisherman, an old couple, a boy with a baseball glove.
都是拍普通人的黑白照片：一个渔夫、一对老夫妇、一个抱着棒球手套的男孩。
One portrait was drawing quite a crowd, so I went over to see what the fuss was about.
有张人像围了一大群人，我也凑过去看热闹。
It showed a young woman looking into the distance, full of adventure, full of fire, and the title was 'Dream Catcher'.
照片上是个望向远方的年轻女子，满是冒险劲儿、满是一团火，标题叫《捕梦网》。
I stood in front of it for a long time; the picture seemed to tell a whole life story.
我在它面前站了很久，这张照片好像讲完了一整段人生。
At the opening, people mostly schmoozed and drank wine, but that one photo made the whole evening for me.
开幕式上大家主要是寒暄喝酒，但那一张照片就值回了整个晚上。
My friend said I was the star of the evening for asking the artist so many questions.
朋友说我不停地问摄影家问题，都快成当晚的明星了。
I got home really late and had to pull an all-nighter to finish my homework, but it was worth it.
我回家已经很晚，作业只能熬通宵赶完，但这很值得。
Since then I've paid more attention to photography — you don't need to understand art deeply; one picture that speaks to you is enough.
从那以后我更留意摄影了——不必多懂艺术，有一张照片对你开口说话，就够了。

topics.question: Describe a gift you have received that meant a lot to you. Who gave it to you, and why was it special?
topics.questionZh: 描述一件对你意义重大的礼物。是谁送的？它为什么特别？
hints: 什么礼物、谁送的
a dream catcher / a close friend handed me a small box
送礼的场合与用意
'Go ahead, open it.' / I was going through a stressful time
礼物背后的心意
it just lets the good dreams through / he'd clearly thought about me
为什么难忘
the best gifts are never about price
vocab: It just lets the good dreams through
I won't have any more bad dreams
sample: The gift I want to talk about is a dream catcher — you know, that handmade hoop with threads and feathers, which is believed to catch your bad dreams.
我想说的是一个捕梦网——就是那种带线和羽毛的手工圆环，据说能拦住噩梦。
It was from a close friend, at a time when I was under a lot of pressure and often woke up at night.
那是一段关系很好的朋友送的，当时我压力很大，夜里常常惊醒。
One evening after a party, he handed me a small box and said, 'Go ahead, open it.'
一天晚会结束后，他递给我一个小盒子，说：'来，打开看看。'
Inside was the dream catcher he had chosen specially for me.
里面正是他特意为我挑的捕梦网。
He said, 'It just lets the good dreams through.'
他说：'它只放好梦进来。'
I laughed, but I was really touched, and I told him, 'That's very kind of you.'
我笑了，但心里真的很暖，跟他说：'你真是太好了。'
It wasn't expensive at all, yet he had clearly thought about what I was going through — he even remembered a story I'd told him months before.
它一点都不贵，但他显然认真想过我的处境——连我几个月前随口讲过的事他都记得。
I joked that I won't have any more bad dreams now, and I hung it by my window that same night.
我开玩笑说这下再也不会做噩梦了，当晚就把它挂在了窗边。
Funny thing is, my sleep really did get better.
有意思的是，我的睡眠真的好了起来。
Of course it's not magic — it's more like knowing that someone cares about you, and that feeling protects you.
当然这不是魔法——更像是知道有人在乎你，这种感觉本身就在保护你。
I've kept it for years. To me, the best gifts are never about price; they just say, 'I see you, and I want you to sleep well.'
我留了它好多年。对我来说，最好的礼物从来不在贵贱，它只在说：'我看见你，我想让你睡个好觉。'

topics.question: Do you think it is a good idea for a family to sell a long-running family business? Why or why not?
topics.questionZh: 你认为卖掉经营多年的家族生意是个好主意吗？为什么？
hints: 背景：什么生意、什么诱因
the restaurant has been in the family for thirty years / investors offered a lot of money
赞成卖的理由
sell and take the money / retire without worrying about money / a chance of a lifetime
反对卖的理由
it's not only our business; it's our home / I like good hard work
你的立场与结论
a family business is more than an asset / the whole family has to feel right about it
sample: This question reminds me of a real debate in my own family a while ago.
这个问题让我想起前阵子我们家的一场真实争论。
My uncle runs a small restaurant that has been in the family for about thirty years, and out of nowhere, some investors offered a lot of money for it.
我叔叔经营一家小餐馆，已经传了三十年，忽然有投资人出了一大笔钱想买下它。
The family split into two camps immediately.
家里立刻分成了两派。
My cousin argued, 'Sell and take the money. Don't you want to retire without worrying about money?'
我堂哥主张：'卖了拿钱。你们不想退休以后不为钱发愁吗？'
He kept saying this was a chance of a lifetime, and that if the family hesitated, the investors would walk away — but if they sold, everyone would be on easy street.
他反复说这是千载难逢的机会，家里人一犹豫投资人就走了；可要是卖了，人人都能过上安逸日子。
My uncle disagreed, and to me his reason was simple and honest.
我叔叔不同意，在我看来他的理由简单又实在。
'This restaurant is not only our business; it's our home,' he said. 'I like hard work, good hard work.'
他说：'这间餐馆不只是生意，它是我们的家。我喜欢干活，踏踏实实地干活。'
He wasn't being stubborn — he just valued the life inside those walls more than the number on the cheque.
他不是固执，他只是更看重那四面墙里的生活，而不是支票上的数字。
Honestly, both sides had a point.
说实在的，两边都有道理。
Money can be earned again, but a place full of memories cannot be rebuilt somewhere else.
钱可以再挣，但装满回忆的地方没法在别处重建。
In the end, they didn't sell, and although life isn't luxurious, nobody regrets it.
最后没卖，日子虽不奢华，也没人后悔。
So my view is that a family business is more than an asset; selling it shouldn't be just a financial decision — the whole family has to feel right about it.
所以我的看法是：家族生意不只是一笔资产，卖不卖不能只算经济账——得全家人心里都过得去才行。

topics.question: Describe a time when you had to explain something difficult to a child. What did you say, and how did it go?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你不得不向孩子解释难题的经历。你说了什么？效果如何？
hints: 孩子问了什么
'Why did Mom and Dad get divorced?' / he asked me straight out
你怎么解释
sometimes two adults change / it's not the child's fault
孩子的反应与后续提问
are you going to get married again? / 'Only if I meet the right person'
你的感悟
don't lie to children to protect them / tell the truth gently
vocab: Only if I meet the right person
只有遇到合适的人才会
I wish you could come, too
sample: I remember when my little cousin asked me why his parents got divorced.
我记得小表弟问我他爸妈为什么离婚的那次。
It was a difficult moment, because he was only seven, and it wasn't even my story to tell.
那真是不好应付的一刻：他才七岁，而且这本来也轮不到我来讲。
He asked me straight out, 'Why can't Mom and Dad live together anymore?'
他直截了当地问：'为什么妈妈和爸爸不能再住在一起了？'
I took a breath and explained as simply as I could: sometimes two adults change, and they can't be together anymore — but it is never the child's fault, and both of them love him just the same.
我吸了口气，尽量简单地解释：有时候两个大人变了，没法再在一起了——但这绝不是孩子的错，而且两个人都一样爱他。
Then he asked if his dad would get married again.
接着他问爸爸会不会再结婚。
I said, 'Only if he meets the right person. But right now, it's just you and him, and that's OK too.'
我说：'只有遇到合适的人才会吧。不过现在就是你和爸爸两个人，这样也挺好。'
He nodded, and a minute later he was asking about dinner — kids are stronger than we think, as long as you're honest with them.
他点点头，一分钟后就开始问晚饭吃什么——只要你对孩子诚实，他们比我们想的坚强得多。
I also realised that he'd been asking the grown-ups the same question for a long time, and everyone kept avoiding it.
我还意识到，这问题他已经问过大人们很久了，只是一直没人正面回答。
Once, when he heard I was going out with his dad, he even said, 'I wish you could come, too' — children feel the silences much more than we imagine.
有一次他听说我要跟他爸爸出门，还说'真希望你也一起来'——孩子对沉默的感知，远比我们想象的敏锐。
So when a child asks something hard, I believe the best thing is to tell the truth gently, and then make sure they know they are loved.
所以当孩子问起难堪的事，我认为最好的办法是温和地说实话，然后让他确信自己是被爱着的。
That certainty is what they're really asking for.
那份确定感，才是他们真正想问的答案。

topics.question: Describe an outdoor activity or picnic you have taken part in with a group of people. What did you do?
topics.questionZh: 描述你参加过的一次集体户外活动或野餐。你们做了些什么？
hints: 活动背景
a picnic for the after-school program / about thirty kids and their parents
好玩的环节
the three-legged race / 'On your marks... get set... GO!'
有趣的小插曲
one boy ate five hot dogs / 'You're gonna get sick!'
累并快乐着
I'm beat, but in a good way / kids don't need expensive entertainment
vocab: On your marks, get set, GO
sample: Last summer I helped organise a picnic for the children at our community after-school program.
去年夏天，我帮着给社区课后活动班的孩子们组织了一次野餐。
It was a big day — about thirty kids, their parents, hot dogs, games, the lot.
那可是个大日子——三十来个孩子，加上家长，热狗、游戏，全套都有。
The funniest part was the three-legged race, where two kids tie their legs together and hobble towards the finish line.
最搞笑的环节是二人三足：两个孩子把腿绑在一起，跌跌撞撞往终点挪。
I was the one shouting, 'On your marks... get set... GO!', and then trying not to laugh as everyone fell over each other in the grass.
我负责喊'各就位——预备——跑！'，然后强忍着笑看大家在草地上摔作一团。
When a pair finally made it over the line, the whole field screamed for their double high five.
等有一组终于冲过线，全场都在为他们的双击掌欢呼。
There were small dramas too.
也有不少小插曲。
One boy ate about five hot dogs, and when I warned him, 'You're gonna get sick! Save some for the other kids!', he just asked for a cheeseburger.
有个男孩一口气吃了五个热狗，我警告他'你会吃坏的！给别的孩子留点！'，他倒好，又要了个芝士汉堡。
Kids will be kids.
孩子就是孩子。
By the end of the afternoon I was completely soaked in sunshine and exhausted — I'm beat, as the kids say, but in a good way.
到了傍晚，我整个人晒得发烫、累得不行——用孩子们的话说，我累瘫了，但瘫得舒坦。
Watching them cheer for each other, even the ones who lost every race, was genuinely heart-warming.
看他们互相打气，连场场垫底的也一起欢呼，真的特别暖心。
That day taught me that children don't need expensive entertainment.
那天让我明白，孩子根本不需要昂贵的娱乐。
A field, some simple games and a bit of encouragement are enough to make a memory they'll talk about for weeks.
一片草地、几个简单的游戏，再加一点鼓励，就够他们念叨好几个星期了。

topics.question: Describe a time when you saw someone being treated unfairly. What did you do about it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你目睹有人受到不公平对待的经历。你做了什么？
hints: 看到了什么
some boys called a Chinese boy racist names / others stood around and laughed
你当时怎么做
I told them to leave him alone / I'd call the police if I saw them again
对围观者的态度
'You should be ashamed of yourselves'
事后的思考
prejudice is everywhere / face it together
sample: I remember one incident very clearly, and it still makes me uncomfortable.
有件事我记得清清楚楚，现在想起来还是不舒服。
At a community picnic, a group of older boys started calling a Chinese-American boy racist names.
在一次社区野餐上，一群大孩子开始用一个美籍华人男孩的族裔骂侮辱性的绰号。
They told him to go back to where he came from — even though he was born in this country, just like them.
他们让他'滚回自己来的地方'——可他明明和她们一样出生在这个国家。
What shocked me even more was that some other children stood around and laughed.
更让我震惊的是，另一些孩子围观着哄笑。
They didn't start it, but their laughter made it worse.
事情不是他们挑起的，可他们的笑声让事情更糟。
I went over immediately, told the boys to leave him alone and get out of the area, and warned them I'd call the police if I saw them again.
我立刻走过去，让那些男孩别碰他、离开这块地方，并警告再让我看见就报警。
Then I turned to the kids who had laughed and said, 'You should be ashamed of yourselves. How would you feel if people laughed at you?'
然后我转向那些哄笑的孩子说：'你们应该为自己害臊。要是别人这么笑你，你什么感受？'
Later, I blamed myself a little, because I had been supposed to keep an eye on them and it all happened so fast.
事后我也有点自责，因为我本该盯着他们的，可一切发生得太快。
But the deeper lesson is this: prejudice is everywhere, and pretending it isn't there doesn't protect children — it only teaches them to look away.
但更深的一课是：偏见无处不在，假装看不见并不能保护孩子，只会教他们把头扭开。
The only thing that works is to face it together.
唯一管用的办法，是大家一起面对它。
I'm just glad that boy had a friend who stood in front of him — that small act of courage mattered more than anything the adults said afterwards.
幸好那孩子有个朋友挡在他身前——这一下小小的勇敢，比大人们事后说的任何话都管用。

topics.question: Do you think it is right to fight back with violence when you see your friend being bullied? What would you do instead?
topics.questionZh: 看到朋友被欺负时用暴力还击对吗？换作是你，你会怎么做？
hints: 亮明观点：理解但不赞成
that's a natural reaction, but violence isn't right
身边例子：孩子挥拳
he punched one of them right in the nose
更好的做法
fight back with words, not with violence / get an adult
深层原因
nobody taught those boys right from wrong
vocab: I tried to make them stop
fight back with words, not with violence
sample: I'd say no — violence is understandable, but it's not right, and it usually makes things worse.
我的回答是不——暴力可以理解，但不对，而且通常把事情弄得更糟。
I saw this with my own eyes at a community event.
我就在一次社区活动上亲眼见过。
When some older boys bullied his best friend, a nine-year-old I know told them to stop, they pushed him, and he punched one of them right in the nose.
一群大孩子欺负好朋友的时候，我认识的一个九岁男孩让他们住手，被推了一把，他一拳打中了其中一个的鼻子。
His heart was in the right place — as people say, that's a natural reaction when someone hurts your friend.
他出发点没错——就像大家说的，朋友被欺负时这是很自然的反应。
But afterwards, he was the one who nearly got punished, and the fight didn't change those boys at all.
可事后差点挨罚的反而是他，而且那一架丝毫没有让那帮孩子改变。
As one teacher told him, you should fight back with words, not with violence — because nobody had ever taught those boys right from wrong, and a punch doesn't teach them either.
就像一位老师对他说的：应该用言语而不是暴力还击——那帮孩子根本没人教过是非对错，一拳同样教不会他们。
If I saw my friend being bullied, I would first stand beside them and speak up loudly, because bullies hate attention.
要是我看见朋友被欺负，我会先站到他身边，大声说出来，因为欺负人的人最怕引人注目。
Then I'd get an adult — a teacher, a parent, anyone with authority.
然后去找大人——老师、家长，任何有权威的人都行。
It feels less heroic, but it actually protects your friend.
听起来没那么英雄，但这样才能真正保护朋友。
Of course, I'm not saying you should just stand and watch.
当然，我不是说就该站在边上看。
Standing up for someone is important; the question is choosing a way that doesn't blow back on your friend.
为朋友出头很重要，关键是选一种不会反伤到朋友的方式。

topics.question: Do you think parents should ask their children for their opinion before making big decisions, such as where to live? Why?
topics.questionZh: 你认为父母在做重大决定（比如住在哪里）之前应该征求孩子的意见吗？为什么？
hints: 亮明观点：要听，但别让孩子拍板
listen to the children, but don't put the final choice on their shoulders
例子：离异后去留之争
the parents might go back to court / the child still doesn't know anything
隐瞒的伤害
kids always sense that something is wrong / silence makes them imagine the worst
更好的做法
explain in simple words / let the adults weigh the child's feelings
vocab: We were just kids when we got married
I can't imagine you without Alex
我无法想象你身边没有阿里克斯
sample: I believe parents should at least listen to their children before making big decisions like moving to another city — though they shouldn't put the final choice on the child's shoulders.
我认为父母在做搬家这类重大决定前，至少要听听孩子的意见——但别把最终拍板的担子压到孩子肩上。
I saw a sad example of this recently.
最近我就见到一个让人难受的例子。
A boy's parents got divorced — they admitted they were just kids when they got married — and now his mother planned to move to another city and take him along, while his father wanted him to stay.
一个男孩的父母离了婚——他们自己也承认结婚时还太年轻——现在妈妈打算搬去外地并带走他，爸爸却想让他留下。
I told the father, 'I can't imagine you without Alex,' and he said quietly, 'I can't either. We're trying to work things out, but it's not gonna be easy.'
我跟那位父亲说：'我无法想象你身边没有阿里克斯。'他轻声说：'我也没法想。我们在想办法解决，但这不会容易。'
The worst part was that for weeks nobody had told the boy anything — 'He doesn't know yet,' his father said — while everyone around him was tense and whispering.
最糟的是，好几个星期没人跟孩子说半个字——他爸爸说'他还不知道'——可他身边的大人个个紧张兮兮、交头接耳。
Kids always sense that something is wrong, and silence just makes them imagine the worst.
孩子总能察觉出不对劲，沉默只会让他们往最坏处想。
In my view, the fair approach is honesty without burden: explain the situation in simple words, ask how he feels, and let the adults weigh his feelings in the decision.
依我看，公平的做法是'坦诚但不加压'：用简单的话讲清情况，问问他的感受，再由大人把他的感受掂量进决定里。
A child's opinion may not decide where the family lives, but being heard is what tells him he still matters to both parents.
孩子的意见未必能决定这个家搬去哪里，但'有人听我说'这件事，会让他知道：在爸妈心里，我依然重要。

topics.question: Describe someone you know who moved to a new country and had to learn a new language. How did they manage?
topics.questionZh: 描述一个你认识的、搬到新国家后必须学新语言的人。他们是怎么应对的？
hints: 她是谁、初到的困难
she moved here from China / she could hardly say a word of English
她怎么学
still working on her English every day / watches the local news, practises small talk
她的目标
she wants to apply for citizenship
她给你印象最深的一点
she's learning fast / it's less about talent, more about refusing to stay silent
sample: The person who comes to mind is the mother of a boy I taught at an after-school program.
我想到的，是我在课后活动班教过的一个孩子的妈妈。
She moved here from China a couple of years ago with her husband and their little boy.
几年前她跟着丈夫带着小儿子从中国来到这里。
At first she could hardly say a word of English.
一开始，她一句英语都说不出口。
Shopping, parents' meetings, doctor's visits — everything depended on her husband or her son translating for her, and you could see how frustrating that was.
买东西、开家长会、看医生，全得靠丈夫或儿子当翻译，那种憋屈，看都看得出来。
But she never gave up.
但她从没放弃。

She's still working on her English every single day: she watches the local news, she practises small talk with the neighbours, and she even attends citizenship classes, because she wants to apply for citizenship.
到今天她还在天天练英语：看本地新闻、跟邻居练寒暄，甚至还上入籍辅导班，因为她想申请入籍。
And honestly, she's learning fast.
而且说实话，她学得很快。
The first time she greeted me in English and made a little joke — 'My pleasure', she said, with a perfect smile — I was so happy for her.
她第一次用英语跟我打招呼还开了个小玩笑——'我的荣幸'，她笑着说——我真是替她高兴。
Her son told me proudly that his mum studies at night after he goes to bed.
她儿子特别骄傲地告诉我，妈妈都是等他睡了以后夜里学。
That's real determination, especially for an adult with a family and no spare time.
这才叫真正的决心，尤其对一个拖家带口、一点空闲都没有的大人来说。
By the way, her boy is the most good-natured child in the class, always sharing his snacks.
顺便说一句，她家孩子是班里性情最好的孩子，老把自己的零食分给别人。
Watching this family, I understood that learning a language is less about talent and more about refusing to stay silent.
看着这一家人我明白了：学语言拼的不是天分，而是不肯一直沉默的那口气。

topics.question: Describe a lesson or classroom discussion you remember well. What was it about, and why was it memorable?
topics.questionZh: 描述一堂你记忆深刻的课或课堂讨论。它讲的是什么？为什么难忘？
hints: 什么课、为什么开这堂课
a police officer came to talk to us after a bullying incident
课上学到的概念
a hate crime is a crime motivated by bias
印象最深的互动
'That's a natural reaction, but we don't treat violence with violence'
这堂课对你的影响
words can be a real weapon / you can't pretend you don't know
sample: The most memorable lesson I ever had wasn't a normal class.
我上过的最难忘的一堂课，不是普通的课。
After an unpleasant incident at our school — some boys had bullied a Chinese classmate — our teacher invited a police officer to talk to us about it.
学校出了事——几个男孩欺负了一个华裔同学——之后，老师请来一位警察跟我们谈这件事。
The officer explained that what those boys did wasn't just 'mean': it was a hate crime, a crime motivated by bias against someone's race or background.
警官解释说，那些男孩的行为不只是'缺德'，而是仇恨犯罪——出于对某人种族或出身偏见的犯罪。
I remember the whole room went silent when she said that someone could actually go to jail for that.
我记得她说有人真会因此坐牢时，全班一下子安静了。
We were only ten or eleven, and most of us had never thought of name-calling as a crime.
我们那时才十岁十一岁，多数人从没想过骂人绰号也算犯罪。
Then one boy admitted he had punched one of the bullies.
接着有个男孩承认自己打了其中一个动手的人。
The officer said, 'That's a natural reaction, but we don't treat violence with violence.'
警官说：'那是很自然的反应，但我们不能以暴制暴。'
Those words stayed with me ever since.
这句话从那以后一直留在我心里。
What I appreciated was that nobody was simply scolded.
我很感激的是，没有人被简单训斥一顿。
The officer asked us questions instead: did any of you laugh? Do you like it when someone laughs at you? The teacher added that it happened at our picnic, so it became our problem too.
警官反而问我们：你们有人笑了吗？别人笑你的时候你好受吗？老师还补了一句：事情发生在我们的野餐会上，也就成了我们大家的问题。
Suddenly everyone understood the hurt from the inside.
一下子，每个人都从心里明白了那种伤害。
That lesson changed how I see teasing: words can be a real weapon.
那堂课改变了我对'开玩笑'的看法：语言可以是真的武器。
And once you know that, you can't pretend you don't.
而一旦你知道了这一点，就再也没法装不知道。

topics.question: Do you think handwritten letters and cards still matter in the age of text messages? Why or why not?
topics.questionZh: 在短信时代，你认为手写的信和卡片仍然重要吗？为什么？
hints: 观点：依然重要
a card you can hold in your hands / texts disappear
卡片背后的故事
we decided to write some letters and draw some pictures for a classmate who left
卡片上写了什么
'I hope you can forgive me' / 'We are a team'
为什么打动人
let him know how we feel / handwriting takes time and effort
vocab: write some letters, draw some pictures
let him know how we feel
I hope you can forgive me
你的卡片做得怎么样了
sample: I absolutely believe handwritten cards still matter — sometimes more than a hundred text messages.
我百分百相信手写卡片依然重要——有时候比一百条短信都重要。
When I was at school, a classmate left after he was bullied, and our teacher suggested we write some letters and draw some pictures to let him know how we felt about what happened.
我上学的时候，有个同学被欺负后退了学，老师建议我们写写信、画画画，让他知道我们对这件事的感受。
So we spent a whole afternoon making cards, and everyone kept walking around asking each other, 'How's your card coming along?'
于是我们花了一下午做卡片，大家转来转去互相问：'你的卡片做得怎么样了？'
The cards were simple, but they were honest.
卡片很朴素，但都很真心。
One girl wrote, 'To Vincent, you are my friend.'
一个女孩写：'给文森特，你是我的朋友。'

A boy who had laughed at the incident wrote, 'I hope you can forgive me' — and when the teacher asked him why he had laughed, he could only say that he'd thought it was funny, but you could see he didn't think so anymore.
一个当时跟着笑的男孩写：'我希望你能原谅我。'老师问他当时为什么笑，他只说以为那很好玩，可看得出他早就不这么想了。
My best friend and I drew two baseball players, because the three of us were a team.
我最好的朋友画了两个棒球手，因为我们仨是一个队。
Later we heard that the boy read every single card at home.
后来听说，那孩子把每一张卡片都读了。
His mother said he slept with them next to his bed.
他妈妈说，他睡觉都把卡片放在床头。
A text would have been read and forgotten; a card you can hold in your hands.
短信看完就忘了，卡片却能捧在手里。
That's the difference, I think.
我想，区别就在这儿。
Handwriting takes time and effort, and people can feel that effort.
手写要花时间花心思，而这份心思，收的人感受得到。
In the age of instant messages, that's exactly why a small card means so much.
在这个即时通讯的年代，一张小小的卡片之所以珍贵，恰恰因为这个。

topics.question: What do you think is the best way to respond to people who are different from us?
topics.questionZh: 你认为面对与我们不同的人，最好的回应方式是什么？
hints: 观点：用好奇心代替恐惧
being interested instead of afraid
课堂上的趣味瞬间
'You look exactly like him!' / 'You two are identical twins, aren't you?'
老师的关键一问
what if we all looked the same? It would be boring
落到自己身上
ask questions instead of staring / difference makes a community interesting
vocab: 长得一模一样的双胞胎
sample: In my opinion, the best response to difference is simple curiosity — being interested instead of afraid.
在我看来，面对差异最好的回应就是简单的好奇——有兴趣，而不是害怕。
I learned this in a school workshop about prejudice.
这是一堂关于偏见的课上，我学到的东西。
The teacher was making the point that some boys had attacked a classmate simply because he was different from them.
老师想说明：有的孩子攻击同学，仅仅因为对方跟自己不一样。
Then she joked, 'But guess what? We're all different — look, you look exactly like him!', pointing at two confused kids in the front row.
接着她开玩笑说：'可你们猜怎么着？我们每个人都不一样——瞧，你长得跟他一模一样！'边说边指着前排两个一脸茫然的孩子。
Everyone laughed, and then she went on, 'Oh no, maybe not... you two are identical twins, aren't you?'
全班哄笑，她又接了一句：'哦不对，也许不是……你们俩是一模一样的双胞胎吧？'
It sounds silly, but it worked.
听着傻乎乎的，但真管用。
She asked us, 'What if we all looked the same? Wouldn't it be boring?', and we all agreed that it would be.
她问我们：'要是所有人都长得一样呢？是不是特无聊？'我们全都同意：那也太无聊了。
That minute of laughter taught us more than a two-hour lecture.
那一分钟的笑声，比两小时的讲座教的都多。
Since then, when I meet someone with a different accent, different food or different customs, I try to ask questions instead of staring or joking behind their backs.
从那以后，遇到口音、饮食、习惯不同的人，我都尽量开口问，而不是背后盯着看或者笑话人家。
Usually people are happy to share — ask a classmate about his mother's cooking, and you'll probably get invited to dinner.
通常人们都乐意分享——问问同学他妈妈做的菜，搞不好还能蹭顿饭。
Difference is what makes a community interesting.
是不同让一个群体变得有意思。
The problem is never that people are different; the problem is treating people badly because they're different.
问题从来不是'人与人有差异'，问题是因为差异就不好好待人。
And unlike difference itself, that is a choice.
而且与'不同'本身不同——那是一种选择。

topics.question: Do you think parents should protect their children from every unpleasant situation? What could be the effects?
topics.questionZh: 你认为父母应该让孩子远离一切不愉快的情境吗？这样做可能有什么影响？
hints: 观点：过度保护弊大于利
overprotection feels like love, but often does more harm
例子：事件后退班
his mother pulled him out of the program / 'Children who laugh at you are not your friends'
孩子自己的感受
'I miss my friends. He tried to help me. He's my friend'
更好的做法
face the problem together / teach the child how to walk, don't clear every stone
vocab: Children who laugh at you are not your friends
嘲笑你的孩子不是真朋友
sample: I don't think parents can — or should — protect their children from every unpleasant situation.
我不认为父母能够、也不应该让孩子远离所有不愉快的事。
Overprotection feels like love, but it often does more harm than the thing it protects against.
过度保护感觉是爱，但它带来的伤害，常常比它想挡掉的那件事还大。
I saw a sad example of this.
我就见过一个让人难过的例子。
After a boy was bullied by some outsiders at a picnic, his mother decided to pull him out of the whole after-school program.
一个男孩在野餐会上被外人欺负后，他妈妈决定让他退出整个课后活动班。
She felt terrible about what had happened, and her logic was simple: 'Children who laugh at you are not your friends.'
她为发生的事难过极了，逻辑也很简单：'会嘲笑你的孩子，就不是你的朋友。'
From her point of view, leaving was the safest choice.
站在她的角度，离开是最安全的选择。
But the boy himself saw it differently.
可孩子本人的想法不一样。
He kept saying, 'I miss my friends. One boy didn't laugh — he tried to help me. He's my friend. Please let me go back.'
他一直念叨：'我想我的朋友们。有个男孩没笑，他还帮了我，他是我朋友。求你让我回去吧。'
In other words, one bad afternoon was erasing all his good afternoons, and his real friends were being taken away from him too.
换句话说，一个糟糕的下午，正把他所有美好的下午一并抹掉，连他真正的朋友也被一起带走了。
To me, that's the real cost of overprotection: it removes the risk, but it also removes the people who help a child face the risk.
在我看来，这就是过度保护的真正代价：风险挪走了，可帮孩子扛住风险的人，也被一并挪走了。
Children don't grow strong inside a bubble; they grow strong with support beside them.
孩子不是在泡泡里变强的，是在身边有人撑着的时候变强的。
Of course parents must protect their kids, but the better way is to face the problem together: talk to the school, teach the child what to do, and keep the good friends close.
当然父母必须保护孩子，但更好的办法是一起去面对：找学校谈、教孩子怎么办、让好朋友留在身边。
You can't clear all the stones from a child's road; you can only teach them how to walk.
你没法替孩子把路上的石头全搬走，你只能教会他怎么走。

topics.question: Describe a time when you tried to persuade someone to change their mind. Did you succeed in the end?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你试图说服别人改变主意的经历。你最后成功了吗？
hints: 背景：想劝谁、劝什么
persuade a father to let his son come back to the program
对方的立场
he was very polite but not ready to change his mind
你的策略：先共情再坦诚
may I speak frankly? / I shared my own story
结果与感悟
we kept our fingers crossed / persuasion is about earning trust, not winning an argument
vocab: not ready to change his mind
a very difficult decision for our family
对我们家是个艰难的决定
sample: Yes — and it was one of the most delicate conversations I've ever had.
有过——那是我经历过的最不好拿捏的一次谈话。
After a boy in our program was hurt by racist bullies, his father decided to take him out and never send him back.
我们班里一个男孩被种族歧视的坏孩子伤害后，他爸爸决定让他退出，再也不回来了。
My colleague and I made an appointment and visited the family, carrying a pile of cards the children had made, hoping to persuade him to let the boy return.
我和同事约好去家访，抱着一摞孩子们亲手做的卡片，想劝他让孩子回来。
He was very polite, but clearly not ready to change his mind.
他非常客气，但显然不打算改变主意。
'I understand there is hate in this world,' he said, 'but my son is just a child. Parents must protect their children.'
他说：'我知道这个世界上有仇恨，可我儿子只是个孩子。做父母的必须保护自己的孩子。'
You can't argue with that feeling.
这份心情，你没法反驳。
So instead of pushing, I asked, 'May I speak frankly?', and then I shared my own story — how I was teased as a child, and how I got through it.
所以我没有硬劝，而是问了一句'我能坦率地说吗'，然后讲了我自己的故事——小时候怎么被人取笑，又是怎么挺过来的。
I told him his son had real friends here, and that overcoming prejudice is only possible when we work together.
我告诉他，他儿子在这里有真正的朋友，而克服偏见，只有大家一起努力才做得到。
He listened quietly and finally said, 'This is a very difficult decision for our family.'
他安静地听完，最后说：'这对我们家是个艰难的决定。'
We didn't win that day, and afterwards I wasn't very optimistic.
那天我们没能说动他，之后我也不太乐观。
But we kept our fingers crossed, and about a week later he gave it some thought and softened — the boy came back.
但我们一直盼着好结果，大约一周后他认真考虑、态度松了口——孩子回来了。
That taught me that persuasion isn't about winning an argument; it's about earning trust first.
这让我明白：说服别人不在于赢得争论，而在于先赢得信任。

topics.question: Describe a difficult experience that made you stronger. How did you get through it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一段让你变得更坚强的艰难经历。你是怎么挺过来的？
hints: 什么逆境
the new kid with a strange accent / classmates made fun of me
当时的感受
it hurt a lot, especially as a child
你是怎么挺过来的
I got through it with family support and one true friend
这段经历的馈赠
now I can tell bullied children: it gets better
sample: The experience that made me stronger was being the new kid with a strange accent.
让我变得更坚强的经历，是当那个'口音怪异'的转学生。
When I changed schools, my classmates made fun of almost everything about me — the way I pronounced certain words, my packed lunch, my clothes.
转学之后，同学们几乎什么都能取笑我——某些词的发音、我带的午饭、我的衣服。
They called me names I don't even want to repeat.
他们给我起的外号，我连复述都不愿意。
I was about nine, and it hurt a lot, especially as a child, because you slowly start believing that something is genuinely wrong with you.
那时我九岁，真的很受伤，尤其是对孩子来说，因为你会慢慢相信：真的是自己有问题。
What saved me was twofold.
把我拉出来的是两件事。
First, my grandmother refused to pity me.
一是我奶奶拒绝可怜我。
She'd say, 'They laugh at what they don't know. Be patient with them.'
她总说：'他们笑的是他们不认识的东西。对他们耐心点。'
Second, one classmate kept sitting with me at lunch on the worst days.
二是在最难熬的日子里，始终有一个同学陪我吃午饭。
One true friend outweighs twenty mockers.
一个真朋友，抵得过二十个嘲笑你的人。
Slowly I stopped hiding.
慢慢地，我不再躲了。
I answered questions in class, joined the choir, and let people hear my accent on purpose.
上课举手回答，参加合唱团，故意让大家听清我的口音。
By the second year, the same kids were asking me to teach them words in my family's language.
到了第二年，同一批孩子反而来找我，让我教他们我家乡话的词。
I got through it, and those teasing voices lost all their power.
我挺过来了，那些嘲弄的声音也彻底失去了威力。
That's why I believe children can overcome prejudice if they have two things: someone who believes in them, and a small success of their own.
所以我才相信，只要有这两样，孩子就能扛过偏见：一个相信他的人，和一次属于自己的小小成功。
I'm living proof, and whenever I meet a child who is being bullied, I tell them so.
我就是活生生的例子，每次遇到被欺负的孩子，我都会这么告诉他。

topics.question: Describe a time when you did something to make up for something you felt responsible for.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你为自己觉得有责任的事采取行动去弥补的经历。
hints: 发生了什么、你负有什么责任
I sat down for one minute and didn't protect him / I felt partly responsible
愧疚之外你做了什么
I offered free guitar lessons / it was my way of apologizing
对方的反应
he tried to pay me three times / I refused, I insisted
感悟
guilt is only useful if you turn it into action
vocab: my way of doing something about it
我为此做点什么的方式
throw in the lessons for free
the least a father can do
一个父亲最起码能做的
sample: Last year at a community event, I was the adult responsible for a group of children.
去年一次社区活动上，我是一群孩子的带队负责人。
For one minute — literally one minute — I sat down to take a phone call.
就一分钟——真的就一分钟——我坐下来接了个电话。
In that minute, some troublemakers picked on the quietest boy, and a small disaster followed: tears, angry parents, and one boy left the program.
就在那一分钟里，几个捣乱的孩子盯上了最安静的那个男孩，随后是一场小灾难：眼泪、愤怒的家长，还有一个孩子退了班。
Nobody blamed me directly.
没有人直接怪我。
Everyone said, 'It wasn't your fault — those kids weren't even from our group.'
大家都说：'不是你的错，那些孩子根本不是我们班的。'
But I kept thinking: I was there to watch them, and I didn't protect him.
可我一直在想：我就是去看住他们的，而我没能护住他。
I felt partly responsible, and that feeling didn't go away.
我觉得自己负有部分责任，这种感受挥之不去。
So I decided to do something instead of just feeling bad.
于是我决定做点什么，而不是光难受。
I knew the boy loved guitar but his family wasn't eager to spend on lessons, so I offered to teach him and his best friend for free, at his home, wherever his parents felt safe.
我知道那孩子喜欢吉他，但家里不太愿意掏课费，于是我提出免费教他和他最好的朋友，就在他家里上，他父母觉得安全的地方。
That was my way of doing something about it — my way of apologizing to the family.
这是我为此做点什么的方式，也是向这一家人道歉的方式。
To his credit, the father tried to pay me three times.
说句公道话，那位父亲试着付了三次钱。
I refused every time — I insist, I told him — because the whole point was to give, not to trade.
每次我都拒了——'我坚持'，我告诉他——因为这件事的意义就在于给予，而不是交易。
In the end he accepted, saying it was the least a father can do to keep thanking me.
最后他接受了，说一个父亲能做的，至少是不停地谢我。
What I learned from this is simple: guilt is only useful if you turn it into action.
这件事教给我的很简单：内疚只有在变成行动时才有用。
An apology ends a conversation; making amends starts a relationship.
道歉只会结束一次谈话，弥补才能开启一段关系。

topics.question: How important do you think friendship is for young children? Should parents help maintain their children's friendships?
topics.questionZh: 你认为友谊对小孩子有多重要？父母应该帮忙维系孩子的友谊吗？
hints: 观点：友谊对孩子至关重要
friendship is as vital as food and sleep
两个孩子的友谊
they were inseparable / 'We are a team. I miss you.'
大人的做法
arrange the lessons so they can keep up the friendship
小小举动的意义
it takes one weekly lesson, one lift, one phone call
sample: I think friendship for young children is almost as vital as food and sleep — and yes, I believe parents have a real duty to help maintain it.
我觉得对小孩子来说，友谊几乎跟吃饭睡觉一样重要——而且我认为，父母确实有责任帮忙维系它。
I watched this with two boys, both about nine.
我亲眼看着两个九岁左右的男孩经历了这一切。
They were inseparable — same class, same baseball team, the kind of friends who write 'We are a team. I miss you' on a handmade card.
他们形影不离——同班、同一支棒球队，是那种会在手绘卡片上写'我们是一个队，我想你'的朋友。
Then one of them had to leave the after-school program, and suddenly they had no place to meet.
后来其中一个不得不退出课后班，两人一下子没了见面的场合。
An adult could easily have said, 'Kids forget quickly, they'll make new friends.'
大人很容易说一句：'孩子忘性大，很快会交到新朋友。'
But in my experience that's not quite true: children grieve friendships too — they just show it by going quiet.
但依我的经验，这话不太对：孩子也会为友谊伤心——只不过他们表现出来的是变得沉默。
So the people around them did a small, clever thing.
于是身边的人做了一件聪明的小事。
They arranged guitar lessons for both boys, at one boy's house, once a week, so the friendship had a fixed time and place.
他们给两个孩子安排了吉他课，在其中一个家里，每周一次，让这份友谊有了固定的时间和地点。
No speeches, no big plan — just keeping the door open.
没有说教，没有宏大的计划——只是把门留着。
When the father came to pick up his son, all he said was, 'Take it easy, champ,' and drove off with two boys chattering in the back seat.
那位父亲来接儿子时只说了句'别急，小伙子'，就载着后座上叽叽喳喳的两个孩子开走了。
A year later those two are still best friends.
一年过去，他俩还是最好的朋友。
Watching them, I realised adults often underestimate children's feelings and overestimate the cost of helping.
看着他们我意识到：大人常常低估孩子的感受，又高估帮忙的代价。
It usually takes so little — one weekly lesson, one lift, one phone call — to keep a friendship alive.
维系一段友谊，往往只需要这么一点点——一周一次课、一趟顺风车、一个电话。

topics.question: Describe an instrument you play, or would like to learn to play. Why did you choose it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一种你会弹奏或想学的乐器。你为什么选择它？
hints: 什么乐器、怎么开始的
guitar lessons once a week, free of charge
起步的困难
my fingers hurt / the teacher counted us off slowly
现在的状态
practice every night / my favourite half hour of the day
你的小梦想
part of me would love to be a rock star / you can be anything you want to be — after homework
vocab: be anything he wants to be
成为他想成为的任何人
sample: The instrument I play is the guitar, and it started almost by accident.
我会弹的是吉他，学它纯属偶然。
A teacher at my after-school program played beautifully, and one day she offered to give me and my best friend lessons — free of charge, once a week.
课后活动班有位老师吉他弹得特别好，有一天她提出教我和我最好的朋友——每周一次，分文不收。
I remember counting the days and telling everyone, 'I can't wait till Tuesday!'
我记得天天数日子，逢人就说：'我等不及到周二了！'
The beginning was humbling.
起步阶段很打击人。
My fingers hurt, the strings buzzed, and rhythm escaped me completely.
手指疼、琴弦打品、节奏完全找不着。
The teacher would count us off — 'nice and slow: one... two... one, two, three, four' — at a painfully slow speed.
老师会给我们报拍子——'慢慢来：一……二……一、二、三、四'——慢得让人难受。
But she never rushed us, and little by little my hands stopped arguing with my head.
但她从不催我们，渐渐地，我的手不再跟脑子打架了。
My best friend was just as clumsy as me, which honestly helped a lot.
我那位好朋友弹得跟我一样笨，说实话这让心里好受多了。
Now the guitar is my favourite half hour of the day.
现在，弹吉他成了我一天里最喜欢的半小时。
Every night after dinner I practice, even if it's just the same three chords over and over.
每天晚饭后我都练琴，哪怕就是把同样的三个和弦翻来覆去地弹。
When I'm stressed, my breathing slows down all by itself.
压力大的时候，呼吸会自己慢下来。
My dream, if I'm honest, is a bit silly: part of me would love to be a rock star.
老实说，我的梦想有点傻：我心里有一部分真想当摇滚歌星。
My father just laughs and says a son can be anything he wants to be — but first, homework, and practice tonight.
我爸听了只是笑，说儿子想成为什么都可以——但先写作业，今晚练琴。
Fair enough. The music isn't going anywhere, and neither am I.
行吧，公平。音乐跑不了，我也跑不了。

topics.question: When someone helps you for free, do you think you should insist on paying them back in some way? Why?
topics.questionZh: 当有人无偿帮助你时，你认为应该坚持以某种方式回报吗？为什么？
hints: 观点：善意不能当成理所当然
never let a favour sink without a ripple
两种回报方式
'I must pay for the lessons' / the mother came back with a small gift
坚持付钱与收礼各说明什么
it's the least a father can do / she wants you to have it
你自己的原则
pay it, gift it, or pass it on
vocab: she wants you to have it
sample: This is a lovely question, because I've watched it argued — politely — between two adults I respect.
这个问题有意思，因为我见过两位我敬重的大人，客客气气地为它争执过。
A young teacher offered to teach two boys guitar completely free of charge, as her way of apologizing for something that wasn't really her fault.
一位年轻老师提出完全免费教两个男孩弹吉他，以此为她并无大过的一件事表达歉意。
One boy's father immediately said, 'Great idea — but I must pay for my son's lessons.'
其中一个孩子的爸爸马上说：'好主意——但我必须为儿子的课付钱。'
She refused; he insisted; in the end he won, saying it was the least a father could do.
她不肯，他坚持，最后他赢了，说这是一个父亲最起码能做的。
The other family handled it differently.
另一家的做法不同。
When the teacher tried to refuse any payment, the mother disappeared for a moment and came back with a small gift.
老师想拒绝任何报酬时，那位母亲走开了一会儿，回来时手里多了件小礼物。
'I can't accept this,' the teacher said, but the answer came back through the boy: his mother says she wants you to have it.
'这个我不能收。'老师说。回答通过小男孩传了过来：妈妈说，她希望你能收下。
And that was that.
事情就这么定了。
I think both families were right.
我觉得两家都没错。
When someone helps you for free, insisting on paying respects their effort; accepting a gift respects their dignity.
有人无偿帮你时，坚持付钱，是尊重对方的付出；收下礼物，是尊重对方的心意。
The real mistake would be taking the kindness as if it were owed to you.
真正的错，是把这份善意当成理所当然。
My own rule is: never let a favour sink without a ripple.
我自己的原则是：绝不让一份好心意掉进水里连个响都没有。
Pay it, gift it, or pass it on — but somehow let the kindness come back into the world.
或回礼、或收下、或传下去——总之要让这份善意以某种方式回到世界上。
That, I think, is what keeps people willing to help.
我想，正是这个，让人愿意一直帮下去。

topics.question: Do you think children can live happily when they split their time between two homes after their parents' divorce?
topics.questionZh: 父母离异后，孩子在两个家之间轮流生活，你觉得他们能过得快乐吗？
hints: 观点：可以，但取决于父母
it depends almost entirely on the parents' attitude
表弟的双城生活
every other weekend with his mum, the rest of the time with his dad
孩子真正担心什么
will Mum and Dad get back together? / nobody wants to answer
什么在起作用
tell the truth gently / both parents love him
vocab: Sometimes it's hard. Sometimes I like it
sample: I believe they can live happily — but almost none of that happiness happens automatically; it depends almost entirely on the parents' attitude.
我相信他们可以过得快乐——但这快乐几乎不会自动发生，几乎全看父母的态度。
My cousin is nine and lives in two places: every other weekend and part of the holidays with his mum, the rest of the time with his dad.
我表弟九岁，在两个家之间生活：每隔一个周末和一部分假期跟妈妈，其余时间跟爸爸。
When I asked him whether living in two places was hard, he shrugged and said, 'Sometimes it's hard. Sometimes I like it.'
我问他两边住难不难，他耸耸肩：'有时挺难，有时也挺好。'
Two birthdays, he explained — but also two school bags to forget in two different houses.
他解释说，生日能过两次——但书包也会忘在两个不同的家里。
What worries him isn't the schedule — it's the silence.
真正让他不安的不是时间表，而是大人的沉默。
He keeps asking whether his parents will ever get back together, or whether his dad will start going out on dates.
他不停地问：爸妈还会不会复合？爸爸会不会开始出去约会？
Nobody wants to answer, so he collects clues from half-heard phone calls.
没人肯回答，他就从偷听到一半的电话里自己拼线索。
From watching him, I've noticed what actually works.
观察他这几年，我注意到真正管用的东西。
His grandmother tells him the truth gently: 'Your mum has a new husband now. I don't think they'll get back together.'
他奶奶会温和地告诉他实话：'妈妈现在有新丈夫了，我觉得他们不会复合了。'
And when he asked if his dad would date someone, his dad didn't mock him — he just said, 'Not for now. It's just you and me, OK?'
他问爸爸会不会跟人约会时，爸爸也没笑话他，只说：'暂时不会。现在就是我和你，好吗？'
Honesty, it turns out, is easier to live with than hope that keeps being postponed.
事实证明，跟'一直被推迟的希望'比起来，实话反而更好过日子。
So yes, children can thrive between two homes — if the two homes don't turn the child into a messenger or a prize to be won.
所以，是的，孩子在两个家之间也能茁壮成长——前提是这两个家别把孩子变成传话筒，也别把他变成争夺的战利品。
