What a child needs is simple: the truth, and the certainty that both parents love him.
孩子需要的其实很简单：真话，以及'爸妈都爱我'的确定感。

topics.question: What rules do you think families should have for children about homework, television and housework?
topics.questionZh: 关于作业、看电视和做家务，你认为家里应该给孩子立下什么规矩？
hints: 规矩一：作业优先
no guitar until your homework is finished
规矩二：自己收拾
clean up after yourself / pick it up right now
规矩三：屏幕时间
he watches too much television / turn it off this minute
规矩背后的温度
firm limits, delivered with a smile
vocab: No guitar until your homework is finished
作业做完前不许弹吉他
turn that television off this minute
sample: I grew up with quite a few house rules, and looking back, I'd keep most of them.
我是在一堆家规里长大的，现在回头看，大部分我都愿意留着。
The first rule in our house was homework first.
我家第一条规矩是作业优先。
My father had one phrase for everything: no guitar until your homework is finished.
我爸万事一句话：作业没做完，不许碰吉他。
It sounded strict, but it actually protected my free time — once the books were closed, the evening was truly mine.
听着严苛，其实反而保护了我的自由时间——书一合上，整晚就真是我自己的了。
The second rule was to clean up after yourself.
第二条是自己的东西自己收拾。
Once I got popcorn all over the carpet in front of the TV, and my grandmother made me pick it up right then, piece by piece, while my favourite show was on.
有一回我把爆米花撒得满地毯都是，奶奶就让我当场一粒一粒捡，那会儿正放着我最爱的动画片。
I thought it was cruel and unusual punishment; now I'm the tidiest person in my flat.
我当时觉得这简直是酷刑；现在我是整个公寓最爱干净的人。
There was also a limit on screens.
屏幕时间也有限制。
If I watched too much television, the set went off 'this minute', no discussion.
电视看多了，电视机会'立刻'被关掉，没有商量。
I resented it back then, but I notice now that friends who grew up without limits still struggle to stop even as adults.
那时我特别不服，可现在我发现，从小没规矩的朋友，长成了大人还是管不住自己。
Of course, rules only work with warmth behind them.
当然，规矩要有效，背后得有温度。
I once complained that rock stars don't have to pick up popcorn, and instead of getting angry, my father smiled and said, 'You can be anything you want to be — right after you pick up the popcorn.'
有一次我抱怨说摇滚歌星肯定不用捡爆米花，我爸没发火，笑着说：'你想当什么都行——先把爆米花捡了。'
That's the balance, I think: firm limits, delivered with a smile.
我觉得分寸就在这儿：规矩要硬，语气要软。

topics.question: When parents separate, do you think children should have a say in deciding which parent to live with? Why?
topics.questionZh: 父母离异时，你认为孩子在跟谁生活这件事上应该有发言权吗？为什么？
hints: 孩子的感受需要被听见
children shouldn't be kept in the dark
但让孩子二选一太沉重
it's a heavy burden to choose between parents
大人如何好好沟通
sit down and talk it through
最终为孩子着想
promise to do what's best for the child
sample: Yes, I do, although with one condition: children should be heard, but they shouldn't be forced to make the final choice.
我认为应该，不过有个前提：孩子的心声要被听见，但最后的决定不该压在他们身上。
I saw this play out in my own family last year, when my uncle and his wife decided to separate.
去年我叔叔和婶婶决定分开，这件事在我们家真实上演了一遍。
Their ten-year-old son was suddenly told that he might have to move to another city with his mother.
他们十岁的儿子突然被告知，可能得跟着妈妈搬到另一座城市去。
Nobody had really talked it through with him first, so at a family dinner he just exploded and shouted that it wasn't fair.
事先没人好好和他谈过，于是一次家宴上他当场爆发，喊着这不公平。
He said he wanted everything the way it was, with his mum and dad together, and honestly that broke my heart.
他说他想要一切照旧，爸爸妈妈和他在一起，说实话那一刻我心都碎了。
In my view, a child that age absolutely deserves to know what's happening and to express his feelings.
在我看来，那个年纪的孩子完全应该知道发生了什么，也应该把感受说出来。
But asking him to pick one parent over the other is a heavy burden, because he'll feel guilty either way.
可要他在爸妈之间二选一太沉重了，因为选哪边他都会内疚。
What adults should do is sit down and talk it through, the way my uncle finally did.
大人该做的是坐下来把事情谈透，我叔叔后来就是这么做的。
He reminded his son how they used to sit together and discuss important things, like the time his bike was stolen.
他提醒儿子，他们以前常常坐在一起商量重要的事，比如自行车被偷那次。
Then he promised to try to do what was best for the boy, not what was easiest for the grown-ups.
然后他承诺尽力做对孩子最好的安排，而不是对大人最省事的。
That, I think, is the right balance: take the child's voice seriously, but let the adults work the problem out.
我觉得这才是恰当的分寸：认真对待孩子的声音，但让大人去把问题解决好。

topics.question: Do you think retirement is an enjoyable time of life, or can it be boring? Why?
topics.questionZh: 你觉得退休是人生中一段快乐的时光，还是可能很无聊？为什么？
hints: 自由时间多，但社交圈缩小
it's not easy to make new friends when you stop working
身边退休者的真实状态
most of them just stay home all day
培养爱好、参与活动
join a community choir / take part in local activities
心态与规划决定质量
you get used to the slower rhythm eventually
vocab: retirement can get a little boring
退休生活可能会有点无聊
spend some time with our relatives
和亲戚们待上一段时间
sample: To be honest, I think retirement can be both, and the difference comes down to one thing: whether people plan for it.
说实话，我觉得退休生活两种可能都有，关键看一点：有没有提前规划。
My neighbour retired from the railway two years ago, and for the first few months he looked completely lost.
我邻居两年前从铁路上退休，头几个月整个人都是懵的。
He'd been a train driver for over thirty years, and suddenly there was nowhere to go every morning.
他开了三十多年火车，忽然每天早上没地方可去了。
He once told me that retirement can get a little boring, which surprised me, because I'd always imagined it as an endless holiday.
他跟我说过退休生活会有些无聊，这话让我挺意外，因为我一直把它想象成一个无限长的假期。
He said it's not easy to make new friends when you're no longer working, so his world shrank to his flat and his TV.
他说不上班以后交新朋友不容易，他的世界一度缩小到房子和电视机。
In his area most neighbours are retired people as well, and they basically just stay home all day.
他那个小区的邻居也多是退休的人，基本整天待在家里。
Then his daughter pushed him to join the community choir, and everything changed.
后来他女儿劝他去参加社区合唱团，一切就都变了。
Now he practises twice a week, performs at local events, and even went back to his hometown to spend some time with his relatives.
现在他每周排练两次，还在社区活动上演出，甚至回老家和亲戚们待了一阵子。
Compared with him, the retirees who lock themselves at home seem to age much faster.
跟他比起来，那些把自己关在家里的退休老人老得明显快得多。
He told me you get used to the slower rhythm eventually, but only if you fill the time yourself.
他跟我说，慢节奏最终是能习惯的，但前提是你得自己去把时间填满。
So my conclusion is that retirement itself isn't boring; an empty schedule is.
所以我的结论是：退休本身并不无聊，空白的时间表才无聊。
The happiest retired people I know treat it like a new chapter, not a long wait.
我认识的最快乐的退休老人，都把退休当作新篇章，而不是漫长的等待。
That's exactly what I want to copy when my time comes.
等到我退休那天，我也想照这样过。

topics.question: Describe an unusual or unexpected way you met someone who later became important to you.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次不同寻常、出乎意料的相识经历，那个人后来对你很重要。
hints: 时间地点与当时处境
my car broke down on a country road
对方如何意外出现
a car pulled over out of the blue
之间发生的趣事
the hood nearly hit her head, like a scene from a film
后来的关系与感悟
good things sometimes arrive out of the blue
vocab: stranded in the middle of nowhere
被困在前不着村后不着店的地方
The hood of my car fell on his head.
我的车引擎盖砸到了他头。
sample: The most unexpected person in my life is my best friend from university, and I met her because my car broke down.
我生命中最意想不到的人，是大学时最好的朋友，而我们的相识是因为我的车抛锚了。
It happened on a country road last summer, when I was driving home for the holiday.
那是去年夏天，在一条乡间公路上，我当时正开车回家过节。
To make things worse, it started to drizzle.
更糟的是，天还下起了小雨。
The engine made a strange noise, then died completely, and I was basically stranded in the middle of nowhere with almost no signal.
发动机先是发出怪声，然后彻底熄火，我被困在前不着村后不着店的地方，手机几乎没信号。
While I was panicking, a car pulled over out of the blue.
正当我慌得不行时，一辆车出乎意料地停了下来。
A girl about my age got out, and it turned out her father ran a garage in the next town.
下来一个和我差不多大的女孩，后来才知道她爸爸在邻镇开修理厂。
She waited with me for almost two hours, we talked about everything, and by the time the tow truck came we'd exchanged numbers.
她陪我等了差不多两个小时，我们什么都聊，拖车到的时候我们已经互留了电话。
While she was checking the engine, the hood slipped and nearly hit her head, which felt like a scene from a film.
她查看发动机时，引擎盖滑下来差点砸到她的头，那一幕像电影情节。
People say 'How romantic!' when they hear this story, and I never argue with them.
别人听完这故事都说'真浪漫'，我从来不反驳。
We became inseparable after that, and we always joke that my terrible old car brought us together.
从那以后我们形影不离，还总开玩笑说是我那辆破车把我们凑到一起的。
If the car had been reliable that day, I would have driven past the most important friend of my life.
如果那天车靠得住，我可能就与这辈子最重要的朋友擦肩而过了。
So when people say good things arrive out of the blue, I believe them completely.
所以别人说好事会不期而至时，我完全相信。

topics.question: Do you think parents and grandparents should get involved in young people's decisions about marriage and having children?
topics.questionZh: 你认为父母和祖父母应该参与年轻人在结婚、生孩子这些事上的决定吗？
hints: 长辈的出发点是关心
her generation measured a good life by a stable family
催婚催育带来的压力
the questioning became too much to take
时代不同，选择更个人
marriage is a deeply personal decision
折中的沟通方式
share your plans honestly and hold your line
vocab: You can never have too many grandchildren.
sample: This is a question I face every Chinese New Year, so I have quite strong feelings about it.
这个问题我每年春节都要面对，所以感受特别深。
My grandmother is a warm person, but she believes nobody is complete until they settle down and have children.
我奶奶人是热心，但她坚信一个人不结婚生子就不算圆满。
In her eyes, a steady job means nothing if there's no one waiting at home.
在她看来，工作再稳定，家里没人等你也是白搭。
At every family dinner she studies me like a detective, asks whether I'm seeing anyone, and sighs if the answer is no.
每次家宴她都像侦探一样打量我，问我有没有对象，一听没有就叹气。
When my cousin turned thirty, she told him straight out to make up his mind fast if he wanted kids.
我表哥三十岁那年，她直截了当跟他说，想要孩子就赶紧拿定主意。
She also loves to say you can never have too many grandchildren, which makes the whole table laugh except the person she's aiming at.
她还爱说孙子孙女永远不嫌多，全桌都笑，只有被点名的那位笑不出来。
I understand where she's coming from: her generation measured a good life by a stable family, and she genuinely worries about us.
我明白她的出发点：她们那代人拿安稳的家庭定义好日子，她是真的在为我们操心。
But times have changed; people study longer, cities are expensive, and marriage is a deeply personal decision.
但时代变了，读书读得更久，城里生活成本高，婚姻又是非常个人的决定。
Two of my cousins actually skipped family gatherings for a year because the questioning became too much.
我有两个表哥表姐因为被问得太狠，整整一年没参加家庭聚会。
So my answer is: relatives can care, but they shouldn't decide.
所以我的答案是：长辈可以关心，但不该替你做决定。
The smart way is to share your plans honestly so they feel included, and then calmly hold your line.
聪明的做法是坦诚说说自己的规划，让他们有参与感，然后温和而坚定地守住的立场。
When I finally told my grandmother my five-year plan, she stopped hinting — mostly.
等我终于把五年计划告诉奶奶后，她就不怎么旁敲侧击了——基本上。

topics.question: Describe a small, inexpensive gift you gave or received that meant a lot to you.
topics.questionZh: 描述一件你送出或收到的小小的不贵重的礼物，但它对你意义重大。
hints: 什么礼物、谁送的
a four-leaf clover / a lucky coin
礼物的来历与心意
her brother gave it to her before she left home
为什么贵重：故事而非价格
luck is no good if you can't share it
之后如何传递这份心意
pass it on whenever a friend faces something scary
vocab: a little surprise for you to cheer you up
给你个小惊喜，让你开心起来
It's supposed to bring you good luck.
What good is luck if you can't share it with the people you love?
好运不能和爱的人分享还有什么意义？
That must be very special to you.
sample: The gift I'm thinking of cost almost nothing, but I still keep it in my pencil case.
我要说的这件礼物几乎没花钱，但我至今还把它放在笔袋里。
It's a four-leaf clover pressed between two pieces of clear plastic, given to me by my roommate before a huge exam.
那是一片压在两层透明塑料片之间的四叶草，是室友在一场大考前送我的。
She got it from her brother when she left home for school, so it was clearly special to her.
那是她离家上学时弟弟送给她的，所以对她来说显然很特别。
The night before the exam I was a nervous wreck, and she just put it on my desk and said it was supposed to bring good luck.
考试前一晚我紧张得不行，她把四叶草放在我桌上，说它能带来好运。
She added that luck is no good if you can't share it with the people you love, which I found really touching.
她还补了一句，好运不能和爱的人分享就没了意义，这话让我特别感动。
Honestly, I don't know whether the clover worked or I simply calmed down, but I passed with a better grade than expected.
说实话，我不知道是四叶草灵验还是我自己平静了下来，反正我考得比预期好。
The next term she was the one panicking before her driving test, so I gave it back to her for a week.
下学期轮到她在驾照考试前发慌，我就把四叶草还给她用了一周。
It's become a small tradition between us now, passing it around whenever one of us faces something scary.
现在这成了我们之间的小传统，谁遇到害怕的事，它就传到谁手里。
That little leaf taught me that a good gift doesn't need a price tag.
那片小叶子让我明白，好礼物不需要价签。
It needs a story and a bit of your heart.
它需要的是一段故事和一点真心。
That's why I always prefer small, thoughtful presents to expensive ones.
所以我一向喜欢用心的小礼物，胜过昂贵的那种。

topics.question: Describe a time you gave a toast or a short speech at a family celebration.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你在家庭庆祝活动上举杯致辞或发表简短讲话的经历。
hints: 什么场合、有哪些人
my parents' wedding anniversary dinner
紧张与准备过程
my hands were shaking like leaves
说了什么内容
propose a toast / thank them for raising us
现场反应与感悟
a toast doesn't need fancy words, just true details
vocab: May every day be better than the last.
May your life continue to be an adventure
愿你的生活继续充满惊喜
sample: The toast I gave was at my parents' twenty-fifth wedding anniversary dinner last autumn.
我致辞的那次，是去年秋天我父母的银婚纪念家宴。
There were about thirty guests, mostly relatives and old neighbours, and my parents had no idea I would speak.
来了大概三十位客人，多是亲戚和老邻居，我父母完全没想到我会讲话。
My sister and I had secretly planned it for a month.
我和我姐为这个惊喜偷偷筹备了一个月。
I stood up with my glass after the cake, and my hands were shaking like leaves.
切完蛋糕我端着杯子站起来，手抖得像树叶一样。
I said I wanted to propose a toast to my parents, who had run a small noodle shop for over twenty years.
我说我想为父母举杯，他们经营一家小面馆二十多年了。
I thanked them for raising us while working from dawn to dusk, and wished them health, money and love.
我感谢他们起早贪黑把我们养大，祝他们健康、有钱花、有人爱。
At the end I raised my glass and said may every day be better than the last.
最后我举杯说，愿往后的每一天都比前一天更好。
To my surprise, my father, a man who almost never cries, had wet eyes, and the neighbours clapped for ages.
让我意外的是，我那个几乎从不落泪的父亲眼眶湿了，邻居们鼓了好久的掌。
An old friend of theirs stood up afterwards and told stories about them from twenty years ago, which made the toast even warmer.
随后他们的一位老朋友站起来讲了二十年前的事，让整段致辞更暖了。
What I learned is that a toast doesn't need fancy words.
我学到的是，致辞不需要华丽的辞藻。
It needs one or two true details, like a cake made with loving care, or a memory only your family shares.
需要的是一两处真实的细节，比如用心做的蛋糕，或只有你们家才懂的一段回忆。
Since then I've stopped being afraid of speaking in public, because I know sincerity carries you through.
从那以后我不再怕当众讲话，因为我知道真诚能带你撑完全场。

topics.question: Describe a time when you received urgent news and had to act quickly.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你接到紧急消息、必须马上行动的经历。
hints: 什么消息、几点接到
my phone rang at two in the morning
第一反应与慌乱
my mind went completely blank
如何迅速安排
book the earliest flight, whatever it costs
结果与事后反思
keep an emergency list on your phone
sample: I'll never forget the night my phone rang at two in the morning.
我永远忘不了凌晨两点电话响起的那晚。
It was my mother's neighbour, and she said my mum had chest pain and an ambulance was on the way.
是我妈妈的邻居打来的，她说我妈胸口疼，救护车已经在路上了。
My mind went completely blank for a few seconds, and then I switched into a strange, super-practical mode.
头几秒我大脑一片空白，然后一下子进入了某种特别务实的状态。
I booked the earliest flight online while packing with one hand, whatever it cost.
我一边单手收拾行李一边订了最早一班机票，完全没管价格。
A taxi driver saw my face and drove faster without me even asking.
出租车司机看了看我脸色，我没开口他就开快了。
Before boarding I called my little brother, who was at home, and just said, 'Hang in there, I'm taking the next flight out.'
登机前我给在家的弟弟打了个电话，只说：撑住，我赶下一班飞机回来。
When I arrived at the hospital ten hours later, Mum was stable, and the doctor said the first hours had been critical.
十个小时后我赶到医院，妈妈情况已经稳定，医生说头几个小时是关键。
My brother had handled everything calmly, and I hugged him in the corridor for a long time.
弟弟把一切处理得井井有条，我在走廊里抱了他很久。
That night taught me two things.
那一晚教会了我两件事。
First, in a real emergency you find out what you're made of; second, preparation, not panic, is what saves time.
第一，真正的紧急时刻才能看清自己的成色；第二，省时间的是预案，不是慌乱。
I now keep a small emergency list on my phone: relatives, insurance and neighbours, so I'll never have to hunt for numbers again.
现在手机里存着一张紧急清单：亲属、保险和邻居的电话，我再也不用临时翻号码了。

topics.question: When the owners of a long-running family business retire, do you think the family should keep it going or sell it?
topics.questionZh: 当家传老店的经营者退休时，你认为家人应该把店继续开下去，还是卖掉？
hints: 老店的情感价值
it's where my parents first took me
顾客与社区的意义
for the neighbours it's not just a business
下一代的现实压力
no weekends and no holidays
我的折中看法
keep it if the children truly want it
vocab: I'm so glad your parents decided not to sell.
真高兴你父母决定不卖店。
Here's to the next thirty years.
as joyful as the first thirty years
It's a pleasure to be here.
sample: There's a noodle restaurant downstairs from my old flat that my family visited for nearly twenty years.
我以前住的老楼下面有家面馆，我们家光顾了快二十年。
Last spring the owner couple finally retired, and everyone in the neighbourhood worried the shop would be sold.
去年春天老板夫妇终于退休了，整条街的邻居都担心店要被卖掉。
At their farewell dinner, their son announced that the family had decided not to sell.
在告别宴上，他们的儿子宣布家里决定不卖店。
He said the tradition would continue, and asked everyone to drink to the next thirty years.
他说这家店的传统会延续下去，还请大家为下一个三十年干杯。
The mother joked that the only thing she regretted was that her husband cooked too well.
老板娘开玩笑说，这些年唯一的遗憾就是丈夫手艺太好。
Half the street cheered, because for us that shop is not a business; it's where my parents first took me, and where I did my homework after school.
半条街的人都在欢呼，因为对我们来说那不只是一门生意：是我父母第一次带我去的地方，是我放学后写作业的地方。
I completely understand why families fight to keep such places alive.
我完全理解为什么有的家庭拼了命也要把老店撑下去。
A shop like that carries recipes, regular customers and a family's pride.
那样一家店承载着配方、老主顾和一家人的体面。
On the other hand, I don't think the next generation should be forced to take over.
但另一方面，我不觉得下一代应该被迫接班。
Running a restaurant means no weekends and no holidays, and it's simply not for everyone.
开餐馆意味着没有周末没有假期，这活儿真不是谁都能干的。
So my view is: keep it if the children genuinely want it; if not, sell it with dignity and keep the recipes.
所以我的看法是：孩子真心想接就接着开；不想接，就体面地卖掉，把配方留下。
What matters is that the story of the family doesn't get lost with the signboard.
重要的是，一家的故事不能随着招牌一起消失。

topics.question: Do you think it is selfish for young people to move far away from home to pursue their dreams?
topics.questionZh: 你认为年轻人为了追求梦想而远离家乡是自私的吗？
hints: 亲历：离家时的反对
when I asked for his approval, the answer was no
父母态度的转变
if you ever need help, remember we're here
远方的内疚时刻
did I miss signs that something was wrong
如何平衡梦想与亲情
go for your dream but never let them feel forgotten
vocab: Did she miss signs that something was wrong?
她是不是忽略了出事的征兆？
sample: This question touches me personally, because I left my hometown three years ago to study in a city a thousand kilometres away.
这个问题对我而言很切身，因为三年前我离开家乡，去一千多公里外的城市读书。
Some relatives called me selfish at the time, and their words stung for quite a while.
当时有亲戚说我自私，这话扎了我很久。
The truth is my father was against it at first.
其实我爸一开始是反对的。
When I asked for nothing except his approval, his answer was a flat no.
我说我什么都不要、只要他一句支持，他给我的回答干脆就是一个不字。
But a week later he drove me to the station anyway and said that if I ever needed help or changed my mind, they would be there.
可一周后他还是开车送我到车站，说只要我需要帮忙或改了主意，家里一直都在。
Looking back, I understand him; he was scared, not angry.
现在回头看，我懂他了：他不是生气，是害怕。
Living far away does bring guilt, especially when things go wrong at home.
离家远确实会带来愧疚，尤其家里出事的时候。
Once my dad was in hospital for a check-up and hadn't told me, and I felt terrible for missing the signs that something was up.
有一次我爸去医院检查都没告诉我，知道自己漏看了那些不对劲的征兆，我心里特别难受。
Now I ask direct questions about their health instead of just chatting about the weather.
现在我会直接问他们的身体，而不是只聊聊天气。
Still, I don't think leaving equals loving less.
但我始终不认为离开就等于爱得少。
I video-call my parents twice a week, and I've become more independent than they ever imagined.
我每周和他们视频两次，自己也变得比他们想象的独立得多。
In my experience, the fair deal is: go for your dream, but never let the people at home feel forgotten.
以我的经验，公平的安排是：去追你的梦，但别让家里人觉得被丢下了。
Distance tests love, but it doesn't have to break it.
距离考验感情，但不必然毁掉感情。

topics.question: Describe your first few months living in a new city. What was the hardest part and what made it easier?
topics.questionZh: 描述你在新城市生活的头几个月。最难的是什么？又是什么让日子好过起来？
hints: 初到的忙乱与孤独
everything was new and slightly frightening
工作学业的挑战
I was asked to take over a group in my first week
遇到的好人好事
my landlady invited me to dinner twice a week
逐渐安定的节点
raise our glasses to the beginning of a new life
vocab: Here's to the beginning of a new life.
Let me introduce you to the children.
让我把孩子们介绍给你。
sample: When I moved to Chengdu for my first job, the first three months were honestly the busiest and loneliest of my life.
我到成都开始第一份工作时，头三个月说实话是我这辈子最忙也最孤单的日子。
I arrived in August with two suitcases, and everything after that was new and slightly frightening.
我拖着两个行李箱在八月抵达，之后的一切都新鲜得让人发怵。
On my first day I got lost twice on the way to the office.
上班第一天，我就在找办公室的路上迷了两次路。
The hardest part was the job itself, because my manager asked me to take over a training group in my very first week.
最难的是工作本身，因为经理在第一周就让我接手一个培训小组。
I had to introduce myself to thirty people and pretend I knew what I was doing.
我得向三十个人做自我介绍，还得装出胸有成竹的样子。
At night I had so much homework from the induction courses that I fell asleep on my notes.
晚上入职课程的作业多得我经常趴在笔记上睡着。
What saved me was people.
救了我的是人。
My landlady invited me to dinner twice a week, and a colleague walked me through every process at work.
房东阿姨一周请我吃两次饭，一位同事把工作流程一条条讲给我听。
On National Day some new friends took me hiking in the mountains, and I remember thinking that the city was finally becoming mine.
国庆节几个新朋友带我进山徒步，我记得那一刻心想：这座城市终于有点属于我了。
When I got my first paycheck, I took them all out for hotpot and we raised our glasses to the beginning of a new life.
拿到第一笔工资后我请他们吃了顿火锅，我们举杯，为新生活的开始。
By December I could give directions to tourists, which felt like a small victory.
到了十二月，我已经能给游客指路了，这感觉像个小胜利。
All of it was overwhelming at the beginning, but looking back, I wouldn't shorten those months by a single day.
起初这一切都让人应接不暇，但现在回头看，那些日子一天我都不想删掉。
They taught me how quickly strangers can turn a city into a home.
它们教会我，陌生人把城市变成家的速度，可以有多快。

topics.question: Describe an experience of helping a child with their schoolwork.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你辅导孩子功课的经历。
hints: 孩子是谁、什么科目
he had a spelling test the next day
孩子起初的状态
he'd already decided he would fail
你怎么帮他：方法
turn revision into a game
结果与感悟
patience plus a bit of play beats pressure
vocab: I have a big test tomorrow.
Do you want me to help you study?
I have a lot of homework tonight.
sample: I'd like to talk about my little cousin, who was nine that year and panicked about every single test.
我想讲讲我小表弟的事，那年他九岁，逢考必慌。
I picked him up from school twice a week while his parents were working late.
他父母加班的日子，我一周接他两次放学。
One afternoon he climbed into the car looking miserable and admitted he had a big test the next day.
一天下午他钻进车里，蔫蔫地承认第二天有个大测验。
When I asked what it was on, he mumbled 'spelling', and I could tell he'd already decided he would fail.
我问考什么，他咕哝说拼写，我看得出来他已经认定自己会砸。
It broke my heart a little, because spelling was exactly my weak point at his age.
这让我有点心疼，因为拼写正是我在他这个年纪最差的一项。
So instead of forcing him to copy words, I turned it into a game.
于是我没逼他抄单词，而是把它变成了游戏。
The rule was simple: whoever misspelled a word had to do five star jumps.
规则很简单：谁拼错一个词，就做五个开合跳。
We spelled words with fridge magnets, made up silly stories for the difficult ones, and quizzed each other over snacks.
我们用冰箱贴拼单词，给难词编傻故事，边吃零食边互相考。
He laughed at my terrible pronunciation, and I laughed at his, and somehow an hour passed like ten minutes.
他笑我发音烂，我笑他的，不知不觉一小时像十分钟一样过去了。
The next day he ran out of school waving his paper: he got most of the words right.
第二天他挥着卷子冲出校门：大部分词都拼对了。
From then on he actually asked me to help him study, which hardly ever happens with nine-year-olds.
从那以后他居然主动找我帮他复习，这在九岁孩子身上几乎不可能。
That experience showed me that with children, patience plus a bit of play beats pressure every single time.
那次经历让我明白：对孩子来说，耐心加一点游戏感，永远比施压管用。

topics.question: Describe an experience of learning to do something you were not good at, with someone's help.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次在别人帮助下，学习做一件你并不擅长的事情的经历。
hints: 场合与不擅长的原因
I don't dance very well, and I knew it
当时的窘迫
I stood there like a lamppost
谁怎么教你
she said we'd only do the slow ones
突破后的收获
being bad at something isn't embarrassing; refusing to try is
vocab: I have to warn you, I don't dance very well.
I only do the slow ones.
sample: I have to warn you first: I don't dance very well, and that's exactly why this story is worth telling.
先跟你说好：我舞跳得不好，而这恰恰是这段经历值得讲的原因。
It happened at my cousin's wedding, where refusing to dance is basically impossible.
事情发生在我表姐的婚礼上，那种场合想不下场跳舞基本不可能。
The moment the music started, my aunties pulled me onto the floor, and I stood there like a lamppost.
音乐一响，姑妈们就把我拽进了舞池，我杵在那儿活像根路灯。
The lights, the clapping and about a hundred relatives watching made it a hundred times worse.
灯光、掌声，加上一百来号亲戚围观，让场面难堪了一百倍。
A friend of the bride saw my face and offered to teach me some basic steps.
新娘的朋友看出了我的窘迫，主动提出教我几个基本步。
She said not to worry, that we'd only do the slow ones until I found the rhythm.
她说别担心，先只跳慢的，等找到节奏再说。
I stepped on her toes at least three times, and I apologised so much that she started laughing.
我至少踩了她三次脚，道歉道到她都笑出声了。
But she kept counting one-two-three for me, and by the second song my body finally believed it could move.
但她一直帮我数着一二三，到第二首歌，我的身体终于相信自己能动了。
When a Latin song came on later, I even tried a few turns, badly, but with total joy.
后来放拉丁曲时，我还试着转了几圈，转得很烂，但特别开心。
Honestly, dancing in public had been on my fear list for years.
说实话，当众跳舞在我恐惧清单上挂了好多年。
That night I learned that being bad at something is not embarrassing; refusing to try is.
那晚我学到：做不好一件事不丢人，不敢尝试才丢人。
Now at parties I'm always the first clumsy person on the floor, and slow songs are a beginner's best friend.
现在聚会时我总是第一个笨手笨脚下场的那个，顺便说一句，慢歌是新手最好的朋友。
If I could survive a wedding dance, anyone can, and that confidence carries into other parts of my life too.
我都能撑过婚礼舞池，谁都可以，这份底气也延续到了我生活的其他方面。

topics.question: Describe an emergency situation that you or someone in your family experienced. What did you do?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你或家人经历的紧急情况。你当时是怎么做的？
hints: 什么紧急情况
my grandfather suddenly collapsed at home
第一反应：保持镇静
the most important rule is to stay calm
打电话时说清什么
the address, the symptoms, is he conscious
等待救援与结果反思
keep a card with the address and medical history
sample: The emergency I remember best happened last winter, when my grandfather suddenly collapsed in his bedroom.
我记得最清楚的一次紧急情况发生在去年冬天，我爷爷突然在卧室里倒下了。
I was the only other person at home, and those ten minutes changed how I see myself.
家里只有我一个人在，那十分钟改变了我对自己的认识。
He fell while getting dressed, and when I touched him he could answer, but his speech was slurred.
他穿衣时摔倒的，我碰他时还能应声，但说话已经含糊了。
I noticed his mouth had dropped slightly to one side.
我注意到他的嘴角有点往一边歪。
My hands were shaking, but I remembered the most important rule: stay calm, then call for help.
我的手在抖，但我记得最重要的一条：先镇静，再呼救。
I dialled the emergency number and told the operator clearly, 'This is an emergency, my grandfather has fallen and he can barely speak.'
我拨了急救电话，清楚地告诉接线员：情况紧急，我爷爷摔倒了，话都说不清了。
The operator asked me a series of questions: is he conscious, is he breathing, what's your address.
接线员接连问我：他有意识吗？有呼吸吗？地址是哪里？
She told me to stay on the line and not to move him, and her steady voice slowed my heartbeat down.
她让我别挂电话、别挪动他，她平稳的声音让我的心跳都慢了下来。
She even said I was doing fine, which I really needed to hear at that moment.
她甚至说我做得很好，那一刻我太需要这句话了。
While waiting, I unlocked the door and turned on the entrance light for the medics.
等待时我打开了门锁，把楼道的灯也开了，方便医护进门。
The ambulance arrived in about six minutes, and the doctors later said the fast response saved part of his brain.
救护车六分钟左右就到了，医生后来说，反应快救回了他一部分脑功能。
Since that day I've kept a card with our address and his medical history by the phone.
从那天起，我在电话旁边放了一张卡片，写着家庭住址和他的病史。
In an emergency, the calmest voice in the room has to be yours.
危急关头，屋里最镇定的那个声音，只能是你自己的。

topics.question: When a family member is seriously ill, do you think relatives should stay at the hospital around the clock, or is resting at home more helpful?
topics.questionZh: 家人病重时，你认为亲属应该日夜守在医院，还是回家休息更好？
hints: 陪伴的心理意义
being there is all I can do for him
硬撑的代价
an exhausted guard helps nobody
轮流值守更合理
we made a schedule and both finally slept
病人真正需要什么
a cheerful room, not two exhausted faces
vocab: The one thing I can do is be here for him.
我唯一能做的就是守在他身边。
You need to get some rest.
他还处在镇静剂的作用下
sample: I believe relatives should take turns rather than compete over who suffers more at the hospital.
我认为家人应该轮班，而不是比谁在医院熬得更狠。
Two years ago I would probably have answered differently.
要是两年前，我的答案可能会不一样。
I formed this opinion during the week my father had heart surgery.
这个看法是在我父亲做心脏手术那一周形成的。
For the first two nights my brother refused to leave the ward at all.
头两个晚上，我弟弟一步都不肯离开病房。
He kept saying 'I can handle it', but he looked grey and hadn't eaten a proper meal.
他嘴上一直说我撑得住，可脸色灰败，一顿正经饭都没吃过。
He'd been the one who found Dad on the floor, and the guilt wouldn't let him go home.
当初发现爸爸倒在地上的人是他，内疚感让他回不了家。
The one thing he kept repeating was that being there was all he could do for Dad.
他翻来覆去只有一句话：守在这儿是我唯一能为爸爸做的。
I understood him, but I also saw that an exhausted guard helps nobody.
我理解他，但我也看得出来，累垮了的守夜人谁都帮不了。
So I told him gently that Dad was under sedation anyway and wouldn't even know who was sitting there.
于是我温和地提醒他：爸爸反正还在镇静状态，根本不知道坐在那儿的是谁。
We made a schedule: I took the nights, he took the days, and we both finally slept.
我们排了班：我守夜，他守白天，两个人总算都能睡了。
When Dad woke up, what he actually needed was a cheerful room, not two zombies.
爸爸醒来后，他真正需要的是一间气氛轻快的病房，而不是两个行尸走肉。
He told us to go home and get some rest, and for once we obeyed.
他让我们回家好好休息，这一回我们听话了。
A shift system also stops the family from quarrelling, which sadly happens a lot in hospitals.
轮班还能避免家人互相埋怨——可惜这种争吵在医院里太常见了。
Now I always say: taking care of yourself is part of taking care of the person you love.
现在我常说：照顾好自己，就是照顾所爱之人的一部分。

topics.question: If a doctor's explanation is difficult to understand, do you think asking for a second opinion is a good idea? Why?
topics.questionZh: 如果医生的解释很难听懂，你觉得再找另一位医生听听第二意见是好主意吗？为什么？
hints: 医学信息为何难懂
terms that ordinary people simply don't use daily
不懂装懂的后果
we nodded like students and signed
第二意见的经历
we insisted on getting a second opinion
就诊前的准备
prepare a list of questions and take notes
vocab: 再找一位医生看看（征求第二意见）
in no condition to undergo surgery
身体状况不适合做手术
我们往最好的方向期待
sample: Absolutely yes, and my family learned this lesson the hard way.
当然该问，我家是付出过代价才懂这个道理的。
Medicine is full of terms that ordinary people simply don't use in daily life.
医学里全是普通人日常生活根本用不到的词。
When my aunt was diagnosed with a heart problem, the first doctor spoke so fast that we understood almost nothing.
我姑姑查出心脏问题时，第一位医生语速快得我们几乎一句没懂。
He mentioned damaged arteries and poor pumping action, and then simply asked us to sign a form.
他提到动脉受损、泵血功能变差，然后就直接让我们签同意书。
We were too polite and too scared to ask questions.
我们又客气又害怕，一个问题都没敢问。
We nodded like students and signed, and my aunt cried the whole way home.
我们像学生一样点头签字，姑姑在回家路上哭了一路。
Her daughter then insisted on getting a second opinion at a bigger hospital.
后来她女儿坚持去更大的医院再听一位医生的意见。
There, a doctor spent twenty minutes drawing a picture of the heart and explaining why surgery was too risky in her current condition.
那位医生花了二十分钟画了颗心脏，解释以她目前的身体状况为什么不宜手术。
He told us they were considering every possible procedure, and introduced us to the chief of cardiology.
他告诉我们正在考虑所有可行的治疗手段，还把我们介绍给了心脏科主任。
The two plans matched, and strangely that made us feel calm rather than disappointed, because two matching opinions meant the diagnosis was solid.
两套方案完全一致，说来奇怪，这反而让我们安心而不是失望——两位医生说法一致，说明诊断靠得住。
After that, we always prepare a list of questions before any appointment, and two of us go together so one can take notes.
打那以后，每次就诊我们都提前列好问题清单，而且两个人同去，一个专门记笔记。
Doctors are experts, but they can't read our minds.
医生是专家，但他们不会读心术。
Asking again, or asking someone else, isn't rude; it's responsible.
多问一遍，或者换个人问，不是没礼貌，而是负责任。

topics.question: How well do you know your parents' health conditions and medical insurance? Do you think young people should know these things?
topics.questionZh: 你对自己父母的健康状况和医疗保险了解多少？你认为年轻人应该了解这些吗？
hints: 平时的疏忽
my honest answer would have been no
突发时才发现一无所知
asked to fill out forms about his insurance
该了解哪些信息
blood type, conditions, medication, insurance hotline
怎么开始补课
keep a card in your wallet and update it
vocab: I'm sorry to bother you at a time like this.
很抱歉在这种时候打扰你。
sample: Until three years ago, my honest answer would have been no, and that gap almost cost us.
三年前要老实回答这个问题，答案就是不了解，而这个空白差点让我们吃亏。
I only realised how little I knew when my father was suddenly hospitalised.
直到父亲突然住院，我才意识到自己知道得多么少。
At the payment window, an administrator asked me to fill out a couple of forms about his insurance.
在缴费窗口，管理员让我填几张关于他保险的表格。
I froze: I didn't know the name of his plan, his policy number, or even what medicine he took daily.
我当场愣住：我不知道他保险的名字、单号，甚至连他每天吃什么药都不知道。
The clerk was patient, but I could feel the queue behind me burning holes in my back.
窗口人员倒是有耐心，可我能感觉到身后排队的人的目光快把我后背烧穿了。
I only managed to say that he had high blood pressure and that his old employer's coverage was supposed to be good.
我只答上来他有高血压，以及老单位的医保应该还不错。
Later, in his flat, I found out he'd been feeling unwell for weeks and hiding it, with an empty fridge and his pills all mixed up.
后来在他家里，我才发现他身体不舒服已经好几个星期，一直瞒着，冰箱是空的，药片混在一起。
I felt ashamed, because noticing all this was never about love; it was about attention, and I hadn't paid any.
我特别羞愧：注意到这些从来不是爱不爱的问题，而是上不上心的问题，而我压根没上过心。
Now I keep a card in my wallet with his blood type, his conditions like high blood pressure, his medication list and the insurance hotline.
现在钱包里放着一张卡片：他的血型、高血压等病史、用药清单和医保热线。
Every time something changes, he teases me, but he tells me.
每次有变动，他都会笑我一句，但还是一五一十告诉我。
I'd urge every young person to do the same before an emergency forces the lesson on them.
我劝每个年轻人都趁早把这些弄清楚，别等一场急症把这一课硬塞给你。

topics.question: Do you think people should try to reconnect with a relative they haven't spoken to for many years?
topics.questionZh: 你认为应该尝试与多年不相往来的亲戚重新联系吗？
hints: 隔阂的起因与年限
they haven't talked to each other for thirty years
什么契机促成联系
a serious illness makes people rethink
谁先低头最难
someone has to pick up the phone first
和解后的意义
they made peace, and that mattered more
vocab: My father and uncle don't talk to each other.
我父亲和叔叔互不理睬。
I'll take the next flight out.
我这就赶下一班飞机过去。
sample: Yes, I do, and my family's story is the reason I feel so strongly about it.
我的答案是应该，而我们家的故事就是我说这话的底气。
My grandfather and his younger brother didn't talk to each other for almost thirty years.
我爷爷和他弟弟，差不多三十年互不理睬。
The quarrel was about a piece of farmland, and both of them were too proud to pick up the phone first.
吵架是为了一块地，两个人都太要面子，谁也不肯先拿起电话。
Even their wedding photos stopped appearing in the family album after that year.
从那年起，连两家的婚礼照片都不再出现在家庭相册里。
They sent greetings through relatives at Spring Festival, but never met, and my father grew up hardly knowing he had an uncle.
春节时靠亲戚捎句话，但从不见面，我爸从小几乎不知道自己还有个叔叔。
Then my grandfather had a stroke, and in the hospital he whispered that he wanted to see his brother.
后来爷爷中风了，在病房里他小声说想见弟弟。
My father gave it some thought overnight, found the number, and made the call.
我爸考虑了一整夜，找到号码，打了过去。
Honestly, none of us knew how the call would end.
说实话，谁也不知道这通电话会是什么结果。
He said he was afraid he had some bad news, and my great-uncle simply answered that he'd take the next flight out.
我爸说恐怕有个坏消息，叔公只回了一句：我赶下一班飞机过来。
The two old men met at the bedside, and after a long silence my grandfather said, 'We've been two stubborn fools.'
两个老人在病床边见了面，沉默了半天，爷爷说：咱们是两个倔老头。
They didn't solve the land question that day, but they made peace, and that mattered more.
地的事那天并没有解决，但他们和解了，而这才是更要紧的。
Watching them, I learned that time doesn't heal this kind of wound; someone has to reach out.
看着他们我明白了：这类伤口时间治不好，必须有人先伸出手。

topics.question: If you found out that a friend was probably being hurt by their partner, what would you do?
topics.questionZh: 如果你发现朋友很可能正在被伴侣伤害，你会怎么做？
hints: 留心异常信号
sunglasses indoors and long sleeves in summer
温和但直接的询问
what on earth happened to you?
明确表态：没有任何借口
there is no excuse for being hit, none
提供实际帮助
take photos of the bruises and see a counsellor
vocab: What on earth happened to you?
sample: If I suspected a friend was being hurt by a partner, I would speak up, carefully but firmly.
如果怀疑朋友正被伴侣伤害，我会开口——小心地，但坚定地。
Staying silent feels polite, but it often leaves someone alone with danger.
沉默显得有分寸，但那常常是把一个人单独留在危险里。
I know this because it happened to my college roommate, and I nearly missed it.
我之所以知道，是因为这发生在了我大学室友身上，而我差点没看出来。
For weeks she wore sunglasses indoors and long sleeves in summer, and joked about being clumsy.
好几周她室内戴墨镜、大热天穿长袖，还自嘲笨手笨脚。
I started noticing she flinched whenever her phone buzzed.
我还注意到，她的手机一震她整个人就缩一下。
When I finally asked what on earth had happened to her, she said she'd bumped into a door.
等我终于问她到底怎么了，她说自己撞到门上了。
Her wrist was all black-and-blue, and the door excuse simply didn't cover it.
她手腕青一块紫一块，撞门这个说法根本圆不上。
I didn't push, but I told her one thing very clearly: no matter what she had or hadn't done, there was no excuse for being hit, none.
我没有逼她，只把一件事说得很清楚：不管她做没做错什么，被打都没有任何借口，一点都没有。
She cried, then admitted the truth about her boyfriend.
她哭了，然后说了男朋友的实情。
I stayed with her that night, helped her photograph the bruises and pack a bag, and went with her to the campus counsellor the next morning.
那晚我陪着她，帮她给淤青拍照、收拾行李，第二天一早又陪她去见了学校咨询师。
The counsellor knew exactly which local services to call.
咨询师非常清楚该联系哪些本地救助机构。
It took her two attempts to leave him for good, and I never blamed her for going back the first time.
她用了两次才彻底离开那个人，她第一次回头时我没有责怪她。
What I learned is that victims rarely open up if you attack their partner loudly.
我学到的是：如果你激烈地攻击她的伴侣，受害者反而往往闭嘴。
Quiet questions, clear support and practical help do the real work.
起作用的是轻声的询问、明确的支持和实实在在的帮忙。

topics.question: When something terrible happens, some people keep their feelings inside. Do you think that is a healthy way to cope?
topics.questionZh: 遭遇巨大变故时，有些人把情绪都憋在心里。你认为这是健康的应对方式吗？
hints: 谁在憋着不说
he kept everything inside, exactly like our father
表面坚强的假象
people praised him for being so strong
不逼问的陪伴
show up with food and sit with him in silence
开口的转折点
one night, out of nowhere, he started talking
vocab: Your dad's always been a fighter.
sample: I don't think keeping feelings inside is healthy, though I completely understand why people do it.
我不认为把情绪憋在心里是健康的，尽管我完全理解人们为什么这么做。
The person I'm thinking of is my older brother, when our father passed away two years ago.
我想说的是我哥，两年前我父亲去世的时候。
At the funeral he shook every hand, answered every call, and organised everything perfectly.
葬礼上他跟每个人握手、接每一个电话，把所有事安排得妥妥帖帖。
People praised him for being so strong, but I could see he was a statue walking around.
大家都夸他坚强，可我看得出来，他只是一尊还能走动的雕像。
He kept everything inside, exactly like our father always had.
他把一切都憋在心里，跟我们父亲生前一模一样。
For weeks he said he was fine and went back to work after three days.
那几周他一直说自己没事，第三天就回去上班了。
I didn't force him to talk, because I knew that would just make him build higher walls.
我没有逼他说话，因为我知道那只会让他把墙砌得更高。
Instead I showed up with food, dragged him out for walks, and sat with him fixing his old bike in silence.
我只是带着饭出现，拉他出去散步，陪他一声不吭地修那辆旧自行车。
Then one night, out of nowhere, he started talking about Dad, and we stayed up till three in the morning.
后来某个晚上，他毫无预兆地开始聊起爸爸，我们一直聊到凌晨三点。
He said the house was too quiet, and that was all he could manage.
他说家里太安静了，说完这一句他就说不下去了。
That conversation didn't fix everything, but it was the first crack in the wall, in a good way.
那次长谈没有解决所有问题，但那是墙上裂开的第一道缝——好的那种。
Now I believe grief kept inside doesn't disappear; it just finds quieter ways to hurt people.
现在我相信，憋着的悲伤不会消失，只会换一些更安静的方式伤人。
Sometimes the best help is not advice but patient company.
有时最好的帮助不是建议，而是有耐心的陪伴。

topics.question: Describe the most difficult phone call you have ever had to make.
topics.questionZh: 描述你不得不打的最艰难的一通电话。
hints: 什么消息、打给谁
to my aunt far away, the night grandma died
拨号前的心情与准备
I wrote down three sentences and read them twenty times
怎么开口、对方反应
I'm afraid I have some bad news
事后的感悟
bad news should come from a person, never a text
vocab: I'm afraid I have some bad news
I'm so sorry to hear that.
sample: The hardest call I've ever made was to my aunt in Ireland, the night my grandmother died.
我打过的最难的电话，是奶奶去世那晚打给远在爱尔兰的姑姑的。
My father asked me to do it because his English wasn't good enough for such a moment.
是父亲让我打的，因为这样的时刻，他的英语不够用。
I wrote down three sentences beforehand and read them twenty times, but my voice still shook.
我提前写下三句话，念了二十遍，可拨通时声音还是在抖。
When she picked up, I said, 'I'm afraid I have some bad news — Grandma passed away this evening.'
她接起来时，我说：恐怕我有个坏消息——奶奶今天晚上去世了。
There was a silence that felt like a year, and then she just said, 'Oh, no, no, no.'
接着是一段像一年那么长的沉默，然后她只是说：不，不，不。
Hearing her cry on the other side of the world was almost unbearable.
听着她在地球另一端哭，我几乎承受不住。
I told her what little we knew, that it was sudden but peaceful, and that the wake would be the day after tomorrow.
我把仅知道的都告诉了她：走得很突然，但没有痛苦，守灵定在后天。
She asked about flights, and I promised to book her ticket and pick her up at the airport myself.
她问起航班，我答应帮她订票，并亲自去机场接她。
At the end she thanked me for calling, which felt strange, because calling was the least I could do.
最后她谢我打这通电话，这让我很惭愧，打电话不过是我能做的最起码的事。
That night taught me that bad news should come from a person, never from a text message.
那晚我明白：坏消息应该由一个人亲口说出来，绝不该是一条短信。
It also taught me that being the calm voice for someone else can hold you together too.
我还明白，做别人的那个镇定声音，反过来也能撑住你自己。
I still keep that draft of three sentences in my notes app, untouched.
那三句话的草稿，如今还原样留在我手机的备忘录里。

topics.question: Describe a time when two people you know ended a quarrel that had lasted for years.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你认识的两个人终于结束多年积怨、重归于好的经历。
hints: 积怨的起因与时长
they didn't speak to each other for eleven years
家人夹在中间的尴尬
the whole family walked on eggshells
促成和解的契机
a hospital stay changed everything
和解的场景与感悟
ready to forgive and forget
vocab: I wish it were under happier circumstances.
真希望是在更开心的场合见面。
sample: The two people in my story are my grandmother and her elder sister, who didn't speak for eleven years.
故事里的两个人是我外婆和她的姐姐，她们有十一年互不说话。
Their quarrel started over the sale of the old family house, and pride kept it alive.
起因是老房子卖掉的事，而面子让这场冷战一直持续。
Every Chinese New Year they sat at opposite ends of the table and pretended the other didn't exist.
每年春节，她们一个坐桌子这头、一个坐那头，假装对方不存在。
The whole family walked on eggshells around them at every gathering.
每次聚会，全家人在她们俩跟前都小心翼翼。
Then my great-aunt was hospitalised with pneumonia, and the doctor wasn't optimistic.
后来姨外婆因肺炎住了院，医生说情况不乐观。
My grandmother went quiet for a whole day, and finally asked me to drive her to the hospital.
外婆沉默了一整天，最后让我开车送她去医院。
At the bedside she said, 'We're two stubborn old women with short tempers and long memories, and I'm tired of it.'
病床边，外婆说：咱们是两个又倔、脾气又急、记性又长的老太婆，我过够了。
She said she was ready to forgive and forget if her sister was.
她说，只要姐姐愿意，她可以既往不咎。
My great-aunt just reached out and held her hand, and both of them cried.
姨外婆只是伸出手握住她，两个人都哭了。
I stood by the door, and honestly, I couldn't believe my eyes.
我站在门边，说实话，简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。
My great-aunt recovered, and now they call each other every Sunday like teenagers.
姨外婆后来康复了，现在她们每周日通电话，像两个小姑娘。
My grandmother told me she only wished it hadn't taken a hospital bed to end the silence.
外婆跟我说，她只可惜这场沉默竟要靠一张病床才结束。
Watching them, I decided I would never let pride run my family relationships.
看着她们，我下定决心：绝不让面子掌管我家里的关系。
Life is simply too short for long grudges.
人生实在太短，经不起太长的记仇。

topics.question: Describe a funeral or memorial event you attended, and how it made you feel.
topics.questionZh: 描述你参加过的一场葬礼或悼念活动，以及它带给你的感受。
hints: 谁的活动、什么形式
a wake from six to nine in the evening
到场的人与陌生感
I didn't know a soul there at first
让人动容的瞬间
an old colleague told stories about him
对告别式的新理解
funerals are really for the living
vocab: The wake is gonna be tomorrow
Thank you for making the trip.
sample: The memorial event I attended was my grandfather's wake last spring, and it changed how I think about funerals.
我参加的那场悼念活动，是去年春天我外公的守灵，它改变了我对葬礼的看法。
It was held at a funeral home, from six to nine in the evening, exactly as he had wished.
仪式设在殡仪馆，晚上六点到九点，完全按他生前的愿望安排。
His passing was a terrible shock to all of us, because it all happened so fast.
他的离世对我们全家是巨大的打击，一切都发生得太快了。
I arrived early with my parents and stood by the door, greeting people I didn't know.
我和父母早早到场，站在门口迎接着一张张陌生的面孔。
To be honest, I didn't know a soul there at first, which felt strange at my own grandfather's farewell.
说实话，起初那儿我一个人都不认识，在外公的告别式上，这感觉很奇怪。
Then the hall slowly filled: his old workmates, neighbours from our building, and relatives I'd only heard of.
大厅渐渐坐满：他的老同事、我们楼里的邻居，还有只听长辈提起过的亲戚。
When some old friends of Grandpa's arrived from another city, Dad shook their hands and thanked them for making the trip, and that small warmth made everyone smile through tears.
几位外公的老友从外地赶来时，爸爸握着他们的手，谢谢他们专程赶来，这点小小的暖意让所有人都含着泪笑了。
An old colleague gave a short speech about how grandfather once carried an injured workmate on his back to the hospital.
一位老同事做了简短致辞，讲外公曾背着重伤的工友一路跑到医院。
Hearing strangers tell these stories, I suddenly felt proud instead of only sad.
听陌生人讲这些往事，我忽然觉得骄傲，而不只是悲伤。
Late in the evening, a huge bunch of white flowers arrived, sent by an old friend who was too ill to travel.
傍晚时分，一大束白花送到了，是一位病得无法远行的老友订的。
That night taught me that funerals are really for the living.
那晚我懂得：葬礼其实是办给活人的。
They gather the pieces of a person's life and hand them back to the family.
它把一个人一生的碎片收拢起来，交还到家人手里。
I left grieving, yes, but also knowing my grandfather far better than before.
离开时我依然悲伤，但对外公的了解，也远超从前。
Now I understand why people say every goodbye is also a remembering.
现在我明白了，为什么人们说每一次告别，也都是一次重温。

topics.question: Describe an occasion when you learned something new and surprising about a family member.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你意外了解到家人全新一面的经历。
hints: 什么场合发现的
at the memorial gathering, a retired fireman came up to me
了解到什么往事
he saved two children but never mentioned it at home
当时的震撼
I felt like a stranger to my own family
之后的行动与建议
ask your elders while you can
vocab: I don't know a soul here.
这儿我一个人都不认识。
worked with Dad at the fire department
和父亲在消防队共过事
我简直不敢相信自己的眼睛！
used to get Christmas cards from her
以前每年都收到她的圣诞卡
sample: I used to think I knew my grandfather completely, until his memorial gathering proved me wrong.
我一直以为自己足够了解外公，直到那场悼念活动证明我错了。
It turned out there was a whole side of him I'd never met.
原来他还有整整一面，是我从未见过的。
That afternoon, a retired fireman came up to me and asked whether I was his grandson.
那天下午，一位退休消防员走到我跟前，问我是不是他外孙。
He said he had worked with my grandfather at the fire department for fifteen years.
他说他和外公在消防队共事了十五年。
Then he told me that my grandfather had saved two children from a burning building in the eighties and never mentioned it to anyone at home.
接着他告诉我，外公在八十年代从着火的楼里救出过两个孩子，而这件事他对家里一个字都没提过。
He said the whole station had a nickname for my grandfather: 'the quiet hero'.
他说整个消防站都给我外公起了个外号，叫'沉默的英雄'。
I stood there feeling like a stranger to my own family.
我站在那里，觉得自己像自己家里的外人。
Another neighbour remembered him fixing radios for free for half the street.
还有位邻居记得，他曾免费帮半条街的人修收音机。
Later I found an old photo of him young, in uniform, laughing with friends I couldn't name.
后来我翻到一张他年轻时的照片：穿着制服，和一群我叫不上名字的朋友大笑。
I realised we had boxes of photos at home and nobody left who could explain them all.
我意识到家里有成箱的照片，却已经没有几个人能讲清它们了。
Since then, I've started asking my parents and uncles questions at every family dinner.
从那以后，每次家宴我都会拉着父母和舅舅们问东问西。
Small things: who was this person, why did they stop writing, what was Grandpa like at thirty.
都是小事：这个人是谁，为什么后来不再通信，外公三十岁时什么样。
I even recorded two of my grandmother's stories on my phone.
我甚至用手机录下了外婆讲的两段往事。
My advice to anyone is to ask your elders while you can, because funerals tell you facts, but only the living tell you stories.
我给每个人的建议是：趁长辈还在赶紧问，因为葬礼只告诉你事实，只有活着的人才能讲出故事。

topics.question: Do you think a quick, sincere apology can stop a small family argument from getting worse? Use your own experience to explain.
topics.questionZh: 你认为一句及时而真诚的道歉，能阻止家庭小争吵恶化吗？请结合自身经历说明。
hints: 危机中人更容易吵架
exhausted and scared is perfect fuel for fights
为琐事争执的经过
we argued about who forgot the charger
道歉的时机与方式
I handed over some change and said sorry first
和好后的默契
put the relationship above your pride
vocab: I'm sorry I yelled at you.
sample: I genuinely believe one sincere apology can stop a family argument from poisoning everything.
我真心相信，一句真诚的道歉能阻止家庭争吵把一切搞坏。
My brother and I tested this during the hardest week of our lives, at the hospital.
我和我哥在人生最难的那一周、在医院里验证了这一点。
Our father was critically ill, and we were both exhausted and scared, which is perfect fuel for fights.
父亲病情危重，我们俩又累又怕，而这是吵架的完美燃料。
We argued about tiny things: who would sign a form, who forgot the charger, whose turn it was to buy water.
我们净为鸡毛蒜皮吵：谁去签字、谁忘了拿充电器、轮到谁买水。
At some point I raised my voice at him in the corridor, and he walked away without a word.
有一次我在走廊里冲他喊了起来，他一言不发地走开了。
A nurse gave us a look that could have frozen the hallway.
一位护士看了我们一眼，那一眼能把整条走廊冻住。
The next evening we ran into each other at a vending machine that wouldn't take his coins.
第二天傍晚，我们在一台不收他硬币的自动售货机前碰上了。
I dug out some change, handed it over, and said, 'I'm sorry I yelled at you.'
我掏出零钱递过去，说：对不起，我昨天冲你嚷嚷了。
He looked at me and said, 'That's all right,' and that was the end of the war.
他看了看我，说：没事了。战争就这么结束了。
We sat on the bench sharing one bottle of water and finally talked about the thing we were actually afraid of: losing Dad.
我们坐在长椅上分喝一瓶水，终于聊起了真正害怕的那件事：失去爸爸。
Funny how seventy-five cents can repair what a whole speech couldn't.
真有意思，七毛五分钱的硬币，能修复一整篇道理都修复不了的东西。
That moment taught me that in a crisis, families need each other, not perfect decisions.
那一刻让我明白：危急之中，家人需要的是彼此，不是完美的决定。
Saying sorry first isn't losing; it's putting the relationship above your pride.
先道歉不是认输，是把感情放在面子前面。
Now whenever tension builds at home, I try to be the one who breaks it first.
现在家里气氛一紧，我都试着先做那个打破僵局的人。

topics.question: Describe a funeral or memorial event you attended that stayed with you. What happened, and how did you feel?
topics.questionZh: 描述一场你参加过的、令你难忘的葬礼或追悼会。当时发生了什么？你有什么感受？
hints: 背景：谁的追悼会、在哪举行
the memorial service for my grandfather / held at a small funeral home
印象深刻的一个环节
his old colleagues came up and said a couple of words / presented the family with his helmet
你自己的角色
I stood up and said a few words about him
感受与思考
it hit me all at once / I realised how many lives he had touched
vocab: I'm gonna miss the pleasure of his company
我会怀念有他相伴的快乐
sample: Well, the memorial service I'll never forget was for my grandfather on my mother's side, who passed away suddenly two years ago.
嗯，我永远忘不了的追悼会，是两年前突然离世的外公的那一场。
The whole family gathered at a small funeral home near his old neighbourhood, and the room was completely full.
全家人聚集在他老居民区附近的一家小殡仪馆，屋子里坐得满满当当。
What moved me most was a gesture from his old workplace.
最让我动容的是他老单位的一个举动。
Two of his former colleagues stood up, said they wished to express their deepest sympathy, and then presented our family with his work helmet, in recognition of his thirty years of service.
他的两位老同事站起来，说他们谨致以最深切的慰问，然后把他当年的工作头盔赠给我们家，以表彰他三十年的辛勤工作。
After that, an old friend of his came up to say a couple of words.
之后，他的一位老朋友上前讲了几句话。
He told us, 'He probably never told you this, but he saved my neck more than once. If you ever need anything, please call on me.' I was in tears.
他告诉我们：'他可能从没跟你们说过，但他不止一次救过我的命。你们要是需要任何帮助，随时来找我。'我一下子就哭了。
Later, people came by for a second just to pay their respects — old neighbours, former workmates, even his chess partners.
后来，老邻居、老同事，甚至他的棋友们，都顺路过来短暂停留，向他致以敬意。
Some of them I'd never met before, and it struck me how many lives he had quietly touched.
有些人我从未见过，那一刻我才意识到，他悄悄影响过多少人的生活。
To be honest, I didn't cry at first; it all felt unreal.
说实话，起初我并没有哭；一切都感觉不真实。
But when I stood up and said a few words about him myself, my voice shook, and everything hit me at once.
可当我自己站起来讲了几句时，我的声音发抖，所有情绪一下子涌了上来。
I simply told everyone I was gonna miss the pleasure of his company, and that was enough.
我只告诉大家，我会怀念有他相伴的快乐，这就足够了。

topics.question: Describe an older person you know who had simple dreams. What were those dreams, and did they come true?
topics.questionZh: 描述一位你认识的、怀有朴素梦想的长辈。他们的梦想是什么？实现了吗？
hints: 是谁、和你的关系
my grandfather on my mother's side / a retired factory worker
他/她的小梦想是什么
he dreamed of a little house with a garden / going fishing on a deep-sea boat
为什么没实现
life got in the way / he always put the family first
你从中学到什么
dreams don't have to be big to matter
vocab: not big dreams, but small ones
不是大梦想，而是小梦想
a little house with a garden
provide a shoulder to lean on
sample: The person I'd like to talk about is my grandfather, a retired factory worker who lived a very plain life.
我想说的是我外公，一位退休工人，一辈子过得很朴素。
To be honest, he wasn't famous or successful in the usual sense, but he had dreams — not big dreams, but small ones.
说实话，按一般标准他既不出名也不算成功，但他有梦想——不是大梦想，而是小小的梦想。
His biggest dream was to go fishing on one of those deep-sea fishing boats, just once, with his old workmates.
他最大的梦想，就是和老工友们一起，坐一回深海渔船去钓鱼，哪怕一次也好。
He talked about it every summer, but somehow he never did it — there was always something more urgent: my grandmother's medicine, my father's tuition, repairs to the house.
每年夏天他都念叨这件事，可不知怎么就是没去成——总有更紧急的事：外婆的药钱、我爸的学费、房子要修。
He also dreamed of a little house with a garden, where he could grow tomatoes and sit in the sun.
他还梦想有一栋带小花园的小房子，可以在里面种西红柿、晒晒太阳。
Sadly, neither dream came true.
遗憾的是，两个梦想都没实现。
When he retired, his health was already failing, and he passed away before we could take him to the sea.
退休时他身体已经不行了，没等我们带他去看海，他就走了。
But here's the thing: I never once heard him complain.
但奇怪的是，我从没听他抱怨过一句。
He always said he'd had a good life, and he provided a shoulder to lean on for everyone in the family.
他总说自己这辈子过得挺好，而且他是全家人可以依靠的肩膀。
I think about him a lot, especially when I'm chasing big goals.
我常常想起他，尤其是在追逐大目标的时候。
He taught me that dreams don't have to be grand to make a life meaningful.
他让我明白，梦想不必宏大，也能让一生有意义。
He had a big heart, and honestly, that matters more than any dream coming true.
他心地宽厚，说实话，这比任何梦想成真都更重要。

topics.question: What do you think is the best way to comfort someone who has just lost a loved one?
topics.questionZh: 你认为安慰一个刚刚失去亲人的人，最好的方式是什么？
hints: 观点：陪伴和行动比完美的话重要
being there matters more than saying the right words
具体可以做的事
walk her home / sit with her in silence / check on her every few days
别人什么做法打动人
an old friend said 'if you ever need anything, call on me'
避免什么
avoid vague offers / don't disappear after the funeral
vocab: He saved my neck more than once
sample: In my view, the best way to comfort someone who has just lost a loved one is simply to be there — practical support matters far more than finding perfect words.
在我看来，安慰刚失去亲人的人，最好的方式就是陪在身边——实际的支持远比说出完美的话重要。
People often worry about saying the wrong thing, but honestly, presence is the message.
人们常常怕说错话，但说实话，人到场本身就是最好的话。
I learned this when my classmate lost her father last year.
去年我同学失去父亲时，我明白了这一点。
At first I didn't know what to say, so I just told her, 'I'm so sorry. It's such a shame — he wasn't all that old.'
起初我不知道说什么，只能对她说：'我很遗憾。太让人难过了——他还没那么老。'
Then, instead of giving advice, I did small things: I walked her home, sat with her in silence, and checked on her every few days.
之后我没有讲道理，而是做些小事：陪她回家、安静地陪她坐着、每隔几天去看看她。
I remember thinking my words were useless, but she said later that my being there was what got her through.
我记得当时觉得自己的话毫无用处，但她后来说，正是我陪着，她才撑了过来。
What helped her most, she told me later, was when people shared stories about her father instead of avoiding his name.
她后来告诉我，最让她温暖的，是大家讲起她父亲的往事，而不是刻意回避他的名字。
Her father's old friend said, 'He saved my neck more than once. If you ever need anything, and I mean anything, please call on me.' That kind of concrete offer beats a hundred polite phrases.
她父亲的老朋友说：'他不止一次救过我的命。你们需要任何帮助，我是说任何事，都请来找我。'这种具体的承诺，胜过一百句客套话。
So my advice is: show up, listen more than you talk, and offer specific help rather than vague ones.
所以我的建议是：出现，多听少说，提供具体的帮助而不是空泛的客套。
And when you leave, a simple 'take care' — and actually coming back next week — means everything.
临走时一句'保重'，以及下周真的再回来，比什么都重要。

topics.question: Describe a time when a close friend made a decision about a relationship that you disagreed with. What did you do?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次好友做出让你不认同的感情决定。你当时是怎么做的？
hints: 什么情况、朋友的决定
she went back to a boyfriend who treated her badly
她为什么回去
he promised never to do it again / she said they had talked it over
你的反应与担心
I'd been calling and calling / I couldn't believe it
你怎么处理：不吵架但守住底线
I said 'I'm here, whatever happens' / I kept in touch without lecturing her
vocab: He's promised never to do it again
他保证再也不会那样了
You mean you're going back to him?
你是说你要回到他身边？
我一遍又一遍地打电话
sample: A situation I remember well involved my close friend from high school, who went back to a boyfriend who treated her badly.
我记得很清楚的一件事，是我的高中好友回到了一个对她很糟糕的男朋友身边。
We were both nineteen at the time.
那时我们都十九岁。
He had a bad temper, and one night she showed up at my door with a bruise on her arm.
他脾气很坏，一天晚上她出现在我家门口，胳膊上有淤青。
I'd been calling and calling that day because she hadn't answered, and I'd been worried about her all evening.
那天我一直打电话她都不接，整个晚上我都提心吊胆。
When she finally admitted what happened, I asked her directly, 'Did he hit you again?'
等她终于说出实情，我直接问她：'他又打你了？'
She said no, that they had talked, and that he'd promised never to do it again.
她说不是，说他们谈过了，他保证再也不会那样了。
I couldn't believe it when she said she was going back to him.
听到她说要回去，我简直不敢相信。
I asked, 'You mean you're going back to him?' — and she just nodded.
我问：'你是说你要回到他身边？'她只是点了点头。
Everything in me wanted to grab her and argue, but I'd learned that anger only pushes people away.
我心里特别想拉住她大吵一架，但我知道愤怒只会把人越推越远。
So I said quietly, 'I can't make this choice for you, but I'm here, whatever happens.'
于是我平静地说：'这个选择我替你做不了，但无论发生什么，我都在。'
For the next few months I kept in touch without lecturing her.
之后几个月，我一直和她保持联系，从不说教。
Eventually she left him for good, and she told me the reason she could walk away was knowing the door was always open.
最终她彻底离开了那个人。她告诉我，之所以能下决心走，是因为知道我这扇门永远开着。
That experience taught me: you can disagree with a friend's decision and still stand by the friend.
那段经历教会我：你可以不认同朋友的决定，但依然站在朋友身边。

topics.question: Describe a time when neighbours or your community helped your family through a difficult period.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次邻居或社区帮助你们家渡过难关的经历。
hints: 什么困难时期
the weeks after my grandfather passed away / a family emergency
邻居做了什么
she dropped a casserole off at our door / sent cards with warm wishes
别人如何表达心意
one family made a donation in memory of him / you are in our prayers
感受与回报
a considerate neighbour is worth more than relatives far away / kindness goes around
vocab: make a donation in memory of
sample: I'd like to talk about the weeks after my grandfather passed away, when our neighbours really carried my family through.
我想讲的是外公去世后的那几个星期，是邻居们帮我们家撑了过来。
It was a hard time — my parents were busy with the funeral and everything, and none of us had the energy to cook.
那段日子很难——爸妈忙着料理后事，谁都没有力气做饭。
Our next-door neighbour, an elderly lady, dropped a big casserole off at our door on the second day.
第二天，隔壁一位上了年纪的阿姨就在我家门口放了一大锅热菜。
She didn't stay long; she just squeezed my mother's hand and said to call her if we needed anything.
她没多待，只是握了握我妈的手，说有事就打电话给她。
Other neighbours sent cards with warm wishes — one family even made a donation to the heart association in memory of my grandfather.
别的邻居送来写满祝福的卡片，还有一家以纪念我外公的名义向心脏协会捐了款。
My mother kept rereading those cards; she said 'you are in our prayers' meant more than any gift.
我妈把那些卡片翻来覆去地读，她说'我们为你们祈祷'比任何礼物都珍贵。
What impressed me was how quiet and considerate it all was.
让我触动的是，这一切都做得安静又周到。
Nobody made a fuss; they just appeared with food, took out our rubbish, and looked after my little brother when my parents were at the funeral home.
没有人兴师动众，他们就是默默送来饭菜、帮我们倒垃圾，在爸妈守在殡仪馆时帮忙照看我弟弟。
Our community proved that a considerate neighbour is worth more than a dozen relatives far away.
那段经历让我明白：一位好邻居，胜过远方的十几个亲戚。
Because of that, whenever a neighbour is in trouble now, my mother is the first one at their door with a pot of soup.
正因如此，现在只要有邻居遇上难处，我妈总是第一个端着一锅汤上门的人。
That's how kindness goes around, I guess.
我想，善意就是这样传递下去的。

topics.question: Describe an experience of sorting through the belongings of a family member who passed away. What did you find, and how did you feel?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次整理已故亲人遗物的经历。你找到了什么？感受如何？
hints: 什么时候、整理什么
we cleaned out my grandmother's room after the funeral
发现的旧物
shirts that must have been twenty years old / old papers and photos
一件意外发现的东西
a photo of relatives we'd never met / a letter in an old tin box
怎么处理这些东西
we gave most clothes to charity / kept the small things that mattered
vocab: give some things to the Salvation Army
把一些东西捐给慈善组织
It makes me sad to come in here
These shirts must be twenty years old
这些衬衫肯定有二十年了
Someday I'd like to go to Ireland
总有一天我想去爱尔兰
sample: After my grandmother passed away, my mother and I had to clean out her room, and that experience stayed with me.
外婆去世后，我和妈妈要整理她的房间，那段经历一直留在我心里。
It took us a whole weekend, and we cried and laughed the entire time.
那花了我们整整一个周末，我们一路哭着又笑着。
The room still smelled like her, so honestly, it made me sad just to walk in.
房间里还有她的味道，说实话，光是走进去就让人难过。
We started with the wardrobe and found shirts that must have been twenty years old, all neatly folded and mended.
我们从衣柜整理起，发现了肯定有二十年历史的衬衫，都叠得整整齐齐、缝缝补补过。
My grandmother lived by 'waste not, want not' — she never threw away anything that still worked.
外婆信奉'勤俭不愁缺'——凡是还能用的东西，她从来不扔。
Then, in an old tin box at the back of a drawer, we found a treasure.
后来，在抽屉最里面的一个旧铁盒里，我们发现了宝贝。
There were papers, some old photos, and a letter from a relative we'd never even heard of.
里面有证件、几张老照片，还有一封我们从来没听说过的亲戚写来的信。
One photo showed cousins of my mother living overseas — they looked surprisingly like her.
有张照片上是旅居海外的妈妈的表亲，长得和她像极了。
My mother held it for a long time and whispered, 'Someday I'd like to go and meet them.'
我妈捧着照片看了很久，轻声说：'总有一天，我要去见见他们。'
In the end, we gave most of the clothes to a charity shop, but we kept the photos, the letter, and one of those old shirts.
最后，我们把大部分衣物捐给了慈善商店，但留下了照片、那封信和一件旧衬衫。
It's strange: the cheapest things turned out to be the most precious.
很奇怪：最不值钱的东西，反倒成了最珍贵的。
Going through her belongings made her feel close again, and it taught me that objects can hold a whole life.
整理遗物让我们觉得她仿佛又回到身边，也让我懂得：物件可以装下一个人的一生。

topics.question: Do you think older siblings should take responsibility for their younger brothers and sisters? Use your own experience to explain.
topics.questionZh: 你认为哥哥姐姐应该为弟弟妹妹承担责任吗？请结合自身经历说明。
hints: 观点：关心自然，但不能越界当父母
caring is natural, but you can't act like their parent
你的经历
our parents went to another city for work / I looked after my sixteen-year-old brother
出现的矛盾
he exploded: 'stop acting like my mother' / I had butted in too much
学到的边界
persuade instead of ordering / respect them as adults
vocab: I'm not a baby, and you're not my mother
我不是小孩，你也不是我妈
sample: I'd say yes — up to a point. Older siblings naturally feel responsible for younger ones, but there's a line between caring and controlling.
我要说：是——但有限度。哥哥姐姐自然而然会为弟弟妹妹操心，但关心和控制之间有条线。
In Chinese families this is quite common, especially when parents are absent or busy.
在中国家庭这很常见，尤其是父母不在身边或特别忙的时候。
I know this from my own life.
这一点我自己深有体会。
When our parents went to another city for work for a year, I looked after my younger brother, who was sixteen.
父母去外地工作的一年里，由我照看十六岁的弟弟。
I cooked, paid the bills, and basically became the adult of the house.
我做饭、付账单，基本上成了家里的'大人'。
At first I checked everything: his homework, his friends, even his phone.
一开始我什么都管：作业、朋友，甚至他的手机。
Finally he exploded: 'Stop acting like my mother! I'm not a baby, and you're not my mother!'
终于他爆发了：'别再像我妈一样！我不是小孩，你也不是我妈！'
That hurt, because I was only trying to help.
那句话很伤人，因为我只是想帮忙。
But later I realised I had butted in too much, exactly like the classic overprotective big sister.
但后来我意识到，我确实管得太多了，就是那种典型的爱插手的老姐。
So I changed my approach: instead of giving orders, I tried to persuade — 'Could I persuade you to consider this?' became my opening line.
于是我换了方式：不再下命令，而是试着说服——'我能劝你考虑一下这个吗？'成了我的开场白。
We also made a deal to write down all our options whenever we disagreed, and then choose together.
我们还约定，每次意见不合就把所有选择写下来，再一起决定。
Interestingly, once I stopped controlling him, he actually asked for my advice more often.
有意思的是，我不控制他之后，他反而更常来征求我的意见。
So my conclusion is: support your siblings, be there when it counts, but respect them as adults — otherwise love becomes a burden.
所以我的结论是：支持你的弟弟妹妹，关键时刻在场，但要尊重他们是独立的人——否则爱就变成了负担。

topics.question: Describe a time when something happened that you found hard to accept or believe. How did you deal with it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你难以接受或难以相信的事情。你是怎么走出来的？
hints: 什么事情
the sudden death of my uncle / a loss without any warning
当时不真实的感觉
it just doesn't feel real / it's like he went away for the weekend
什么时候真正意识到
it hit me when I saw his slippers by the door
如何慢慢接受
talking with family / grief comes in waves
vocab: It's like he just went away for the weekend
就好像他只是出门度周末
sample: The moment I found hardest to accept was the sudden death of my uncle, who was like a second father to me.
我最难接受的，是舅舅的突然离世，他就像我的第二个父亲。
I saw him at dinner every Friday for as long as I can remember.
从我记事起，每周五的晚饭都能见到他。
He had a heart attack at fifty-two, with no warning at all.
他五十二岁突发心脏病，事先毫无征兆。
For weeks afterwards, it just didn't feel real.
之后的几个星期，一切都不像真的。
I kept thinking it's like he just went away for the weekend and would walk in with takeaway food, shouting hello.
我总觉得他只是出门度周末了，随时会拎着外卖推门进来打招呼。
No kidding — my brain simply refused the fact.
真的不夸张——我的大脑就是拒绝接受这个事实。
At his funeral I watched everything like a spectator, dry-eyed and numb.
葬礼上我像个旁观者一样看着一切，没有眼泪，只有麻木。
The strange thing is where it finally hit me.
奇怪的是，真正被击中的地点很意外。
A month later I visited his flat, saw his slippers by the door, and suddenly understood: he's not coming back.
一个月后我去他的公寓，看见门口的拖鞋，突然明白了：他不会再回来了。
I sat on his sofa and cried for an hour.
我在他的沙发上哭了整整一个小时。
What helped me get through all of this was talking — my aunt let me tell the same stories about him over and over, and never got tired of listening.
帮我撑过这一切的是倾诉——舅妈任由我把同样的往事翻来覆去地讲，从不嫌烦。
Slowly, the unreal feeling faded into ordinary missing.
慢慢地，那种不真实感淡去，变成了平常的想念。
Now I understand grief isn't a switch; it arrives in waves, and you just have to let them come.
现在我懂了：悲伤不是一按就关的开关，它是一波波涌来的，你只能让它来。

topics.question: Describe an old object or piece of jewellery in your family that has special meaning. What is its story?
topics.questionZh: 描述一件你们家里有特殊意义的老物件或首饰。它背后有什么故事？
hints: 是什么物件
a silver ring passed down for four generations
它的来历
my great-great-grandmother brought it when the family moved
上面的含义或刻字
the hands mean friendship, the crown means loyalty
将来传给谁
it's always passed to the youngest daughter / one day I'll pass it on
vocab: 一枚古老的爱尔兰戒指
The hands mean friendship, and the crown means loyalty
双手代表友谊，皇冠代表忠诚
sample: The object I want to talk about is a silver ring that has been in my family for four generations.
我想说的物件，是一枚在我们家传了四代的银戒指。
We call it our family ring.
我们管它叫'传家戒'。
It's not valuable — you couldn't sell it for much — but for us it's priceless.
它并不值钱——卖不出什么高价——但对我们家来说它无价。
It was my great-great-grandmother's, and she brought it with her when the family moved across the country a century ago.
它是我太祖母的，一百年前全家迁徙时她随身带着它。
There's something engraved on the inside, in the old dialect, which the family says means 'love, friendship and loyalty.'
戒指内侧刻着字，是老家的方言，家里人说是'爱、友谊与忠诚'的意思。
My grandmother explained it to me like a story: the heart means love, the hands mean friendship, and the crown means loyalty.
外婆像讲故事一样给我解释：心代表爱，双手代表友谊，皇冠代表忠诚。
The ring is always passed to the youngest daughter, so it went to my grandmother, then my mother.
这枚戒指总是传给最小的女儿，所以先到了外婆手里，再到我妈手上。
When my mother gave it to me on my eighteenth birthday, she said, 'It must have been Grandma's — now it's yours to keep.'
我十八岁生日那天，妈妈把它交给我，她说：'这一定是外婆传下来的——现在由你保管了。'
To be honest, I rarely wear it; it stays in a small box on my desk.
说实话我很少戴，它一直放在我书桌上的小盒子里。
But whenever I look at it, I think of the women who wore it before me.
可每当看到它，我就会想起在我之前戴过它的那些女性。
Isn't it beautiful, how one small circle can hold a whole family's history?
一个小小的圆环，竟能装下一个家族的历史，多奇妙啊。
One day I'll pass it on, and I hope the story goes with it.
总有一天我也会传下去，我希望故事能跟着它一起传下去。

topics.question: Describe a time when you discovered a surprising or touching side of someone you knew well.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你发现熟悉的某人身上令人意外或感人一面的经历。
hints: 谁、什么契机
after my grandfather passed away, we opened the old trunk in his study
发现了什么
letters he never showed us / a program from a school play I was in
为什么意外
I didn't know he was so sentimental / he never talked about feelings
对这个人新的认识
he cared more than he ever said
vocab: I had no idea he kept all this
我完全不知道他保存着这一切
I didn't know he was so sentimental
我不知道他这么多愁善感
把这一切都悄悄收藏着
I guess your father was thinking of you
我想你父亲一直记挂着你
a woman he saved in the hotel fire
他在酒店大火中救出的女士
sample: This happened after my grandfather passed away, when my father and I finally opened the old trunk he kept in his study.
这件事发生在外公去世后，我和爸爸终于打开了他书房里那只旧箱子。
My grandfather was a quiet, serious man — or so we all thought.
外公是个沉默严肃的人——至少我们一直这么以为。
Inside, we found things we never knew existed.
箱子里有我们从来不知道存在的东西。
There were old letters, his army papers, and — this is the part that killed me — a program from a school play I was in when I was seven.
有旧信件、他的服役证明，还有最让我受不了的——一张我七岁那年参加学校演出的节目单。
He had kept it for over fifteen years, perfectly flat, in an envelope with my name on it.
他保存了它十五年多，平平整整，装在一个写着我名字的信封里。
It's amazing what people stash away.
人悄悄收藏的东西，真让人惊叹。
My father just said quietly, 'I had no idea he kept all this. I didn't know he was so sentimental.'
爸爸只是轻声说：'我完全不知道他存着这些。没想到他这么多愁善感。'
There was another surprise: a thank-you letter from a woman he saved in a hotel fire, years before I was born.
还有个惊喜：一封感谢信，来自一位在我出生前多年、他在酒店大火中救出的女士。
He never mentioned it to anyone.
这件事他对谁都没提过。
It made me rethink him completely — the strict old man who scolded us at dinner was quietly proud, grateful and loving all along.
这让我彻底重新认识了他——那个在饭桌上训我们的严厉老人，其实一直悄悄地骄傲着、感恩着、爱着我们。
I guess he was thinking of us far more than he ever showed.
我想，他心里记挂我们的程度，远比表现出来的多。
That day changed how I remember him.
那天改变了我记忆中他的样子。
Now, when I think of him, I don't see the serious face; I see a man carefully folding a child's program into an envelope.
现在想起他，我看到的不再是那张严肃的脸，而是一个把孩子的节目单仔细折好、装进信封的老人。

topics.question: Do you think it is a good thing for young people to come into a large sum of money suddenly? Why or why not?
topics.questionZh: 你认为年轻人突然得到一大笔钱是好事吗？为什么？
hints: 观点：是礼物更是考验
it's a test as much as a gift
钱容易带来的冲动
the temptation to buy a motorcycle or a laptop right away
更稳妥的做法
put it towards education / cover the bills first / ask an adult you trust
例子/故事
one minute you're broke, and the next minute you're loaded
vocab: One minute we're broke, and the next minute we're loaded
前一分钟还身无分文，下一分钟就腰缠万贯
我们这是发财了还是怎么的？
sample: Personally, I think a sudden windfall is a test as much as a gift — and many young people fail it.
就我个人而言，突然而来的横财与其说是礼物，不如说是考验——而很多年轻人过不了这一关。
Money that arrives without effort is easily spent without thought.
轻易得来的钱，花起来也毫不心疼。
I remember watching this happen to a friend of mine.
我亲眼见过这种事发生在我朋友身上。
After his father died, an old insurance policy paid out, and suddenly he was rich — one minute you're broke, and the next minute you're loaded.
他父亲去世后，一份旧人寿保险赔了下来，他突然就'富'了——前一分钟还穷得叮当响，后一分钟就腰缠万贯。
'Are we rich, or what?' he kept saying, while making lists: a motorcycle, a laptop, the newest phone.
他不停念叨'我们这是发财了还是怎么的？'一边列清单：摩托车、笔记本电脑、最新款手机。
His sister had to remind him, 'Try to remember why we're getting this money.'
他姐姐只好提醒他：'想想我们拿这笔钱的缘由。'
To his credit, he calmed down.
难得的是，他冷静了下来。
They cashed in some savings bonds, covered the bills, and put the rest towards college.
他们把一些储蓄债券兑现，付清账单，剩下的都留作上大学用。
The insurance company even made them wait months for the cheque, which turned out to be a good cooling-off period.
保险公司还让他们等了好几个月才拿到支票，事后证明这段冷静期反而是好事。
Later he told me the scariest part was how fast the money felt unreal — like game points, not years of someone's work.
后来他告诉我，最可怕的是那笔钱很快就变得不真实——像游戏点数，而不是某人多年的辛劳。
So my view is: sudden money does more good than harm only if there's guidance.
所以我的看法是：只有有人指引，意外之财才利大于弊。
Without a plan, it's not a blessing; it's a trap with a bow on it.
没有计划，它就不是福，而是包装精美的陷阱。
If I came into money tomorrow, I'd probably lock it away for six months before touching a coin.
要是明天我得了笔钱，我很可能会先锁上六个月，再碰一分。

topics.question: Do you think sharing an apartment with friends is a good idea? What problems can it cause?
topics.questionZh: 你认为和朋友合租公寓是好主意吗？可能产生什么问题？
hints: 观点：可以，但选对人、立规矩
it works if you choose roommates carefully / set rules first
好处
split the rent four ways / company and fun
潜在问题
someone couldn't cover the rent / friends got thrown out of their apartment
相处之道
a house meeting / someone has to keep everyone in line
vocab: get thrown out of an apartment
sample: I think sharing a flat with friends can work brilliantly, but it depends entirely on choosing the right friends — and writing down some rules first.
我认为和朋友合租完全可以相处得很好，但成败全在选对人，并事先立好规矩。
In China, renting with classmates after graduation is really common now.
在中国，毕业后和同学合租现在非常普遍。
I shared an apartment with three university classmates in my second year, and we split the rent four ways, which made life much cheaper.
大二时我和三个同学合租，四个人分摊房租，日子一下轻松了不少。
Compared with dorms, it felt like real adult life.
和宿舍比，那才像真正的大人生活。
We had fun — cooking together, playing games at midnight — but we also saw each other's worst sides.
我们过得很开心——一起做饭、半夜打游戏——但也见识了彼此最难堪的一面。
The trouble came when one roommate lost his part-time job and couldn't cover the rent for two months.
麻烦来了：一个室友丢了兼职，连着两个月付不起房租。
We covered for him at first, but tensions grew, and honestly the friendship nearly broke.
起初我们帮他垫付，但气氛越来越僵，说实话友谊差点就断了。
I remembered a story about some guys who got thrown out of their apartment — I really didn't want that to be us.
我想起听说过的一伙人被房东赶出公寓的事，真不希望那是我们的下场。
So I called a house meeting and set rules: rent on the first of the month, a shared budget, and a warning system — someone had to keep us all in line.
于是我召集了一次'家庭会议'，立下规矩：每月一号交房租、共用账本、违规警告——总得有个人让大家守规矩。
It worked; he found a new job, paid us back, and we're still friends today.
规矩奏效了；他找到新工作，还清了钱，我们至今还是好朋友。
My conclusion: go in with your eyes open — your funniest friend can be your most annoying roommate.
我的结论是：入伙前要想清楚——最能逗你笑的朋友，也可能是最让你抓狂的室友。

topics.question: Describe a food you tried for the first time that you were not sure about. Did you like it in the end?
topics.questionZh: 描述一种你第一次尝试时心里没底的食物。最后你喜欢上它了吗？
hints: 什么食物、什么场合
raw oysters at a famous old seafood restaurant / my uncle's treat
为什么犹豫
I'd never had oysters / they're raw, which scared me
别人怎么劝你
don't worry, they slide right down / you'll love 'em
结果与感受
it's an acquired taste / your taste buds grow up
sample: The food I want to talk about is raw oysters, which I tried for the first time at a famous old seafood restaurant with my uncle.
我想说的食物是生蚝，第一次吃是在一家有名的老海鲜馆，叔叔带我去的。
The place was famous for them.
那家店就是以生蚝出名的。
He took me there for my birthday and announced, 'This is my treat — order anything.'
他带我去那里过生日，还宣布：'今天我请客——随便点。'
When the waiter asked, 'Would you like an appetizer?' my uncle ordered oysters for the table.
服务员问'要来点开胃菜吗？'，叔叔直接给全桌点了生蚝。
I'd never had oysters, and I wasn't sure I'd like them — they're raw, which honestly terrified me.
我从没吃过生蚝，心里没底会不会喜欢——毕竟是生的，说实话有点吓人。
My first reaction was to say sorry, folks, these are not for me, but my uncle laughed: 'Don't worry. They slide right down. You'll love 'em.'
我第一反应就是'不好意思，这个我真不行'，但叔叔笑了：'别担心，一口就滑下去了，你会爱上的。'
Everyone watched as I squeezed lemon on one and swallowed it in one go.
所有人盯着我往生蚝上挤了柠檬，一口吞了下去。
The texture was cold and slippery, and my face must have said everything, because the whole table burst out laughing.
那口感又凉又滑，我的表情肯定出卖了我，因为全桌人都笑翻了。
My uncle just grinned and said, 'Told you.'
叔叔咧嘴一笑：'我说什么来着。'
To be fair, the taste was fine — fresh and briny, like the sea — it was the idea that was hard to swallow.
平心而论，味道不错——鲜咸，带着海的味道——难以下咽的其实是'生'这个念头。
I tried them twice more over the following years, and you know what?
之后几年我又试了两次，你猜怎么着？
They really are an acquired taste — I actually order a dozen now.
这玩意儿真是'越吃越爱吃'——现在我自己都会点上一打。
That experience taught me something bigger too: 'no thanks' foods deserve a second chance, because your taste buds grow up along with you.
这段经历还教会我一个大道理：那些被你'pass'的食物值得第二次机会，因为你的口味会跟着你一起长大。

topics.question: Describe an old restaurant, shop or building you have visited that made a strong impression on you.
topics.questionZh: 描述一家你去过、给你留下深刻印象的老餐馆、老店或老建筑。
hints: 在哪里、有多老
a teahouse in the old quarter / it dates back to the early 1900s
里面的陈设细节
dark wooden tables / old portraits and black-and-white photos
食物或服务
an elderly waiter greeted us with 'How many?' / the menu has barely changed
感受：与历史的连接
it feels like history you can sit inside
sample: I'd like to describe a century-old teahouse in my hometown, which left a deep impression on me.
我想说说家乡一家百年老茶馆，它给我留下了极深的印象。
It's in the old quarter, and local people say it dates back to the early 1900s, which makes it one of the oldest businesses in the city.
它坐落在老城区，据说可以追溯到二十世纪初，是全城最老的铺子之一。
When I first walked in, I told my friend 'you weren't kidding — this place really is old.'
第一次走进去时，我跟朋友说：'你还真没夸张——这地方是真老。'
The moment you step inside, the modern world disappears.
一跨进门，现代世界就消失了。
There are dark wooden tables polished by generations of elbows, and along the walls hang old portraits of the founders and black-and-white photos of the street a hundred years ago.
深色木桌被几代人的胳膊肘磨得发亮，墙上挂着创始人的旧画像和一百年前这条街的黑白照片。
The last time I went, an elderly waiter in a long gown greeted us with 'How many?' and showed us to a corner booth, saying 'I'll take your coats.'
我上次去时，一位穿长衫的老服务员招呼'几位？'，把我们领到角落的卡座，还说'大衣我来挂'。
We ordered the house tea and some traditional snacks, and the waiter told us stories about the place — which writers used to sit where, and how the menu had barely changed in decades.
我们点了招牌茶和几样传统茶点，老服务员给我们讲这店的故事——哪位作家常坐哪个位子，菜谱几十年几乎没变过。
Sitting there, drinking tea that people had drunk for a hundred years, I felt connected to something bigger than myself.
坐在那里，喝着一百年来人们喝过的同一款茶，我感觉自己连上了比自己更大的东西。
What impressed me most was that it's a living place, not a museum — old men play chess there every morning, exactly as they always have.
最打动我的是，它是个活的地方，不是博物馆——每天早晨老人们在里面下棋，一如既往。
In a city where everything gets torn down and rebuilt, that teahouse feels like history you can actually sit inside.
在一个什么都拆了重建的城市里，那家茶馆像是能坐进去的历史。
That's why I always take visitors there instead of the shopping malls.
所以我带客人总去那儿，而不是去商场。

topics.question: When friends or family eat out together, who do you think should pay? Describe the customs you know.
topics.questionZh: 朋友或家人一起下馆子，你认为该由谁买单？说说你了解的习惯。
hints: 你的文化里的习惯
in China, people often fight over the bill
常见的说法/场景
this is my treat / get out of here, it's my turn
不同做法对比
going Dutch / taking turns / splitting by phone transfer
你的偏好与理由
treating shows generosity / fairness matters too
vocab: 哪儿的话！／怎么可能让你请！
order another dozen for the table
sample: In China, when friends or family finish a meal, the real drama begins at the bill.
在中国，朋友或家人吃完饭，真正的大戏才刚开场——买单。
Who pays says a lot about the relationship.
谁买单，很能说明关系。
With family, the older generation usually wins the fight.
在家庭聚餐里，通常是长辈'赢'。
My grandmother is famous for it: the moment the waiter approaches, she'll have already slipped out 'to use the bathroom', paid at the counter, and returned looking innocent.
我奶奶就是出了名的这样：服务员还没过来，她已经'去洗手间'顺路把账结了，回来还一脸无辜。
Once my two uncles actually argued at the restaurant door for five minutes.
有一次我两个叔叔在店门口足足争了五分钟。
Whoever loses will say 'Get out of here! This was supposed to be my treat!' — and the winner will laugh and promise the loser can pay next time.
输的那个会喊'哪儿的话！这顿明明该我请！'——赢的那个笑着答应下次让对方请。
With friends my age, the customs are mixed.
跟我同龄的朋友之间，习惯就比较多样了。
Some groups still fight over the bill — the phrase 'this is my treat' is a badge of honour.
有些圈子还是抢着买单——'我请客'这仨字是荣耀。
Others prefer going Dutch, transferring money by phone, or simply taking turns, which I personally find the fairest system.
也有人喜欢 AA、手机转账，或者轮流做东——我个人觉得轮流最公平。
By the way, when someone treats me, I never order the most expensive thing; leaving some face for everyone is part of the custom.
顺便说一句，别人请客时我从不点最贵的菜；给彼此留面子，也是这习俗的一部分。
