My own view is that who pays matters less than the spirit behind it.
我自己的看法是：谁付钱不重要，重要的是背后的心意。
Treating someone says 'our relationship is worth more than money'; splitting fairly says 'we're equals.' Both are fine — as long as nobody keeps score.
请客是在说'我们的关系比钱重要'；平摊是在说'我们是平等的'。都挺好——只要没人锱铢必较。

topics.question: Do you think staying with relatives for a while is a good way to deal with a difficult time? Why?
topics.questionZh: 你认为在困难时期去亲戚家住一阵子是好办法吗？为什么？
hints: 观点：有时正是需要的
sometimes it's exactly what you need / a change of scene
好处：换环境、被照顾
away from daily noise / relatives say 'come home with us'
顾虑：怕打扰人家
you don't want to impose / they have their own family and responsibilities
边界与回报
agree it wouldn't be forever / help with the chores
vocab: You're our family. Come home with us
你们是我们的家人，跟我们回家吧
It might be just what we need
也许那正是我们需要的
sample: I believe staying with relatives for a while can be exactly the right medicine during a rough patch — as long as you're honest about limits.
我相信，在低谷期去亲戚家住一阵，有时正是对症的药——前提是把界限说清楚。
Sometimes you can't see your own life clearly because you're standing too close to it.
有时候你看不清自己的生活，只是因为站得太近了。
This is pretty much what happened to me after I failed an important exam and lost my direction completely.
我考砸一场重要考试、彻底失去方向之后，差不多就是这样。
My aunt and uncle invited me to their farm: 'You're our family. Come home with us for a while — it might be just what you need.'
姑姑和姑父邀请我去他们的农场：'你是我们的家人，来跟我们住一阵吧——说不定正是你需要的。'
My first reaction was to refuse — you don't want to impose, and they have their own family and responsibilities.
我的第一反应是拒绝——你不想打扰人家，他们也有自己的家庭和责任。
But my mother pushed me to go, and honestly, it turned out to be the best decision.
但我妈劝我去，说实话，那成了最好的决定。
For six weeks I fed chickens, picked vegetables, and went to bed at nine like everyone else.
六个星期里，我喂鸡、摘菜，跟大家一起九点睡觉。
Nobody asked about the exam; my uncle just said farming gives you time to weigh your options.
没人问考试的事；姑父只说，干农活能让人有时间掂量各种选择。
By the end I could think about the failure calmly, and I came home with a plan to retake it.
到最后，我能平静地面对那次失败了，回家时还带着重考的计划。
Of course, it worked because we agreed it wouldn't have to be forever — I helped with chores and set a leaving date.
当然，这次能成，是因为我们说好了不会一直住下去——我帮忙干杂活，也定了离开的日子。
A relative's home isn't a hotel, and treating it with respect is what keeps the invitation open.
亲戚的家不是旅馆，心存敬重，邀请的门才会一直开着。

topics.question: Describe a place you like to go to when you want to be alone or clear your head.
topics.questionZh: 描述一个你想独处或理清思绪时喜欢去的地方。
hints: 什么地方
a small hill behind the airport / a river bank
多久去一次、什么时候
whenever life gets heavy / after a bad grade or an argument
在那里做什么
watch the planes take off and land / just sit and breathe
为什么有效
the noise of the world fades / things slowly fall into place
sample: My place is a small hill behind the airport, about twenty minutes from my home by bike.
我的地方是机场后面的一座小山，从我家骑车过去大约二十分钟。
It's my favorite spot in the whole city, though most people don't even know it exists.
它是全城我最喜欢的地方，尽管大多数人根本不知道它的存在。
From there, you can watch the planes take off and land, one after another, all evening.
在那儿能整晚看飞机一架接一架地起落。
I discovered it in high school by accident, during a lonely walk, and I've been going back ever since.
高中时一次孤独的散步，我偶然发现了它，从此一直回去。
When life gets heavy — a bad grade, an argument, or just too much noise in my head — I go up there with a bottle of water and sit on the grass.
每当生活沉重——考砸了、吵架了，或者脑子里太吵——我就带着一瓶水上去，坐在草地上。
Sometimes I stay until it gets dark and the runway lights come on.
有时我会待到天黑，跑道灯亮起来。
There's something about the airplanes and all that distant roaring that empties my mind.
飞机和那些遥远的轰鸣，有种让大脑清空的力量。
The planes have their routes, the city has its lights, and my problems suddenly look small and solvable.
飞机有航线，城市有灯火，而我的问题忽然显得渺小、有解。
I don't even think that much; I just breathe, and things slowly fall into place on their own.
我其实不怎么想事；只是呼吸，事情就自己慢慢理顺了。
It's also where I make big decisions — I chose my university major on that hill.
我做重大决定也在那儿——我的大学专业就是在那座山上定下的。
I once took my best friend there when he was down, and now he goes there too.
有一次朋友情绪低落，我带他去了那里，现在他自己也常去。
Everyone needs a spot where the world is big enough to shrink your worries.
每个人都需要一个地方，世界足够大，大到能缩小你的烦恼。

topics.question: Describe a time when a family member or close friend was missing or very late, and you were really worried.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次家人或好友失踪/迟迟不归、让你非常担心的经历。
hints: 什么情况
my younger brother took the car and disappeared for hours
你做了什么
I called all of his friends one by one / called a friend who knew who he hung out with
心情起伏
every car sound made us jump / we were worried sick
结果与后续
he came back safely / the real conversation happened the next day
vocab: Where the hell have you been?
to make a long story short
sample: The night I remember most vividly is when my younger brother disappeared for six hours with my uncle's car.
我记得最清楚的那个晚上，是我弟弟开着我叔叔的车消失了六个小时。
He was seventeen, and we'd had a huge family argument that evening about his future.
他当时十七岁，那天晚上我们全家刚为他的前途大吵了一架。
Around nine we realised the keys were gone from the hall table — and so was the car.
九点左右，我们发现门厅桌上的钥匙没了——车也没了。
At first we told ourselves he'd be back in an hour, but by midnight, panic took over.
起初我们安慰自己他一小时后就回来，可到了午夜，恐慌占了上风。
I called all of his friends, at least the ones I knew, one by one.
我挨个打给他所有的朋友——至少是我认识的那几个。
To make a long story short: nobody had seen him.
长话短说：谁都没见过他。
It was a long shot, but a friend of mine knew who he hung out with, so I called her at one in the morning.
希望渺茫，但我一个朋友知道他平时和谁混，我凌晨一点还是打了过去。
She hadn't seen him either, and by then every car sound in the street made us jump.
她也没见过他。到那时，街上一有一点汽车声，我们全家就心头一紧。
We were worried sick — the insurance didn't even cover him driving, and we imagined everything.
我们担心死了——保险根本不覆盖他开车，我们把最坏的情况都想了一遍。
At three in the morning, headlights finally swept the window, and there he was.
凌晨三点，车灯终于扫过窗户——他回来了。
Relief, then anger, then relief again — I ran out before anyone could stop me.
先是松了口气，接着火冒三丈，然后又是后怕——我抢在所有人前面冲了出去。
We didn't lecture him that night; we just made tea, and the real conversation happened the next day.
那晚我们没训他，只是泡了茶；真正的谈话是第二天才进行的。
Now we laugh about it, but I never want to feel that way again.
现在我们能笑着说起那晚，但我再也不想有那种感觉了。

topics.question: Describe a time when you cheered someone up in an unusual or creative way.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你用特别或有创意的方式逗人开心的经历。
hints: 谁、为什么情绪低落
my cousin had just lost his father / he barely spoke for weeks
通常的做法为什么不灵
advice just bounced off him / he said 'just leave me alone'
你的特别做法
I made up a silly song with two chords / did something ridiculous
效果
he laughed for the first time in weeks / then we could really talk
vocab: That's the stupidest song I've ever heard
这是我这辈子听过最傻的歌
sample: I'd like to talk about the time I cheered up my little cousin with what might be the world's stupidest song.
我想讲讲我用大概是全世界最傻的一首歌，把我表弟逗笑的那次。
He was fifteen, and he'd just lost his father, my uncle, after a long illness.
他十五岁，我的舅舅久病之后刚去世，他一下子没了父亲。
For weeks he barely spoke, and everything we said just bounced off him.
好几个星期他几乎不说话，我们说什么他都不接。
If I said 'it's normal to be sad', he'd shrug; if I tried to put myself in his place, he'd say 'just leave me alone.'
我说'难过很正常'，他耸耸肩；我试着设身处地，他就说'别管我'。
The more we pushed him to talk, the further he disappeared into his room.
我们越劝他说话，他就把自己关得越深。
One afternoon I gave up on wisdom and did something ridiculous instead.
一天下午，我不再讲道理，干了件特傻的事。
I grabbed his old toy guitar and made up a song on the spot — two chords, silly lyrics, basically 'life stinks, life stinks, say it with me, bro.'
我抄起他的旧玩具吉他，当场编了首歌——俩和弦，傻乎乎的歌词，核心就是'生活糟透了，生活糟透了，兄弟跟我一起唱'。
He stared at me like I was crazy... then a laugh escaped, then another.
他盯着我，像看疯子一样……接着一声笑漏了出来，然后又是一声。
'That's the stupidest song I've ever heard!' he said — but he was grinning, and honestly, 'it could use some work' was the first full sentence he'd said in weeks.
'这是我这辈子听过最傻的歌！'他说——但他咧着嘴笑了，而且说真的，'还得再改改'是他几周来说的第一句完整的话。
That laugh broke the ice.
那一声笑破冰了。
That evening, for the first time, he talked about his dad — properly, for two hours.
那天晚上，他第一次好好聊了聊他爸爸——整整聊了两个小时。
Sometimes people don't need perfect words; they need permission to feel something other than pain. A dumb song gave him that.
有时候人需要的不是完美的话，而是允许自己感受痛苦之外的东西。一首傻歌给了他这个许可。

topics.question: Do you think a friendship can survive when one person becomes very busy with work or study?
topics.questionZh: 你认为当一方忙于工作或学习时，这段友谊还能维持吗？
hints: 观点：可以，但节奏要变
yes, but the rhythm has to change / don't take silence personally
常见的问题
one gets all wrapped up in school / can't even write one lousy letter
你的经历
my best friend went to university in another city
维系的方法
short messages instead of long letters / a fixed monthly video call
vocab: 哪怕一封敷衍了事的信
Are you going to be OK?
sample: I believe such friendships can survive, but only if both sides accept that the rhythm has to change — and neither side takes silence personally.
我相信这样的友谊能存活，但前提是双方都接受节奏必须改变——而且都不把沉默当作针对自己。
My best friend from high school went to university in another city, and in her first term she basically vanished.
我高中最好的朋友去了另一座城市上大学，第一个学期她几乎人间蒸发。
Back then we wrote real letters, and I got maybe one lousy letter in three months.
那时我们还写真正的信，三个月里我大概只收到一封敷衍的信。
I kept writing anyway, like a newspaper nobody read.
我还是一直写，像一份没人读的报纸。
When she finally called, I complained, 'You couldn't write one lousy letter?' and she admitted she'd been all wrapped up in school, in a real work mode.
她终于来电话时，我抱怨：'你就不能写一封破信吗？'她承认自己一头扎进了学业，整个人处于全力用功模式。
I was hurt at first — I even wondered whether the friendship was over, or whether she'd simply found new people.
起初我很受伤——我甚至怀疑友谊是不是完了，或者她只是交了新朋友。
But then I remembered how my own hardest semester looked from the inside.
但随后我想起自己最难的那个学期，从内部看是什么样子。
So instead of guilt-tripping her, I adjusted: short messages instead of long letters, no expectations of instant replies, and a fixed video call once a month.
于是我没有让她内疚，而是调整了自己：用短消息代替长信，不指望秒回，每月固定视频一次。
Ten years later she's still my closest friend.
十年后，她依然是我最亲密的朋友。
The letters eventually came — a whole box of them, written at midnight.
那些信最后都来了——满满一盒，都是深夜写的。
When we talk now, we pick up exactly where we left off.
现在每次聊天，我们都从上次断的地方无缝接上。
So my answer is: busy seasons don't kill friendships; bitterness about them does.
所以我的答案是：忙碌的季节杀不死友谊；对忙碌的怨气才会。

topics.question: Describe a time when you helped a friend get out of a difficult situation. What did you do?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你帮助朋友摆脱困境的经历。你做了什么？
hints: 朋友遇到什么困难
she wanted to leave a harmful relationship for good
她下决心的时刻
she called and said 'I've made up my mind. I've had it'
你具体做了什么
I offered her a room / we drove over and packed her stuff
结果与感受
she never went back / showing up with a car matters
sample: I want to talk about the night I helped my closest friend move out of her boyfriend's apartment — for good.
我想讲讲那个晚上，我帮我最好的朋友搬出她男朋友的公寓——永远地搬出来。
She'd been in that relationship for two years, and it had turned dark.
那段感情她谈了两年，后来变得很黑暗。
That night she called me at eleven and her voice was shaking.
那天晚上十一点她打来电话，声音在发抖。
She said, 'I've made up my mind. I've had it. I'm leaving — for good.'
她说：'我下定决心了。我受够了。我要走——永远不回来了。'
He had been drinking, she told me, and when he got angry he pulled the phone right out of the wall.
她告诉我他一直在喝酒，一发起火来能把电话从墙上扯下来。
I said, 'Good for you. I'm coming now — pack a small bag.'
我说：'好样的。我马上过来——收拾个小包。'
My brother drove me over — he insisted, and that was final.
我弟弟开车送我去——他坚持要去，就这么定了。
When we arrived, there were broken plates on the kitchen floor; she'd locked herself in the bathroom.
我们到的时候，厨房地上全是碎盘子，她把自己锁在了浴室里。
She looked like a wreck — she hadn't slept all night — but she'd already packed her stuff.
她整个人像垮了一样——一夜没睡——但她已经把自己的东西装好了箱。
We carried her boxes out in ten minutes, before things could get worse.
趁着事态还没恶化，我们十分钟就把她的箱子全搬了出来。
She stayed in our spare room for two months.
她在我们家的空房里住了两个月。
People say leaving is hard, and it's true: she cried, she doubted, she nearly went back twice.
人们都说离开很难，确实如此：她哭过、动摇过，有两次差点回去。
But today she has a new job and a new flat, and she says that phone call was the turning point of her life.
但现在她有了新工作和新公寓，她说那通电话是她人生的转折点。
I didn't do much, really — I just showed up with a car.
其实我没做什么——我只是带着一辆车出现了。

topics.question: Describe a time when you had to apologise to someone for something serious. How did it go?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你为比较严重的事向别人郑重道歉的经历。过程如何？
hints: 做错了什么
I took my uncle's car without asking / I caused all that worry
道歉前的犹豫
I was so ashamed I could barely speak
怎么道歉的
no excuses / a proper, face-to-face apology
对方的反应与结果
he said 'it's over, as far as I'm concerned' / it brought us closer
vocab: as far as I am concerned
sample: The apology that took me the most courage happened when I was seventeen, after I took my uncle's car without asking.
最需要勇气的一次道歉发生在我十七岁，那时我没打招呼就开走了叔叔的车。
It sounds small now, but at the time it nearly caused a family breakdown.
现在听起来是小事，但当时几乎让全家崩溃。
I was angry after an argument at home, and I just wanted to drive somewhere, anywhere.
那天在家吵了架，我一肚子火，只想开车去个地方，哪儿都行。
So I swiped the keys from the hall table and disappeared for half the night.
于是我顺走了门厅桌上的钥匙，消失了半夜。
My family had no idea where I was; they called every hospital in the city.
家里人完全不知道我在哪儿，把全市的医院都打了个遍。
When I got back, my sister was furious, and my uncle just went pale and sat down.
我回来时，姐姐气疯了，叔叔脸都白了，跌坐在椅子上。
The next morning I had to face them, and I was so ashamed I could barely speak.
第二天早上我必须面对他们，我羞愧得几乎说不出话。
But I knew a mumbled 'sorry' wouldn't do, so I apologised properly: 'I'm very sorry that I took your car and caused all that worry.'
但我知道含糊一句'对不起'不够，于是我郑重地道了歉：'非常抱歉我开走了您的车，还带来那么多担心。'
I didn't make excuses — I admitted that what I did wasn't clever and could have ended much worse.
我没找任何借口——我承认自己的所作所为并不明智，本可能酿成大祸。
My uncle was quiet for a moment, and then he said, 'It's over, as far as I'm concerned. We all did foolish things when we were young.'
叔叔沉默了片刻，然后说：'就我而言，这事翻篇了。我们年轻时都干过傻事。'
But he added one condition: next time I feel like running, I talk to someone first.
但他加了一个条件：下次我再想逃跑，先找人聊聊。
That apology actually brought us closer; being honest about a mistake repairs more than the mistake broke.
那次道歉反而让我们更亲近了；坦诚面对错误，修复的东西比错误毁掉的更多。

topics.question: Describe a time when you or someone close to you finally said 'enough' and made a big change in life.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你（或身边亲近的人）终于说'受够了'并做出人生重大改变的经历。
hints: 之前忍受了什么
a job with a manager who shouted daily / a situation everyone told her to quit
转折的一刻
one night something inside her snapped / 'I don't know where I'm going, but I'm leaving'
改变后的难与易
no income at first / what a nightmare, but what a relief
回看这件事
'I've had it' isn't giving up — it's standing up for yourself
vocab: I don't know where I'm going, but I am leaving
我不知道要去哪里，但我必须离开
sample: I'd like to tell the story of my cousin, who finally said 'enough' to a job that was destroying her.
我想讲讲我表姐的故事，她终于对一份正在摧毁她的工作说了'够了'。
She'd worked for three years under a manager who shouted at the team daily and took credit for their work.
她在一个天天冲团队吼叫、还抢下属功劳的经理手下干了三年。
Everyone told her to quit, but she kept hoping things would improve — and, honestly, she needed the salary.
所有人都劝她辞职，但她总盼着情况会好转——说实话，她也确实需要那份工资。
Then one night the manager humiliated her in front of a client, and something inside her simply snapped.
后来某个晚上，经理当着客户的面羞辱了她，她心里有什么东西彻底断了。
She called me at midnight and said, 'I don't know where I'm going, but I'm leaving. For good.'
她半夜给我打电话：'我不知道要去哪里，但我必须离开。永远不回来了。'
The next morning she handed in her resignation letter — typed, printed, unstoppable.
第二天一早她递交了辞职信——打字、打印，义无反顾。
She packed her stuff and was out of there before lunch.
她收拾好东西，午饭前就离开了那里。
Those first weeks were genuinely hard: no income, doubts at three in the morning, relatives asking awkward questions.
头几个星期真的很难：没有收入、凌晨三点的自我怀疑、亲戚们尴尬的追问。
'What a nightmare,' she kept saying — but also, what a relief.
她总说'真是一场噩梦'——但同时，也是一种解脱。
Two months later she found a better position in a smaller company, where nobody raises their voice.
两个月后，她在一家小公司找到了更好的职位，那里没人会大吼大叫。
Looking back, she says the hardest part wasn't leaving; it was admitting, for years, that something was wrong while pretending it was fine.
回头看，她说最难的不是离开，而是那些年一边假装一切都好，一边不肯承认有问题。
Sometimes saying 'I've had it' isn't giving up — it's standing up for yourself for the first time.
有时候说'我受够了'不是放弃——而是第一次为自己挺身而出。

topics.question: Do you think changing your environment helps people make difficult decisions? Use an example to explain.
topics.questionZh: 你认为换个环境有助于人们做出艰难的决定吗？请举例说明。
hints: 观点：非常有帮助
a change of scene gives you space to weigh the options
为什么有效
away from daily noise / nobody arguing at you
例子
I stayed at my uncle's farm for a few weeks after graduation
注意什么
it wouldn't have to be forever / you still have to come back and decide
vocab: It wouldn't have to be forever
in case the farm isn't for me
sample: Yes, I really do — a change of environment is often the fastest way to see your own problem clearly.
是的，我真心这么认为——换个环境往往是最快看清自身问题的办法。
When you stay in the middle of the mess, everyone's opinions, old habits and daily noise keep pushing you around.
身处乱局之中时，别人的意见、旧习惯和日常噪音会不停推着你走。
I experienced this after graduation, when I couldn't decide between a stable job offer and going abroad to study.
毕业后我体会过这一点：一边是稳定的工作机会，一边是出国读书，我迟迟决定不了。
My parents leaned one way, my friends another.
爸妈偏向一边，朋友偏向另一边。
I was going in circles for two months; every dinner turned into a family debate, and I stopped sleeping properly.
我原地打转了两个月；每顿晚饭都变成家庭辩论赛，觉也睡不好。
Then my uncle invited me to his farm for a few weeks — 'It wouldn't have to be forever,' he said, 'just enough time to weigh the options.'
后来叔叔邀我去他的农场住几周——'不必长住，'他说，'够你掂量掂量各种选择就行。'
Out there, nobody discussed my future at breakfast; I fed the pigs, repaired fences, and took long walks.
在那儿，没人吃早饭时讨论我的前途；我喂猪、修围栏、长时间散步。
Strangely, without anyone arguing at me, I could finally hear my own voice.
奇怪的是，没人和我争论之后，我终于能听见自己的声音了。
By the second week, the answer felt obvious — I chose the job offer first, and graduate school later.
到第二周，答案已经显而易见——我先接受工作，读研以后再说。
I think distance works because it removes the audience.
我觉得'距离'有效，是因为它撤走了观众。
You stop performing a decision and start actually figuring things out.
你不再为决定而表演，而是真正开始把事情想明白。
The cows, frankly, were excellent listeners.
顺便说，奶牛绝对是极好的倾听者。
Of course, a retreat only works if you eventually come back and decide — the farm gives you time, not answers.
当然，这种'退一步'要起作用，前提是你最终回来做出决定——农场给你的是时间，而不是答案。

topics.question: Describe a time when you helped a friend who was in serious trouble. What did you do, and how did things turn out?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你帮助陷入严重困境的朋友的经历。你做了什么？结果如何？
hints: 朋友遇到了什么困境
a friend of mine was in a really rough patch / things got serious one night
你具体做了什么
I rushed over and stayed with her / I told her, what's mine is yours
对方起初的反应
she was too embarrassed to accept / she thought there was nothing she could do
帮忙后的感受与感悟
helping isn't about grand gestures / showing up matters most
vocab: take you up on your offer
sample: A couple of years ago, one of my best friends was going through a really rough patch with her boyfriend, and it was much more serious than an ordinary argument.
几年前，我最好的朋友之一和她男朋友闹得很僵，那次远比普通吵架严重。
One night she called me, crying so hard that she could hardly speak, and I knew I had to do something.
一天夜里她打来电话，哭得几乎说不出话，我知道我必须做点什么。
I rushed over, stayed with her until she stopped shaking, and just listened without asking too many questions.
我立刻赶过去，陪着她直到她不再发抖，只是听她说，没有追问太多。
The next day, I helped her think through her options step by step, and I told her, 'What's mine is yours. You can stay at my place as long as you need.'
第二天，我帮她一步一步理清选择，还告诉她：'我的就是你的，我那儿你想住多久住多久。'
I wasn't trying to fix her whole life; I just wanted her to know somebody was on her side.
我没打算一下子解决她的全部问题，只想让她知道有人在支持她。
Honestly, at first she was too embarrassed to accept any help, because she felt she had failed somehow.
说实话，起初她不好意思接受任何帮助，因为她觉得自己很失败、很没面子。
Like many people in that situation, she thought there was nothing she could do about it.
和很多身处类似处境的人一样，她一度觉得自己无能为力。
But after talking to people who had been through the same thing, she slowly changed her mind, and a few weeks later she finally took me up on my offer.
但和经历过同样事情的人聊过之后，她慢慢想通了，几周后终于接受了我的提议。
That experience taught me that helping a friend isn't about grand gestures.
那段经历让我明白，帮朋友不在于多大的举动。
It's about showing up, keeping her secret, and being patient when she isn't ready to decide.
而是在于出现、替她保密，以及在她还没准备好做决定时保持耐心。
The night she moved into my spare room with one small suitcase, she looked exhausted but somehow relieved.
她拖着一个小行李箱搬进我空房间的那晚，看起来疲惫不堪，却如释重负。
These days she's doing much better, and she always says that phone call changed everything.
如今她好多了，她总说那通电话改变了一切。
I'm just glad I picked up.
我很庆幸自己接了电话。

topics.question: What do you think should be done to support people who suffer from domestic violence?
topics.questionZh: 你认为社会应该怎样帮助遭受家庭暴力的人？
hints: 法律层面的保护
get a restraining order / warn him to stay away
安全的住所
a shelter for battered women / keep the location secret
心理与同伴支持
a support group meeting / going for therapy
普通人不该旁观
don't just stay out of it / speak up for the victim
sample: I believe protecting victims of domestic violence is everyone's responsibility, not just a private family matter.
我认为保护家暴受害者是所有人的责任，而不只是别人家的私事。
A friend's experience opened my eyes to this issue, and since then I've thought about it a lot.
一位朋友的经历让我开始关注这个问题，从那以后我想了很多。
From what I've seen, support needs to come from three directions: the law, safe housing, and emotional care.
依我看，支持需要来自三个方向：法律、安全的住处，还有情感上的关怀。
First of all, the legal system has to act quickly.
首先，法律系统必须快速行动。
When my friend reported her boyfriend, the police kept him overnight, warned him to stay away, and told her how to get a restraining order from the court.
我朋友举报她男朋友后，警方拘留了他一夜，警告他离远点，并告诉她如何向法院申请保护令。
Without that official protection, many victims are simply too scared to leave.
没有这种官方保护，很多受害者根本不敢离开。
Second, safe places matter enormously.
第二，安全的场所极其重要。
My friend stayed in a shelter for battered women for a while, and the location was kept secret so nobody could find her.
我朋友在受虐妇女庇护所住了一段时间，地点保密，谁都找不到她。
There she joined a support group meeting, and she told me it was a relief to discover she wasn't the only one in that mess.
在那里她参加了互助小组会，她告诉我，发现不是只有自己陷在这种泥潭里，让她松了口气。
Third, emotional recovery needs long-term support, because the scars aren't only on the body.
第三，情感的恢复需要长期支持，因为伤疤不只留在身上。
Therapy helped my friend a lot; she used to blame herself, but slowly she learned to see things clearly.
心理治疗帮了我朋友很多；她以前总怪自己，但慢慢学会了看清事实。
As she put it, if you want to turn your life around, you need some help along the way.
用她的话说，想让人生翻篇，路上总得有人帮一把。
Finally, ordinary people shouldn't stay out of it.
最后，普通人不该置身事外。
Sometimes a single neighbour who notices the problem and speaks up can change, or even save, a life.
有时一个注意到问题并开口的邻居，就能改变甚至挽救一条命。

topics.question: Describe a time when you decided to make a big change in your life. Why did you make it, and what happened?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你决定对生活做出重大改变的经历。为什么改变？结果如何？
hints: 为什么想改变
I felt stuck / I needed a change
改变是什么、怎么决定
move to a new city / I hesitated for weeks, then said yes
家人的态度
my mum worried it was too risky / you'll have no regrets
结果与感悟
you make your own luck / it was worth it
sample: Two years ago I made probably the biggest change in my life: I quit a stable job and moved to a completely new city.
两年前我做了人生中大概最大的一次改变：辞掉稳定的工作，搬去一座完全陌生的城市。
People around me thought I was crazy, but deep down I knew I needed a change.
身边人都觉得我疯了，但我心底清楚，我就是需要换个环境。
At that time my life looked fine on paper, but I felt stuck.
那时我的生活纸面上看不错，可我觉得卡住了。
Every day was exactly the same, and I kept asking myself whether this was really all I wanted.
每天都一模一样，我不断问自己：这真的就是我想要的全部吗？
When a former classmate invited me to join her small team in another city, I hesitated for weeks, and then I just said yes.
当一个老同学邀请我去另一座城市加入她的小团队时，我犹豫了几个星期，然后干脆答应了。
Of course my parents worried a lot.
当然，我父母很担心。
My mum kept saying it was too risky, but my dad, to my surprise, told me, 'You'll have no regrets. People regret the things they didn't try.'
我妈一直说太冒险，但出乎意料，我爸对我说：'你不会后悔的。人只会后悔没尝试过的事。'
Those words really stayed with me.
这句话我一直记着。
The first few months were honestly harder than I expected.
说实话，头几个月比我预想的难熬。
I couldn't get used to the noise, and I missed my old friends terribly.
噪音让我很不习惯，我也特别想念老朋友。
But little by little I found my rhythm, made new friends, and started to enjoy the challenge.
但一点一点地，我找到了节奏，交了新朋友，开始享受这种挑战。
Leaving my comfort zone made it easier to leave old worries behind as well.
走出舒适区，也让我更容易把旧的烦恼甩在身后。
Now, whenever someone asks me about that decision, I say it was tough but absolutely worth it.
现在有人问起那个决定，我都会说：过程艰难，但绝对值得。
I used to think I just had bad luck; now I realise you make your own luck by taking chances.
我以前总觉得自己运气差；现在我明白，好运是自己抓住机会挣来的。

topics.question: Describe a home you lived in for a long time. How did you feel when you left it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一套你住了很久的房子。离开它时你是什么心情？
hints: 老屋的样子与年代
small and a bit shabby / we lived there for almost twenty years
房子里承载的回忆
so many memories / my height was marked on the door frame
离开那天的细节
hand over the keys / forward the mail to the new address
心情与感悟
strange to think someone else will live there / a home is more than walls
sample: The home I'd like to talk about is the old apartment where my family lived for almost twenty years.
我想说的是我家长住了差不多二十年的那套老公寓。
It was small and a bit shabby, but it was the background of my whole childhood.
它又小又有点破，却是我整个童年的背景。
Even the smell of the staircase, old books and cooking oil, makes me feel safe whenever I think of it.
就连楼道里旧书和油烟混着的味道，现在想起来都觉得安心。
There were so many memories in every corner.
每个角落都是回忆。
My height was marked on the kitchen door frame, and my drawings were still stuck on the fridge.
厨房门框上刻着我的身高线，冰箱上还贴着我小时候的画。
When we were packing, my mum found an old photo of my grandpa, and we ended up sitting on the floor looking through albums instead of cleaning.
收拾东西时，我妈翻出一张外公的老照片，结果我们坐在地板上翻相册，正事都忘了。
I still remember the day we handed over the keys.
交钥匙那天的情形我还记得。
It was strange to think that someone else would be living there, sleeping in my room, and that our marks on the door frame would probably be painted over.
一想到别人要住进去、睡在我的房间，门框上的身高线大概会被刷掉，就觉得怪怪的。
I walked through every room one last time, and honestly my eyes got a bit wet.
我最后把每个房间都走了一遍，说实话眼眶有点湿。
Before leaving, we cancelled the internet, and I went to the post office to forward the mail to our new address.
走之前我们注销了网络，我还去邮局把邮件转寄到新地址。
It sounds like a boring little job, but standing there, I suddenly realised it was really time to go.
这听起来是件无聊的小事，可站在那儿我突然意识到：真的要走了。
On the way back I passed our old mailbox half hoping there'd be one last letter, but you never know.
回去路上我经过旧信箱，半希望里面还躺最后一封信——谁知道呢。
These days I sometimes pass by that building on purpose.
现在我有时会特意绕到那栋楼前。
A home is never just walls; it's the people and the years inside them, and I carried those with me.
家从来不只是四面墙，而是里面的人和岁月，而这些我都带走了。

topics.question: Describe a visit you made to friends or relatives in the countryside. What did you do there, and how did you feel?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你去乡下拜访亲友的经历。你在那里做了什么？感受如何？
hints: 谁邀请你去、去了哪儿
my uncle and aunt invited me to their farm / a village in the mountains
受到怎样的款待
they opened the door with a big smile / homemade food and drinks
体验了什么活动
a quick tour of the village / feed the chickens and walk by the river
感受与人情味
it felt really homey / I didn't want to leave
vocab: a quick tour of the farm
sample: Last autumn my uncle and aunt invited me to spend a long weekend at their place in the countryside, and it turned out to be one of the most relaxing trips I've ever had.
去年秋天，叔叔婶婶邀请我去乡下他们家住一个长周末，结果那成了我放松过的最惬意的一次旅行。
I hadn't seen them for a couple of years, so I accepted right away.
我有两三年没见他们了，所以立刻就答应了。
The moment I arrived, they opened the door with a big smile and said, 'Come on in,' as if I'd only been away for a week.
我一到，他们就笑着开门说'快进来'，好像我才离开了一个星期。
My aunt barely gave me time to catch my breath after the long drive.
长途开车之后，婶婶几乎没让我喘口气就开始张罗。
She kept offering coffee, tea and homemade snacks, and my uncle was already planning a quick tour of the village for the next morning.
她不停地端咖啡、茶和自己做的小吃，叔叔已经在盘算第二天早上带我快速转转村子。
Their house was simple but really homey, with wooden furniture and quilts made by my grandmother.
他们的房子朴素但特别温馨，摆着木头家具，还有我奶奶缝的被子。
Over the next two days, my uncle showed me the vegetable garden, the chickens, and the small river where he used to swim as a boy.
接下来两天，叔叔带我看了菜园、鸡舍，还有他小时候常去游泳的那条小河。
I even helped feed the animals, which sounds silly but made me ridiculously happy.
我还帮忙喂了牲口，听着傻乎乎的，但我开心得不行。
What touched me most was how they kept saying it was good to have me there.
最打动我的是，他们一直念叨着我来他们特别高兴。
They admitted they don't see the family often enough, so every visit felt precious to them.
他们承认和家人见得不够多，所以每次有人来都格外珍惜。
When I left, my aunt filled my bag with eggs and vegetables from the garden.
我走的时候，婶婶往我包里塞满了鸡蛋和园子里的菜。
I realised hospitality like that can't be bought in any hotel.
我意识到，那样的热情招待是再多钱的酒店也买不来的。

topics.question: Do you think small family farms can survive in the modern economy? Why or why not?
topics.questionZh: 你认为小型家庭农场能在现代经济中生存下去吗？为什么？
hints: 小农场面临什么困难
when demand goes down and costs go up, they're in trouble
为什么越来越难做
lay off farmhands / very few small farms left
可能的出路
go high-tech / sell directly to customers online
你的立场与理由
it's a struggle, but not impossible / tradition needs new tools
vocab: it's a struggle to run a small family farm
经营小家庭农场很不容易
lay off one of the farmhands
sample: I believe small family farms can survive, but honestly it's a struggle, and they can't do it the old way any more.
我相信小型家庭农场能活下去，但说实话很艰难，而且靠老办法是不行了。
I got interested in this question after visiting a relative who runs a dairy farm.
拜访了一位经营奶牛场的亲戚后，我开始对这个问题上心。
He told me the farm has been in the family since the early twentieth century, but every year the maths gets harder.
他告诉我，这座农场从二十世纪初就属于他们家，可账一年比一年难算。
Whenever the demand for milk goes down or feed and seed prices go up, they're in trouble.
只要牛奶需求下降，或者饲料种子涨价，他们就麻烦了。
That year was a bad one: he couldn't afford to get the tractor fixed and had to lay off one of the farmhands.
那年尤其糟糕：他没钱修拖拉机，还不得不辞掉一个帮工。
This explains why there are so few small farms left; young people simply don't see a future in them.
这也解释了为什么剩下的小农场那么少；年轻人根本看不到前途。
Working the land means milking cows twice a day, three hundred and sixty-five days a year, even on Sundays, and the income is never guaranteed.
种地意味着一天挤两次奶，一年三百六十五天，周日也不例外，收入却毫无保障。
Still, I don't think the story has to end there.
不过我觉得故事未必就此结束。
Some farmers around him have survived by going high-tech, selling directly to customers online, or turning the farm into an experience, like cheese-making workshops for city visitors.
他周围一些农户靠科技化活了下来：网上直营，或者把农场做成体验项目，比如给城里来的客人办奶酪工坊。
It's the price of doing business, as my uncle says, but the price can be paid in smarter ways.
用我叔叔的话说，这是做生意的代价，但这代价可以用更聪明的办法来付。
So my view is: small farms won't disappear if they're willing to change.
所以我的看法是：只要愿意改变，小农场就不会消失。
The romance of the countryside is beautiful, but someone has to make the numbers work too.
田园牧歌很美，但总得有人把账算平才行。

topics.question: Describe a place where you can really relax and sleep well. Why does it help you unwind?
topics.questionZh: 描述一个能让你彻底放松、睡得安稳的地方。它为什么能帮你解压？
hints: 这是个什么地方
a cozy room facing the fields / a farmhouse in the countryside
为什么能彻底放松
no traffic, no notifications / the slow rhythm of country life
身体的直接感受
I slept like a baby / slept straight through the night
难忘的小细节
a thick homemade quilt / fresh air after a long drive
sample: The place where I sleep best is, without any competition, my uncle's farmhouse in the countryside.
要说哪里睡得最香，毫无悬念，是我叔叔乡下的农舍。
The first time I stayed there, I was going through a stressful period, and one night there fixed me more than a month of weekends at home.
第一次去住时我正压力山大，在那里睡的一晚，比在家歇一个月的周末都管用。
My aunt showed me to a cozy room at the back of the house, with a thick quilt and a window facing the fields.
婶婶把我安排在房子后面一间温馨的小屋，厚厚的被子，窗外正对着田野。
After a long drive, I washed my face to freshen up, lay down, and the next thing I knew it was morning.
长途开车后我洗了把脸清醒了一下，躺下，再一睁眼就是第二天早上了。
I had slept like a baby, straight through the night, for the first time in months.
几个月来头一回，我睡得像个小婴儿，一觉到天亮。
Why does it work so well on me?
为什么那地方对我这么灵？
First, there's simply nothing to disturb you: no traffic, no notifications, because the signal is weak anyway.
首先，那里根本没有东西打扰你：没有车流，没有消息推送，反正信号也弱。
Second, the daily rhythm is completely different; you get up with the sun, eat simple food, and do physical work that makes you pleasantly tired.
其次，那里的生活节奏完全不同；跟着太阳起床，吃简单的饭，干点体力活，累得恰到好处。
My uncle jokes that breathing the farm air will put hair on your chest.
我叔叔开玩笑说，多吸吸农场的空气能让身体结实。
I can't speak for the chest, but it definitely cleared my head.
结实不结实我不知道，但脑子确实清醒了。
Whenever life in the city gets too noisy, I picture that quiet room, and I start planning my next visit.
每当城市生活太吵，我脑子里就会浮现那间安静的屋子，然后开始盘算下一次去。
A good night's sleep, I've learned, is the cheapest medicine there is.
我算是明白了，睡个好觉是最便宜的药。

topics.question: Do you think people in traditional industries such as farming need to learn new technology?
topics.questionZh: 你认为务农等传统行业的人需要学习新技术吗？
hints: 为什么传统行业也要科技
you've gotta be high-tech in today's world / otherwise you can't compete
科技具体用在哪
keep the accounts on a computer / track where every dollar goes
怎么学会的
take night classes at a community college / teach yourself
你的看法
technology keeps tradition alive / old skills and new tools can work side by side
vocab: 必须高科技起来（才跟得上时代）
sample: Definitely yes, I think people in traditional industries need new technology more than anyone, because their competitors aren't waiting.
绝对需要。我认为传统行业的人比谁都更需要新技术，因为他们的竞争者可不会等。
My mind goes straight to a dairy farmer I met, a man in his sixties who surprised me completely.
我脑海里立刻浮现一位奶牛场主，六十多岁，完全颠覆了我的想象。
I had never realised that farmers used computers, but his desk had a proper setup, and he tracked every cow and every expense on it.
我从没想过农民会用电脑，可他桌上摆着整套设备，每头牛、每笔开销都在上面记着。
He said you've got to be high-tech in today's world, otherwise you simply can't compete.
他说如今这世道就得高科技，不然根本竞争不过。
The amazing thing was that he knows exactly where every dollar goes, which is more than I can say about my own budget.
厉害的是，他清楚每一块钱花在哪儿——这话我自己都不敢说。
And here's the part I really admire: he taught himself.
最让我佩服的是，这些都是他自学的。
He took a bunch of night classes down at the community college, in the evenings after a full day of physical work.
他在社区大学上了一堆夜校课，都是白天干完一整天体力活之后去的。
If a farmer can do that, I don't think any of us has an excuse.
农民都能做到，我觉得我们谁都没借口了。
Technology also changes what these industries can offer.
科技还改变了这些行业能提供的东西。
With online orders and social media, small producers can now sell directly to people in big cities instead of being squeezed by middlemen.
有了网购和社交媒体，小生产者可以直接卖给大城市的顾客，不用再被中间商盘剥。
Old skills and new tools can work side by side.
老手艺和新工具完全可以并肩干活。
So my view is that technology isn't the enemy of tradition; it's often the only thing that keeps tradition alive.
所以我的看法是：科技不是传统的敌人，它往往还是让传统活下去的唯一办法。

topics.question: Describe a festival or holiday when your whole family got together. What made it special?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你们全家团聚过节的经历。那次团聚有什么特别之处？
hints: 什么节日、谁组织
the whole family gathered at my grandparents' house / we hadn't all been together for years
节日前的忙碌准备
spend entire mornings cooking / clean the whole house
最难忘的瞬间
the youngest cousins met for the first time / a huge family photo
团聚对你的意义
a holiday isn't the same without family around the table
vocab: the whole family will be here
take the rest of the day off
这一天剩下的时间都不干活了
do what we can to make it easier
sample: The holiday I remember best is the Spring Festival three years ago, when the whole family finally gathered at my grandparents' house in the countryside.
我记得最清楚的是三年前的春节，全家终于都聚到了乡下爷爷奶奶家。
For various reasons we hadn't all been together for years, so that reunion felt really special.
因为种种原因，我们好些年没凑齐过，所以那次团聚格外特别。
The days before it were pure chaos in the best way.
节前几天是一片大乱，但乱得幸福。
The women spent entire mornings in the kitchen, the men cleaned the yard, and the kids ran everywhere stealing food from the table.
女人们整个上午都泡在厨房，男人们收拾院子，孩子们满院子乱跑，顺手从桌上偷吃的。
On the day itself, my grandfather announced that everyone should take the rest of the day off and just enjoy the family.
正日子那天，爷爷宣布这一整天谁都不许干活，只管好好享受一家人在一起。
The best moment was watching the youngest cousins meet each other for the first time.
最棒的瞬间是看着最小的几个堂表弟妹头一回见面。
They were so eager to play together that they refused to sleep, and by the end of the evening they were best friends.
他们急着一起玩，死活不肯睡，到晚上已经成了最好的朋友。
We took a huge family photo, and my grandmother kept saying it was the best present she could ask for.
我们拍了一张全家福，奶奶不停地说这就是她能收到的最好的礼物。
That was also the first big holiday after my grandfather got sick, so we all tried to do what we could to make things easier for him.
那也是爷爷生病后的第一个大节，所以我们都尽力让他省心些。
Nobody said it out loud, but everyone felt how precious that time was.
没人说出口，但每个人都感觉到那段时间有多珍贵。
Since then, I always travel home for the festival, no matter how expensive the tickets are.
从那以后，不管票多贵，过节我一定回家。
A holiday without the whole family around the same table just isn't the same holiday.
全家不围坐一桌的节日，就不算真正的节日。

topics.question: Describe a family celebration or gathering that is especially memorable for you. What happened and why was it special?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次对你特别难忘的家庭聚会或庆祝活动。发生了什么？为什么特别？
hints: 什么节日/场合、在哪里、都有谁
the whole family got together at my grandparents' place
具体细节：食物、仪式、小意外
the table was full of dishes / grandpa proposed a toast
情感高潮的一刻
before we started eating, my uncle said a few words
为什么难忘
it reminded me that family is what really matters
sample: The family celebration I'll never forget is last year's Spring Festival at my grandparents' house in the countryside.
我最难忘的家庭聚会，是去年在乡下爷爷奶奶家过的春节。
It was special because, for the first time in years, everyone was there — my uncle's family flew back from Shenzhen, my aunt came with her new baby, even my cousin who is always 'too busy' turned up.
它特别，是因为多年来第一次全家人都到齐了——叔叔一家从深圳飞回来，姑姑带着刚出生的宝宝来了，连那个永远'太忙'的堂哥也露面了。
I remember the kitchen was like a battlefield.
我记得厨房像个战场。
Grandma had been cooking since dawn, and the table was absolutely full — fish, dumplings, eight-treasure rice, everything.
奶奶天没亮就开始忙，桌子上摆得满满当当——鱼、饺子、八宝饭，应有尽有。
Before we started eating, my grandpa, who is a man of few words, stood up and said a few words of thanks.
开饭前，一向话少的爷爷站起来说了几句感谢的话。
He said he was grateful that the family could be together again, healthy and safe.
他说他很感激全家人又能健康平安地团聚。
It wasn't a fancy speech, but I saw several people, including my dad, quickly wipe their eyes.
那不是什么华丽的讲话，但我看见好几个人，包括我爸，都飞快地抹了抹眼睛。
Then my uncle proposed a toast to the new baby, and everyone laughed and cheered.
接着叔叔举杯敬刚出生的小宝宝，大家都笑着欢呼。

After dinner, we didn't watch TV like usual; we just sat around the fire, eating sunflower seeds and talking about old times — how my dad and uncle fought over a bicycle when they were kids, things like that.
晚饭后我们没有像往常那样看电视，而是围着火炉嗑瓜子聊往事——比如我爸和叔叔小时候为一辆自行车打架之类的事。
What made it so memorable was a feeling that's hard to describe: everything outside — work, money, stress — disappeared for one evening.
让它如此难忘的是一种很难形容的感觉：外面的所有东西——工作、钱、压力——在那个晚上全都消失了。
Now I understand why older people care so much about family reunions.
现在我明白为什么长辈们那么看重团圆了。
Life pulls people in different directions, so those moments when everyone is around one table are precious.
生活把人们拉向四面八方，所以全家人围坐一张桌子的时刻才格外珍贵。
I've decided to go back every year, no matter how busy I am.
我下定决心，以后不管多忙，每年都回去。

topics.question: Describe a childhood memory that you treasure. What is it about, and why has it stayed with you?
topics.questionZh: 描述一段你珍藏的童年记忆。它是关于什么的？为什么一直留在你心里？
hints: 记忆是什么：一个人、一个物件或一首歌
my mother's lullaby / an old blanket I carried everywhere
具体画面：声音、味道、触感
she would tuck me in and sing softly
长大后再想起的时刻
it all slips away so fast — the memories
为什么珍贵
it connects me to someone I love
vocab: carry it around all the time
sample: The childhood memory I treasure most is my grandmother's lullaby.
我最珍藏的童年记忆是奶奶的摇篮曲。
When I was little, my parents worked in another city, so I lived with my grandma, and she was the one who put me to bed every night.
小时候父母在外地工作，我跟着奶奶生活，每晚哄我睡觉的都是她。
I can still see the scene clearly.
那画面我至今历历在目。
The room was dim, with just a small lamp, and she would tuck me in carefully, pat the quilt flat, and then start humming this old tune.
房间里只开着一盏小灯，光线昏暗，她会细心地替我掖好被子、把被角拍平，然后开始哼那支老调子。
I don't even remember the exact words anymore — something about the moon and the stars — but the melody is still in my head.
歌词我已经记不清了——大概是关于月亮和星星——但旋律还在我脑子里。
To be honest, as a child I didn't think it was anything special.
说实话，小时候我并不觉得这有什么特别。
It was just... normal life.
那只是……平常的日子。
But after I moved back to my parents' city, and especially after grandma passed away a few years ago, that melody suddenly became precious.
但等我回到父母的城市，尤其是几年前奶奶去世后，那段旋律突然变得无比珍贵。
Sometimes when I can't sleep, I hum it to myself quietly, and it calms me down immediately, like a switch.
有时睡不着，我会轻轻哼给自己听，它总能立刻让我安静下来，像按了个开关。
It's strange how memory works: you forget exam answers and birthdays, but a tune from thirty years ago stays perfectly intact.
记忆的运作很奇妙：你会忘掉考试答案和生日，但三十年前的一段旋律完好无损。
I think this memory has stayed with me because it represents a kind of love that asked for nothing.
我想这段记忆一直留在我心里，是因为它代表一种不求回报的爱。
Grandma never said 'I love you' — people of her generation didn't say such things — but every night, that lullaby said it for her.
奶奶从没说过'我爱你'——她那一代人不讲这种话——但每天晚上，那首摇篮曲替她说了。
Now I believe we should try to remember everything, the happy moments especially, because time slips away so fast.
现在我相信，我们应该努力记住一切，尤其是那些快乐的时刻，因为时间溜走得太快。
And whenever I visit her grave, I hum that song one more time, just for her.
每次去她坟前，我都会再哼一遍那首歌，只唱给她听。

topics.question: Describe a sacrifice that someone in your family made for another family member. What did they give up, and how did it affect everyone?
topics.questionZh: 描述一位家人为另一位家庭成员做出的牺牲。他/她放弃了什么？对全家有什么影响？
hints: 谁、为谁、放弃了什么
my uncle gave up his job in the city / put his own plans on hold
为什么这么做
so that my mother could go back to school / to take care of grandpa
当时的具体情形
it wasn't an easy decision / he never complained
对全家的影响与你的感受
we're all grateful / I admire him for that
sample: I'd like to talk about my uncle, who made a big sacrifice for my mother — his younger sister — when they were young.
我想讲讲我叔叔，他年轻时为我的母亲——他的妹妹——做出了很大的牺牲。
At that time, my grandparents were farmers and money was extremely tight.
那时候我祖父母都是农民，家里的钱非常紧。
My mother had just been admitted to a good university, but the family could only afford to send one child to school, and my uncle was actually the better student.
我母亲刚考上很好的大学，但家里只供得起一个孩子读书，而叔叔其实成绩更好。
After a long family meeting, my uncle quietly packed his things, dropped out, and went south to work in a factory.
开了很久的家庭会议之后，叔叔默默收拾行李，退了学，南下进厂打工。
He sent most of his salary home every month so that my mother could finish her studies.
他每个月把大部分工资寄回家，让我母亲读完了大学。
What moves me most is that he never complained, not once.
最让我动容的是，他从没抱怨过，一次也没有。
When I asked him about it years later, he just smiled and said, 'Your mum studied better than me anyway. One of us had to go.'
多年后我问起，他只是笑笑说：'反正你妈学习比我好，总得有一个人去读。'
That single sentence allowed my mother to become a teacher, and honestly, it changed the whole direction of our family.
就这一句话，让我母亲后来成了老师；说实话，它改变了我们整个家的走向。
Because of his sacrifice, my mother has always felt she owed him something, but he refuses to be thanked.
因为他的牺牲，我母亲一直觉得欠他什么，但他从不肯接受感谢。
Every Spring Festival, he's the one who organises the family dinner, and everyone treats him with special respect.
每年春节，张罗家宴的都是他，全家人对他都格外敬重。
From this story I learned that family is not just about blood — it's about the people who quietly give up their own chances so that you can have yours.
从这个故事里我明白：家人不只是血缘，更是那些默默放弃自己的机会、好让你拥有机会的人。
If my uncle hadn't done that, I probably wouldn't have had the education I have today.
如果没有叔叔当年的决定，我可能不会有今天受的教育。
I didn't choose to be born into their debt, but I can choose to pass that kindness on.
这份恩情不是我选择背上的，但我可以选择把这份善意传递下去。

topics.question: Some family members stop talking to each other for years. Do you think people should always try to fix old family conflicts? Why or why not?
topics.questionZh: 有些家人会多年互不说话。你认为人们是否总应设法化解陈年家庭矛盾？为什么？
hints: 观点：值得修复，但需要台阶
yes, in most cases — life is too short
身边的例子：谁和谁多久不说话
they didn't talk for almost ten years over...
转机是什么：一件事或一个人
it took an illness to bring them back together
结果与感悟
they both regretted the wasted years
sample: Yes, I firmly believe people should try to fix old family conflicts, even after many years — and my family is living proof.
是的，我坚信人们应当设法化解陈年的家庭矛盾，哪怕已过去很多年——我家就是活生生的例子。
My father and my uncle had a serious falling-out when I was a child.
我小时候，我父亲和伯父大吵一架，彻底闹翻了。
It started from a business dispute — money, of course, plus a lot of angry words that couldn't be taken back.
起因是生意纠纷——当然是钱，外加许多收不回的气话。
After that, they simply stopped talking to each other.
那之后，他们干脆互不理睬。
For almost ten years, at family dinners they would sit at opposite ends of the table and exchange maybe three sentences.
差不多十年里，家宴上他们一个坐桌子这头、一个坐那头，能说上三句话就不错了。
The whole family walked on eggshells around them.
全家人在他们面前都小心翼翼。
The turning point came when my grandfather fell seriously ill.
转折点出现在祖父病重的时候。
In the hospital corridor, the two brothers, both grey-haired by then, finally talked.
在医院走廊里，那时都已两鬓斑白的兄弟俩终于开口了。
My father said, 'Let's not do this anymore.'
我父亲说：'我们别再这样了。'
And that was it — no big apology, no detailed discussion of who was right.
就这样——没有郑重的道歉，也没有细究谁对谁错。
They just agreed to move on.
他们只是说好，翻篇。
What struck me afterwards was what my uncle said: 'We wasted ten years over something that stopped mattering after one.'
后来让我震动的是伯父那句话：'我们浪费了十年，为了一件一年后就不再重要的事。'
And the sad truth is, it often takes a funeral or an illness to bring people back together, which is exactly why we shouldn't wait.
而悲哀的现实是，往往要一场葬礼或一场大病才能让人重新走到一起——这恰恰说明我们不该等。
Of course, I understand some hurts are very deep, and forcing a reconciliation doesn't always work.
当然，我理解有些伤害很深，强求和解未必有用。
But in most cases, the conflict itself fades; only pride keeps it alive.
但大多数时候，矛盾本身早就淡了，是自尊心让它活着。
Family is one of the few things you can't buy back later.
家人是少数几样以后花多少钱都买不回来的东西。
So my principle is: make the first move, even if you were the wronged one.
所以我的原则是：先迈出第一步，哪怕吃亏的是你。
You'll rarely regret it.
你几乎不会为此后悔。

topics.question: Describe someone in your life you are truly grateful to. What did they do for you, and how do you express your gratitude?
topics.questionZh: 描述一位你真心感激的人。他/她为你做过什么？你如何表达感激？
hints: 是谁、与你的关系
my high-school teacher / my mother / a friend
具体做过的事（细节取胜）
she stayed after class to help me / she believed in me when I didn't
对你人生的影响
it changed the direction of my life
你如何表达感谢
I visit her every year / I try to pass on the kindness
vocab: be grateful to sb for sth
at a time when we needed it most
pay it back / pass it on
回报 / 把善意传递下去
sample: The person I'm most grateful to is Ms. Lin, my high-school English teacher — and no, not because she helped my grades, but because she helped me believe in myself.
我最感激的人是高中英语老师林老师——不是因为她帮我提了分，而是因为她让我开始相信自己。
I was a quiet student from a small town, and my spoken English was poor.
我是个从小镇来的安静学生，口语很差。
In my first year, I once froze completely during a reading aloud exercise, and some classmates laughed.
高一有一次朗读练习，我彻底卡了壳，有同学笑出了声。
I decided English wasn't for me and basically gave up.
我认定自己不是学英语的料，基本放弃了。
But Ms. Lin noticed.
但林老师注意到了。
She started asking me to come to her office for ten minutes after class, twice a week — nothing formal, just chatting about football and music, in English.
她开始让我每周两次课后去她办公室待十分钟——不是正儿八经上课，就是用英语聊聊足球和音乐。
She never corrected me harshly; she just listened, nodded, and said, 'See? You can express yourself.'
她从不大声纠正我，只是听着、点头，然后说：'看，你能表达清楚。'
Slowly, I dared to open my mouth.
慢慢地，我敢开口了。
In my second year, she pushed me to enter the school speech contest.
高二那年，她推我参加了学校的演讲比赛。
I came last of the finalists, but I stood on that stage and finished my three minutes.
我在决赛选手里拿了最后一名，但我站上了舞台，完整讲完了三分钟。
Afterward she said something I'll never forget: 'I'm proud of you — not for the result, for not running away.'
赛后她说了一句我永远忘不了的话：'我为你骄傲——不是为成绩，而是为你没有逃。'
That was exactly the time I needed support most.
那正是我最需要支持的时候。
Now, how do I express my gratitude?
那么，我是怎么表达感谢的呢？
Every Spring Festival I visit her with flowers.
每年春节我都会带花去看她。
But more importantly, I try to pass it on — when a junior colleague is struggling, I do for them what she did for me: listen, encourage, and never let them feel small.
但更重要的是把这份善意传下去——当年轻同事陷入困境时，我会为他们做林老师为我做过的事：倾听、鼓励，绝不让对方觉得自己渺小。
That, I think, is the best way to thank a teacher.
我想，这才是感谢一位老师最好的方式。

topics.question: Describe a time when you had to catch up on a lot of work after being away for some time. How did you manage?
topics.questionZh: 描述一段你因故离开后需要大量补课或补工作的经历。你是怎么应付的？
hints: 为什么落下进度
I was away for weeks because of a family matter
回来后的第一反应
I wondered if I could make it up / everything had moved on without me
具体怎么追赶
email my advisor / study with classmates and share notes
支撑你的信念
take it one step at a time / things have a way of working out
vocab: take it one step at a time
things have a way of working out
so much catching up to do
sample: Last year I had to take almost two months off university because of a family emergency, and coming back was one of the hardest things I've done.
去年因为家里突发状况，我不得不从大学请了将近两个月的假，回来后的日子是我经历过最难熬的。
When I returned, everything had moved on without me, and at first I honestly wondered whether I could make it up at all.
我回来时，一切都照常往前跑了，起初我真的很怀疑自己到底能不能补回来。
The first step, which I was really nervous about, was emailing my advisor and asking for an honest assessment of where I stood.
第一步——也是我心里打鼓的一步——是给导师发邮件，请她如实告诉我现在的处境。
She didn't sugar-coat it: the finals would be tough, and I had missed a lot.
她没有粉饰太平：期末考试会很难，我落下了很多。
But she also said, 'Take it one step at a time,' and somehow that simple sentence made the whole thing feel possible.
但她也说'一步一步来'，不知怎么的，就这么简单一句话让整件事显得可行了。
So I made a boring, realistic plan: which courses to save, which notes to borrow, and how to split each day.
于是我定了个无聊但现实的计划：先保哪几门课、借谁的笔记、每天怎么分配。
I got together with classmates, borrowed their notes, and studied with them, which helped more than reading alone.
我和同学碰头、借笔记、一起自习，这比一个人闷头看书管用多了。
There was so much catching up to do that I basically lived in the library for a month.
要补的东西太多，那个月我基本上住在图书馆。
What kept me calm was something a friend told me: things have a way of working out, but only if you keep moving.
支撑我冷静下来的，是朋友说的一句话：事情总会解决，前提是你得一直往前走。
Once I got settled into the routine, the panic slowly disappeared.
一旦安顿进这套节奏，恐慌就慢慢散了。
In the end I passed everything, not with brilliant grades, but I passed.
最后我全都过了，分数不算漂亮，但都过了。
That period taught me that starting over isn't about one heroic push; it's about small, boring steps repeated daily.
那段日子让我明白：重新开始靠的不是一次英雄式的冲刺，而是每天重复那些小而无聊的步骤。

topics.question: Do you think it is right to send elderly family members to a nursing home? What are the difficulties?
topics.questionZh: 你认为把年迈的家人送进养老院是对的吗？这中间有哪些难处？
hints: 为什么这是艰难决定
professional care is needed / love alone isn't enough
老人和子女各自的感受
he keeps asking to come home / the guilt never goes away
文化压力
seen as unfilial in some cultures / people judge the family
你的立场
the real question is whether the person feels visited and loved
vocab: I did what I thought was best
我做了我认为最好的选择
can't take care of him anymore
sample: This is a question my family actually went through, so I know exactly how painful it can be.
这个问题我家真真切切经历过，所以我太清楚它有多煎熬。
My grandmother's brother needed professional care after a stroke, and his daughter simply couldn't take care of him anymore.
我奶奶的兄弟中风后需要专业护理，他女儿实在照顾不动了。
She visited him every single day at first, and it broke her heart every time, because he kept asking to come home.
起初她每天都去看他，可每去一次心就碎一次，因为老人一直闹着要回家。
People around her kept saying, 'You did the right thing,' but somehow that never made the guilt go away.
身边人不断安慰她'你做得对'，可不知为什么，负罪感就是散不掉。
She just kept repeating that she had done what she thought was best, and I believe she truly had.
她只是反复念叨：我做了我认为最好的选择。我相信她确实是。
In my culture, sending parents to a nursing home is still seen by many as unfilial, which makes the decision even heavier.
在我们的文化里，把父母送养老院至今被很多人视为不孝，这让决定更加沉重。
But I think we have to be honest: modern medical care is complicated, and love alone isn't always enough.
但我觉得得诚实一点：现代医疗护理很复杂，光有爱并不总是够的。
A good home with trained nurses can give an elderly person safety and dignity that an exhausted family simply cannot provide.
一个有专业护士的好养老院，能给老人精疲力竭的家人给不了的安全和体面。
To me, the real question isn't the building; it's whether the person is visited, included, and treated like a family member still.
对我来说，真正的问题不在于那栋楼，而在于这个人是否还有人探望、还被当成家里的一份子。
Placement should be the last option, but when it's truly necessary, families shouldn't be shamed for choosing it.
送养老院应该是最后的选择，但真到那一步时，不该有人指责这样的家庭。
In the end, what matters is that Grandma's brother never felt abandoned, because we never stopped visiting.
归根结底，重要的是奶奶的兄弟从未觉得自己被抛弃，因为我们从没停止去看他。

topics.question: Describe an interesting story from your family's past that you discovered. How did you find out, and how did you react?
topics.questionZh: 描述一个你后来才发现的家族往事。你是怎么知道的？当时什么反应？
hints: 怎么知道这个故事的
my aunt told me on a long train ride / some old photos
故事的内容
they were both in love with the same girl / the brothers stopped talking
你当时的反应
I couldn't believe it at first / suddenly things made sense
故事的结局与意义
they finally made peace / our elders were young once too
vocab: have a mind of her own
sample: This is a story I only discovered two years ago, and it completely changed how I see my family.
这个故事我两年前才知道，它彻底改变了我对自己家的看法。
It came out during a long train ride with my aunt, when we somehow started talking about her younger days.
那是和姑姑一起坐长途火车时聊出来的，不知怎么就聊起了她年轻的时候。
She told me that my grandfather and his brother were both in love with the same girl, who later became my grandmother.
她告诉我，我爷爷和他弟弟当年同时爱上了同一个姑娘，也就是后来我奶奶。
The brothers never got along after that, and for years they simply stopped talking to each other completely.
从那以后兄弟俩就再没好过，一连好多年彻底不说话。
What amazes me is that my grandmother had a mind of her own: everyone expected her to choose the safer brother, but she went ahead and married the one she actually loved.
最让我惊叹的是，我奶奶特别有主见：所有人都以为她会选更稳妥的那个兄弟，她偏偏嫁给了自己真正爱的人。
When I heard this, I couldn't believe it at first, because the two old men I remembered always seemed peaceful.
刚听到时我不敢信，因为我记忆里的两位老人一直安安静静的。
Suddenly a lot of small things made sense, like why the brothers never appeared in the same photo after a certain year.
一下子许多小事都说通了，比如为什么某一年之后，兄弟俩再没出现在同一张照片里。
The story has a gentle ending: shortly before my grandfather passed away, the two brothers finally talked and made peace.
故事有个温柔的结尾：爷爷去世前不久，兄弟俩终于坐下来谈了，和解了。
My aunt said watching them shake hands was one of the most moving moments of her life.
姑姑说，看他们握手是她一生中最动容的时刻之一。
I love this story because it shows that our elders were once young, stubborn and romantic, just like us.
我喜欢这个故事，因为它说明长辈们也曾年轻、固执、浪漫，跟我们一模一样。
Now I always ask older relatives about the past; every family is hiding a novel somewhere.
现在我总缠着长辈问过去的事；每个家里都藏着一本小说。

topics.question: Describe an opportunity you lost but later got back. What did you do in between?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你失去后又失而复得的机会。在那段时间里你做了什么？
hints: 失去了什么机会、为什么
I had to go home for a family matter / someone took my place
当时的感受
I understood, but it still hurt / I felt replaced
你怎么争取第二次机会
ask her to keep me in mind / keep improving on my own
转机与感悟
an opening came up / second chances favor the prepared
vocab: I had to find someone for your old job
不得不找人顶了你的职位
sample: A few years ago I lost a part-time job I really loved, through no fault of my own.
几年前，我丢了一份自己特别喜欢的兼职，而且完全不是我的错。
I had to go home for a family matter, and when I finally came back, my position was gone.
因为家里的事我回了老家，等我终于回来时，职位已经没了。
My manager was honest with me: they had been so shorthanded that she'd had to find someone for my old job.
经理对我很坦白：那阵子太缺人手，她不得不找人顶了我的位置。
She apologised, and I understood, but understanding didn't make the disappointment smaller.
她道了歉，我也理解，可理解归理解，失落一点没少。
I enjoyed that job so much, mainly because I loved working with the kids, and people said I was great with children.
我太喜欢那份工作了，主要因为我喜欢和孩子们待在一起，大家都说我很会跟小孩相处。
Before leaving her office, I asked her to keep me in mind if anything opened up.
离开她办公室前，我请她留意：要是有空缺，记得考虑我。
Then, instead of feeling sorry for myself, I kept improving: I took a short training course and kept teaching privately on weekends.
接下来我没有自怨自艾，而是继续提升自己：报了个短期培训，周末还坚持做家教。
A friend joked that I was being too patient, but I figured patience costs nothing.
朋友笑我太能熬，可我觉得耐心又不要钱。
About three months later, right after the New Year, she called me out of the blue.
大约三个月后，新年刚过，她突然打来电话。
There was an opening, and because she remembered me, I didn't even have to compete with a crowd of strangers.
有个空缺，因为她一直记着我，我连跟一群陌生人竞争都不用。
Getting that phone call felt better than getting the job the first time.
接到那通电话的感觉，比第一次得到那份工作还要好。
That experience taught me two things: lose gracefully, and never disappear from people's radar.
那段经历教会我两件事：输要输得体面，还有，永远别从别人的视野里消失。
Second chances usually go to the ones who stayed ready.
第二次机会，通常属于那些一直准备着的人。

topics.question: Describe a time when you were under great pressure to pass an exam or finish an important task. How did you deal with it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你顶着巨大压力应付考试或重要任务的经历。你是怎么扛过来的？
hints: 压力有多大、赌注是什么
if I failed, I would lose my scholarship
摆在面前的两个选择
repeat the courses / study like mad and go for it
具体怎么突击
every waking hour / share notes and test each other
结果与收获
I gave it my best shot / I pulled it off
sample: The most stressful period of my life was definitely the final exams in my second year at university.
我这辈子压力最大的时期，毫无疑问是大二那年的期末考试。
I had missed weeks of classes because of family problems, and the stakes were brutally clear: if I didn't pass, I would lose my partial scholarship.
因为家里的事，我落了好几个星期的课，代价残酷而明确：考不过，我就会失去部分奖学金。
When I asked my advisor to be honest with me, she was.
我请导师跟我讲实话，她也真讲了。
She said the finals would be real tough, and that I could either repeat the courses next semester or study like mad and go for it.
她说期末考会非常难，我要么下学期重修，要么玩命学习搏一把。
I chose the second option, mostly because I couldn't afford another semester.
我选了后者，主要因为多读一学期我负担不起。
What followed was about three weeks of the most focused madness I've ever experienced.
接下来大概三个星期，是我经历过的最专注的疯狂。
It took every waking hour: I woke at six, studied till midnight, and saw my classmates more than my own family.
醒着的每一刻都用上了：六点起，半夜睡，见同学的时间比见家人还多。
We shared notes, tested each other, and drank an ocean of coffee.
我们共享笔记、互相抽查，喝下了大片咖啡的海洋。
There were moments when I wanted to give up, especially when a practice test went badly.
有好几次我都想放弃，尤其是模拟考砸了的时候。
My roommate kept telling me not to panic, and honestly that helped as much as the studying.
室友一直让我别慌，说实话，这话的作用不比复习本身小。
In the end I gave it my best shot, and against my own expectations, I pulled it off.
最后我倾尽全力一搏，结果连我自己都没料到——成了。
Those weeks taught me that I'm tougher than I thought, and that pressure, in the right dose, can actually concentrate the mind.
那几个星期让我明白，我比自己以为的更能扛；而且压力只要剂量合适，反而能让头脑专注。

topics.question: How do people in your country deal with the loss of a loved one? Do you think taking time to grieve is important?
topics.questionZh: 在你的国家，人们如何面对失去亲人的痛苦？你认为留出时间悲伤重要吗？
hints: 你们的文化怎么做
we don't work for a time / we take time to remember
为什么时间重要
give yourself time to grieve / the pain will go away, but it takes time
身边人怎样安慰
a handwritten letter meant a lot / presence matters more than words
幽默的作用
laughter is the best medicine / from tears to laughter
sample: In my culture, when someone loses a close family member, life stops for a while, and I think that's exactly as it should be.
在我的文化里，失去至亲时，生活会停摆一阵子，我觉得本该如此。
We don't jump back into work; we take time to remember the person.
我们不会马上扑回工作，而是留出时间去怀念那个人。
When my grandfather passed away, my colleagues in the city kept asking when I'd be back, and I felt almost guilty for staying away.
外公去世时，城里的同事不停地问我什么时候回来，多待几天我几乎都有负罪感。
But my relatives reminded me that grief isn't an illness you cure quickly; you have to give yourself time to grieve.
但亲戚们提醒我：悲伤不是能速治的病，得给自己时间去哀伤。
The pain will go away, they said, but it takes time, and they were right.
他们说痛苦会过去，但需要时间——他们说得对。
During those weeks, the small gestures meant the most.
那几个星期里，最珍贵的是那些小小的举动。
A classmate I barely knew sent me a handwritten letter, and a friend simply came and sat with me without talking.
一个几乎不熟的同学给我寄了封手写信，还有个朋友只是过来坐在我身边，什么也不说。
Nobody needs clever words at a time like that; presence matters more than speeches.
那种时候没人需要漂亮话，陪着比说什么都重要。
I also learned that laughter has its place in mourning.
我还学到，哀悼中也容得下笑声。
One evening my uncle told a story about my grandfather's terrible cooking, and the whole room suddenly switched from tears to laughter.
一天晚上，舅舅讲了个外公做饭难吃得离谱的往事，满屋子人瞬间从流泪变成了大笑。
It sounds strange, but that was the first evening that felt warm again.
听起来奇怪，但那是第一个重新让人感到温暖的夜晚。
So yes, taking time to grieve is essential, and societies that rush people back to normal are doing them no favours.
所以，留出时间悲伤至关重要；那些催人赶紧恢复正常的社会，其实是在帮倒忙。

topics.question: Do you think taking a break and having fun helps when you are under pressure? Use your own experience to explain.
topics.questionZh: 你认为压力大的时候，放松出去玩有帮助吗？请结合自身经历说明。
hints: 你的观点
a break is part of the work / all work and no play
一次被拉去放松的经历
a friend invited me to a concert during exam week
一开始为什么拒绝
I couldn't make any plans / I was too exhausted
放松之后的效果
a little diversion might help / I got through more the next day
vocab: get back into the swing of things
sample: Yes, I'm absolutely convinced that taking a break under pressure isn't wasted time; it's part of the work itself.
是的，我深信压力之下歇口气不是浪费时间，它本身就是学习的一部分。
I learned this during an exam period, when I was studying from morning to midnight.
这一点我是在一个考试周里领教的，那时我从早到半夜都在复习。
One afternoon, a friend called and invited me to a concert that same evening.
一天下午，朋友打来电话，约我当晚去听音乐会。
My first reaction was to refuse; I told her I couldn't make any plans because I had so much studying to do.
我的第一反应是拒绝；我说我没法做任何安排，要复习的东西太多了。
I was exhausted and irritable, and deep down I knew coffee wasn't fixing that any more.
我又累又烦，心底明白咖啡已经救不了我了。
She laughed and said, 'What's that expression, all work and no play? Just two hours.'
她笑着说：'那句俗话怎么说的来着，只干不玩？就两个小时。'
For some reason I said yes, and it turned out to be the best decision of that week.
不知怎么我就答应了，结果那成了那一周最正确的决定。
The music carried me completely out of my notes, and I forgot the exams existed for a whole evening.
音乐把我整个人从笔记里带了出来，一晚上都想不起来还有考试这回事。
The next morning I woke up strangely fresh and got through more material in one day than in the previous three.
第二天早上醒来，我出奇地清醒，一天消化的内容比前三天加起来还多。
A little diversion really does help; the brain isn't a machine you can run non-stop.
稍微换换脑子真有用；大脑不是能连轴转的机器。
Of course, balance matters: a break should recharge you, not replace the work.
当然，平衡很重要：休息是给你充电，不是替你干活。
But if I'm ever overwhelmed by everything again, I'll go out instead of staring at the same page for hours.
但下次再被压得喘不过气，我会出去走走，而不是盯着同一页书熬几个钟头。

topics.question: Describe your experience of learning a musical instrument, or a time when you taught someone to play.
topics.questionZh: 描述你学习乐器的经历，或一次教别人演奏的经历。
hints: 怎么开始学的
I picked up the guitar at fourteen / pure stubbornness
学得多笨拙
totally tone deaf / sounded like someone stepped on a cat
教别人的经历
we picked up where we left off / explaining basics helps you too
音乐对你的意义
a way to express feelings / worth every clumsy hour
vocab: pick up where we left off
从上次停下的地方接着来
sounds like someone stepped on a cat
sample: I started learning the guitar when I was fourteen, and these days I even give lessons to a boy in my neighbourhood, so music has given me experiences from both sides.
我十四岁开始学吉他，如今甚至给邻居家一个男孩上课，所以音乐让我两头都体验过了。
My own beginning was rough, mostly because I'm not naturally musical at all.
我起步时很惨，主要因为我压根没什么音乐天分。
People in my family are basically tone deaf, and for the first year my playing honestly sounded like someone stepped on a cat.
我们家的人基本五音不全，第一年我弹的琴声实在像有人踩了猫尾巴。
Tuning the guitar was a nightmare; I remember my teacher sighing before every lesson.
调弦简直是噩梦；我记得每节课前老师都要叹口气。
What saved me was stubbornness: I practised twenty minutes every day, even when it sounded terrible.
救我的是一股倔劲：每天练二十分钟，哪怕难听至极也照练。
Teaching, surprisingly, improved my own playing.
出乎意料的是，教别人反而提升了我自己的琴技。
My student stopped for a while because of school, and when he came back, we simply picked up where we left off.
我的学生因为学业中断了一阵，回来后我们就从上次停下的地方接着练。
Explaining basics to him forced me to understand things I had been doing by pure habit.
给他讲解基础，逼着我弄懂了自己一直凭习惯在做的动作。
The best moment came before a small school performance, when he was extremely nervous.
最难忘的时刻是在一场小型校园演出前，他紧张得不行。
I told him the audience wants him to succeed, and after he played, his parents thanked me with shining eyes.
我告诉他，观众都盼着他成功；他弹完后，他父母亮着眼睛来谢我。
That little thank-you meant a lot to me.
那声道谢对我意义重大。
Playing guitar has become my way of expressing feelings I can't put into words.
弹吉他成了我表达难以言说情绪的方式。
It hasn't been an easy road, but it's been absolutely worth every clumsy hour.
这条路走得不轻松，但每一个笨拙的小时都绝对值了。

topics.question: Describe a time when a friend helped you get through a stressful period. What was the pressure, and what did your friend do?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次朋友帮你熬过压力时期的经历。压力是什么？朋友做了什么？
hints: 压力是什么：考试/截止日期/面试
the final exam was coming up / the deadline was looming
朋友具体做了什么：陪学、鼓励
she studied with me in the library / she kept saying 'you're gonna ace it'
一个印象深的瞬间
I couldn't keep up, and she slowed down for me
结果与感受
I passed / more importantly, I felt I wasn't alone
vocab: I need all the help I can get
我能得到的帮助都需要
sample: The period I want to talk about is my final exams at university, especially one course — data structures — that I was genuinely afraid of.
我想讲的那个阶段是大学期末考试，尤其是一门我真心害怕的课——数据结构。
Two weeks before the exam, I was basically living in the library.
考前两周，我基本住在图书馆。
I remember my friend Xiao came up to me one afternoon and said, 'Don't you ever leave the library? No wonder you're going crazy!'
记得有天下午朋友小肖走过来对我说：'你是从来不离开图书馆吗？难怪你要疯了！'
I was close to breaking down: too much to learn, too little time.
我几乎要崩溃了：要学的太多，时间太少。
And honestly, studying alone, everything felt twice as heavy.
而且说实话，一个人学习，什么都感觉重了一倍。
What she did next was simple but meant a lot.
她接下来做的事很简单，却意义重大。
She suggested we study together in the study room, and she went through the past papers with me, one by one, patiently.
她提议我们一起去自习室，然后耐心地陪我一套一套过历年真题。
Whenever I made progress, even a small one, she'd say, 'See? You're gonna ace this test.'
每当我有一点进步，哪怕很小，她都会说：'看吧，你这次肯定能考好。'
When I panicked, she made me tea and told me to breathe.
我一慌，她就给我泡杯茶，让我深呼吸。
She didn't solve the problems for me, but she made me believe I could solve them myself.
她没有替我解题，但她让我相信我自己解得出来。
In the end, I passed with a much better mark than I expected.
最后我考出的分数远超预期。
But the result almost doesn't matter.
但结果几乎不重要。
What I remember is the feeling that I wasn't fighting alone — someone was sitting next to me in the trench.
我记得的是那种感觉：我不是一个人在战斗——有人跟我蹲在同一条战壕里。
Later I asked her why she spent her own revision time on me.
后来我问她，为什么把自己的复习时间花在我身上。
She said, 'Because two years ago, you did the same for me.'
她说：'因为两年前，你也这样帮过我。'
I had totally forgotten.
我完全忘了这回事。
That taught me something: kindness is never wasted; it just comes back when it's needed most.
这教会我一件事：善意从不浪费，它只会在最需要的时候回来。
Now, whenever a friend is under pressure, I try to be that person sitting next to them.
现在，每当朋友有压力，我都会努力做坐在他们身边的那个人。

topics.question: Describe a decision you made about your studies or career that your parents disagreed with. How did you handle it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一个你做出的、父母不赞成的学习或职业决定。你是怎么处理的？
hints: 什么决定、父母为何反对
they said I'd never make money doing that / do something respectable
冲突的场面
we had a big argument at dinner / they kept pressuring me
你如何沟通：解释理由、给证据
I showed them my plan / I asked them to give me two years
现状如何、学到了什么
they came around gradually / respect takes time
sample: A few years ago, I decided to switch from a stable, boring position to software development.
几年前，我决定从一份稳定但乏味的岗位转做软件开发。
My parents were strongly against it, and I'd like to share how I dealt with that.
我父母强烈反对，我想讲讲自己是怎么处理的。
In their eyes, my old job was 'respectable' — a big company, a fixed salary, an iron rice bowl.
在他们眼里，我原来的工作很'体面'——大公司、固定工资、铁饭碗。
When I told them I wanted to learn programming and find a dev job, my father's first reaction was: 'You'll never make money jumping around like this. Do something steady.'
当我说想学编程找开发工作时，父亲的第一反应是：'这样跳来跳去，你永远挣不到钱。做点安稳的。'
For weeks, almost every phone call ended in an argument.
接连几个星期，几乎每通电话都以争吵收场。
They kept pressuring me, and I kept avoiding the topic, which only made things worse.
他们不断给我施压，我一直回避话题，结果只会更糟。
Then I changed my strategy.
后来我换了策略。
Instead of fighting, I tried to get them off my back with a plan, not promises.
我不吵了，而是用一份计划——而不是空口承诺——让他们别再逼我。
I showed them three things: the salary data for developers, a study schedule I had already started, and a small app I had built by myself.
我给他们看了三样东西：开发岗位的薪资数据、一份我已经开始执行的学习计划，还有一个我自己做的小应用。
I said, 'Give me one year. If I fail, I'll go back and never mention it again.'
我说：'给我一年。失败了我就回去，再也不提这事。'
They didn't say yes, but they stopped saying no.
他们没说同意，但也不再反对了。
And over the following year, as I finished courses and finally got an offer, they slowly came around.
接下来那一年，我陆续学完课程、最终拿到 offer，他们的态度慢慢转变了。
Last month my father actually asked me to help him install a program on his computer and told his friends, proudly, 'My kid does computers.'
上个月，父亲居然让我帮他装软件，还自豪地跟朋友说：'我家孩子是搞电脑的。'
What I learned is that parents' opposition usually comes from worry, not from a desire to control you.
我学到的是：父母的反对通常源于担心，而不是想控制你。
You can't argue worry away — you can only replace it with evidence.
担心是吵不走的——只能用事实去替换它。

topics.question: Describe something you are passionate about even though it doesn't bring you any money. Why do you keep doing it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一件你热爱、但不能带来任何收入的事。你为什么坚持做它？
hints: 是什么爱好
for me, it's playing the guitar / running / photography
它给你的感受（打比方）
making music is like breathing / it's my way of recharging
别人怎么看你还在坚持
people say it's a waste of time / money isn't everything
它如何平衡你的生活
it reminds me who I am outside of work
vocab: 就像呼吸一样（不可或缺）
sample: The thing I'm truly passionate about, even though it earns me nothing, is playing badminton — but let me talk about it properly, because 'playing badminton' sounds too casual.
我真正热爱、却挣不到一分钱的事是打羽毛球——不过让我好好说说，因为'打羽毛球'听起来太随便了。
What I mean is: training seriously, twice a week, with a proper coach, like an amateur athlete.
我的意思是：像业余运动员那样，每周认真训练两次，还有正经教练。
It costs me money, actually — coaching fees, shoes, rackets, travel to amateur competitions.
其实它反而要花钱——教练费、球鞋、球拍、去打业余比赛的路费。
And it brings in exactly zero.
而收入恰好是零。
Some of my colleagues tease me: 'You're too old for this. Why not spend the time making money instead?'
有同事打趣我：'你这岁数就算了吧，干嘛不拿这时间多挣点钱？'
But honestly, money isn't all that important to me when it comes to this hobby.
但说实话，在这项爱好上，钱对我来说没那么重要。
For me, playing is like breathing.
对我来说，打球就像呼吸。
On the court, everything else disappears — deadlines, meetings, messages.
球场上，其他一切都消失了——截止日期、会议、消息。
There is only the shuttle, my movement, and the next shot.
只剩下球、我的移动，和下一拍。
After two hours I'm exhausted but strangely clean inside, like someone pressed the reset button on my brain.
两小时下来我筋疲力尽，内心却出奇地澄澈，像有人在我脑子里按了重置键。
I also love the community around it.
我也喜欢球场上的人际圈子。
My doubles partner and I have played together for five years; we understand each other without talking.
我和双打搭档配了五年，不用说话就能读懂彼此。
That kind of friendship you can't buy.
这种友谊花钱买不到。
I think everyone needs at least one thing they do purely for love, not for profit.
我觉得每个人都需要至少一件纯粹为热爱、而不是为利益做的事。
Work already forces us to calculate everything — time for money, effort for promotion.
工作已经逼我们把一切算得清清楚楚——时间换钱、努力换升职。
If your whole life is a transaction, you slowly forget who you are.
如果整个人生都是一场交易，你会慢慢忘了自己是谁。
Badminton is the part of my life that refuses to be monetised, and that's exactly why it's precious.
羽毛球是我生活里拒绝被'变现'的那部分，而这恰恰是它珍贵的原因。
It keeps me fit, keeps me sane, and keeps me, well, me.
它让我健康、让我清醒，也让我始终是我自己。

topics.zh: 一次敞开心扉的深夜长谈
topics.question: Describe an honest, deep conversation you had with a friend or family member that brought you closer together.
topics.questionZh: 描述一次与朋友或家人的坦诚深谈，它让你们的关系更近了。
hints: 时间地点氛围：深夜、散步、开车
it was almost midnight / we were just driving around
之前的关系状态
we hadn't really talked for a long time
谈了什么、谁先开口
at first we joked around, then suddenly it got serious
之后的改变
we've talked openly ever since / absolutely worth it
sample: I'd like to describe a late-night conversation with my older brother two years ago, which I consider the moment we became real friends, not just brothers.
我想讲讲两年前和哥哥的一次深夜长谈，我认为那是我们从'兄弟'变成'真正的朋友'的时刻。
At that time, I had failed an important professional exam and was in a low mood for weeks.
那时我一场重要的职业考试没过，情绪低落了好几个星期。
One night I couldn't sleep, and around midnight I found my brother still awake in the living room.
一天夜里我睡不着，快十二点时发现哥哥还醒着，坐在客厅里。
I sat down, more to have company than to talk.
我坐下，与其说是想聊天，不如说是想有人陪。
We started with nonsense — a football match, a stupid film — and then, out of nowhere, I said, 'Honestly, I think I'm not good enough for this line of work.'
我们先聊了些有的没的——球赛、烂片——然后不知怎么，我突然说：'说实话，我觉得自己不适合干这行。'
He didn't rush to comfort me.
他没有急着安慰我。
He just put down his phone and said, 'Say more.'
只是放下手机说：'接着说。'
So I did.
于是我说了。
Everything came out: the fear of wasting years, the pressure of comparing myself with classmates, the feeling of letting our parents down.
全都倒了出来：怕白白蹉跎几年、跟同学比较的压力、觉得辜负了父母。
He listened the whole time, and then he shared his own story — how he had nearly given up his business eight years ago and cried in a parking lot.
他一直听着，然后讲了自己的故事——八年前他差点放弃生意，在停车场里哭。
I had no idea.
我完全不知道。
To me he had always been the strong one.
在我眼里，他一直是那个坚强的人。
Then he said something that still guides me: 'Failing an exam means you failed an exam. It doesn't mean you are a failure. Don't sell yourself short.'
然后他说了一句至今指引我的话：'一次考试挂了，只说明这次考试挂了，不说明你这个人不行。别看轻自己。'
We talked until three in the morning.
我们一直聊到凌晨三点。
Nothing was solved on paper — I still had to retake the exam — but I felt lighter, because the weight was finally shared.
现实问题一个都没解决——考试还得重考——但我感觉轻了，因为那份重量终于有人分担了。
Since that night, we talk properly at least once a month.
从那晚起，我们每个月至少好好聊一次。
It's strange: we grew up in the same house, but it took a midnight conversation to really meet each other.
很奇怪：我们在同一个屋檐下长大，却要靠一场午夜长谈才真正认识彼此。

topics.zh: 伴侣/挚友最看重的品质
topics.question: What qualities do you value most in a close friend or life partner? Explain why these matter to you.
topics.questionZh: 你在挚友或人生伴侣身上最看重哪些品质？为什么这些品质对你重要？
hints: 总起：两三个品质
if I had to pick, I'd say understanding, humour and patience
每条配一个小例子
when I was under pressure, she gave me understanding, not blame
反面：什么品质你受不了
what I can't stand is selfishness / someone who makes everything about them
收尾：对的人需要等待
if it's what you want, you have to be patient
vocab: Things are never as simple as they might appear
事情从不像表面那么简单
sample: If I had to pick the qualities that matter most in a close friend or partner, I would choose three: understanding, humour, and patience.
如果非要挑出挚友或伴侣身上最重要的品质，我会选三个：善解人意、幽默、耐心。
Understanding comes first, because life has seasons.
善解人意排第一，因为生活有四季。
Sometimes you're busy, sometimes you're stressed, sometimes you're simply not fun to be around.
人有时忙、有时压力大、有时就是不好相处。
A good partner doesn't demand to be the center of attention all the time.
好的伴侣不会时刻要求自己被关注。
Last year I was tied up with work for months, and a friend of mine never complained about my slow replies.
去年我被工作缠了几个月，一位朋友从没抱怨我回消息慢。
Instead she said, 'Focus on your thing; I'm here when you're done.'
她只是说：'忙你的，忙完我在。'
That's understanding — and honestly, it's rarer than intelligence.
这就是善解人意——说实话，它比聪明更稀缺。
Second, humour.
第二，幽默。
Life is long, and a lot of it is boring or difficult — bills, illness, delays.
人生很长，其中大部分平淡或艰难——账单、生病、误点。
Someone who can make you laugh in a traffic jam is worth more than someone who is impressive at a dinner party.
能在堵车时逗你笑的人，比在宴会上光彩照人的人更值钱。
In my experience, couples who laugh together survive arguments much better.
依我的经验，能一起笑的伴侣，吵架也更容易熬过去。
And third, patience — with people and with life.
第三，耐心——对人，也对生活。
Good things, especially relationships, don't happen on schedule.
好事，尤其是感情，不会按时间表发生。
If it's what you want, you have to be patient.
如果那真是你想要的，你就得有耐心。
I've seen friends rush into marriage or rush out of it, both because they couldn't wait.
我见过有人匆忙结婚，也有人匆忙离婚，都是因为等不起。
What I can't stand, on the other hand, is selfishness — people who treat you as an audience for their life.
反过来，我最受不了的是自私——把你当成他们人生的观众。
So in short: someone who understands your busy seasons, laughs with you in the dark ones, and stays patient in between.
总之：一个在你忙碌时理解你、在你低谷时陪你笑、在中间的岁月里保持耐心的人。
Such people are not easy to find, but they're absolutely worth waiting for.
这样的人不好找，但绝对值得等。

topics.question: Do you think a family should move to another country for a better job opportunity? What should they consider?
topics.questionZh: 你认为一个家庭应该为了更好的工作机会搬去另一个国家吗？他们该考虑什么？
hints: 机会的吸引力
a definite offer / a senior position and better pay
孩子的处境与感受
born here, friends and school here / teased and called names
身份认同的两难
seen as a foreigner everywhere / where do they belong
你的立场
decide together as a family / children pay part of the price
vocab: 知道这个艰难的决定迟早会来
骂他、给他起难听的外号
sample: This is a real dilemma, and I've watched a family in my neighbourhood go through it, so I know there's no easy answer.
这是个真实的两难，我亲眼看着小区里一户人家经历了全过程，所以我清楚没有轻松的答案。
The father received a definite offer from a company back in his home country, and suddenly the whole family had to decide their future in one week.
父亲收到了他祖国一家公司的正式录用信，全家突然必须在一周之内决定未来。
On one side, the opportunity was genuinely attractive: a senior position, a higher salary, and the chance to live closer to the grandparents.
一方面，这个机会确实诱人：高级职位、更高的薪水，还能住得离祖父母更近。
The father kept calling it their golden opportunity, and in career terms, he wasn't wrong.
父亲一直称之为他们的黄金机会，单从职业角度说，他没说错。
On the other side stood the children.
可另一边站着孩子。
The son was born in this country, had friends here, and was doing well at school.
儿子在这个国家出生，朋友都在这儿，学业也不错。
The mother reminded her husband of something painful: some local kids had hurt the boy by calling him names, so he never fully belonged here, but he wouldn't automatically belong there either.
母亲提醒丈夫一件扎心的事：有些本地孩子曾骂他是外人来伤害他，所以他在这里从来没真正融入，可回去也未必就自动属于那里。
In the end they decided to move, telling themselves and the boy that they would adjust.
最后他们还是决定搬，一边说服自己一边安慰孩子：我们会适应的。
From what I've seen, the first year was genuinely hard, especially for the child.
据我观察，第一年是真的难，尤其对孩子。
So my view is: such a move can be right, but only if the family decides together and accepts that the children pay part of the price.
所以我的看法是：这样的搬迁可以是对的，但前提是全家一起做决定，并且承认孩子也要付出一部分代价。
A golden opportunity that destroys a family isn't golden.
一个会拆散家庭的黄金机会，就算不上黄金。

topics.question: Do you think children should sometimes do things they don't want to do, such as visiting a parent who lives far away?
topics.questionZh: 你认为孩子有时应该做他们不想做的事吗？比如去看望住在远方的父母？
hints: 孩子面对什么不情愿的事
fly to another city to visit his mother / he didn't want to go, no way
家长怎么解释
many times we must do things we don't want / your mum needs you
怎样让孩子好受些
promise daily phone calls / small rituals and gifts
你的看法与边界
force rarely works / honesty and warmth matter
vocab: do things we do not want
get an idea into their heads
脑子里一有主意就（放不下）
我突然一下子难受起来
sample: Generally speaking, yes, I do think children sometimes have to do things they don't want to, as long as the reasons are solid.
总体上说，是的，我认为孩子有时必须做他们不想做的事，只要理由站得住脚。
A situation I witnessed recently explains what I mean.
我最近目睹的一个情形正好能说明我的意思。
After a divorce, a friend's nine-year-old son had to fly to another city to spend the holidays with his mother.
离婚后，朋友九岁的儿子得飞去另一座城市陪妈妈过节。
He didn't want to go, no way; he wanted to stay with his father and his friends.
他压根不想去，坚决不去；他想留在爸爸和朋友们身边。
The father didn't pretend it was fun; he simply said that many times we must do things we do not want, and that his mum needed him.
父亲没有假装这多好玩，只是说：很多时候我们都得做不想做的事，而且妈妈需要他。
What impressed me was how the father handled the details.
