让我佩服的是父亲处理细节的方式。
He promised the boy could call every day, and he had to promise, right away, to pass on small gifts to everyone, so the boy felt important rather than exiled.
他保证孩子每天都能打电话，还得马上保证把小礼物转交给家里的每个人，这样孩子觉得自己被重视，而不是被流放。
Kids that age get an idea into their heads, and careful little rituals help them let it go.
那个年纪的孩子脑子里一有主意就放不下，而用心的小仪式能帮他们放下。
When the boy came back, he was proud of the trip rather than angry about it.
男孩回来时，对这趟旅行挺自豪，而不是满肚子气。
The relationship with his mother clearly improved.
他和妈妈的关系明显变好了。
So I'd say making children do things occasionally is acceptable when it protects something bigger, like family bonds.
所以我想说，偶尔让孩子勉强做事是可以接受的，只要它守护的是更大的东西，比如亲情。
But it should come with honesty and warmth, not just 'because I said so.'
但必须配上坦诚和温情，而不是一句'我说了算'。

topics.question: Describe a festival or holiday you once spent away from your family. How did you feel, and what did you do?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你没有和家人一起度过的节日。你当时感受如何？是怎么过的？
hints: 为什么独自过节
my parents were abroad / all my friends had gone home
节日当天的感受
it just hit me / the flat felt enormous and silent
你怎么安排那一天
video-call home / cook a family recipe badly but proudly
那次的收获
I understood what festivals really mean / booked tickets early ever since
vocab: our first Christmas without my dad
没有爸爸的第一个圣诞节
sample: Last year, for the first time in my life, I spent the biggest family festival of the year completely alone.
去年，我有生以来第一次独自过最重要的团圆节。
My parents were abroad visiting relatives, my friends had all gone home, and I stayed in the city because of work.
父母在国外走亲戚，朋友们都回了家，我因为工作留在了城里。
I told everyone, and myself, that it was no big deal.
我跟所有人、也跟自己说，这没什么大不了。
But on the day itself, it just hit me: walking back to the empty flat, I suddenly understood I'd never been alone at a festival before.
可节日当天，情绪突然就上来了：走回空荡荡的公寓时，我忽然意识到自己从没一个人过过节。
The house felt enormous and strangely silent.
那房子显得格外大，也出奇地安静。
I decided not to feel sorry for myself, so I built a tiny routine.
我决定不自怜自艾，于是给自己安排了点小仪式。
I video-called my parents while they were preparing dinner, cooked my grandmother's dumpling recipe badly but proudly, and then went out to see the neighbourhood lights.
趁父母做饭时跟他们视频，笨手笨脚但很骄傲地照奶奶的方子包了饺子，然后出门看了小区的彩灯。
Later I called my brother as well, because it was our first festival without our grandfather, and we both needed to hear each other's voice.
后来我又给弟弟打了电话，因为那是我们没有爷爷的第一个节日，我们都需要听听对方的声音。
A friend had invited me to go skiing, but skiing's not my thing, and somehow that would have felt like escaping rather than celebrating.
有朋友约我去滑雪，可滑雪不是我擅长的，而且总觉得那像是逃开，而不是过节。
Strangely, by midnight I felt peaceful rather than sad.
奇怪的是，到了半夜，我心里是平静的，而不是难过。
Being alone taught me how much these celebrations actually mean to me.
独自过节反而教会我，这些团聚对我的意义有多重。
This year I booked my ticket home two months in advance.
今年我提前两个月就订好了回家的票。
Festivals, I've decided, are simply not the same without family around the table, and I refuse to turn into the Grinch who hates them.
我想明白了：全家不围坐一桌，节日就不是那个味儿——我可不想变成讨厌过节的怪人。

topics.question: Describe a tradition your family keeps during a festival. Why is it important to you?
topics.questionZh: 描述你们家在节日里保持的一项传统。它为什么对你重要？
hints: 传统是什么
we go from house to house / carry food we've prepared ourselves
传统怎么来的
it goes back three generations / my grandmother insists on it
有哪些讲究与细节
each family must invite you in / nobody is left alone that night
为什么对你重要
it turns neighbours into relatives / it wouldn't be the festival without it
sample: Every year during the Spring Festival, my family keeps a tradition that goes back at least three generations, and it's the part of the holiday I love most.
每年春节，我们家都会延续一项至少传了三代的传统，这也是节日里我最喜欢的部分。
On the first evening, we walk from house to house visiting our relatives, carrying food we've prepared ourselves.
头一天晚上，我们带着自己做的吃食，挨家挨户去看望亲戚。
The rule is old-fashioned and beautiful: at each door we call out a greeting, and the family inside must invite us in, offer tea, and add a dish to our basket.
规矩老派却美好：每到一家门口我们高声道贺，里面的人家必须请我们进屋、上茶，再往我们篮子里添一样菜。
It sounds simple, but by the end of the evening the whole street smells of dumplings and laughter.
听起来简单，可到了晚上，整条街都弥漫着饺子味和笑声。
My grandmother explains it as sharing the year's story house by house: who got married, who had a baby, who needs help.
奶奶的说法是，这是挨家挨户分享这一年的故事：谁结婚了，谁添了孩子，谁需要搭把手。
In a way, it's our version of asking for shelter, which is what the tradition originally meant.
某种意义上，这就是我们'请求留宿'的版本，也正是这项传统最初的本义。
Nobody is left alone on that night, which I think is the real point.
那一晚没有人会被落下，我觉得这才是真正的用意。
Two years ago my grandmother was too weak to walk the whole route, so we drove her between the houses.
两年前奶奶体力不支走不完全程，我们就开车送她挨家走。
She insisted on going anyway, saying it wouldn't be the festival without it.
她坚持一定要去，说少了这一环就不算过节。
That's why this tradition matters to me: it turns neighbours back into relatives and reminds us what the holiday is actually for.
这就是这项传统对我重要的原因：它让街坊重新变回亲人，提醒我们节日到底是为了什么。
I hope I'll be walking that route with my own children one day.
我希望有一天能带着自己的孩子继续走那条路。

topics.question: Describe a time when you received an invitation that was difficult to accept or refuse. What did you do?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你收到一份难以接受也难以拒绝的邀请的经历。你是怎么做的？
hints: 什么邀请、为什么尴尬
a single-father colleague asked me to spend the holiday with him
尴尬在哪里
it was more than friendly / I didn't feel the same way
你怎么回应
I chose my words carefully / please don't misunderstand me
后续与反思
he said he was out of line / honesty over a comfortable lie
vocab: I don't know what to say
sample: Last winter I received an invitation that took me completely by surprise and put me in a genuinely awkward position.
去年冬天，我收到一份完全出乎意料的邀请，一下子陷入了实实在在的尴尬。
A colleague I like and respect, a single father, asked me, very nervously, to spend the New Year holidays with him and his son.
一位我敬重也喜欢的同事——一位单亲爸爸——非常紧张地问我和他还有他儿子一起过新年。
The problem wasn't him; the problem was the meaning behind it.
问题不在他这个人，而在这份邀请背后的含义。
I could tell it was more than a friendly invitation, and I didn't feel the same way.
我看得出来这不只是朋友式的邀请，而我对他没有同样的感觉。
I remember thinking I didn't want to make a fool of myself, and I really didn't want to hurt him either.
我记得当时心想，我既不想让自己出洋相，也实在不想伤害他。
He asked so quietly that for a second I honestly didn't know what to say.
他问得那么小声，有一秒钟我真不知道该说什么。
Then I told him the truth carefully: that he was one of the kindest men I knew, a wonderful father, and that I valued our friendship enormously.
然后我斟酌着说了实话：他是我认识的最体贴的男人之一，是一位好父亲，我非常珍惜我们的友谊。
I said please don't misunderstand me, but I couldn't accept.
我说请别误会我，但我不能接受。
He reacted better than I feared, apologising and saying he was out of line, which broke my heart a little.
他的反应比我想象的好，连声道歉说自己失礼了，这反而让我有点心酸。
I answered that he hadn't bothered me at all, and I meant it.
我回答说他完全没有打扰到我，这是真心话。
Things were strange between us for about two weeks, and then, slowly, back to normal.
有两周左右我们之间有点别扭，然后慢慢地恢复了正常。
Looking back, I'm proud I chose honesty over a comfortable lie.
回头看来，我很庆幸自己选择了诚实，而不是一个体面的谎言。

topics.question: Describe a time when you waited a long time for something important. Was the wait worth it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你为一件重要的事情漫长等待的经历。等待值得吗？
hints: 在等什么、等了多久
an open audition / we'd been there for hours
等待中反复挣扎
how much longer do you want to wait / I wanted to leave more than once
为什么坚持下来
this is gonna be worth it / we'd counted on this chance
结局与感悟
we were told to leave our tapes / disappointment showed me what I cared about
vocab: this is gonna be worth it
how much longer do you want to wait
我们在这儿等了好几个小时
I was told we could play for them
说好了我们能给他们演奏
sample: A couple of months ago, a friend dragged me to an open audition for a local band, and the waiting taught me more than the audition itself.
几个月前，朋友硬拉我去参加一个本地乐队的公开试音，那段等待教给我的东西比试音本身还多。
We had an appointment at three in the afternoon, and we arrived early, completely full of hope.
我们约的是下午三点，到得很早，满心希望。
At first everything looked promising: someone met us at the door and told us to follow him.
起初一切看起来很有戏：有人在门口接我们，让我们跟着走。
Then we were asked to wait outside, because the manager was tied up right now.
然后我们被请到外面等，说经纪人这会儿正忙着。
And that 'right now' turned into hours.
结果这个'这会儿'一等就是几个钟头。
The waiting room had no clock, so I kept asking my friend what time it was.
等候室里没有钟，我就不停地问朋友几点了。
At some point he laughed and said, 'It's ten minutes later than the last time you asked me. How much longer do you want to wait?'
后来他笑说：'比你上次问的时候晚了十分钟，你到底还想等多久？'
Honestly, I wanted to leave more than once, but my friend refused: 'We've been here for hours. This is gonna be worth it.'
说实话我不止一次想走，但朋友不肯：'我们都等了几个钟头了，肯定会值得的。'
In the end we got bad news: the band had to leave without seeing us.
最后等来的是坏消息：乐队临时有事走了，没能看我们。
We were told to leave our tapes, except I didn't have a tape with me, and neither did my friend.
对方让我们留下样带，可我手上没带，朋友也没带。
You'd think the day was a total failure, but strangely it wasn't.
你会觉得那天彻底失败了，但奇怪的是并没有。
Standing there, I realised I was disappointed, which meant I genuinely cared about music.
站在那里，我意识到自己很失落——这说明我是真心在乎音乐的。
That afternoon convinced me to prepare properly and try again.
那个下午让我下定决心，好好准备，再来一次。

topics.question: Do you think students should avoid romantic relationships in order to focus on their studies?
topics.questionZh: 你认为学生应该为了专心学业而回避恋爱吗？
hints: 你的立场
it depends on the person / for me, study comes first right now
一次真实的选择
someone I liked showed interest / I came here to get a college education
怎么处理感情问题
be honest and stay friends / you can't do both half-heartedly
辩证看
romance isn't the natural enemy of study / losing focus is
vocab: I came here to get a college education
我来这儿是上大学读书的
my music and my music alone
it hasn't been easy to get this far
走到今天这一步不容易
sample: My honest answer is: it depends on the person and the moment, and I say that from experience.
我的诚实回答是：因人、因时机而异，这是我的切身体会。
For me personally, at this stage of my life, study has to come first, and I've actually made that choice consciously.
对我个人而言，在人生这个阶段，学业必须排在第一位，而且我是有意识地做出了这个选择。
When I started university, someone I liked very much showed interest in me.
刚上大学时，一个我很喜欢的人对我表露了好感。
It was flattering, but I paused and asked myself what I actually came here for, and the answer was clear: I came here to get a college education.
这让人飘飘然，但我停下来问自己：我到底为什么来这儿？答案很清楚：我是来读书的。
It hasn't been easy to get this far, and my family sacrificed a lot for it.
走到今天这一步并不容易，家里为此付出了很多。
So I told him honestly that I couldn't be involved with anyone right now.
于是我坦白告诉他，眼下我不能和任何人谈恋爱。
It wasn't a dramatic refusal; we simply stayed friends.
那不是什么戏剧化的拒绝；我们只是继续做朋友。
Right now it's got to be my music, and my music alone, at least until I stand on my own feet.
现在只能是音乐，也只有音乐，至少等我能自己站稳脚跟。
That said, I don't think romance and study are natural enemies.
话虽如此，我并不认为恋爱和学业是天敌。
I've seen couples who pushed each other forward and became better students together.
我见过互相促进、一起进步的情侣。
The real enemy is losing focus, and you can lose focus through gaming or laziness just as easily.
真正的敌人是失焦，而打游戏、犯懒同样能让人失焦。
So my advice is simple: know your priority, be honest about it, and don't judge people who choose differently.
所以我的建议很简单：想清楚你的优先级，坦诚面对它，也别去评判选择不同的人。

topics.question: Describe a time when you performed or showed your talent in front of strangers. How did you feel?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你在陌生人面前表演或展示才艺的经历。你当时感觉如何？
hints: 什么场合、怎么轮到你
the engineer offered one quick take / my friend said, give it a go
开口前的心情
here goes nothing / my heart was hammering
表演时发生了什么
I sang a song I wrote / after the first line, the fear disappeared
这次经历的收获
opportunities don't wait for ready people / it changed how I see myself
sample: The performance I'll never forget lasted about ninety seconds and happened almost by accident.
我永远忘不了的那次表演只持续了大约九十秒，而且几乎纯属偶然。
After a long day of waiting, the studio engineer suddenly offered to record a quick track for us.
在漫长等待之后，录音棚的录音师突然提出给我们快速录一小段。
My friend sat down at the piano and asked what key I sang in.
朋友在钢琴前坐下，问我是唱什么调的。
I said G, my heart was hammering, and then the engineer said, 'Tape's rolling. Any time you're ready.'
我说 G 调，心咚咚直跳，这时录音师说：'开始录了，你准备好随时开始。'
Ninety seconds earlier I had been complaining that I still had an exam to study for, and I'd only agreed after my friend said, 'Come on, give it a go.'
九十秒前我还在抱怨还有考试要复习，是朋友一句'来吧，试一把'才把我推上去的。
I stepped up to the microphone thinking, here goes nothing.
我走向麦克风，心里想着：豁出去了。
I introduced myself, and then I sang a song I wrote myself, the first one I'd ever finished.
我报上名字，然后唱了一首我自己写的歌，那是我写完的第一首。
The strange thing is that the fear disappeared after the first line; the song simply carried me.
奇怪的是，唱完第一句恐惧就消失了，是歌带着我走。
When I finished, the engineer nodded without any comment, which somehow felt like the highest praise possible.
我唱完，录音师什么也没说只是点了点头，不知怎么，这感觉像是最高的褒奖。
My friend said my voice was shaking a little, but the emotion was real.
朋友说我的声音有点抖，但感情是真的。
Walking out into the cold evening, I couldn't stop smiling.
走进寒冷的夜色里，我笑得合不拢嘴。
That minute and a half changed how I see myself.
那九十秒改变了我对自己的看法。
I learned that opportunities don't wait for you to feel ready; you just have to start.
我明白了：机会不会等你觉得自己准备好了，你只能先开口。

topics.question: Describe a time when your plans changed suddenly and completely. How did you handle it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你的计划被突然彻底打乱的经历。你是怎么应对的？
hints: 原计划是什么
an appointment at three / two songs prepared
变故怎么发生
the manager was tied up / the band had to leave without seeing us
当场怎么应对
we looked for plan B / one quick take instead of a full audition
学到了什么
a plan is only a starting point / plan B sometimes beats plan A
vocab: I don't have a tape with me
sample: I'm generally a planner, so when my plans collapse suddenly, I remember it for years.
我这个人习惯做计划，所以计划突然崩盘的事，我能记好多年。
The clearest example is an audition day, which began with a schedule and ended in pure improvisation.
最典型的例子是试音那天：开局是排好的日程，收场是彻底的即兴发挥。
The plan looked solid: an appointment in the afternoon, two songs prepared, and my friend on the piano.
计划看着很稳：下午有约，备好两首歌，朋友弹钢琴。
Then reality took over: the manager was tied up, then unreachable, and the waiting had no end in sight.
然后现实接管了一切：经纪人先是抽不开身，接着联系不上，等待遥遥无期。
At some point my friend went to find out what was happening, and came back with the news I was dreading.
后来朋友去打听情况，带回了我最怕听到的消息。
I've got some bad news, he said; the band had to leave.
他说：有个坏消息，乐队不得不走了。
For a moment we just stood there, because we had counted on this chance for weeks.
那一瞬间我们俩僵在原地，因为这个机会我们盼了好几个星期。
We were even asked to leave tapes behind, which neither of us had.
对方还让我们留下样带，可我们俩谁都没带。
But here's the part I'm proud of: instead of going home bitter, we looked around and saw an opportunity inside the disappointment.
但最让我自豪的是这一段：我们没有带着怨气回家，而是在失望里看到了机会。
The engineer, in a hurry to leave, agreed to record one quick take for us, and that scratch recording became my first studio experience.
急着下班的录音师同意给我们快速录一版，那段小样成了我第一次进棚的经历。
That day taught me that a plan is only a starting point.
那天让我明白，计划只是个起点。
What matters is refusing to walk away when the plan dies, because plan B sometimes beats plan A.
真正重要的是计划死掉时不肯离场，因为 B 计划有时反而胜过 A 计划。

topics.question: Describe a time when you had to study or prepare for something under great pressure. How did you handle it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你不得不在巨大压力下学习或备考的经历。你是怎么应对的？
hints: 什么考试或任务、压力有多大
four finals in five days / I'd missed three weeks of class
为什么压力这么大
if I fail my exams, I lose my scholarship / there's a lot at stake
你怎么安排时间
it's going to take every waking hour / I made a strict plan
结果与感悟
I did all right in the end / pressure didn't crush me once I broke it down
sample: Last December I went through the most stressful week of my student life: four final exams in five days, and I had missed almost three weeks of classes because of a family emergency.
去年十二月我经历了学生时代压力最大的一周：五天之内四门期末考，而因为家里有急事，我落了将近三周的课。
I knew catching up would take every waking hour, so I turned down every invitation that week and locked myself in my room.
我知道赶进度要占掉醒着的每一刻，所以那周我推掉了所有邀请，把自己关在房间里。
The pressure was enormous because there was a lot at stake: if I failed even one exam, I would lose my scholarship, and my parents would have to borrow money for my tuition.
压力特别大，因为赌注不小：只要挂掉一门，我就会失去奖学金，爸妈就得借钱给我交学费。
So I studied like mad. I got up at six, reviewed two subjects a day, and only stopped to eat.
于是我拼命学：六点起床，每天复习两门，只有吃饭才停一下。
Whenever I wanted to give up, I told myself, 'Just one more chapter, and then you can rest.'
每当想放弃，我就跟自己说：'再看一章，就能歇了。'
The sweetest part was the small kindness from people around me.
最暖心的是身边人小小的好意。
My landlady noticed how pale I looked and left a box of chocolates outside my door with a note saying, 'You deserve a special treat.'
房东太太看我脸色苍白，在门口放了一盒巧克力，还留了张条子：'你该好好犒劳自己。'
Honestly, that little gesture cheered me up more than a whole night of sleep.
说实话，这份小小的心意比睡一整晚觉还让我振奋。
In the end, I passed everything, and one course even got the second-highest grade in my class.
最后我全都过了，还有一门拿了班里第二高的分。
That week taught me that pressure doesn't crush you if you break it into small daily tasks.
那一周让我明白：只要把压力拆成每天的小任务，它就压不垮你。
Now whenever finals come, I don't panic — I make a plan and get going.
现在每逢期末我都不慌——定好计划就开工。

topics.question: Do you think talent alone is enough to succeed in a competitive field such as music or sport?
topics.questionZh: 你认为在音乐或体育这类竞争激烈的领域，单凭才华就足以成功吗？
hints: 观点先行：才华只是起点
talent is only the starting point / it opens the door
行业现实：成功还涉及生意
you need more than talent to make it in this business
还需要什么：自律、人脉、运气
discipline, connections and a bit of luck
热爱让人撑下去
making music is like breathing / keep your passion alive
sample: To be honest, I don't think talent alone is enough — not even close.
说实话，我觉得光有才华远远不够——差得远呢。
A friend of mine is a gifted songwriter, and watching her struggle in the music business really changed my view on this.
我有个朋友是个很有天赋的写歌人，看着她在音乐圈里摸爬滚打，我对此的看法彻底变了。
She has a wonderful voice, and people always say there's real talent there.
她嗓音很棒，大家总说她真有才华。
But as a producer once told her, you need more than talent to make it in this business, because it is a business — it means selling records, doing big tours, and, well, making money.
但正如一位制作人跟她说的：在这个行当成事，光有才华不够，因为它本质是门生意——要卖唱片、做大型巡演，说白了要赚钱。
Talent opens the door, but hard work, connections and a bit of luck keep you in the room.
才华能开门，但努力、人脉加上一点运气才能让你留在屋里。
What impresses me most is that she never lost her love for music.
最让我佩服的是，她从未丢掉对音乐的热爱。
She once said, 'Making music is like breathing — I can't imagine my life without it.'
她说过：'做音乐就像呼吸，没法想象没有它的人生。'
For her, success isn't only fame; it's being able to keep making music every single day.
对她来说，成功不只是名气，而是每天还能继续做音乐。
Don't get me wrong — I'm not saying talent doesn't matter; it's the entry ticket.
别误会，我不是说才华不重要，它是入场券。
But in any competitive field, the ones who last combine talent with discipline and a clear head about the business side.
但在任何竞争激烈的领域，能坚持到最后的，都是把才华和自律、再加上对生意一面的清醒头脑结合起来的人。
My friend is still on her way, but I'd bet she'll make it, each in her own way.
我朋友还在路上，但我打赌她会以自己的方式成功。

topics.question: Describe a time when you performed in front of others or took part in an audition. How did you feel before and after?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你在别人面前表演或参加试音的经历。之前和之后你各是什么心情？
hints: 什么场合、为什么参加
I signed up for an audition / a friend said I should give it a shot
准备过程
we rehearsed for two weeks / my partner arranged the song
上台前的紧张
my hands were shaking / my heart was pounding
结果与收获
don't call us, we'll call you / it was worth it anyway
vocab: don't call us; we'll call you
别打给我们，我们打给你（等通知）
sample: Last spring I took part in an audition for the campus music club's annual show, and I still remember every minute of it.
去年春天我参加了校园音乐社年度演出的试音，每一分钟我都还记得。
A classmate had heard me play guitar in the dorm and said, 'You should give it a shot.'
同学在宿舍听我弹过吉他，说：'你应该去试试。'
We rehearsed for two weeks, and my partner, who arranged the whole song, kept saying, 'Hey, relax! Leave everything to me.'
我们排练了两周，编曲的搭档总说：'放松！一切交给我。'
I was still nervous on the day. My hands were shaking so much that I could barely hold the pick.
当天我还是紧张，手抖得几乎握不住拨片。
But once we started, the music carried me, and the two minutes flew by.
但音乐一响起来，我就被带着走了，两分钟一晃而过。
Afterwards, the judges were polite but cold: 'Thanks for coming in. If we like the songs, we'll call you. Remember, don't call us; we'll call you.'
之后评委客气又冷淡：'谢谢你们来。如果我们喜欢，会打电话给你们。记住，别打给我们，我们打给你们。'
On the way out, my partner laughed and said, 'Some audition, huh? They probably won't even listen to the tapes.'
出来时搭档笑着说：'这也算试音？他们八成连带子都不会听。'
I just answered, 'Who cares! We did our best,' and I really meant it.
我只回了一句：'管它呢！我们尽力了。'——而且我是真心的。
A week later we actually got the call and performed in the show.
一周后我们真接到了电话，上了那场演出。
That experience taught me two things: seize the chance and give it a shot, and never let other people's coldness decide how you feel about your own performance.
那次经历教会我两件事：抓住机会去试，还有绝不让别人冷淡的态度来决定你对自己表现的评价。

topics.question: Describe a piece of advice that an older relative or family friend gave you. Did you follow it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一位年长的亲戚或世交长辈给过你的一条忠告。你听从了吗？
hints: 谁给的忠告、什么场合
my godmother sat me down one evening and said...
忠告的内容
you have to make up your mind / we don't want history to repeat itself
你的第一反应
honestly, I didn't want to hear it at first
后来怎么想、怎么做
deep down I knew she was right / I finally made my decision
vocab: put my nose into your business
we don't want history to repeat itself
get your nose out of the books
sample: The advice I want to talk about came from my aunt, who is like a godmother to me — straight-talking and never afraid to put her nose into my business.
我想说的忠告来自我姑姑，她就像我的教母——心直口快，从不怕掺和我的事。
Two years ago I was dragging my feet between two universities: one was safe and close to home, and the other had my dream programme but was far away and expensive.
两年前我在两所大学之间犹豫拖延：一所稳妥离家近，另一所有我梦想的专业，但又远又贵。

One evening my aunt sat me down and said, 'You're going to have to make up your mind, dear. If you keep hesitating, you'll end up choosing nothing. We don't want history to repeat itself — your father made the same mistake at your age.'
一天晚上姑姑让我坐下，说：'你得拿定主意了。再犹豫下去，你最后什么也选不成。我们不想让历史重演——你爸在你这岁数就犯过同样的错。'
Honestly, my first reaction was to roll my eyes — nobody likes hearing the truth about themselves.
说实话，我第一反应是翻白眼——没人爱听关于自己的实话。
But that night I couldn't sleep, because deep down I knew she was right.
可那晚我睡不着，因为心底里我知道她说得对。
The next morning I sent my application to the dream school.
第二天一早，我就把申请寄给了梦想的学校。
Looking back, that was some of the best advice I've ever received.
回头想想，那是我收到过的最好的忠告之一。
What made it work was the relationship: she knew my family's story, so her warning carried weight.
它之所以管用，靠的是我们的关系：她了解我家的故事，所以她的提醒有分量。
Now when younger cousins come to me, I try to be like her — honest, caring, and brave enough to speak up.
现在小辈们来找我时，我也想成为她那样的人——诚实、关爱，还敢开口直说。

topics.question: Do you think a man and a woman can be just good friends? Use your own experience or people you know to explain.
topics.questionZh: 你认为男性和女性可以成为纯好朋友吗？请结合自己或身边人的经历说明。
hints: 观点先行：可以，但需要坦诚
yes, but feelings can get complicated
经历：一段差点变味的友谊
a few things got misunderstood between us
怎么把话说开
we sat down and talked it out / the very best friendship
现在的关系
we still call each other about once a month
vocab: it's been one heck of a relationship
sample: Yes, I believe a man and a woman can be just good friends — but I also know it takes honesty, because feelings can get complicated.
我相信男女之间可以纯粹做朋友——但我也知道这需要坦诚，因为感情可能会变复杂。
My best friend at university was a boy I met on a hiking trip.
我大学最好的朋友，是徒步时认识的一个男生。
We studied different subjects but shared the same sense of humour, and we told each other everything.
我们专业不同，但笑点一致，无话不谈。
For a while things were a bit awkward, because honestly a few things got misunderstood between us — he thought I wanted more than friendship, and I didn't.
有段时间气氛有点尴尬，因为说实话我们之间有些事被误会了——他以为我想要的超出友谊，其实并没有。
Instead of letting the friendship drift, we sat down one afternoon and talked it out.
我们没有任其疏远，而是找个下午坐下来把话说开了。
I told him, 'This friendship means a lot to me, and I know it's going to last a long time.'
我告诉他：'这段友谊对我很重要，我知道它会长长久久。'
He took a breath and answered, 'The very best friendship, then.' After that, the air was clear, and we became closer than before.
他松了口气，答道：'那就做最铁的朋友。'从那以后疙瘩解开了，我们反而更亲近了。
Now he works in another city, and our interests are quite different — skiing is his passion, for example, while it's honestly not my thing.
现在他在另一座城市工作，我们的爱好也差挺多——比如滑雪是他的心头好，而说实话那不是我的菜。
But it's been one heck of a relationship, and I wouldn't trade it for a romance: he's the friend who knows all my faults and stays anyway.
不过这段交情真不一般，拿它换段恋爱我都不干：他是那个清楚我所有缺点却依然留下的朋友。

topics.question: Describe the most special gift you have ever received. Who gave it to you, and why is it so special?
topics.questionZh: 描述你收到过的最特别的礼物。是谁送的？为什么它如此特别？
hints: 什么礼物、谁送的、什么场合
a framed photograph from a friend who was moving away
礼物背后的心思
he remembered how much I admired it at his exhibition
它捕捉了什么
it catches the innocence and spirit of...
现在放在哪、意味着什么
it hangs above my desk / it stops a moment from disappearing
vocab: 捕捉到他的天真与神采
我最喜欢的某人的照片
give sb a ride to the airport
sample: The most special gift I've ever received is a framed photograph that an old friend gave me before he moved to another city.
我收到过的最特别的礼物，是一位老朋友搬去别的城市之前送我的一张装了框的照片。
It's a black-and-white picture he took on a beach trip a few years ago: my little nephew and I are laughing at something silly, and the light is perfect.
那是他几年前在海边旅行时拍的黑白照：我和小侄子因为一件傻事笑作一团，光线刚刚好。
He remembered how much I admired that photo at his little exhibition, so before leaving, he framed it and gave it to me.
他记得我在他的小型摄影展上多么喜欢那张照片，所以离开前，他把它装了框送给我。
He said something I'll never forget: 'I guess it catches his innocence and spirit — and the way you two look at each other.'
他说了一句我永远忘不了的话：'我想它捕捉到了他的天真和神采，还有你们俩看彼此的眼神。'
That's exactly why it's special: a bought gift says 'I have a budget', but a photo like this says 'I was paying attention'.
这正是它特别的原因：买来的礼物说明'我有预算'，而这样一张照片说明'我一直在留意'。
It wasn't top of the line or expensive — it cost him almost nothing — but no money could buy it.
它不是什么顶级奢侈品，几乎没花他什么钱，但多少钱都买不来。
It hangs above my desk now, and whenever work gets me down, I look at it and hear that afternoon's laughter again.
它现在就挂在我书桌上方，每当工作让我沮丧，看一眼就能再听见那个下午的笑声。
To me, that's what a great gift does: it stops a precious moment from disappearing.
对我来说，好礼物就是这样：让一个珍贵的瞬间不再溜走。

topics.question: Describe an experience when you helped people in your community. What did you do, and what did you learn from it?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你在社区里帮助别人的经历。你做了什么？从中学到了什么？
hints: 活动是什么、怎么参与的
we took Christmas dinners over to the community center
具体做了什么
prepare the food the day before / I brought an extra hand
印象最深的人或瞬间
everyone started singing / I almost had tears in my eyes
感悟
in these hard times, it could be any one of us
vocab: it could be any one of us
落难的可能是我们任何人
I can't think of any other place I'd rather be
我想不出还有哪儿更想去
sample: Two winters ago, I helped out at a community centre dinner on Christmas Day, and it completely changed how I see festivals.
两年前的冬天，我在社区中心的圣诞晚餐帮了一天忙，那件事彻底改变了我对节日的看法。
To be honest, I only signed up because a friend was short of people, but it ended up being one of the warmest days of that whole winter.
说实话，我当初报名只是因为朋友缺人手，可它最后成了那个冬天最暖的一天。
The organiser, who runs a small restaurant, cooked most of the food, and volunteers like me prepared the trays and served them.
组织者是家小餐馆的老板，做了大部分菜，我们这些志愿者分装餐盘、端给来客。
I brought some canned food and, as I joked at the door, 'an extra hand'.
我带了些罐头，还在门口打趣说自己带来了'一双有空的手'。
When someone asked why I wasn't at home celebrating, I said, 'I can't think of any other place I'd rather be.'
有人问我怎么不在家过节，我说：'我想不出还有哪儿更让我想待的。'
The people who came were mostly elderly folks living alone and a few families in real trouble.
来的大多是独居老人，还有几户真正困难的家庭。
In these hard times, it could be any one of us — that thought kept going through my head while I poured soup.
时世艰难，落难的可能是我们任何人——盛汤的时候，这个念头一直在我脑中打转。
At one point everyone started singing together, and I almost had tears in my eyes.
后来大家齐声唱起歌来，我眼眶都差点湿了。
What stayed with me is that we got as much pleasure out of serving as they got out of eating.
最留在我心里的是：我们服务他们所得到的快乐，不比他们吃饭得到的少。
Since then, helping out stopped being a holiday thing for me and became a habit all year round.
从那以后，帮忙对我来说不再是节日限定，而成了一年四季的习惯。

topics.question: Do you think people today still keep the true spirit of festivals, or has it been lost?
topics.questionZh: 你认为如今的人们还保有节日的真正精神吗？还是说它已经丢失了？
hints: 现状：节日越来越像购物
festivals feel more and more commercial
转折经历：一次找回节日精神
I hadn't felt this much festival spirit since I was a kid
节日精神从哪来
it's something you do — cooking, visiting, singing together
你现在怎么做
I invite friends who can't go home / this kind of holiday shapes up better than I thought
vocab: Christmas comes only once a year
here's to a very special Christmas
I almost had tears in my eyes
shaping up better than I thought
sample: To be honest, I used to complain that festivals had lost their spirit — everything felt like shopping.
说实话，我以前总抱怨节日没了味道——什么 都像在购物。
My family's New Year ritual was basically everyone staring at their phones around a table full of expensive food.
我家过新年的固定节目，基本就是一桌贵价菜周围人人盯着手机。
Then I spent the holiday with my grandmother in her small town, and it woke me up.
后来有一年我陪奶奶在小城过节，一下子被点醒了。
Neighbours dropped by with homemade cakes, kids ran between houses, and on festival night the whole street sang together.
邻居端着自家做的糕点串门，孩子们在房子之间跑来跑去，节日当晚整条街一起唱歌。
I remember telling her, 'I haven't felt this much festival spirit since I was a kid.'
我记得跟她说：'我从小时候起，就没感受过这么浓的节日气氛了。'
That's when I realised the spirit never disappeared — we just stopped making it.
那一刻我明白，节日精神从未消失，只是我们不再去营造它。
Festivals aren't something you consume; they're something you do — cooking together, visiting people, singing badly but loudly.
节日不是用来消费的，而是用来'做'的——一起下厨、走亲访友、唱得难听却大声。
So now I take the initiative: I invite friends who can't go home, I cook one dish from my grandmother's recipe, and I put my phone away after dinner.
所以现在我主动起来：邀请回不了家的朋友，照奶奶的方子做一道菜，晚饭后把手机收起来。
This kind of holiday always ends up shaping up better than I thought.
这样过节，最后总是比预想的还要圆满。
After all, a big festival comes only once a year — it deserves a little effort.
毕竟大节日一年才一次，值得为它花点心思。
So yes, the spirit is still out there; we just have to show up for it.
所以，节日精神其实一直都在——只是我们得肯为它现身。

topics.question: Do you think a handmade gift is more meaningful than an expensive one bought in a shop? Why?
topics.questionZh: 你认为手工做的礼物比商店里买的贵重礼物更有心意吗？为什么？
hints: 观点：心意大于价格
it's the thought that counts
经历：收到过的手作礼物
he made the little statue at school / wrapped in newspaper
为什么难忘
I'll keep it forever / it cost him a whole week of lunch breaks
让步：买的礼物也可以有心意
a well-chosen bought gift can be thoughtful too
vocab: he made the statue at school
这雕像他在学校亲手做的
sample: Yes, in most cases I find a handmade gift more meaningful, and I say this as someone who has received both kinds.
是的，多数情况下我觉得手工礼物更有心意——作为一个两种都收到过的人，我这么讲。
The gift I treasure most is a little clay statue of a baseball player that my ten-year-old student made at school.
我最珍视的礼物，是一个十岁学生在学校亲手捏的小泥像——一个棒球击球手。
He wrapped it in newspaper and wrote 'Merry Christmas' on a card that was spelled half wrong.
他用报纸把它包着，卡片上的'圣诞快乐'还拼错了好几个字母。
Honestly, it isn't beautiful — one leg is shorter than the other — but when I opened it, I shouted, 'What a riot! I'll keep it forever!'
说实话它并不精美——一条腿比另一条短——但打开的那一刻我还是喊了出来：'太逗了！我要永远留着！'
Compare that with an expensive scarf my uncle once gave me: it was probably ten times the price, but it has stayed in a drawer ever since.
再对比舅舅送过我的贵围巾：价格恐怕是十倍，却从那以后一直躺在抽屉里。
The statue sits on my desk, because every time I see it I remember that kid's proud face.
而泥像就摆在我桌上，每次看到，我都会想起那孩子自豪的脸。
The scarf cost money; the statue cost a whole week of his lunch breaks.
围巾花的是钱；泥像花的是他整整一周的午休时间。
Of course, handmade isn't always possible, and a well-chosen bought gift can be thoughtful too.
当然，手工并不总是可行，精心挑选的礼物同样可以很有心意。
But if you have the time and the skill, make something — because what people keep forever is rarely the price tag.
但只要有余力和手艺，就动手做点什么——因为人们永远留存的，几乎从来不是价签。

topics.question: Describe an object that you keep for good luck or that has a special meaning to you.
topics.questionZh: 描述一件你留着求好运、或对你有特殊意义的物件。
hints: 物件是什么、哪来的
a small clay figure a friend brought back from Peru
它的传说或故事
legend has it that he can bring you good luck
你把什么愿望寄托在上面
hang all your dreams on it / a tiny diploma, a mini guitar
你真的信吗
not literally, but it reminds me of what I'm working towards
vocab: hang all your dreams on it
sample: The object I'd like to describe is a small clay figure called an ekeko, which a friend brought back from Peru for me.
我想讲的物件是一个叫'爱卡克'的小陶人，是朋友从秘鲁带回来送我的。
It sits on my bookshelf now, between two dictionaries, and almost every visitor asks me what on earth it is.
它现在就摆在我的书架上，夹在两本词典中间，几乎每个来做客的人都会问我这到底是什么。
It's a chubby little man about ten centimetres tall, wearing a knitted hat, with tiny goods hanging all over his body — mini rice bags, tiny banknotes, even a little house.
他是个约十厘米高的圆滚滚小人，戴着针织帽，身上挂满微型物件——迷你米袋、袖珍钞票，甚至还有一间小房子。
Legend has it that he can bring you good luck and fulfil your dreams if you hang all your dreams on him.
传说只要把梦想都挂在他身上，他就能带来好运、帮你实现梦想。
So I did exactly that: I tied a small paper diploma on his arm when I was preparing for a difficult exam, and a tiny guitar when I started learning music.
于是我真这么做了：备考那阵子，我在他胳膊上系了个小纸文凭；开始学音乐时，又挂了把迷你吉他。
When my friend told me the ekeko needs a cigarette once a day to work, I laughed and said, 'You're joking?' — apparently not.
朋友告诉我，这小人每天得抽一根烟才灵，我笑着说：'你开玩笑吧？'——居然还不是玩笑。
But I never smoke, so I just let him stay unlit and healthy.
不过我不抽烟，就让他保持'未点燃'的健康状态。
Do I really believe in the magic? Not literally.
我真信这魔力吗？倒也不是。
But every time I glance at him on my shelf, I remember what I'm working towards, and that little reminder is luck enough for me.
但每次瞥见架上的他，我就会想起自己正在为什么努力——这点提醒，对我来说就够幸运了。
Maybe that's why, before big exams or interviews, I still give the little fellow a gentle pat on the head — just in case.
也许正因如此，每逢大考或面试前，我还是会轻轻拍拍这个小家伙的头——万一灵呢。

topics.question: Do you think it is worth travelling a long way to visit family members, or are phone calls and video chats enough?
topics.questionZh: 你认为值得长途旅行去探望亲人吗？还是打电话、视频聊天就足够了？
hints: 观点：见面无可替代
nothing beats being there in person
经历：只靠屏幕联系的日子
we only 'met' through the screen / conversations got shorter
一次跨越距离的探望
a round-trip ticket as a birthday present / I showed him the town
感悟
distance tests family bonds, but a visit recharges them
vocab: I just wish sb were here
that's what airplanes were made for
sample: I believe phone calls and video chats are wonderful, but they can't replace actually being there — and my family learned this the hard way.
我认为电话和视频很棒，但替代不了人到场的陪伴——这一点，我家是深有体会的。
My brother and I live in different cities, and for about two years we only 'met' through the screen.
我和弟弟住在不同的城市，大概有两年，我们只靠屏幕'见面'。
We said the usual things — work, health, 'take care' — but somehow the conversations got shorter and shorter.
聊的无非是工作、健康、'保重'，可不知怎么，话越来越少。
Last spring, our aunt gave him a round-trip ticket to visit me as a birthday present, saying, 'You miss her, don't you? That's what airplanes were made for.'
去年春天，姑姑送了他一张来看我的往返机票当生日礼物，还说：'你想姐姐了，不是吗？飞机就是为这个造的。'
Those three days changed everything.
那三天改变了一切。
I showed him the town — my favourite noodle shop, the park where I jog, my office — and we cooked together like when we were kids.
我带他把这座城市逛了个遍——我最爱的面馆、我跑步的公园、我上班的地方——我们还像小时候那样一起做饭。
When he left, he said quietly, 'I miss this — the real you, not the small square face on my phone.'
他走的时候轻声说：'我想念这些——真实的你，而不是手机里那个小方块脸。'
We stayed up talking until two in the morning, about nothing important — and that, it turned out, was exactly the point.
我们聊到凌晨两点，聊的都不是什么要紧事——后来想想，这恰恰才是重点。
Since then, we fly to see each other at least twice a year, no matter how busy we are.
从那以后，无论多忙，我们每年至少飞去见对方两次。
Distance tests family bonds, but one good visit can recharge them like nothing else.
距离确实考验亲情，但一次好好的探望，比什么都能给它充电。

topics.question: Describe how you usually spend New Year's Eve, and tell the story of one celebration that was especially memorable.
topics.questionZh: 描述你通常怎么过新年前夜，并讲一次特别难忘的跨年经历。
hints: 通常怎么跨年
a big dinner with family / counting down together
一次特别的邀请
a friend asked me to come to his restaurant and be his guest
那晚最有意思的部分
strangers became friends / we rang in the new year with bells and hugs
你的新年决心
my resolution was simple — spend more time with the people who matter
vocab: Are you two an item yet?
sample: New Year's Eve is my favourite night of the year, and I've spent it in all kinds of ways — but one stands out.
新年前夜是我一年里最喜欢的夜晚，我试过各种过法，但有一次最难忘。
Two years ago, a friend who manages a restaurant invited me to celebrate there as his guest.
两年前，一位经营餐馆的朋友请我去他店里跨年，做他的客人。
I hadn't made any plans, and he said, 'It's a big night at the restaurant. Why don't you come and be my guest?'
我本来没什么安排，他说：'那晚店里可热闹了，你来做我的客人怎么样？'
I said yes almost immediately, and I'm glad I did.
我几乎立刻就答应了，后来也庆幸自己答应了。
The place was full of warmth: the band played, strangers became friends over shared desserts, and the cooks came out to dance between courses.
店里暖意融融：乐队在演奏，陌生人因为分甜点成了朋友，厨师们趁着上菜的间隙出来跳了一段舞。
Then came the countdown — ten, nine, eight — and when everyone shouted 'Happy New Year', we literally rang in the new year with bells and hugs.
接着是倒计时——十、九、八——当所有人喊出'新年快乐'时，我们真的是伴着铃声和拥抱迎来了新年。
Afterwards my landlady teased me the way only old friends can: 'So? Are you two an item yet? Don't be coy with me!'
事后我的房东太太用只有老朋友才有的口吻打趣我：'怎么样？你们俩在一起了吗？别跟我扭捏！'
For me, the perfect New Year's Eve needs three things: people you care about, a bit of noise, and one small resolution.
对我来说，完美的新年前夜需要三样东西：在乎的人、一点热闹、一个小决心。
That year mine was simple — spend more time with the people who matter — and honestly, it's going well so far.
那一年我的决心很简单：多陪陪重要的人。说实话，执行得还不错。

topics.question: Describe a time when you discovered a new side of a family member. How did it change your relationship?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你发现了家人身上全新一面的经历。这如何改变了你们的关系？
hints: 原来的印象是什么
for years she was just 'the quiet one' at home
什么场合让你改观
I visited her in another city / she took me to her recording session
你看到了什么
I just didn't know my sister was so cool / she was all focus
关系的变化
we stopped being just 'siblings at the dinner table'
vocab: I just didn't know my sister was so cool
我真不知道我姐这么酷
sample: I'd like to talk about my older sister, and about the evening I discovered she was, well, kind of cool.
我想讲讲我姐姐，讲讲那个我发现她——怎么说呢——挺酷的晚上。
For years she was just 'the quiet one' at home — glasses, books, early to bed.
多年来她在家里就是'安静的那个'——戴眼镜、抱着书、早早睡。
Then I visited her in the city where she studies music, and she took me to her recording session.
后来我去她读书的城市看她，她带我去了她的录音棚。
I walked in and my jaw dropped: walls of equipment, microphones, a huge mixing desk — and she just sat down and used it all, saying calmly, 'We're all set.'
我一进门就惊了：满墙的设备、话筒、一张巨大的调音台——而她径直坐下操作自如，还平静地说：'都准备好了。'
I remember thinking, 'I just didn't know my sister was so cool.'
我记得当时心想：'我真不知道我姐这么酷。'
Even better was watching her record her own song with her friend Bill, who had put the whole arrangement together.
更棒的是看她和朋友比尔录她自己写的歌——整个编曲都是比尔一手张罗的。
When the engineer said, 'We only have the studio for an hour, so we'd better get crackin',' she was all focus — no hesitation, no excuses.
录音师说'棚只租了一小时，抓紧开工'时，她立刻全神贯注——不犹豫、不找借口。
Before the take I whispered, 'Knock 'em dead, sis,' and she grinned.
开录前我小声说了句'姐，惊艳全场'，她咧嘴笑了。
That visit changed our relationship completely.
那次探望彻底改变了我们的关系。
We stopped being just 'siblings at the dinner table' and became fans of each other.
我们不再只是'饭桌上的姐弟'，而成了彼此的粉丝。
Now she sends me her new songs before anyone else hears them.
现在她的新歌，总是第一个发给我听。

topics.question: Describe a moment when something you had dreamed about for a long time finally happened.
topics.questionZh: 描述一件你梦想了很久的事终于实现的时刻。
hints: 梦想是什么、梦了多久
I'd been dreaming about this for years
机会怎么来的
the school finally let students book the studio / we booked one hour
那一刻的感受
hearing my own song come back through the speakers / I had to hold back tears
这件事教会你什么
you build dreams in small, sixty-minute pieces
vocab: I've been dreaming about this for years
it just never had the chance to come out
只是以前一直没机会冒出来
I can't wait till you can hear it
sample: The moment I want to describe is the day my band finished recording our first proper song in a real studio.
我想讲的那一刻，是我的乐队在真正的录音棚里录完第一支像样歌的那天。
I'd been dreaming about this for years — literally years, since I first picked up a guitar at fifteen.
这我梦想了好多年——真的是好多年，从十五岁第一次抱起吉他开始。
So when the school finally let students book the studio, my friend and I grabbed the chance and booked one hour.
所以当学校终于允许学生预订录音棚时，我和朋友立刻抓住机会，订了一个小时。
Everything was ready: the engineer, the microphone, and my brother sitting in the control room as the audience.
一切就绪：录音师、话筒，还有坐在控制室当观众的弟弟。
Singing with the headphones on and hearing my own song come back through those speakers — I can't really describe it.
戴着耳机唱，听着自己的歌从音箱里传回来——那种感觉我形容不出来。
When we finished, my brother — the toughest critic I have — said, 'That was totally cool.'
录完时，我那个最挑剔的'乐评人'弟弟说：'太酷了。'
It's hard to believe, but I had to hold back tears right there in the booth.
说出来难以置信，我在棚里当场就强忍住了眼泪。
Before this, the song was just something inside me — it was there, but it never had the chance to come out.
在这之前，这首歌只是我心里的一点东西——它一直都在，只是从没机会冒出来。
That one hour taught me that dreams don't usually arrive as one big moment; you build them in small, booked, sixty-minute pieces.
那一小时让我明白：梦想通常不会作为一个盛大的时刻降临，而是靠一次次预订好的'六十分钟'攒出来的。
I can't wait till more people can hear it.
我等不及让更多人听到它。

topics.question: Describe a close friend who chose a very different path in life from yours. How do you feel about it now?
topics.questionZh: 描述一位与你选择了截然不同人生道路的挚友。你现在怎么看这件事？
hints: 朋友做了什么选择
he decided to drop out and move to L.A. / I stayed to finish my degree
你当时的反应
I said, 'You're kidding me' / I told him he was nuts
分别时的场景
we recorded one last song / 'You have your dream and I have mine'
现在的关系
we're still the first call for each other
vocab: You have your dream and I have mine
你有你的梦想，我也有我的
sample: My closest friend from music school decided to drop out and move to Los Angeles to chase the record industry, while I stayed to finish my degree — so we literally chose opposite paths.
我在音乐学院最要好的朋友决定退学去洛杉矶闯唱片行业，而我留下读完学位——我们真的是选了相反的路。
When he first told me, I said, 'You're kidding me,' because he was one of the best students in our class.
他刚告诉我时，我说：'你开玩笑吧'，因为他可是我们班最好的学生之一。
He just shrugged: 'I'm wasting time here. I've got friends in the record industry there, and if I'm there, they'll get me a job.'
他只是耸耸肩：'我在这儿是浪费时间。我在那边的唱片圈有朋友，只要我人到，他们就能给我份工作。'
I told him he was nuts, and he laughed and said it wouldn't make any difference — he knew I'd say that.
我说他疯了，他笑着说我知道说了也没用——他就知道我会这么说。
Before he left, we recorded one last song together in the school studio.
他走之前，我们在学校录音棚一起录了最后一首歌。
At the door he said, 'You have your dream and I have mine — let's hope our dream catchers let in only the good dreams.'
在门口他说：'你有你的梦想，我有我的——但愿我们的捕梦网只放好梦进来。'
We hugged, and I finally said the thing I'd been avoiding: 'I'm gonna miss you.' He just answered, 'Take care of yourself,' and walked off with his guitar.
我们拥抱，我终于说出一直躲着的那句话：'我会想你的。'他只回了句'照顾好自己'，就背着吉他走了。
People say true friends should walk the same road, but I disagree.
有人说真朋友就该走同一条路，我不同意。
Two years on, he engineers albums in L.A. and I teach music, and we're still the first call for each other.
两年过去，他在洛杉矶做专辑录音，我教音乐，而我们仍然是彼此的第一通电话。
Different paths didn't split us; they just gave us more to talk about.
不同的路没有拆散我们，只是让我们有了更多可聊的。

topics.question: Do you think children should have a say in big family decisions, such as where the family lives? Why?
topics.questionZh: 你认为在重大家庭决定（比如全家搬去哪里住）中，孩子应该有发言权吗？为什么？
hints: 观点：应该有发言权
children should have a voice, but not the final call
例子：被蒙在鼓里的孩子
the boy overheard his parents planning to move abroad
隐瞒的后果
they pulled a crazy stunt / fear of the unknown
怎么做更好
listening costs nothing / a child who feels heard is a child who trusts
vocab: How come parents always make the decisions?
怎么什么都是父母说了算？
sample: Yes, I firmly believe children should have a say in big family decisions, especially ones that turn their lives upside down — like moving to another city or country.
我坚决认为，孩子在大事上应该有发言权，尤其是那些会颠覆他们生活的决定——比如搬到另一座城市或另一个国家。
I saw a perfect example through two ten-year-old boys I know.
我通过认识的两个十岁男孩，见过一个绝佳的例子。
One of them overheard his parents planning to return to their home country, and he said to his friend, 'What a drag. Maybe I'll hate it there.'
其中一个偷听到父母打算回老家，他跟朋友抱怨：'真扫兴，说不定我会讨厌那儿。'
The other boy was caught between a divorce and a possible move to another city — his parents might even go to court over him.
另一个孩子则夹在父母离异和可能搬去另一座城市之间——他的父母甚至可能为他对簿公堂。
When one asked, 'How come parents always make the decisions?' and the other answered, 'Kids have rights, too — we belong here,' I thought: quite right.
当一个问'怎么全是父母说了算'、另一个答'孩子也有权利，我们属于这里'时，我心想：说得对。
The sad part is that nobody had told them anything, so fear grew in the dark.
让人难过的是，没人跟他们交底，恐惧就在黑暗里疯长。
The two of them ended up doing something silly and dangerous, and the whole families got a terrible fright.
最后两个孩子干了件又傻又危险的事，把两家人都吓得够呛。
It came out of fear of the unknown, not out of badness.
那源于对未知的恐惧，而不是本性坏。
Of course, children shouldn't make the final call — parents still carry the responsibility.
当然，最终决定不该由孩子来做——责任毕竟由大人承担。
But listening costs nothing, and it prevents so much heartache on both sides.
可倾听不花一分钱，却能省下双方多少心痛。
A child who feels heard is a child who trusts.
感到被倾听的孩子，才会真正信任大人。

topics.question: Describe something you saved money for when you were a child. Did you finally get it?
topics.questionZh: 描述你小时候攒钱想买的一样东西。你最后得到它了吗？
hints: 攒钱的目标
I saved for months to buy a second-hand skateboard
怎么攒的
all my coins went into a tin piggy bank / washing cars, selling old comics
钱最后花在了哪
one last adventure with my best friend / we had a blast
这段回忆的意义
saving gives you choices, and choices let you be generous
vocab: Sounds like a lot of money
sample: When I was about ten, I saved money for months to buy a second-hand skateboard, and I still remember the exact figure in my bank: thirty-five dollars and fifty-two cents.
大概十岁时，我攒了好几个月的钱想买一块二手滑板，连储钱罐里的确切数字我都记得：三十五块五毛二。
All my coins went into a tin piggy bank on my shelf, and I shook it every night to guess how much was inside.
所有硬币都进了架上的铁皮储钱罐，每晚我都摇一摇，猜里面攒了多少。
When my friend heard the number, he whistled, 'Sounds like a lot of money!'
朋友听到那个数，吹了声口哨：'听着像一大笔钱！'
I'd earned it by washing my neighbour's car, selling old comics, and skipping the ice cream truck — which, for a ten-year-old, was real suffering.
钱是帮邻居洗车、卖旧漫画、忍着不追冰淇淋车攒的——对一个十岁孩子来说，那是真牺牲。
What makes the memory sweet is what finally happened to the money.
让这段回忆变甜的，是这笔钱最后的去向。
My best friend was moving to another city, and we wanted one last adventure together, so we broke the bank, added my Christmas money, and had a blast at the amusement park.
最好的朋友要搬去别的城市了，我们想最后一起疯一次，于是砸开了罐子，加上我的圣诞压岁钱，在游乐园玩了个痛快。
Was it the skateboard I'd dreamed of? No. Was it worth it? Absolutely.
是心心念念的滑板吗？不是。值吗？绝对值。
Our parents did ask, 'Is this idea gonna get you in trouble?' — well, we came home safe and happy, so we were forgiven quickly.
家长们确实问过'这主意不会惹麻烦吧'——我们平平安安、开开心心地回了家，所以很快就被原谅了。
That piggy bank taught me more about money than any class: saving gives you choices, and choices let you be generous.
那只储钱罐教我的'钱商'比任何课都多：攒钱给你选择，而选择让你能慷慨。
I still keep a jar of coins on my desk, just for the memory — and for the next 'last adventure'.
我桌上至今还摆着一罐硬币，就为留个纪念——也为了下一次'最后的冒险'。

topics.question: Describe a time when you were extremely worried about someone's safety. What happened in the end?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你为某人的安全极度担忧的经历。最后结果如何？
hints: 出了什么事
my ten-year-old cousin disappeared for an entire afternoon
当时的种种迹象
his piggy bank was empty / no one was answering the phone
大家怎么找的
the fathers drove around the city / I stayed home to answer the phone
结果与感悟
found safe at a clinic / watch the quiet ones when big changes are coming
sample: The most worried I've ever been was last New Year's Eve, when my ten-year-old nephew disappeared for an entire afternoon.
我最担心的一次是去年新年前夜，十岁的小外甥整整一下午不见了踪影。
He had asked to go out 'for a while' and never came back for lunch.
他说出去'一会儿'，结果连午饭都没回来吃。
His mother called me in a shaking voice: his piggy bank was empty, so he had taken his money and left.
他妈妈声音发抖地打来电话：储钱罐空了，他是拿了钱走的。
We called his best friend's house — that boy was missing too, and nobody was answering the home phone.
我们打给他最好朋友的家里——那孩子也不见了，而且家里电话没人接。
Those next three hours were the longest of my life.
接下来的三个小时，是我一生中最漫长的。
The two fathers drove around the city checking skating rinks and parks, while I stayed behind to answer the phone and pass on messages.
两位父亲开车满城找，滑冰场、公园一个个查，我则守着接电话、传消息。
I kept telling myself, 'They're probably just fooling around somewhere,' but not knowing where a child is — that is a kind of fear I can't describe.
我不停安慰自己'他们八成只是在哪儿瞎玩'，可是不知道一个孩子在哪——那种恐惧，我形容不出来。
At seven o'clock the phone finally rang: a rink attendant had noticed a limping boy, and someone had taken them to a clinic — a sprained ankle, nothing worse.
七点钟，电话终于响了：滑冰场员工注意到一个瘸着腿的男孩，有人把他们送去了诊所——脚踝扭伤，别无大碍。
I cried with relief right into the phone.
我对着电话，如释重负地哭了。
Now I always say: keep an eye on the quiet ones when big changes are coming — that's exactly when kids do crazy things.
现在我总说：大变动要来的时候，多留意那些安静的孩子——孩子干出格的事，往往就在那种时候。

topics.question: Do you think children sometimes do risky or crazy things to express their feelings? What should parents do about it?
topics.questionZh: 你认为孩子有时会通过冒险或出格的行为来表达情绪吗？父母应该怎么应对？
hints: 观点：行为是一种'说话'
it's a way of speaking when nobody listens to their words
例子：两个被蒙在鼓里的孩子
they overheard the adults and understood enough to be terrified
后果与真相
one boy hurt his ankle / 'we just wanted to do something special'
父母该怎么办
punishment treats the symptom / explaining and listening work better
sample: Yes, I really think children sometimes do risky or wild things as a way of speaking, especially when nobody listens to their words.
是的，我确实认为孩子有时会干危险出格的事，那是一种'表达'——尤其在没人听他们说话的时候。
Take the two ten-year-old boys I know.
就拿我认识的那两个十岁男孩来说。
One was about to be taken to another country, and the other might be moved to a different city because of his parents' divorce.
一个即将被带去另一个国家，另一个可能因为父母离异要搬去别的城市。
They overheard the adults, understood enough to be terrified, and told no one.
他们偷听到了大人的谈话，懂得足以害怕，却谁也没告诉。
Instead, they pulled a crazy stunt: they took their savings, slipped out on New Year's Eve and went ice skating — 'one last adventure together', as they later explained.
于是他们干了件出格的荒唐事：带上积蓄，新年前夜溜出门去滑冰——用他们后来的话说，是'最后一起冒险一次'。
One boy hurt his ankle, and the whole thing ended at a hospital with two families half-mad with worry.
一个孩子伤了脚踝，整件事最后在医院收场，两家人急得半疯。
When the parents asked why, the answer was heartbreaking in its simplicity: 'We just wanted to do something special before I have to go.'
当父母问起原因时，答案简单得让人心疼：'在我不得不走之前，我们只想一起做件特别的事。'
They weren't bad kids; they were scared kids with no other channel.
他们不是坏孩子，而是没有其他出口的、害怕的孩子。
So in my view, punishment alone — being grounded for a month, say — only treats the symptom.
所以在我看来，光靠惩罚——比如禁足一个月——只是治标。
What works is explaining, listening, and making children feel safe about the future.
真正管用的是解释、倾听，让孩子对未来有安全感。
Kids'll do crazy things anyway, occasionally — but they'll do far fewer of them when they feel heard.
孩子偶尔总归会干点疯狂事——但当他们感到被倾听，这种事会少得多。

topics.question: Do you think neighbours still look out for each other the way they used to? Why or why not?
topics.questionZh: 你认为如今邻居之间还像过去那样互相照应吗？为什么？
hints: 观点：还在，但方式变了
kindness just moved from the doorway to the group chat
小时候的经历
our neighbour kept an eye on all the kids / she held a spare key
现在的形式
when real trouble comes, twelve doors open at once
一个暖心细节
the babysitter stuck around two extra hours, unpaid
sample: I'd say yes — neighbours absolutely still look out for each other, though the way we do it has changed.
我认为还在——邻居之间当然仍会互相照应，只是方式变了。
In the building where I grew up, we had a neighbour, Mrs Lin, who lived across the street and kept an eye on all the kids on our floor.
在我长大的那栋楼，有位住在街对面的林太太，我们整层的孩子她都帮忙照看着。
When my parents travelled for work, she held a spare key, checked on me every evening, and sent over dumplings that I suspect were made 'by accident, too many'.
我父母出差时，她家存着备用钥匙，每晚来看我一眼，还总送来'一不小心包多了'的饺子。
She was never formal — her greeting was always, 'Come in, make yourselves at home!'
她从不讲究客套，招呼永远是那句：'进来吧，随便点儿，别拘束！'
What struck me recently is how the same instinct shows up in modern form.
最近让我触动的是，同样的本能换上了现代的形式。
In my current apartment we have a group chat: when a delivery goes missing or a child is locked out, twelve doors open at once — missing kids, lost keys, you name it.
我现在住的小区有个群：快递丢了、孩子被锁门外，十二扇门立刻都'开'了——丢孩子、丢钥匙，你尽管说，总有人应。
Not long ago, a babysitter in my friend's building stuck around for two extra hours, unpaid, when a family emergency came up — she said she was 'just helping out'.
不久前，朋友楼里的一位临时保姆遇到那家有急事，甚至无偿多留了两个小时——她说自己'只是搭把手'。
Perhaps we no longer borrow salt door to door, but when real trouble comes, city people still turn up for each other.
也许我们不再挨家挨户借盐了，但真遇到麻烦时，城里人依然会为彼此出现。
Kindness just moved from the doorway to the group chat.
善意只是从门口，搬进了群聊里。

topics.question: Describe a time when your carefully made plans were completely ruined. How did you react?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你精心制定的计划被彻底打乱的经历。你当时是如何应对的？
hints: 原来的计划是什么
my brother was visiting / a restaurant, a party, the fireworks
怎么被打乱的
a phone call: a friend's son had gone missing
你们做了什么
we cancelled the table / he volunteered to answer the phone
结果与感悟
found safe at seven / the meaning isn't in the plan, it's in the people
vocab: check in every half hour or so
每半小时互通一次消息
sample: Last New Year's Eve taught me that plans, however careful, are written in pencil.
去年新年前夜教会我：计划再周密，也不过是铅笔写的。
My brother was visiting me for the first time in two years, and I had arranged everything: a nice restaurant, a party at a friend's place, the fireworks by the bay.
我弟弟两年来第一次来看我，我把一切都安排好了：好餐厅、朋友家的派对、海湾的烟花。
At four in the afternoon, everything was perfect.
下午四点，一切完美。
At half past four came a phone call: the ten-year-old son of a close friend had gone missing.
四点半，一个电话打来：好友家十岁的儿子不见了。
There was no real choice to make.
其实根本没什么可选的。
We cancelled the table, and my brother — who had only just got off the plane — volunteered to sit in their house answering the phone, while I drove the father around the city.
我们退掉了餐厅，刚下飞机的弟弟主动留在那家接电话，我则开车拉着孩子父亲满城找。
The families asked us to check in every half hour or so, so the whole evening became a relay of phone calls.
两家人让我们每半小时互通一次消息，整个晚上就成了一场电话接力。
On the way my brother joked weakly, 'Well, things happen — I didn't think our New Year's Eve would turn out like this.'
路上他有气无力地打趣：'唉，世事难料——我还以为咱们的跨年夜不会变成这样呢。'
At seven we got the call: the boy had been found, safe, at a clinic.
七点，电话来了：孩子在一家诊所找到了，平安。
We ended up eating instant noodles at midnight, too tired to party.
午夜时分，我们累得根本没力气庆祝，最后吃了泡面。
When I thanked my brother for being such a good sport, he just shrugged: 'Family first. We'll party next year.'
我谢谢弟弟这么够意思，他耸耸肩说：'家人优先，明年再嗨。'
Now I plan big days loosely, because the meaning was never in the plan; it's in the people.
现在我安排大日子都留余地，因为意义从来不在计划里，而在人身上。

topics.question: What do you think parents should consider most when making custody arrangements for children after divorce?
topics.questionZh: 你认为父母离异后安排孩子抚养权时，最应该考虑的是什么？
hints: 观点：孩子的感受高于一切
the child's feelings should come before everything else
例子：一个被来回'运送'的孩子
he felt like a piece of baggage being shipped back and forth
大人的问题不该让孩子买单
trying to get back at the ex-wife through the boy
理想的做法
work things out / your happiness will be our first priority
vocab: 一件被运来运去的行李
choose between his mother and me
在我和他妈妈之间做选择
your happiness will be our first priority
sample: When parents divorce, I think the child's feelings should come before everything else — before convenience, before money, and even before fairness between the adults.
父母离异时，我认为孩子的感受应该放在一切之前——比方便重要，比钱重要，甚至比大人之间的公平更重要。
I saw this up close with a family friend, a restaurant owner who was fighting over where his ten-year-old son should live.
我在一位世交身上近距离见过这件事：他开餐馆，正在争十岁儿子该跟谁住。
The poor boy was being asked to choose between his mother in one city and his father in another.
可怜的孩子被要求在两座城市之间做选择：跟妈妈，还是跟爸爸。
One night the father admitted to me, 'I'm ashamed to say it, but I've made him feel like a piece of baggage being shipped back and forth between his mother and me.'
一天晚上，这位父亲向我坦白：'说来惭愧，我让他觉得自己像件行李，在我和他妈妈之间被运来运去。'
He even wondered whether, deep down, he was trying to get back at his ex-wife through the boy.
他甚至怀疑，自己内心深处是不是想借这个孩子报复前妻。
What moved me was how he changed after the boy ran away one night and was found hurt.
让我触动的是，那晚孩子出走、又被找到时受了伤，此后他彻底变了。
He sat his son down and promised, 'You don't have to worry about who you'll live with. Your mother and I will work things out somehow, and your happiness will be our first priority.'
他让儿子坐下，郑重承诺：'你不用再担心跟谁住。我和你妈妈总会把事情解决好，你的幸福才是头等大事。'
That, to me, is the answer: custody shouldn't be about winning; it should be about making the child feel least like luggage.
在我看来，这正是答案：抚养权之争不该论输赢，而该看谁能让孩子最不像一件行李。
And where possible, both parents staying warm to each other matters as much as the arrangement itself.
而且只要做得到，父母之间保持温度，和安排本身同样重要。

topics.question: Describe a difficult experience that made you rethink what is really important in your life.
topics.questionZh: 描述一段让你重新思考人生中什么才真正重要的艰难经历。
hints: 出什么事了
I was running everything single-handedly and I was exhausted
怎么崩的
a problem I'd brushed aside blew up / I nearly lost a friendship
谁点醒了你
a friend said, 'Stop this, right now' / are you spending attention where it counts?
之后怎么改变
enough is enough / fewer hours, more family
vocab: get to the bottom of this
把注意力放在重要的事上
sample: Two years ago, a small crisis at work forced me to rethink what really matters, and it genuinely rearranged my life.
两年前，一场小小的工作危机逼我重新思考什么才真正重要，也确实重排了我的人生。
At the time I was running a team project almost single-handedly — managing everything, answering everything, deciding everything.
当时我几乎单枪匹马地运营一个团队项目——什么都管、什么都答、什么都拍板。
I was proud of it, but I was also exhausted and, looking back, quite blind.
我为此自豪，但也精疲力竭，现在回头看，还相当盲目。
Then a problem I had brushed aside blew up, and in one week I nearly lost the project and a friendship that mattered to me.
接着，一个被我敷衍过去的问题爆发了，一周之内，我差点丢掉项目，还差点失去一段对我很重要的友谊。
At my lowest, I honestly felt like a total jerk.
最低谷的时候，我真觉得自己是个十足的混蛋。
A friend sat me down and said, 'Stop this, right now. I've seen the sacrifices you make. But ask yourself: are you spending your attention where it counts?'
一位朋友让我坐下：'打住，别再说了。你做的牺牲我都看在眼里。但你问问自己：注意力花在真正要紧的地方了吗？'
I finally got to the bottom of the problem, but more importantly, I got to the bottom of myself.
我最终把问题查了个水落石出，但更重要的是，把自己也查了个水落石出。
I'd been playing the tragic hero instead of fixing what was broken.
我一直在扮演悲情英雄，而不是去修好坏掉的东西。
Since then, whenever I drift back into old habits, I say to myself: enough is enough — pay attention to what's important.
从那以后，每当旧习惯复发，我就对自己说：够了就是够了——把注意力放在重要的事上。
I work fewer hours and see my family more, and strangely, the project has never gone better.
现在我工作时间少了、陪家人多了，说来奇怪，项目反而从未运转得这么好。

topics.question: Describe a time when you comforted someone who was very upset. What did you say or do?
topics.questionZh: 描述一次你安慰情绪非常低落的人的经历。你说了什么、做了什么？
hints: 对方怎么了
he nearly broke down while we were searching for his son
他怎么自责的
blaming himself for everything / 'I've caused him nothing but heartache'
你说了什么
you sound like a man who is suffering / I've seen the sacrifices you make
效果与感悟
he went quiet, wiped his eyes / comforting is holding up a mirror
vocab: I must sound like a big cry baby
我听着肯定像个爱哭鬼
一位关爱孩子、甘于付出的父亲
sample: The person I most remember comforting is a family friend who nearly broke down one New Year's Eve, when his son went missing.
我最记得安慰过的人，是一位世交。新年前夜他儿子失踪那晚，他几乎崩溃。
We had been driving around the city for hours, calling hospitals, when he suddenly started talking fast and hard — blaming himself for the divorce, the custody fight, everything.
我们在城里转了好几个小时，挨个给医院打电话，这时他突然急促而激动地说起来——把离婚、抚养权之争、一切都归罪到自己头上。
He said, 'I've caused him nothing but heartache. I can't do it anymore — manage the restaurant, my son, a personal life...'
他说：'我带给他的只有心痛。我撑不下去了——餐馆、儿子、个人的生活……'
Then, catching himself, he whispered, 'I must sound like a big cry baby.'
接着他回过神来，低声说：'我听着肯定像个爱哭的大孩子。'
I didn't rush in with solutions, because there weren't any yet.
我没有急着给方案，因为当时根本没有方案。
I just said, 'No — you sound like a man who's suffering because his son is missing.'
我只是说：'不——你听上去像一个因为儿子失踪而备受煎熬的人。'
Then I reminded him of what I had seen with my own eyes: 'You're a caring and giving father. I've seen the sacrifices you make for him. I can't imagine anyone loving him more than you do.'
然后我提醒他我亲眼所见的一切：'你是个关爱孩子、甘于付出的父亲。你为他做的牺牲我都看在眼里。我想象不出还有谁会比你更爱他。'
He went quiet for a while, then wiped his eyes and said softly, 'Sometimes I get so tired.'
他安静了一阵，然后擦了擦眼睛，轻声说：'有时我真的好累。'
We sat in silence until my phone rang — the boy had been found, safe.
我们沉默地坐着，直到我的电话响起——孩子找到了，平安。
That night taught me that comforting someone isn't about fixing them; it's about holding up a mirror at the right moment.
那晚我明白了：安慰一个人，不是去修理他，而是在对的时刻，为他举起一面镜子。

topics.question: Describe a time when you made a serious mistake as a child and how the adults around you responded.
topics.questionZh: 描述你小时候犯的一次严重错误，以及身边的大人是如何回应的。
hints: 犯了什么错
we slipped out without telling anyone and spent our savings at an ice rink
后果多严重
two families called the police / I sprained my ankle
大人的处理方式
I was grounded for a month, but invited to the New Year's dinner too
你学到了什么
the punishment said 'never again', the dinner said 'you're still ours'
vocab: what do you have to say for yourself
this is going to be a very good year
sample: The biggest mistake of my childhood happened when I was ten, and the way the adults handled it shaped me more than the trouble itself.
我童年最大的一次犯错发生在十岁那年，而大人们处理这件事的方式，比麻烦本身更塑造了我。
My best friend was moving away, and we decided, without telling anyone, to take our savings and spend one 'perfect last day' at an ice rink across town.
最好的朋友要搬走了，我们没告诉任何人，就带上积蓄，想去城那头的滑冰场过'完美的最后一天'。
We turned off our phones — genius, I know — and by evening two families were calling the police and the hospitals.
我们还关了手机——够'聪明'的吧——到晚上，两家人已经在报警、给医院打电话了。
I sprained my ankle badly, which is how we finally got found.
我崴伤了脚踝，我们这才被找到。
I remember standing in the hospital corridor, thinking, 'My dad's going to have a fit.'
我记得自己站在医院走廊里想：'我爸非火冒三丈不可。'
When the fathers arrived, one of them asked quietly, 'What do the two of you have to say for yourselves?' We just mumbled, 'Sorry.'
父亲们赶到后，其中一位轻声问：'你们俩还有什么要说的？'我们只咕哝了一句：'对不起。'
I was grounded for a month — but don't get me wrong, that same night I was also invited to the family's New Year's dinner.
我被禁足了一个月——不过别误会，同一天晚上，我还被请去了那家的新年晚餐。
That combination confused me at ten, but I understand it now: the punishment said 'never again', and the dinner said 'you're still ours'.
十岁时我困惑于这种组合，现在懂了：惩罚说的是'不许再犯'，晚餐说的是'你仍是我们的人'。
Years later, my father admitted that the scariest part wasn't anger — it was simply not knowing where I was.
多年后，父亲承认最可怕的不是生气，而是根本不知道我在哪。
And I made him a promise I've mostly kept: do something foolish, fine — but never disappear.
我也向他许了一个基本守住的诺言：做傻事可以，但绝不消失。
At midnight that year, counting down with everyone, I told myself: this is going to be a very good year — and it was.
那年午夜，和大家一起倒数时，我对自己说：这会是很好的一年——后来果然是。
